title: xray(spec): four deleted config keys and a deleted palette verb are still documented as shipping in six spec pages (rf2-y8doi.27 spec half)
description:
The spec half of rf2-y8doi.27. **The code half merged at `9963d89db5` (PR #10031) and deleted four
config keys and one palette verb. Those names are still documented as SHIPPING in six spec pages, so
the spec is FALSE on trunk right now** — not stale-and-harmless, but describing knobs a user can
try and find absent. `CLAUDE.md` puts it plainly: the spec is the artefact, the code is downstream.

Reported by the rf2-y8doi.27 worker, which named 19 rows and flagged three traps. **Census re-run
and CORRECTED by the mayor at trunk `9963d89db5`** — the counts and two of the three cites moved.

## WHAT WAS DELETED (by PR #10031)

    :rf.xray/filters-storage-key        the filter-persistence localStorage knob
    :rf.xray/show-tool-frames?          the L1 picker's tool-frames slot (never writable)
    :clear-epoch-history                the palette command verb (cleared a mirror)
    day8.re-frame2-xray.filters.persistence   the whole namespace

## THE SITES — census at `9963d89db5`, longest-first alternation, controls both ways

**41 hits across 19 files**, of which the `tools/xray/src` and `tools/xray/test` hits are
**DELIBERATE REMOVAL TOMBSTONES written by PR #10031** (`;; (:show-tool-frames? was REMOVED here —
rf2-y8doi.27 ...)`). **DO NOT TOUCH THOSE.** They are the record of the deletion and the worker
reported them as intentional. Your surface is the six SPEC pages:

    tools/xray/spec/007-UX-IA.md          :1635   verb table row, `:clear-epoch-history`
    tools/xray/spec/015-Configuration.md  :106    prose naming the flat hyphenated shape
                                          :133    Filters TABLE ROW  <- link half of a PAIR
                                          :544    config sample block, `:show-tool-frames?`
                                          :565    prose bullet, `:show-tool-frames?`
                                          :693    `### :rf.xray/filters-storage-key`  <- ANCHOR half
    tools/xray/spec/018-Event-Spine.md    :1356   `(xray-config/configure! {:rf.xray/filters-storage-key ...})`
                                          :1747   `:rf.xray/picker-show-tool-frames?`  <- SEE TRAP 3
    tools/xray/spec/019-Cross-Cutting-Insight.md
                                          :1049   key inventory list
    tools/xray/spec/API.md                :322    surface table, `config.cljc` row
                                          :672    "The six chord-reachable command verbs"  <- TRAP 2
                                          :674    the list itself, includes `:clear-epoch-history`
                                          :699    heading, "the six ... verbs"  <- SECOND count word
                                          :715    verb catalogue TABLE ROW
    tools/xray/spec/Conventions.md        :452    `set-filters-storage-key!` as a LENGTH example  <- TRAP 4

Controls: `rf.xray/filters` (a live sibling that must survive) reads 64; a nonsense key reads 0.
**Re-derive every line at your own base and report the delta** — two of the worker's three flagged
cites had already drifted when I checked them an hour later.

**`tools/xray/spec/API.md` is NOT the hot-zone `spec/API.md`.** Measured: the top-level `spec/` tree
carries ZERO hits for any deleted name, so no hot-zone file and no `api-manifest` sidecar is
involved, and this item is not sequenced behind anything. Do not confuse the two files.

## TRAP 1 — `015:133` AND `015:693` ARE A LINK/ANCHOR PAIR AND MUST MOVE TOGETHER

`:133` carries `[§:rf.xray/filters-storage-key](#rfxrayfilters-storage-key)`; `:693` is the heading
`### :rf.xray/filters-storage-key` that anchor resolves to. `scripts/check_doc_slugs.py` validates
anchors under `tools/*/spec`, **so removing the heading while leaving the link turns that gate RED**,
and removing the link while leaving the heading leaves an orphan section. **This is the one place in
this item where a gate can actually see your diff — use it.** Check whether any OTHER page links to
that anchor before deleting it.

## TRAP 2 — THE COUNT WORD MOVES, AND IT APPEARS TWICE

`API.md:672` reads *"The six chord-reachable command verbs that ship post-rf2-ybjkx —
`:toggle-theme`, `:cycle-reduced-motion`, `:snapshot-app-db`, `:jump-to-settings`, `:toggle-mode`,
`:clear-epoch-history`"*. Deleting the verb makes it **five**, so the NUMBER WORD changes and not
just the list. **The worker named `:674` only; there is a second count word at `:699`**, a heading
reading *"the six 'chord-reachable' verbs from rf2-ybjkx"*. A census keyed on the verb NAME finds
neither. **Census the word "six" in that file as its own axis**, and check `007:1635`'s table and
`API.md:715`'s catalogue for a total that also needs decrementing.

## TRAP 3 — `018:1747` IS A DIFFERENTLY-SPELLED KEY AND A NAME-KEYED CENSUS MISSES IT

It reads `:rf.xray/picker-show-tool-frames?` — a spelling **never implemented under that name**. A
census keyed on `:show-tool-frames?` does not find it. It is still a row describing a knob that does
not exist, under either spelling. **Settle what it was meant to be before editing it**, and take it
as the reason to run a PREFIX axis (`show-tool-frames`, `tool-frames`) beside the exact-key axis.

## TRAP 4 — `Conventions.md:452` IS A NAME-LENGTH EXAMPLE AND WANTS JUDGEMENT, NOT A SWEEP

It reads: *"The longer-key setters (`set-layout-host-selector!` at 23 chars, `set-filters-storage-key!`
at 22) are the necessary cost of clarity; abbreviation is forbidden."* **The claim being made is
about NAMING CONVENTION, not about the key existing**, and the sentence needs two examples to carry
its point. A mechanical sweep deletes the dead one and leaves a rule justified by a single instance
— weakening the convention while "fixing" the spec. **Options: keep it as a historical illustration
and say so, or replace it with another genuinely long setter. Decide deliberately and say which you
chose and why.** Do not just delete it.

## Scope

**Spec prose only. No code change, no test change.** The code half has merged and is correct; if a
passage cannot be made true without touching code, name it and STOP.

**One item the rf2-y8doi.27 worker left deliberately and you may leave too**:
`tools/xray/test/day8/re_frame2_xray/self_noise_cljs_test.cljc:197` still uses
`:rf.xray.filters/persist` as a literal for a pure keyword predicate — it passes, but cites a dead
id. It is a test, not spec; if you touch it, say why.

## Gates

A `tools/xray/spec/*.md` edit arms `cljs_node_test` and `tools_jvm`. Hand the classifier **PATHS,
never revisions** (CLAUDE.md item (v)). **`tools_jvm` is lane-free — run it**, and say unfavourably
what its green covers: `017` and `019` are read by `coverage_matrix_metadata_test.clj` (a real JVM
gate on content), `007` is read by `panel_enum_spec_refs.clj` which serves a CLJS namespace in the
NODE lane, and `015`, `018`, `API.md` and `Conventions.md` are read by NOTHING.

**`check_doc_slugs.py` is a REAL gate for trap 1** — it validates anchors and link targets under
`tools/*/spec`. It inspects no prose and strips fenced blocks before reading a link, so it says
nothing about the rest of your diff; but on the `015` pair it can genuinely fail, and a planted
broken anchor there is an honest control.

**Check the shadow-cljs exclusive before any build**: it is a machine-wide exclusive and two
concurrent runs wedge silently. It was released by rf2-y8doi.27; confirm at dispatch time rather
than trusting this line.

## The control is the deliverable

Show it red when the property is removed, restore, verify by hashing the bytes. **Trap 1 gives you a
real one**: plant a broken anchor in a file you edited and `check_doc_slugs.py` goes red naming the
line — the rf2-y8doi.27 worker did exactly that and got exit 1 at line 226. Restore against the
committed object (`git rev-parse HEAD:<path>`, then `git hash-object`), a match by EITHER form being
a good restore, with `git diff --quiet HEAD` as a second instrument. **Commit before planting.**

## File health and hand verification

Three line-ending numbers with **Python reading the bytes** for every file touched, before and
after: total CR, total CRLF, bare LF. Require CR == CRLF and bare LF == 0. **Never `grep -c`** for
carriage returns; **never `sed -i`** on a `w/crlf` file.

`007`, `015` and `API.md` carry TABLES and nothing in this tree validates one — **verify every
table's column count and the prose BY HAND and say so in the PR body.**

**Add `tools/xray/spec/020-Filter-Predicates.md` §7 to this item's surface. The description above
says six spec pages; it is SEVEN.**

### Why the census missed it, which is the reusable part

The census that built this item keyed on the **deleted NAMES** — `:rf.xray/filters-storage-key`,
`:show-tool-frames?`, `:clear-epoch-history`, `day8.re-frame2-xray.filters.persistence`. `020` §7
returns **zero hits for all four**, so it was correctly absent from a name-keyed sweep and I filed
the item without it.

**But a section can describe a DELETED MECHANISM without naming a deleted key**, and that is exactly
what §7 does. This is the two-token-axes rule arriving one level up: the axes needed here are not two
spellings of a name, they are **NAME** and **MECHANISM**. A deletion falsifies prose that describes
the behaviour, not only prose that names the identifier.

I found it only because the rf2-y8doi.27 worker had listed `020-Filter-Predicates.md` among its 19
falsified rows and my census disagreed with it. **The worker's report was right and my census was
short. When a report and a census disagree, the census is the thing to re-derive.**

title: surface-review(schemas): fix regex-width privacy alignment and printer-dependent digest caching
description:
Fix two schema-layer correctness defects: preserve sensitive-value redaction when a Malli regex child changes sequence width, and make default schema serialization independent of ambient printer limits. Keep this bead OPEN for remediation. These are ordinary supported schema/REPL use cases, not requests for new validation policy, validator hardening, or another public API.

## Scope and revision

Slice: impl_schemas. Owned surface: every tracked path under implementation/schemas/**, enumerated below. Reviewed source revision: 1c9ff9697b0fa3a018c7a4371e02983ad2e79b2f. During review HEAD advanced to 5b89378c457e9997d7eff69b7dec56eec4e5307c (chore(beads): checkpoint); git diff from the baseline over implementation/schemas was empty, so the reviewed source bytes did not change.

SOURCE_ROOT=C:/Users/miket/code/re-frame2
WORKTREE_ROOT=(none; read-only review)

No production edits, compilation, server startup, installs, commits, or pushes were performed by this worker. JVM probes used already-cached dependencies and isolated process state. Root owns durable checkpoint/push.

## Finding 1 — P1: variable-width :cat/:catn can leak a sensitive app-db value into its rejection trace

Source: implementation/schemas/src/re_frame/schemas/walker.cljc:46-70, 239-273, 659-692, 1043-1097; the affected public call is implementation/schemas/src/re_frame/schemas/validate.cljc:994-997, 1051-1052, 1097-1124.

Trigger: a valid Malli concatenation has a regex child that consumes zero or multiple values before a sensitive child. A sequence containing optional/repeated data followed by a sensitive payload is a supported schema shape. The current positional model assumes the input index is the schema-child index, which holds for a tuple and simple fixed-width event :cat, but not for general :cat/:catn.

Reproducer, under the existing schemas JVM reset fixture and with-trace-recorder!:

    (s/reg-app-schema [:items]
      [:cat [:* :int] [:map [:token {:sensitive? true} :int]]])
    (s/validate-app-schema!
      {:items [{:token "schema-review-secret"}]}
      :schema-review)

Malli 0.20.1 returns false and explanation :in paths [[0] [0 :token]]. failing-in-path correctly computes the common ancestor [0], so the emitted :value is the entire map at input index zero. align-in-path incorrectly picks children[0] ([:* :int]), and schema-sensitive-at? therefore returns false for [0]. The sensitive map is schema child 1 but input element 0.

Expected: rejection remains false, and the secret-bearing :value must be :rf/redacted because the failing input element contains the sensitive payload. An ambiguous regex position should use a conservative sensitivity decision rather than identifying a different child as the failing one.

Actual, verified through the real trace recorder, without replacing trace/emit-error!:

    {:operation :rf.error/schema-validation-failure
     :sensitive? true
     :tags {:path [:items 0]
            :registered-path [:items]
            :value {:token "schema-review-secret"}
            :explain :rf/redacted
            :explain-humanized :rf/redacted
            :rollback? true ...}}

The same alignment failure reproduces for:

    [:catn [:prefix [:* :int]]
           [:payload [:map [:token {:sensitive? true} :int]]]]

A fixed-width control, [:cat :int SensitiveMap] against [1 {:token "schema-review-secret"}], correctly emits :value :rf/redacted. This distinguishes the missing width distinction from a broken recorder or universally disabled privacy.

Impact: an explicitly sensitive value enters an actual development validation-failure trace, despite the trace's sensitive stamp and the correctly scrubbed explanation. The candidate still rejects. No production validation bypass or downstream external transmission is alleged; the confirmed defect is disclosure at the diagnostic producer.

Repair recommendation: retain exact element precision for :tuple and demonstrably one-value-per-child :cat/:catn. When a concatenation contains regex-expanding children, treat that affected regex node as ambiguous for declaration extraction and value-path alignment and fall back to its whole-node sensitivity/opacity decision. Apply the same distinction consistently to the existing sanitizer. A conservative fallback is sufficient; do not implement a second Malli regex parser or add another runtime dependency.

Acceptance criteria:

- Real Malli + real trace-recorder regressions for both :cat and :catn with a zero-width repeat before a failing sensitive payload; no secret substring survives any trace value-bearing slot.
- Cover a nonzero repetition and an optional child, so the fix is about input width rather than the particular zero index.
- Keep the existing fixed-width :cat/:catn/:tuple non-sensitive-sibling precision tests passing, as well as sensitive-map and explanation redaction tests.
- Put the new schema cases in the shared CLJ/CLJS fixture corpus where practical and execute both hosts during remediation. The current review reproduced JVM behavior only.

## Finding 2 — P2: ambient *print-length* / *print-level* permanently poison cached schema digest bytes

Source: implementation/schemas/src/re_frame/schemas/validator.cljc:103-116 (compute-edn-print and memo installation); cache.cljc:38-45 stores the computed string by schema alone; digest.cljc:94-98 consumes that string as the schema's SHA-256 input.

Trigger: compute a schema digest for the first time in a REPL/tool context with ordinary bounded-printing bindings. Digest calculation is a public introspection operation and must not depend on how that context chooses to display other values. compute-edn-print binds several printer flags, but leaves *print-length* and *print-level* inherited. The memo then retains the truncated serialization after those bindings end.

Reproducer, in a fresh process (or after clearing the schema and print caches):

    (s/reg-app-schema [] {:frame :digest/a} [:map [:a :int]])
    (s/reg-app-schema [] {:frame :digest/b} [:map [:a :string]])
    (s/clear-edn-print-cache!)
    (binding [*print-length* 1]
      [(s/app-schemas-digest {:frame :digest/a})
       (s/app-schemas-digest {:frame :digest/b})])
    ;; both => "sha256:9d2ec1c0e952d6c3"
    (s/app-schemas-digest {:frame :digest/a})
    ;; still => "sha256:9d2ec1c0e952d6c3", outside the binding

Both schemas were serialized and cached as "[:map ...]". With an empty cache and unbounded printing, the same two registered schemas correctly produce different results:

    :digest/a => "sha256:e4bffe29a0226cac"
    :digest/b => "sha256:6fdca79b912a7ef0"

A separate *print-level* 1 probe prints [:map #], confirming the second display-limit axis also reaches the canonicalization. The use of cache clearing above is only to expose first-computation behavior deterministically; a fresh application's cache starts empty without that call.

Expected: the same schema value always serializes to the same complete bytes, independently of surrounding printer settings, as required by spec/010-Schemas.md:501 and the memoization premise at :516. These two ordinary distinct forms should retain the existing different digests under bounded printing.

Actual: the first printing context changes the process-wide memo value, produces deterministic collisions between unrelated schema forms, and changes subsequent digest calls outside that context.

Impact: the public drift fingerprint can miss a changed schema or disagree between sessions/hosts with identical schema sets solely because their first print context differed. The SSR digest comparison consumes this same hook (implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/hydrate.cljc:491-505, 531-554); an end-to-end hydration mismatch was not separately executed.

Repair recommendation: bind *print-length* nil and *print-level* nil inside compute-edn-print, around both canonicalise-schema-form and final pr-str, alongside its existing print flags. Leave memo keys, the digest algorithm, public API, and custom-printer contract unchanged.

Acceptance criteria:

- Compute default printer bytes and public digests with fresh caches under bounded *print-length* and *print-level* (separately and together); compare with the unbounded baseline.
- Re-read outside each binding without clearing the cache and prove the cached bytes still match the baseline.
- Preserve the distinct digests for the :int/:string forms above and all existing pinned digest fixtures; execute corresponding CLJ and CLJS tests.
- Ensure tests start with an isolated schema registry/cache, so unrelated registered paths cannot change expected digest fixtures (see observed test limitation below).

Inspected registration normalization, metadata/source coordinates, explicit-frame reads, bulk preflight, frame-id side-table ownership and destroy cleanup, hot-reload diagnostics, facade/late-bind publication, default Malli loading, validator/explainer/printer substitution, nil-token declaration presence, cache ownership, digest construction, opacity and sensitive/large walkers, per-slot failure shaping, malformed-schema isolation, and continuation guards around validation callbacks. The schema layer validates values; it does not implement coercive data transformation. Reviewed the optional-artifact deps/release declaration and selected production/bundle test sources. No new ownership or candidate-commit defect was established in this slice.

Executed the following existing JVM namespaces in one focused run: schemas-storage-test, schemas-failure-paths-test, validate-before-install-test, schemas-sensitive-test, schemas-walker-operators-test, schemas.digest-parity-test, schemas.printer-seam-test, schemas-fail-open-test. Result: 218 tests / 1,031 assertions, 2 failures, 0 errors, exit 1. Both failures were printer-seam expectations of an empty/single-path registry after preceding namespaces left registrations behind; its fixture at printer_seam_test.clj:29-44 only resets the function bundle. This combined run is not reported as green. The same printer namespace in a fresh JVM passed 11 tests / 36 assertions, 0 failures/errors, exit 0. The other seven namespaces had no failures. This is an observed test-order isolation limit, not evidence that the two runtime defects are already covered.

Focused process-local evidence:

- tests-impl_schemas-3.log/.exit: combined focused existing tests, exit 1 as detailed above.

All evidence is under ignored ai/surface-review-20260912/, with unique slice and attempt numbers. ## Existing work and duplicate check

VERDICT (schemas-a worker, 2026-09-13): PR #9750, branch worker/schemas-a, commit 5766e14472. Covers rf2-fzbj.25 (both findings), rf2-gwye.11 (finding 1) and rf2-gwye.14 (finding 2).

FINDING 1 FIXED (walker.cljc only). Positional :tuple / :cat / :catn precision (rf2-4q681i, rf2-ss06u.4) now applies only to a :tuple, or to a :cat / :catn whose every element provably consumes one value (a keyword, symbol, fn or non-regex vector form) and which is not itself spliced into an enclosing regex op. Any other sequence:
- descends its elements index-free at the shared base-path, like :sequential, with :catn entry flags claiming the base-path;
- falls back to the whole-node sensitivity/opacity decision in align-in-path;
- takes the fail-closed tail in sanitize-sensitive-path.
There is no second regex parser and no new dependency. validate.cljc needed no change.

FINDING 2 FIXED (validator.cljc). compute-edn-print binds *print-length* and *print-level* to nil beside its existing print flags, around both canonicalisation and the final pr-str. Memo keys, the digest algorithm, the public API and the custom-printer contract are unchanged. implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/hydrate.cljc reads the digest only through the :schemas/app-schemas-digest late-bind hook, so it needed no edit and ssr-a's file was not touched.

REGRESSION TESTS (all under implementation/schemas/test).

  - Six leak cases: zero-width :* in a :cat and in a :catn, an empty :?, a nonzero :* repetition that shifts the payload onto a later schema child, a nested :cat expansion, and a sensitive :map-of key that would ride :path / :reason.
  - Three controls that must still report their value verbatim: a variable-width :cat declaring nothing sensitive, fixed-width :cat sibling precision, and a slot outside a variable-width sequence.

  - One form's collection-valued map keys and set members exercise the canonicaliser's comparator.

RED THEN GREEN. The pre-fix walker.cljc and validator.cljc (their origin/main blobs, verified by blob hash) were planted and the gates run against them:
- jvm-schemas: exit 1, 21 failures, all in the new tests (6 leak cases x 2 assertions, :value redacted and secret absent; 3 printer bindings x inside/after; 3 walker pins).

The walker cannot tell a ref that resolves to a regex op from a primitive without calling into the validator, which is the same documented opaque-schema boundary that already makes keyword refs flag-invisible. # Senior review: xray-effects-panels

Reviewer persona: senior engineer who has built network and side-effect inspectors (a Network tab, a job-queue dashboard) and knows the lifecycle bugs: a request shown pending after it settled, a cancellation shown as an error, a retry counted as a new request, a route shown active that the router already left.
Tree: xray-review-sep17 worktree, trunk 9555881fe3
Scope read: tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/ { managed_fx_helpers.cljc (764), managed_fx_template.cljs (652), managed_fx_subs.cljs (101; the brief said `.cljc`, the file is `.cljs`), cancellation_cascade.cljs (768), cancellation_cascade_helpers.cljc (638), cancellation_cascade_events.cljs (101), cancellation_cascade_subs.cljs (76), resources.cljs (1588), resources_helpers.cljc (1994), routing.cljs (755), routing_helpers.cljc (891), common_helpers.cljc (167), overflow_indicator.cljc (99) } — 8,594 lines, every file read in full; tests under tools/xray/test/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/ for these namespaces skimmed for what is pinned (managed_fx_helpers_cljs_test.cljc read in full). Framework side read for divergence: implementation/resources/src/re_frame/resources/{trace_egress,scope_registry,mutation_events,work_ledger,events}.cljc (targeted), implementation/http/src/re_frame/http/{transport,registry,reply}.cljc (emit sites), implementation/routing/src/re_frame/routing/events.cljc (slice writer), implementation/core/src/re_frame/trace/projection.cljc (bundle grouper).
Owning specs consulted: tools/xray/spec/024-Resources-Panel.md (end to end); tools/xray/spec/019-Cross-Cutting-Insight.md (end to end); tools/xray/spec/021-Dynamic-Panel-Designs.md §7 Routing (end to end — 021 has NO managed-effects or cancellation-cascade section; those live in 019 §2.4 / §M.3, and 021 only cross-references the cascade popover at :1251/:1284); spec/Managed-Effects.md (end to end); spec/016-Resources.md §Status semantics, §Frame work ledger, §Optimistic mutations, §Trace surfacing, §Xray and AI tooling (the owning chapter per spec/Ownership.md); spec/014-HTTPRequests.md §Abort on actor destroy + heading map; spec/012-Routing.md §The `:rf/route` slice; tools/xray/spec/DESIGN-RATIONALE.md (grepped for rulings on these panels — none touch the behaviours below); tools/xray/spec/007-UX-IA.md §Performance budget.

## Findings, ranked

### 1. The HTTP wire-boundary record can never see its own response  [CONFIRMED] [severity: high] [kind: correctness] [size: L]
- Where: tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/managed_fx_helpers.cljc:210-222 (`http-trace-operations`), :293-304 (`fx-event->status`), :353-366 (`surface-events->phase`), :486-526 (`http-adapter`); tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/managed_fx_subs.cljs:52-66
- What: the HTTP collector names eight ops of which the runtime emits two, omits the one completion op it does emit, and the completion is emitted outside any drain — so in production every HTTP record reads `✓ OK · phase: completed` at issue time and `:res`/`:http-status`/`:wire`/`:failure`/`:cancel-cause`/`:duration-ms` stay nil forever.
- Evidence: (a) ripgrep for `:rf.http/handled|:rf.http/managed-issued|:rf.http/decode-failure` over implementation/**/src returns zero emit sites (only `:kind` values in tests/epoch); a multiline grep for `emit!\s+:\w+\s+(:rf\.http/…)` over implementation/**/src lists the complete emitted set: `replied`, `stale-suppressed`, `retry-attempt`, `aborted-on-actor-destroy`, two JVM warnings — control: `:rf.http/replied` is emitted at implementation/http/src/re_frame/http/transport.cljc:557 and named 5 times in spec/014. `:rf.http/transport` / `timeout` / `decode-failure` / `aborted` are failure `:kind`s inside the reply map, never operations. (b) `:rf.http/replied` fires "from the transport callback, OUTSIDE any `with-frame` scope" (transport.cljc:538-541) so it carries no `:rf.trace/dispatch-id` and the grouper files it under `[nil :ungrouped]` (implementation/core/src/re_frame/trace/projection.cljc:150-159, :189-199) — never in the issuing bundle's `:other` that `surface-events-for` scans (:276-289). `:rf.http/aborted-on-actor-destroy` fires inside the DESTROY drain (registry.cljc:869), i.e. on a different bundle. (c) `fx-event->status` maps `:rf.fx/handled` (spec/009:508 — the per-`:fx`-entry handled marker, emitted at issuance) to `:ok`, and `surface-events->phase` maps `:ok` to `:completed`; `:in-flight` is unreachable for any real record. (d) The only tests that exercise `:res`/`:failure` inject `:rf.http/handled`/`:rf.http/transport` as operations into `:other` (managed_fx_helpers_cljs_test.cljc:104-141) — fixtures for a trace shape the runtime does not produce. Shares the phantom-op mechanism with the shared classifier tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/reply_envelope.cljc:416-421 (which at least also names `:rf.http/replied`).
- Action: decide A or B. A (the feature 019 F-C2 promises): join `:rf.http/replied` / `:rf.http/retry-attempt` / `:rf.http/stale-suppressed` to the issuing record across the WHOLE buffer by `:rf.reply/work-id` (or the `:request-id` in `:rf.fx/args`), not bundle-locally; then the status pill can carry the reply's closed `:status` (`:ok`/`:error`/`:cancelled`/`:stale`) and `common-record` :459-463 must stop folding a cancel into `:error`. B (honest now, S): delete the phantom op names, render the status pill as `ISSUED` with no phase/wire/response sections until A lands. Either way delete `:rf.http/handled`/`managed-issued` from the collector and fix 019 F.3 (:644) which names `:rf.http/handled` as the per-attempt op (the real one is `:rf.http/retry-attempt`).

### 2. "app-db wasn't updated" warns on every successful record  [CONFIRMED] [severity: high] [kind: ergonomics] [size: S]
- Where: tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/managed_fx_template.cljs:428-445; managed_fx_helpers.cljc:616-628; managed_fx_subs.cljs:65
- What: the F.4 diagnostic fires unconditionally because production never supplies `paths-by-dispatch-id`, so `:paths-touched` is always `[]`, and (per #1) `:status` is always `:ok`.
- Evidence: the composite calls the 1-arity `(h/event-bundle->managed-fx-records event-bundle)` (subs:65) → `path-touched` nil → `(vec nil)` = `[]` (helpers:620-628); the template renders the amber "⚠ STATUS :ok but no app-db paths changed" whenever `(and (= status :ok) (empty? paths-touched))` (:435-442). Control: ripgrep `paths-by-dispatch-id` across tools/xray finds the 2-arity supplied exactly once, in managed_fx_helpers_cljs_test.cljc:346. This is the nagging diagnostic the stance rejects, on every HTTP/flow/SSR/machine record.
- Action: wire the per-dispatch changed-path set from the app-db-diff projection into the composite (the diff panel already computes it per focused epoch), or remove the warning branch and render "(app-db paths not tracked for this record)" until it is wired. Do not ship the warning as-is.

### 3. Resources panel redacts a sensitive resource in §2 and prints it raw in §5/§6/§6b/§6c/§6d/§8  [CONFIRMED] [severity: medium] [kind: privacy] [size: M]
- Where: tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/resources.cljs:1413-1415 (instances get `on-box-resource-egress-fn`) vs :1455-1484 (every trace-borne projection called with NO egress fn); resources_helpers.cljc:1134-1167, :1197-1212 (egress optional), :1245-1257 (`scope-resolutions` summarises raw `:input-values`/`:scope`), :1294-1299, :1554-1561, :1850 (no egress parameter at all)
- What: rf2-9zix0u closed exactly this leak for the instance rows ("values never leave the box" was rejected — screen-share exposure), but the same panel still `pr-str`s up to 120 chars of a `:sensitive?` resource's raw scope/params, the resolver's raw input VALUES and resolved scope, mutation causes and affected keys, one section down.
- Evidence: on-box trace rows carry raw scoped keys — implementation/resources/src/re_frame/resources/trace_egress.cljc:33-35 ("on-box listeners keep the raw evidence"); the resource emit sites stamp no `:sensitive?` (ripgrep `sensitive` over events.cljc/timers.cljc/mutation_events.cljc/scope_registry.cljc hits only comments and the OFF-BOX projector; the `:rf.resource/scope-resolved` emit at scope_registry.cljc:553-560 ships `:input-values` and `:scope` raw), so Xray's collector gate (config.cljc:791-803) never drops them; `summarize` (:310-346) only recognises the `:rf/redacted` sentinel. Shares the mechanism of the fresco-trace reviewer's lead (declared-sensitive values rendered raw); not re-reported there, but this slice's fix is local. Spec 024:155-174 calls layer 3 "optional", so the spec currently blesses the gap.
- Action: in the composite build `sensitive-rids` from the registry rows (`:sensitive?` at resources_helpers.cljc:441 — the coarse root prop) and pass an egress fn that redacts scope/params/cause/input-values for a key whose resource-id is in it, to `lifecycle-timeline`/`invalidation-graph` (parameter exists) and add the parameter to `scope-resolutions`, `mutation-invalidation-evidence`, `optimistic-lifecycle`, `optimistic-force-clobbers`, `optimistic-reach-lint`. Per-slot declaration parity with `local-render-value-at` is the M half; then reword 024 §PRIVACY layer 3 from "optional" to "the on-box render threads it".

### 4. The cancellation cascade crosses frames  [CONFIRMED] [severity: medium] [kind: correctness] [size: S]
- Where: tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/cancellation_cascade_helpers.cljc:319-355 (`find-anchor`), :357-415 (`gather-related-aborts`), :417-474, :476-499; cancellation_cascade_subs.cljs:66-74
- What: anchor, aborts, teardowns and the decision row are matched on `:rf.trace/dispatch-id` and a 100 ms wall-clock window with no frame predicate, and the focused-event sub drops `(:frame spine-focus)`, so on a multi-frame host frame B's aborts fold into frame A's cascade (or the popover anchors on the wrong frame's destroy).
- Evidence: ripgrep `frame` in the helpers file hits only docstrings and the `:parent-frame-destroyed` reason keyword — zero reads of `[:tags :frame]`; control: routing_helpers.cljc:407-415 reads `(:frame focus)` for exactly this reason (rf2-bz7flo, which fixed managed_fx_subs.cljs:55-59 and routing but not the cascade). The buffer is every host frame merged (trace_collector.cljs:166-211 `snapshot-from-rings`), and the grouper's own contract says dispatch ids are unique only within a frame (projection.cljc:189-194). The helper's docstring (:83) claims "single-cascade-anchor scope only"; the code does not enforce it. The by-window fallback additionally folds ANY `:rf.http/aborted-on-actor-destroy` inside 100 ms with no actor link (:398-401) — intra-frame too.
- Action: thread `(:frame focus)` into `extract-cascade` and filter each gatherer on `(= frame (get-in ev [:tags :frame]))` when a frame is known (nil → today's behaviour); tighten :398-401 to require the actor match once the frame filter lands.

### 5. CURRENT ROUTE reads a `:path` the framework never writes, and drops `:query`/`:fragment`/`:transition`  [CONFIRMED] [severity: medium] [kind: spec-drift] [size: S]
- Where: tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/routing.cljs:170-204 (`{:keys [route-id params path]}` at :175); routing_helpers.cljc:42 (docstring promise); tools/xray/test/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/routing_cljs_test.cljs:265
- What: the slice the router publishes is `{:route-id :params :query :fragment :transition :error :nav-token}` (implementation/routing/src/re_frame/routing/events.cljc:118-126; spec/012:301-311), so the "matched path / URL" 021 §7.2 promises never renders, query and fragment are never shown, and a route whose readiness is `:error` shows nothing — the test passes only because it feeds `:path "/cart"` (:265), a key production never writes.
- Evidence: read both sides; `(when path …)` at :201-204 is dead in production. On the rf2-c5cub question: the framework now keeps canonical query order past 8 keys (array-map, registry.cljc); this panel sorts nothing because it renders no query at all — `(pr-str query)` over the framework's map is order-faithful once it is rendered. Cross-slice: `simulate-navigation-preview`'s `slot-shape` `{:id :path :params}` (routing_helpers.cljc:353-364) IS the "simulate-nav slot shape differs from the framework's" lead the static-catalogue reviewer filed — same mechanism (a hand-written slice shape), not re-reported.

description:
Merged-PR audit #9889, merge 821c73b096830bceb50afb4d839a97d449420e25. The new fail-closed :rf.event/fx projection is incomplete for malformed entries whose head is not a keyword.

At implementation/epoch/src/re_frame/epoch/tool_pair.cljc:1979, redact-fx-entry preserves (first entry) whenever the entry is nonempty and sequential. Its docstring calls that head an fx-id keyword, but the code does not require keyword?. The do-fx terminal trace carries the original returned :fx even after fx-entry-ok? rejected and dropped the entry (implementation/core/src/re_frame/fx.cljc:1990-1994, 2007 onwards). Emit-time classification also leaves undeclared heads alone.

1. Make a frame, register a no-op :audit9889/ok effect and an event returning {:fx [entry]}, dispatch-sync, read last epoch-history, then rf/project-egress with default opts.
2. Valid control entry [:audit9889/ok {:password "audit9889-secret"}] yields :rf.event/fx [[:audit9889/ok :rf/redacted]]; no secret in that carrier.
3. Malformed entry [{:password "audit9889-secret"} {:arg 1}] is rejected as an effect but yields :rf.event/fx [[{:password "audit9889-secret"} :rf/redacted]] on the projected do-fx row. The secret still leaves the process through the newly protected carrier.

Redact a non-keyword-headed malformed entry as a whole; retain the existing nil no-op, valid keyword head, opt-in and idempotence behavior. Add a regression through a real malformed-effect cascade with a payload-bearing map/vector or string head, plus the valid keyword-headed control. This is a small correction to the existing redactor, not a new validation framework or API.

description:
# Senior review: http — managed HTTP requests

Reviewer persona: senior HTTP client-library engineer (axios / ky / clj-http class) — transport over fetch + JDK HttpClient, retries, aborts, content negotiation, privacy layer.
Tree: review-sep16 worktree, trunk d89a41e057
Scope read: implementation/http/src/re_frame/http/** (all 17 files, ~8.8K lines; transport.cljc, managed.cljc, decode.cljc, privacy.cljc, handlers.cljc, registry.cljc, both platform transports, encoding, reply, url, test_support in full); test/ skimmed for pins (abort precedence, backoff cancellation, reply lowering, privacy integration, managed_test JVM abort, empty-body parity); core reply.cljc `trace-summary`, core fx.cljc `emit-fx-error!`, core trace.cljc `emit-error!`, epoch tool_pair.cljc `http-body-slots`; JDK 21.0.10 `src.zip` (RedirectFilter / HttpRequestImpl / Utils).
Owning specs consulted: spec/014-HTTPRequests.md (full: §Decoding, §:auto, §Classification order, §Abort precedence, §Failure categories, §Reply payload shape / §Successful-response metadata, §Middleware §Failure mode, §Testing, §Privacy §1 / §4 / §Response-body classification rules 3-5), spec/Ownership.md row 61, EP-0011 via 014 §Reply payload.

## Findings, ranked

### 1. The `:rf.http/replied` row for a FAILURE carries the raw failure map — denylisted response headers unredacted on-box, raw 4xx/5xx/decode bodies unstamped off-box  [CONFIRMED] [severity: high] [kind: spec-drift]
- Where: implementation/http/src/re_frame/http/transport.cljc:410-447 (`emit-reply-trace!`), :515-523 (`dispatch-failure!`), :740-783 (`emit-and-dispatch-failure!`); implementation/http/src/re_frame/http/privacy.cljc:387-409; implementation/core/src/re_frame/reply.cljc:606-616, 678-685; implementation/epoch/src/re_frame/epoch/tool_pair.cljc:1699-1705
- What: every failure completion emits TWO trace rows — the category row (`:rf.http/http-4xx` etc.) built from a redacted copy, and the canonical `:rf.http/replied` row whose `:error` is the UNredacted failure map (`:headers` with `set-cookie`/`www-authenticate` verbatim, raw `:body` / `:body-text`) — and only the success branch of `emit-reply-trace!` applies header redaction / the off-box stamp.
- Evidence: `emit-and-dispatch-failure!` builds `redacted` (:747-782) and hands it ONLY to `emit-error!` (:783); `dispatch-failure!` (:518) then builds the reply from the raw `failure` and calls `emit-reply-trace!`, where `classify-decoded` is gated on `:ok` (:410-414), `redact-response-meta` touches only `[:meta :headers]` (privacy.cljc:406-409 — a failure reply has no `:meta`), and `:rf.http/off-box-body` is stamped only when `(= :ok (:status reply))` (:445-447). Downstream, `trace-summary` runs `elide-wire-value` over `:error` (core reply.cljc:678-685) and `elision.cljc` has ZERO knowledge of the HTTP header denylist (grep `denylist|set-cookie|authorization|http` → 0; control `sensitive` → 87 hits). Off-box, `http-body-slots` lists `[[:value]]` alone for `:rf.http/replied` (tool_pair.cljc:1699), so `[:tags :error :body]` on a 4xx replied row is never omitted. Spec 014 §1 (line 1235): denylisted headers MUST be redacted "in every `:rf.http/*` trace event that carries a `:headers` slot"; §Response-body classification rule 4 (line 1395): a raw error body is "unconditionally `:omit` off-box". Tests pin the SUCCESS `:meta` case only: grep `\[:tags :meta :headers` → 4 (http_privacy_integration_test.clj:851-892), grep `\[:tags :error|:error :headers` in http/test → 0. Per-call `:sensitive?` IS safe (force-redact of `:error` wholesale) — the leak is the always-on denylist and the off-box raw-body rule for ordinary requests, i.e. the common case.
- Action: decide: (A) in `emit-reply-trace!`, for `:error`/`:cancelled` replies run `:error` through `rf.http.privacy/redact-failure` (same carriers + `sensitive?` as the sibling row) and stamp `:rf.http/off-box-body` (`:omit` when `:error` carries `:body`/`:body-text`, `(off-box-body-disposition decode)` when it carries `:decoded`), then add `[:error :body] [:error :body-text] [:error :decoded]` to tool_pair's `:rf.http/replied` slot paths; or (B) trim `:error` on the replied row to identity + `:kind`/`:status`/`:reason` (the category row already carries the full redacted map) — smaller, but the row then differs from the delivered envelope. Either way add one pin on `[:tags :error :headers "set-cookie"]` for a 4xx.

### 2. JVM user/supersede/actor/frame abort cancels the derived `thenApply` future, not the `sendAsync` exchange — the wire work keeps running  [CONFIRMED] [severity: medium] [kind: correctness]
- Where: implementation/http/src/re_frame/http/transport_jvm.cljc:308-342; implementation/http/src/re_frame/http/transport.cljc:1799-1801, 2049-2083
- What: `jvm-fetch` returns `result` (= `(.thenApply future-resp …)`), the abort closure cancels `@cf-holder` which is that `result`, and `CompletableFuture.cancel` does not propagate upstream — so the JDK exchange (`future-resp`, the `sendAsync` future) downloads to completion after the app has been told the request was cancelled.
- Evidence: transport_jvm.cljc:309 binds `future-resp` to `.sendAsync`, :311 binds `result` to `.thenApply`, :342 returns `result`; transport.cljc:2082 `(reset! cf-holder cf)` stores that `result`, :1799-1801 `(.cancel cf true)` on it. The timeout path at transport_jvm.cljc:335-341 shows the author knows the distinction — it registers a `whenComplete` that cancels `future-resp` on `TimeoutException` (docstring :293-297: "timing out the result alone would leave the download running behind a request the app has already been told timed out") — but that hook is registered only when `timeout-ms` is positive and matches `TimeoutException` only, never `CancellationException`. The reply side is correct (once-only CAS), which is all `http_managed_test.clj:1032` (rf2-on7sj) pins; every `.isCancelled` assertion in test/ (`http_anonymous_frame_ownership_test.clj:78,123,195`, `http_abort_body_prep_race_test.clj:255,372`) is on the future the stubbed `jvm-fetch` RETURNED, so no test observes the exchange. transport.cljc:1649-1651 ("JVM additionally cancels the underlying CompletableFuture so the work actually stops") is wrong for the exchange.
- Action: in `jvm-fetch` register the `whenComplete` unconditionally and cancel `future-resp` on `CancellationException` as well as `TimeoutException` (hoist it out of `(when (pos? timeout-ms) …)`; three lines). A supersede-heavy debounce search on SSR/JVM otherwise keeps N connections busy per keystroke.

### 3. The completion callback is unfenced above the reply tail; one reachable instance — `classify-decoded`'s deliberate fail-loud — hangs the request silently on the JVM and re-sends it on CLJS  [CONFIRMED] [severity: medium] [kind: correctness]
- Where: implementation/http/src/re_frame/http/transport.cljc:1490 (`decoded'`), :2011, :2024-2025, :2094-2099; implementation/http/src/re_frame/http/privacy_body.cljc:180-203
- What: `handle-response!` computes `(classify-decoded decoded decode)` unconditionally on every 2xx (:1490, outside both try/catch blocks); `extract-paths` THROWS `:rf.error/schemas-artefact-missing` when the `:decode` schema declares a `:sensitive?`/`:large?` mark and the schemas walker hook is unbound (privacy_body.cljc:190-201, documented as "fail-loud", rf2-ohfym) — but at this altitude the throw lands inside the platform completion callback, where only `dispatch-reply!` (:225-247) is fenced.
- Evidence: JVM — the throw escapes the `whenComplete` BiConsumer (:2094-2099); the CF `whenComplete` returns is unobserved, so nothing is logged, no reply is dispatched, and `clear-in-flight!` never runs (the slot and its live `:abort-fn` leak). CLJS — the `.then` rejects, `.catch` (:2024) hands it to `classify-cljs-error`, an `ExceptionInfo` has `.-name` "Error" so it lands in the `:else` arm as `:rf.http/transport` (transport_cljs.cljc:454-466), and `maybe-retry!` with `:retry {:on #{:rf.http/transport}}` RE-SENDS the already-completed 2xx — the retry-storm shape rf2-ln85eg fenced for the reply tail, reached one step earlier. The only pin is unit-level (http_privacy_body_test.clj:213); grep `schemas-artefact-missing` in http/test → that file only, no transport-altitude test. Same class of hazard for any other throw in that region (a non-numeric `:max-attempts`/`:backoff` value blows up in `maybe-retry!`/`compute-backoff-ms` at the same altitude — see Considered).
- Action: (1) move the marks check to dispatch time — call `(rf.http.privacy-body/decode-schema-marks decode)` once in `normalise-args` (handlers.cljc:204-271) so the fail-loud surfaces as `:rf.error/fx-handler-exception` at the dispatch site before the wire; (2) wrap the JVM `whenComplete` body and the CLJS `.then` handler so a non-transport throw routes to the same observable non-retrying emit as the reply-tail fence (extend `emit-reply-tail-error!` or a sibling `:rf.error/http-completion-failed`) and still clears the registry via `finalise-failure!` — never to `classify-*-error` → `maybe-retry!`.

### 4. The reply-tail fence is dev-only: a throwing `:after` / bad reply target makes the reply vanish with no production-survivable signal, unlike its request-side "analogue"  [CONFIRMED] [severity: medium] [kind: spec-drift]
- Where: implementation/http/src/re_frame/http/transport.cljc:125-175 (`emit-reply-tail-error!`); implementation/core/src/re_frame/trace.cljc:900-931; implementation/core/src/re_frame/fx.cljc:964-1007
- What: `emit-reply-tail-error!` is gated on `rf.interop/debug-enabled?` (:153) and emits only via `rf.trace/emit-error!`, which is itself debug-gated (trace.cljc:915) and does not fan out to the always-on error channel — whereas the request-side `:rf.error/fx-handler-exception` it is documented as the analogue of goes through `:error-emit/emit-error-both` (fx.cljc:1005-1007, "axis 1 — production-survivable; the source of truth for off-box shippers and the SSR error projector").
- Evidence: grep `error-emit|emit-error-both` in trace.cljc → only a comment at :685, no fan-out; spec 014 §Failure mode item 3 (line 883): the throw is "surfaced once as `:rf.error/http-reply-tail-failed` (the response-side analogue of the request-side `:rf.error/fx-handler-exception`) — observably" and "the reply itself is not delivered". In a CLJS `:advanced` build the request completes, `:on-success`/`:on-failure` never fire, and nothing anywhere says why; on an SSR JVM (debug on) it reaches the dev trace but not the error-listener registry the SSR error projector reads.
- Action: route `emit-reply-tail-error!` through `(rf.late-bind/get-fn-cached :error-emit/emit-error-both)` exactly as `emit-fx-error!` does (fx.cljc:1005), keeping the privacy-composed payload as the `trace-payload` arm; drop the outer `debug-enabled?` gate (the helper handles both channels). Same fix applies to whatever fence finding 3 adds.

### 5. Default `:decode :auto` on a Content-Type-less 2xx (the 204 / empty-PUT-DELETE reply) hands back an empty `Blob` / `byte[]` as `:value`  [CONFIRMED] [severity: low] [kind: ergonomics]
- Where: implementation/http/src/re_frame/http/decode.cljc:96-106 (`sniff-decoder`), :144-151 (`binary-read-kind`); implementation/http/src/re_frame/http/transport_cljs.cljc:207-220; implementation/http/src/re_frame/http/transport_jvm.cljc:319-326
- What: with no Content-Type, `content-type-of` is nil, `json-media-type?` and the `text/` test both fail, and `:auto` resolves to `:blob` — so the most common mutation reply (`DELETE` → 204, no body, no Content-Type) under the DEFAULT decode reads the body with `.blob()` on CLJS / rides raw bytes on the JVM, and `:value` is a host-specific empty binary object rather than `nil`.
- Evidence: decode.cljc:102-106 — `(cond (json-media-type? content-type) :json (and ct (str/starts-with? ct "text/")) :text :else :blob)` with `ct` nil; CLJS `read-body` then takes the `:blob` arm (transport_cljs.cljc:210-212). The schema path already reasons the opposite way about the same header — "A nil content-type is treated as JSON-eligible — many JSON APIs omit the header" (decode.cljc:113-117) — and the §Empty/whitespace-only 2xx body contract (spec line 243) promises `nil` cross-host for `:decode :json` and schema but is silent for `:auto`. No test pins `:auto` on an absent Content-Type (grep `204|no Content-Type|absent Content-Type` in http/test → only the schema-path pin at http_empty_body_parity_cljs_test.cljc:143-155). Spec §:auto (line 271) says "otherwise → `:blob`", written for a PRESENT non-JSON/non-text type. The `:rf.http/replied` `:value` is then a `Blob` on the on-box trace (reply.cljc promises an EDN-serialisable envelope).
- Action: decide: (A) treat an ABSENT Content-Type under `:auto` as `:text` (an empty body then normalises to `nil` via the existing empty-2xx rule — one `cond` arm in `sniff-decoder` plus a sentence in §:auto), or (B) keep `:blob` and say so in §:auto and §Empty/whitespace-only 2xx body. (A) matches the schema path's reading of the same header and what the default is for.

## Considered, left alone
- JDK Authorization forwarding on cross-origin redirect (the persona's classic): JDK 21.0.10 `HttpRequestImpl.newInstanceForRedirection` applies `ALLOWED_REDIRECT_HEADERS` whenever scheme or authority differ, and `Utils.getDisallowedRedirectHeaders` is `#{Authorization Cookie Origin Referer Host}` (Utils.java:195-201); Fetch strips `Authorization` on cross-origin redirect too. Nothing for the library to do on this JDK.
- CLJS `:redirect :error` on a cross-origin URL classifies as `:rf.http/cors` (Fetch rejects with a `TypeError`, transport_cljs.cljc:448-452) while the JVM surfaces the 3xx as `:rf.http/http-4xx` — the heuristic is documented as heuristic (spec line 515) and the config is rare.
- `:retry {:on #{…}}` with no `:max-attempts` silently never retries (`(some? max-attempts)` gate, transport.cljc:1277); spec line 367 says absent ⇒ 1, and `:max-attempts` / `:backoff` values are not shape-validated at dispatch — a non-number throws at completion altitude (finding 3's fence is the right home, not a nagging validator).
- Route-map stubs key on the post-`:before` `:request :url` BEFORE `merge-params` (test_support.cljc:461-463), so two calls differing only in `:params` hit one stub; spec §Testing (line 1085) specifies exactly `:request :method` + `:request :url`, and an unmatched request fails closed as a `:rf.http/transport "no stub matched"` reply (documented in docs/core/testing/pipeline-runs.md:144).
- Transport retry replays non-idempotent requests on `:rf.http/timeout` / `:rf.http/transport` (a POST that timed out may have landed) — `:on` is opt-in and the spec's §Retry table already warns per category; the programmer's call.

## Instruments and controls
- Grep `denylist|set-cookie|authorization|http` (-i) in core/src/re_frame/elision.cljc → 0; control `sensitive` → 87 hits in the same file.
- Grep `\[:tags :error|:error :headers` in implementation/http/test → 0; control `\[:tags :meta :headers` → 4 (http_privacy_integration_test.clj).
- Grep `future-resp|\.cancel|isCancelled|sendAsync` in http/test → 5 `.isCancelled` sites, all on the stubbed `jvm-fetch` return; none on the `sendAsync` future.
- Grep `schemas-artefact-missing` in implementation/**/test → http_privacy_body_test.clj:213 (unit level) + schemas late_bind_missing_test.clj; no transport-altitude pin.
- Grep `error-emit|emit-error-both|defn emit-error!` in core/trace.cljc → `emit-error!` :900 gated at :915, no fan-out; control: fx.cljc:1005 calls `:error-emit/emit-error-both`, and late_bind/directory.cljc:813 lists the key.
- Grep `validate-carriers!` in implementation/**/src → defn + one call site (privacy.cljc:224, emit time).
- Grep `204|no Content-Type|absent Content-Type|content-type-less` (-i) in http/test → abort-precedence fixture + the schema-path absent-CT pin only.
- Grep `:rf.http/replied` in http/test → 29 hits in 2 files (http_privacy_integration_test.clj 23, http_reply_lowering_test.clj 6), every assertion on a `:status :ok` row (`:value` / `:meta` / `:completed-at` / `:off-box-body` / identity facts); none inspects a failure row's `:error`.
- Read-only extraction of JDK 21.0.10 `lib/src.zip` (RedirectFilter.java:121-143, HttpRequestImpl.java:150-190, Utils.java:195-205) into the scratchpad.
- No clj-kondo run, no test run, no edits to any tracked file.

title: False: TanStack mutation scope prevents stale-snapshot rollback clobbering
description:
PR #9842 (b6327dc983162bf95952aaa913b9a00a4fe34fb2), docs/resources/coming-from-tanstack-query.md section 4, presents mutation scope as one of two ways around stale-snapshot rollback clobbering newer cache data. That implication is false: scope serializes the mutation function/network request, but onMutate runs immediately even for a paused same-scope mutation.

Independent headless reproduction with the exact referenced @tanstack/query-core 5.102.8:
1. Cache starts at 1. Mutation A (scope id same-article) captures 1 and optimistically writes 2, then waits on its request.
2. Mutation B, same scope, isPaused true and has not issued its request, but its onMutate already captures 2 and writes 3.
3. A succeeds and its onSettled refetch establishes authoritative cache value 7. Only then does B issue its request.
4. B fails. Its documented onError context restore writes its old snapshot 2 over 7 until B own onSettled refetch restores 7.

Thus serial network mutations still admit the cache rollback window the paragraph says this mechanism avoids. The variables-only UI pattern is correctly described and can stay. Credit mutation.scope for serializing mutation functions, explicitly distinguish the eager onMutate/cache work, and remove the implication that scope alone solves stale-context rollback. Documentation correction only, no framework API or runtime change.

Evidence: gate-9842-audit-sep15-b-1.log/.exit in C:/Users/miket/code/re-frame2-worktrees/audit-sep15-b (exit 0), with assertions for paused/not-issued B, captured snapshot 2, settled value 7, rollback value 2 and final refetch value 7. Probe: C:/Users/miket/.codex/tmp/audit-sep15-b/9842-scope-probe.cjs. Installed upstream src/mutation.ts calls onMutate before retryer.start (lines 225/238). Primary reference https://tanstack.com/query/latest/docs/framework/react/guides/mutations . No exact open Bead records this defect.
acceptance_criteria: The migration comparison credits scope for serial network execution while explicitly noting onMutate runs for paused mutations and stale snapshot rollback can still overwrite newer data. Keep the variables pattern credited. Use the reproduced same-scope sequence as the factual check; no runtime change is required.

No browser; no collision with the live workers (rf2-omahf holds spec 016 and implementation/resources; the Story workers hold tools/story and docs/story).

Order: re-verify the upstream fact at @tanstack/query-core 5.102.8 (onMutate before retryer.start) by a route that writes nothing into the repo, STOP if it does not hold; edit only §4's scope claim (credit scope for serializing mutation functions, distinguish eager onMutate/cache work, drop the "scope alone prevents stale rollback" implication; the variables-only UI pattern stays); planted-anchor control on check_doc_slugs; mkdocs strict.

PREMISE VERIFIED AT SOURCE, @tanstack/query-core 5.102.8 (published npm tarball, unpacked outside the repository):
- src/mutation.ts: isPaused = !retryer.canStart() at :209; await this.options.onMutate at :225; retryer.start() at :238.
- The scope gate is MutationCache.canRun (src/mutationCache.ts :160-175). It is reached only through retryer.canStart / retryer.start (src/retryer.ts :115, :227-235). So onMutate runs before scope can hold anything back.
- Headless re-run of the audit's sequence against that same build, exit 0: B paused with its request not issued, snapshot 2, cache 3; A settles and refetches 7; B fails, its onError restores 2 over 7; B's own onSettled refetch returns 7.

EDIT (the one sentence the bead names). Before: "TanStack does offer two ways around that ... and scope: { id } on useMutation runs mutations sharing that id in serial, so the second stays paused and issues nothing until the first settles."
After: "TanStack does offer one way around that" (the variables pattern, unchanged), then scope is credited for running the mutation functions sharing that id in serial. The new sentence adds that the second mutation's onMutate still runs straight away, its snapshot captures the first one's optimistic value, and if it fails its onError writes that stale snapshot over the newer refetched value all the same. This satisfies the acceptance criteria: scope is credited for serial execution, onMutate is noted to run for paused mutations, stale rollback can still overwrite newer data, and the variables pattern stays credited.

NOT DONE, and outside this fence: the preceding sentence's own measurement (two unscoped overlapping mutations, snapshot 1 over 7) was left as it is. It is a different scenario from the scoped one and it is correct.

title: story: J1 authoring frictions - dialog output needs alias rewrites, the real-setup scaffold drops a decorator, sidebar and Tests pane stay stale after hot reload
description:
DEFECTS measured in rf2-a1v8a Journey 1 (tools/story/spec/findings/parity-2026-09/fable/advantage-measured-2026-09-14.md §2: the "Lost inputs", "Translations" and "Wrong turns" rows, and "What cost"). They were not filed until now. The mayor checked the tracker on 2026-09-15: 0 beads carry the decorator or stale-sidebar findings, and the alias hits were unrelated.

1. DIALOG OUTPUT DOES NOT COMPILE AS PASTED. Each of Story's three transformation dialogs ("save as new variant", "Real setup events", "add expectations…") emitted a form whose aliases had to be rewritten, story/ to rf.story/, before it compiled. That happened once per dialog. A dialog's output must paste and run as it is.

2. THE REAL-SETUP SCAFFOLD DROPS A DECORATOR. The upgrade scaffold extends the nearest unpinned ancestor, which lacked the fx-stub decorator the real events needed, so the decorator was copied by hand. Related: "save as new variant" emits args only and says sub-overrides are "not yet projectable", so the pin was retyped. Check whether that is a spec'd limit before treating it as a defect.

3. STALE CHROME AFTER A HOT RELOAD. After a hot reload the sidebar did not list the new variant and the Tests pane stayed stale. Four page reloads were forced.

J1's stop rule says to add no more transformation UI until these dialogs emit forms that paste and run as they are. This bead is that repair, not new UI.

ACCEPTANCE: re-walk J1's Story side in the browser and confirm:
- each dialog's output compiles when pasted verbatim;
- the upgraded variant carries the decorators its setup needs;
- a hot reload lists a new variant and its tests with no page reload.
Each item gets a regression test.

title: Incomplete: Test-mode promotion recompiles checkpoints without the run's inputs
description:
PR #9819 (merge 2284727767b1e17cefed8e9d79a5063747c5adfc) completes capture for the unparameterized setup/checkpoint shapes, but closed rf2-vgthk remains incomplete for the same shapes run with Test-mode controls or active modes.

The new result->artifact fallback calls promotion/source-program with only :variant/id. That reaches source-steps -> play/variant-play-steps without the options of the completed run. Test-mode state/run-opts explicitly supplies :cell-overrides and :active-modes; store-result! passes them to variant-play-events, but result->artifact/source-program discards them. Recompiling a script with [:arg] therefore either fails and hides the promotion row, or captures a different checkpoint from the one that failed.

Independent JVM reproduction at the exact merge (audit-merged-pr-audit-a-pr9819-inputs-1.clj/.log/.exit, exit 0):
- A :setup boot event writes {:n 1}; the script contains only [:assert [:rf.assert/path-equals [:n] [:arg :expected]]]. Run with {:cell-overrides {:expected 2}} produces [:fail 1] and no dispatch-only play-events.
- With no default :expected, that valid completed run captures nil because the fallback cannot compile without its input.
- With variant :args {:expected 1}, the source still fails against expected 2, but the artifact contains an assertion against 1. Default dialog promotion then runs [:pass 1] against the unchanged faulty app. This is a changed requirement, not a fixed defect.
- Positive control: capture play/variant-play-steps with the actual run opts. The promoted variant then produces [[:fail 1] [:pass 1] [:fail 1]] as the boot handler is faulted, fixed, and faulted again.

Retain the completed run's executed program/input context through capture and promotion, using the existing run result/opts seams, so a later compile cannot substitute defaults or lose mode/cell-only inputs. Add a focused regression for both required-input and default-overridden checkpoint-only shapes and check the Test pane still offers the row. Preserve ordinary inheritance and the single capture flow.

The independently rerun existing focused suite passes 35 tests/139 assertions. rf2-fvmhw is an API documentation recipe defect, and rf2-6h2z3 concerns composed checks; neither records this runtime fallback defect or correction.
acceptance_criteria: For a checkpoint-only source run using cell overrides or active-mode inputs, Test-mode capture is available and preserves the executed checkpoint values. Cover an input with no default and an overridden default. Default dialog promotion of the failing run must remain failing against the unchanged app and pass/fail when the app is fixed/refaulted, retaining its assertion count. Existing nil/non-artifact refusal and setup-once tests continue to pass.

title: story-mcp: project supported callable values before success JSON encoding
description:
Project supported callable values into an honest, JSON-safe success representation before building either result slot. A documented predicate assertion runs successfully in Story but currently makes get-variant, variant->edn, explain-variant and run-variant all return JSON-RPC -32603. This independently actionable issue splits finding 2 of rf2-fzbj.31; preserve its remediation fence until Mike rules who owns remediation.

Ownership/revision: tools_story_mcp; baseline 9e8ca973767f4ecff455421e48e1765d59783261, revalidated at 4df6a3303c68c77ced1f84ce92178bed1d7f7879. Owned source unchanged from baseline. SOURCE_ROOT=C:/Users/miket/code/re-frame2; WORKTREE_ROOT=(none; read-only review).

Source: tools/story-mcp/src/re_frame/story_mcp/tools/result.cljc:173-187 puts raw success data in structuredContent and pr-str output in text. Its wire-safe-value/wire-safe-ex-data policy at :50-156 only protects exception data. tools/docs.cljc:119-124, :389-409 return registered bodies/plans directly; tools/testing.cljc:124-182 returns run evidence through the same builder. protocol.cljc:312-319 invokes the real JSON encoder, and server.cljc:283-291 replaces an encoding failure with -32603. tools/story/spec/001-Authoring.md:516 supports [:assert-db path :pred fn-or-sym]; current Story assertion/schema sources accept and execute the callable.

Fresh real-source fixture:

```clojure
(story/reg-variant :story.review-mcp/predicate
  {:db-seed {:count 1}
   :script [[:assert-db [:count] :pred pos?]]})
(:status @(story/run-variant :story.review-mcp/predicate))
;; => :pass
```

With a plain-atom adapter installed, send initialize and tools/call for each of the four tools through actual server/run-loop! over JSON streams, using the fixture id, dedup false and max-tokens 0. Each response is a -32603 error whose message begins 'Server fault: Cannot JSON encode object of class: class clojure.core$pos_QMARK_' and includes the live object's identity. Changing only the assertion to [:assert-db [:count] 1] makes all four tools succeed; its run reports pass. No handlers, registrar, runner or encoder were stubbed.

Expected: supported authoring remains inspectable and a completed passing run returns its actual verdict and useful surrounding evidence. A closure cannot losslessly round-trip through JSON or EDN printing, but that limitation should be explicit in its value representation, not discard the entire result as a server fault. Disabling dedup and removing the cap do not help. This is independent of shared codec issues rf2-gwye.30-.32 and the conformance decoders.

Repair: introduce one success-value projection before both text/structured construction and before dedup/cap. Preserve plain data and replace an opaque callable with a stable, explicit non-reconstructible marker or supported descriptor. Reuse/extract shape-only encodability policy where suitable, but do not apply wire-safe-ex-data wholesale: its :explain and :rf.error/id semantics belong to exceptions and must not reinterpret literal application keys. Align round-trip prose with callable limitations; do not remove supported predicates or invent source-based callable reconstruction.

Acceptance: exact predicate fixture stays pass in direct Story and returns valid encoded MCP results for all four tools; useful body/plan/evidence and status survive with an explicit callable representation. Exercise both default and disabled dedup, ordinary-data controls and exception encodability regressions. No raw #object identities escape. Literal author keys :explain and :rf.error/id retain their meaning.

Validation: probe-tools_story_mcp-3.clj ran current absolute sources with cached Clojure 1.12.4/JVM dependencies, exit 0 confirming all four failures plus all four data controls. Evidence is ai/surface-review-20260913/tools_story_mcp/probe-tools_story_mcp-3.log/.exit. Process called shutdown-agents and exited. No installs, source changes, shared builds, live server, browser/CLJS, published-artifact dependency proof or broad suite. This is an executable characterization, not a green correctness gate.

Deduplication: current all-status Story-MCP/callable/predicate titles and descriptions yielded the aggregate, no dedicated issue. Read rf2-fzbj.31 and bounded newest-first history. Prior error-data encoding repairs remain present and are not being reopened. Preserve earlier statuses, notes and fence; this review dispatches no fixer.
notes:
FIXED in PR #9759 (branch worker/storymcp-a, commit 7d76bf9c81 post-rebase). Re-verified at tip before fixing: all four tools still answered -32603 on the cited fixture. The ownership hold is lifted by Mike's 2026-09-13 ruling on the parents (rf2-fzbj / rf2-gwye).

Fix. One success-value projection, result/wire-safe-success, applied once inside edn-result — the chokepoint every data-returning handler already shares — so it runs before BOTH wire slots are built and before the wire-boundary transforms (dedup, then the token cap) that follow the handler. A value outside the EDN value space is replaced IN PLACE by the bounded {:rf.story-mcp/unencodable "<class name>"} marker this server already uses; everything around it survives.

Two properties are deliberate, and both were asked for:
- It is NOT wire-safe-ex-data. That projection RENAMES :explain and :rf.error/id, which is right for a caught exception's ex-data and wrong for author data, where those are ordinary keys somebody wrote. A test pins that a variant whose :args carry literal :explain and :rf.error/id keys reads back unchanged.
- It is TYPE-PRESERVING (clojure.walk/postwalk), where wire-safe-value rebuilds every collection through {} / #{} / mapv. That matters because the text slot is the byte-stable EDN an agent DIFFS: a reshaping walk would quietly turn a list into a vector, a sorted map into a hash map and a record into a plain map. A payload carrying no callable comes back equal to what went in.

Regression tests (wire_encodability_test.clj), driven through the real run-loop! boundary and reading the RAW encoded line, with dedup at its default AND disabled: the exact predicate fixture stays :pass through direct Story; get-variant, variant->edn, explain-variant and run-variant each return a success envelope naming the callable by class; no #object form and no identity hash appears in either slot; the surrounding body, plan, args and run evidence survive; the text slot still reads back as EDN carrying the same marker. The equality-only control ([:assert-db [:count] 1]) is retained and asserts that plain data is never marked, and the existing exception-ex-data encodability tests are untouched and still pass.

Evidence. Pre-fix these tests contributed 30 failing assertions (JVM suite: 301 tests / 1709 assertions, exit 1); post-fix 0 failures at the same totals, exit 0, re-run on the final rebased base. Baseline before any test was added: 296 / 1630.

Prose aligned with the actual representation, as the finding asks: the round-trip claim in tools/story-mcp/spec/API.md, spec/002-Tool-Registry.md and the pr-edn docstring now says a callable is NAMED rather than reconstructible, instead of implying a closure round-trips.

Recorded and NOT built: the finding's alternative "supported callable descriptor". The existing marker already says a value was there and what kind it was; a second vocabulary for one fact is what this repo's error-envelope rule warns against. Source-based callable reconstruction was explicitly not required and was not attempted.

Nothing in tools/story was changed: tools/story/spec/001-Authoring.md:516 is cited only as evidence that :pred fn-or-sym is supported authoring, which it is.
Merged-PR audit #9759: new open finding rf2-8m1i records an INCOMPLETE success-projection claim: postwalk retains a callable record extension key and emits its #object identity. Required correction and actual get-variant wire evidence are in rf2-8m1i. Existing closure remains unchanged. This pointer is not evidence of mayor notification or acknowledgment.

title: Activate derived ratom containers when direct listeners attach
description:
Activate ratom-derived containers when their direct listener attaches, using the existing per-substrate activation operation. Keep activation demand-driven and preserve native Reagent batching. This is one shared repair affecting the stock Reagent and reagent-slim adapters, with primary ownership in implementation/core/src/re_frame/substrate/spine.cljs and injected operations supplied by the two adapter namespaces.

Remediation fence: [FENCE: until Mike rules who remediates rf2-fzbj]. This independent finding is split from rf2-fzbj.29 F1 (also cross-referenced by rf2-fzbj.30); this review authorizes recording evidence, not dispatching implementation. Preserve the prior reports and their statuses.

Scope/revision
- Source baseline: 9e8ca973767f4ecff455421e48e1765d59783261. Revalidated 2026-09-13 against HEAD 4df6a3303c68c77ced1f84ce92178bed1d7f7879; the owned adapter paths and relevant helper/spec paths have no difference from baseline.
- Primary source: implementation/core/src/re_frame/substrate/spine.cljs:510-518, 4049-4055, 4303-4304. make-subscribe-container only installs an outward watch, and make-ratom-spine exposes it alongside lazy native Reactions.
- Stock wiring: implementation/adapters/reagent/src/re_frame/adapter/reagent.cljs:54-70, 89-110, 234-238. Guarded construction provides disposal bookkeeping; source activation exists separately in :activate-reaction!.
- Consumer boundary: implementation/core/src/re_frame/substrate/adapter.cljc:692-704 delegates subscribe-container with no activation. Slim shares the ratom spine; coordinate its injected operation and regression assertion within this same issue rather than adding a second subscription algorithm.
- Contract: spec/006-ReactiveSubstrate.md:189 and 199-201: direct subscribe-container works on derived containers as on base containers; watchability alone is insufficient, and observer attachment must activate a demand-driven node.

Trigger and observed behavior
Outside any component or ratom capture context, create source s=1 and derived d=10*s via the adapter container slots. Read d (10), attach subscribe-container to d, replace s with 2, and run reagent.core/flush.
Expected: one [10 20] notification. Actual: no notification; compute count stays 1 and d.watching stays nil. add-watch alone never supplies the stock Reaction's deref-capture, so the observer can remain stale forever until an unrelated consumer activates the node.
Control: run that same Reaction with ratom/run; changing s to 3 and flushing then emits [20 30]. Canceling the observer clears watching, and a later source change emits nothing. This distinguishes missing activation from a faulty source, listener or scheduler.

Suggested repair
Feed a total, idempotent per-substrate activation operation into the ratom direct-observer path and call it at attachment before establishing the listener baseline. Factor the current stock activation lambda so the direct listener and routed ViewCell hook share the same operation. Keep reagent namespaces out of the shared spine. The shared helper also serves eager/plain containers, so either inject an appropriate no-op there or wrap only the ratom attachment path. Do not eagerly activate at construction or enable :auto-run true: that would discard batching and unnecessarily compute unobserved subscriptions.

Acceptance
- Focused tests exercise the actual current adapter :make-state-container, :make-derived-value, :subscribe-container and :replace-container! slots with no component, track!, manual activation or ratom context. Test both reading and not reading the derived container before attachment; mutation plus ordinary flush must notify.
- Two observers share an already-active node without an extra activation recompute. Removing one leaves the other live. Final cancellation releases source watches; cancellation is idempotent. Base containers remain usable.
- Multi-input derived updates retain native batching. A mutation that bypasses attachment activation makes the direct-listener assertion fail.
- Run focused stock and slim lanes for the shared fix. The prior mounted-view/diamond tests already supply capture and cannot prove this direct-listener contract by themselves.

Validation performed and limits
- Fresh run: node C:/Users/miket/code/re-frame2/ai/surface-review-20260913/adapter_reagent/probe-adapter_reagent-1.cjs. Own log and exit file share that stem; captured exit 0 means its assertions reproduced the defect and controls, not that an adapter conformance suite passed.
- Probe loads only the existing compiled stock Reagent dependency prefix, then expresses current guarded construction and make-subscribe-container faithfully in process-local JS. It does not load a stale compiled application adapter. Independently compared sourcesContent from the loaded ratom, batching and core source maps with the locally pinned reagent-2.0.1.jar; all match byte-for-byte. Ratom SHA-256 b390644704d742223b7c58c6f5f627f5210d694b263c2be95cc75d87ffe0b1b7. Dependency receipt: ai/surface-review-20260913/adapter_reagent/dependency-evidence-adapter_reagent-2.json.
- Current producer, consumer and activation-hook source was inspected; no fresh CLJS build, browser, advanced build, install or broad gate ran. This is a pinned-host mechanism witness plus current wiring inspection; an end-to-end adapter regression remains an acceptance requirement. Process completed with no persistent resources.

The old aggregate contains both this and a separate async documentation defect, so it is not an independently dispatchable substitute. No dedicated open identical repair found. Closed rf2-rzeko retains its exactly-once disposal disposition and is a distinct, already-fixed problem; this issue does not reopen it.

notes:
FIXED in PR #9768 (draft opened, branch worker/reagent-a).

Re-verified at tip before fixing: the finding reproduced exactly as written. A fresh derived container observed through the adapter's subscribe-container slot, with no component and no manual activation, received ZERO notifications on a source write plus flush. Confirmed at source in reagent 2.0.1: Reaction's -deref outside *ratom-context* with nil auto-run runs the body RAW rather than through deref-capture, so watching stays nil; _queued-run then requires (some? watching) and flush! moves nothing.

WHAT LANDED. A new shared helper, re-frame.substrate.spine/activating-subscribe-container, wraps make-subscribe-container with the substrate's own :activate-reaction! op, and make-ratom-adapter uses it for the adapter map's :subscribe-container. The wrap sits at the ADAPTER layer, not in make-ratom-spine, and that placement is the point: make-ratom-adapter is where the injected activation op already arrives, so stock Reagent AND reagent-slim get one shared repair with no second subscription algorithm and with no edit in either adapter namespace. Activation runs BEFORE the watch is installed, per Spec 006 section "Activation happens when an observer attaches, never at construction".
