title: mcp-conformance: preserve own __proto__ keys during dedup expansion
description:
Preserve every decoded JSON key as an own enumerable data property, including `__proto__`. The Node conformance decoder currently loses valid application data and changes reconstructed object prototypes whenever a dedup wrapper contains that key.

Ownership and review identity

- Surface: tools_mcp_conformance; parent rf2-gwye; source root C:/Users/miket/code/re-frame2.
- Baseline 9e8ca973767f4ecff455421e48e1765d59783261; reviewed head 4df6a3303c68c77ced1f84ce92178bed1d7f7879. Owned paths are unchanged from baseline.
- Repair site: tools/mcp-conformance/lib/dedup-envelope.cjs:145-168, especially `const out = {}` and `out[jsKey] = expandValue(v[k])`.
- Consumer: tools/mcp-conformance/test/_runner.cjs:504-505. Regression home: test/dedup-envelope.test.cjs.
- WORKTREE_ROOT=(none; read-only review). No production edits, installs or builds.

Trigger and reproduced behavior

An ordinary application map contains root and nested string keys named `__proto__`; an unrelated repeated subtree makes the real encoder create a dedup wrapper. Fresh probe 1 calls re-frame.mcp-base.dedup/dedup-value with enabled=true on:

    {"__proto__" {"marker" "root-payload"}
     "nested" {"__proto__" {"marker" "nested-payload"}}
     "a" {"items" ["repeat" "the" "subtree"]}
     "b" {"items" ["repeat" "the" "subtree"]}}

The probe asserts the real wrapper exists and the Clojure expand roundtrip is exact, then serializes original and encoded maps with Cheshire and feeds that actual JSON to the Node decoder. JSON.parse preserves both keys as own properties. decodeDedupEnvelope drops both: its JSON result is `{"nested":{},"a":{"items":["repeat","the","subtree"]},"b":{"items":["repeat","the","subtree"]}}`. `got.marker` reads inherited `root-payload`, and `got.nested.marker` reads inherited `nested-payload`. Object.hasOwn is false for both original keys. Repeated a/b still share identity.

Expected: the decoded JSON projection equals the original JSON projection, preserving all ordinary keys. The canonical contract is tools/mcp-base/spec/dedup.md's JSON-projection identity guarantee; `__proto__` is not a reserved codec token. Actual: assignment invokes Object.prototype.__proto__'s inherited setter instead of defining a data property.

Impact: semantic conformance assertions operate on a corrupted version of a conforming server response; inherited payload values can also satisfy property reads. This is local reconstructed-object corruption, not a claim of global prototype pollution or a production-server exploit.

Suggested repair and acceptance

Define own enumerable data properties when rebuilding each decoded object, using Object.defineProperty or another setter-free construction while retaining the intended plain-object shape. Do not prohibit programmer data keys. Add Node fixtures transcribed from the real encoder/Cheshire output for root and nested keys; assert deep JSON-projection equality, own-key presence, normal Object.prototype, and no inherited marker. Retain repeated-subtree sharing, escaped-token, missing-reference and cycle controls. Restoring plain assignment must fail the regression.

Validation and limits

Executed `node C:/Users/miket/code/re-frame2/ai/surface-review-20260913/tools_mcp_conformance/probe-tools_mcp_conformance-1.cjs`, exit 0. Its bounded Babashka child uses the current production codec and Cheshire; the rest imports current Node helpers. The exit means the characterization observed the defect and controls, not that conformance passed. Evidence: probe-tools_mcp_conformance-1.log and .exit in that directory. No full suite or live server was run.

Known references and disposition

Fresh revalidation and independent split of rf2-fzbj.14 F1. Current tracker title/description searches found no dedicated matching issue. Read rf2-fzbj.14 and rf2-fzbj newest-first histories (limit 3), plus closed rf2-kjv05's notes/close reason. rf2-kjv05 fixed token spelling collisions; this is object reconstruction after that grammar works. Preserve its decision to use pure Node boundary fixtures rather than introduce a runtime dependency between published mcp-base and conformance.

REMEDIATION FENCE: rf2-fzbj's recorded hold remains in force until Mike rules who owns remediation. This bead records a review finding and does not dispatch a fixer or change prior statuses.

title: schemas: reset ambient printer limits before memoizing digest input
description:
Make the default schema serialization independent of ambient printer limits by binding *print-length* and *print-level* to nil inside compute-edn-print, around canonicalization and final printing. This restores deterministic schema fingerprints and prevents truncated strings from poisoning the process-wide memo. No digest algorithm, memo-key, public API, or custom-printer change is needed.

Ownership: impl_schemas, implementation/schemas/src/re_frame/schemas/validator.cljc, cache.cljc and digest.cljc, plus the existing digest/printer tests. Review baseline 9e8ca973767f4ecff455421e48e1765d59783261; reviewed HEAD 555cd5b8c30327ac815e306ed6c4619e71881b17. Owned source is unchanged between them. SOURCE_ROOT=C:/Users/miket/code/re-frame2; WORKTREE_ROOT=(none; read-only review).

Confirmed behavior and ordinary trigger

A REPL/tool context binds print limits for readable output and computes a schema digest before that schema has entered the memo. With an isolated schemas registry/cache:

    (schemas/reg-app-schema [] {:frame :digest/a} [:map [:a :int]])
    (schemas/reg-app-schema [] {:frame :digest/b} [:map [:a :string]])
    (binding [*print-length* 1]
      [(schemas/app-schemas-digest {:frame :digest/a})
       (schemas/app-schemas-digest {:frame :digest/b})])
    ;; => ["sha256:9d2ec1c0e952d6c3" "sha256:9d2ec1c0e952d6c3"]

Both distinct forms serialize as "[:map ...]". After the binding ends, another ordinary digest call returns those same incorrect equal fingerprints because the truncated serialization is cached under each full schema value. Cache clearing in a test is only how first-computation behavior is isolated; a fresh application already starts with an empty cache.

Unbounded printing of these exact registrations produces the existing distinct fingerprints:

    :digest/a => "sha256:e4bffe29a0226cac"
    :digest/b => "sha256:6fdca79b912a7ef0"

A separate fresh-cache *print-level* 1 binding also collapses them, to "sha256:8ed08014be185777", and rereading outside that binding preserves the collision. Binding both limits reproduces the print-length collision. All three were freshly executed, including subsequent cached rereads outside the bindings.

Expected: the same schema form always supplies the same complete canonical bytes irrespective of surrounding display settings. Different ordinary :int and :string forms retain their different existing fingerprints. Actual: whichever context first prints the schema controls future process-wide digest input, so identical schema sets may disagree across sessions and changed schemas may appear identical.

Cause and impact

validator.cljc:103-111 binds *print-meta*, *print-readably*, *print-dup* and *print-namespace-maps*, but inherits *print-length* and *print-level*. These affect both the canonicalizer's pr-str-based key comparator and the final pr-str. At :115 the result is memoized. cache.cljc:38-45 keys the memo by schema arguments alone; digest.cljc:94-98 hashes the cached string. Spec 010's normative digest step 1 at spec/010-Schemas.md:501 requires stable bytes, and its memoization premise at :516 relies on that purity.

This corrupts the public drift fingerprint. SSR hydration consumes the same digest hook (implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/hydrate.cljc:491-505, 531-554), but this review did not execute end-to-end hydration and does not claim a separately measured hydration failure. The defect is already independently observable through the public schemas API.

Suggested repair and acceptance criteria

Bind *print-length* nil and *print-level* nil within compute-edn-print's existing binding, enclosing canonicalise-schema-form as well as final pr-str. Keep the cache API, custom schema-print companion contract, path canonicalization and hashing unchanged.

- With fresh caches, compute default printer bytes and public digests under bounded *print-length*, bounded *print-level*, and both; each must equal the unbounded baseline.
- Reread outside each binding without clearing the cache and prove the stored bytes/digests remain the baseline.
- Preserve distinct :int/:string digests above and all existing pinned cross-host digest fixtures; include nested maps/sets so comparator canonicalization also happens under the reset printer context.
- Isolate the schema registry and memo in tests, using the shared reset fixture or an equivalent precise fixture; execute CLJ and CLJS coverage during remediation.

Validation and limits

Fresh process-local JVM witness: ai/surface-review-20260913/impl_schemas/probe-impl_schemas-1.clj with .log/.exit; exit 0, source resource URL verified against this checkout. The witness intentionally asserts the current collision and retained cached result, so its successful exit confirms the defect. Its unbounded control distinguishes normal hashing from polluted serializer inputs. The same process ran six focused existing namespaces: schemas-storage-test, schemas-reg-side-effects-test, schemas-presence-test, schemas-walker-literal-operand-test, schemas-walker-opaque-warning-test and schemas.digest-parity-test. Result: 95 tests / 456 assertions, zero failures/errors. No CLJS compilation, shared build, full spine, production gate or SSR integration run. No source changes.

Provenance and duplicate check

Revalidated and split finding 2 from aggregate rf2-fzbj.25. Read its current body/notes and newest three history entries; did not alter its existing remediation fence or status. Current all-status description searches for print-length, print-level and variable-width plus the open issue index found no dedicated owner beyond that two-finding aggregate. This issue does not revisit cache eviction, accepted humanizer bundle cost, or the separate nil-token declaration decisions. Parent rf2-gwye authorizes this fresh individual review finding record; implementation is outside this review.

title: fresco test kit: reject hydrate setup failures through its promise
description:
Make mounted hydrate! turn initial-events setup failures into rejected promises. Enclose complete synchronous construction in the helper's existing rejection boundary, preserve the core exception object, and retain cleanup for resources actually allocated. No new validation, error category or retry mechanism is needed.

Surface: impl_fresco, specifically implementation/fresco/test_kit/**. Revalidated at 9e8ca973767f4ecff455421e48e1765d59783261 on 2026-09-13. SOURCE_ROOT=C:/Users/miket/code/re-frame2. WORKTREE_ROOT=(none; read-only review).

Confirmed path and contract

- implementation/fresco/test_kit/src/re_frame/fresco/test/mounted.cljs:899-912 explicitly promises every failure is a rejection and explains why synchronous throws bypass .catch and hang asynchronous tests.
- Its mint-frame! at :631-647 invokes rf/make-frame with initial-events. Core's strict setup behavior throws if a valid setup event's handler fails, after tearing down its own failed frame.
- hydrate! at :915-923 calls mint-frame! in the outer let at :916, before the first try (which catches only hydrate-root!) and before the Promise construction at :929.
- Supporting producer outside this slice: implementation/core/src/re_frame/frame.cljc:2875-2899 invokes raise-setup-step-failed! for an escaping or captured setup-event error. The handler failure path carries :rf.error/initial-events-step-failed.

Concrete trigger

After normal adapter initialization, with rf=re-frame.core and hm=re-frame.fresco.test.mounted:

(rf/reg-event ::hydrate-seed-boom
  (fn [_ _] (throw (js/Error. "seed failed"))))
(-> (hm/hydrate! [:div "ready"]
                 {:initial-events [[::hydrate-seed-boom]]})
    (.catch (fn [e]
              (assert (= :rf.error/initial-events-step-failed
                         (:rf.error/id (ex-data e)))))))

The registered event and initial-events vector are valid. The setup handler fails during frame construction, as real application setup may. hydrate! throws before returning, so the .catch is never attached. A normal asynchronous test that chains its completion continuation after this call can time out, hiding the actual setup failure.

Expected versus actual

Expected: the call returns a Promise and rejects with the same canonical setup refusal supplied by core, allowing the caller's rejection and completion handlers to execute.
Actual: mint-frame! escapes on the caller's stack, contrary to the helper's documented all-failures rejection channel. Core already rolls back the frame on this specific path; this issue does not allege a leaked frame or virtual clock from the setup exception.

Suggested repair

Move all synchronous hydration construction, including mint-frame!, behind one rejection boundary. One outer try returning Promise.reject, or a Promise executor enclosing that construction, is sufficient. Preserve exception identity and cleanup only resources that were successfully allocated. Keep successful hydration's adoption-window completion and the existing codec-refusal/adoption-timeout cleanup behavior unchanged.

Acceptance criteria

1. Register a setup handler that throws and drive the public hm/hydrate! with it. Assert no synchronous throw, a returned Promise, one rejection with :rf.error/initial-events-step-failed, and execution of the completion continuation.
2. Verify no extra frame, facade-owned container or standing mount remains; a clocked peer remains unchanged if included. Do not require a redundant second rollback of the frame core already destroyed.
3. Retain codec-refusal and adoption-timeout rejection/cleanup witnesses plus successful hydration.

Validation and limits

Fresh source trace from helper to core's producer; no compiled CLJS or browser execution. The existing implementation/fresco/test/re_frame/fresco/test_kit_clock_dom_cljs_test.cljs:81-86 registers the same meaningful throwing setup-handler shape; :367-387 asserts core's canonical refusal for mount!. The mounted suite's existing hydration failure rows at test_kit_mounted_dom_cljs_test.cljs:651 and :717 cover codec refusal and timeout, which occur after the setup hole. Those tests were inspected, not run. The repair should establish the new red public-helper regression before a green repair run. No source edits, shared compilation, dependency installs or servers were performed.

Deduplication and references

Revalidated and split finding 2 from prior aggregate rf2-fzbj.4. title: surface-review(examples-substrates): complete Fresco SSR host startup and asset serving
description:
Recommendation: complete the Fresco login's documented standalone JVM boot and client-asset serving path. Two confirmed P2 defects remain in the SSR example/recipe. Install the SSR adapter explicitly at application startup and supply concrete static-asset routing that matches the emitted client bundle. Keep the reusable page-rendering constructor small; these repairs do not require changing the SSR library, adding a server framework, or restoring per-example browser suites. Keep this report OPEN until both corrections are verified.

Scope and revision

Owned slice: examples_substrates, all 21 tracked paths:
- examples/substrates/README.md
- examples/substrates/fresco/login/README.md
- examples/substrates/fresco/login/core.cljs
- examples/substrates/fresco/login/host.clj
- examples/substrates/fresco/login/index.html

- examples/substrates/fresco/login/server.cljs

- examples/substrates/uix/dashboard/index.html
- examples/substrates/uix/login/README.md
- examples/substrates/uix/login/core.cljs
- examples/substrates/uix/login/index.html

Reviewed source baseline: 1c9ff9697b0fa3a018c7a4371e02983ad2e79b2f. Latest observed HEAD: e88f4e80fb0788325d59e6f5b7cdb39f748a4380. A final `git diff --exit-code <baseline> HEAD -- examples/substrates implementation` returned 0 with no differences: intervening checkpoints did not change these sources. SOURCE_ROOT=C:/Users/miket/code/re-frame2. WORKTREE_ROOT=(none; read-only review). No production edits, commits, builds, installs, or long-lived servers were made by this reviewer; root owns tracker checkpoint/push.

Coverage

Read every owned source, README and host page. Checked counter registrations and explicit frame scoping; UIx hook ordering, captured dispatch, controlled login fields, busy/locked branches, stable roots and reload behavior; slim adapter selection, client-root use, CI-only SSR fixture isolation and finally/with-new-frame cleanup; dashboard base/derived subscription input shapes, tag/range transformations, sparkline arithmetic and roving radio controls; Fresco intent/callback payload shapes, sensitive-password map, client-only ENSURE versus SSR SCOPE boot, retained reload boundary, matching identifier prefix, shared render-state policy and server entry table, undefined return convention, and fresh render-body frame ownership. Followed current adapter/core/SSR source and existing centralized witnesses where those contracts determine the example's behavior.

Inspected build IDs, entrypoints/output paths and host assets in implementation/shadow-cljs.edn, the UIx consumer dependency recipe and adapter deps, the slim bundle-isolation contract, and the current login model. Build metadata and model/runtime defects are not independently owned by this slice. No confirmed distinct counter, dashboard, or client-only login dataflow defect remains from this review. Explicit page-lifetime roots and durable frames are appropriate here; absence of a generic shutdown framework is not a finding.

Finding 1 — P2: the documented Fresco JVM host never installs an adapter

Owned sources: examples/substrates/fresco/login/host.clj:45-52,74-112 and examples/substrates/fresco/login/README.md:231-254, especially the instruction at 251-254 to serve host/handler from any Ring adapter and open the page.

Trigger/reproducer: in a fresh JVM with the example's declared source/dependency classpath, require fresco.login.host and hand its handler (or its equivalent make-handler result) to a Ring adapter. Follow the README's server/client compilation and sidecar setup. Neither that host nor the recipe calls `(rf/init! ssr/adapter)`. Requiring re-frame.ssr merely publishes its adapter; it does not install it, as implementation/core/src/re_frame/substrate/adapter.cljc explicitly specifies.

Expected: the first page request can create its request frame and invoke the configured Node renderer, yielding a rendered login document.

Actual: frame setup has no installed state-container adapter. implementation/ssr-ring/src/re_frame/ssr/ring/pipeline.clj:313-335 calls rf/make-frame; setup failure is projected to HTTP 500 `Internal error` before the renderer is called. The example's Node boot and browser boot both initialize their own processes, but neither can initialize the JVM process.

Confirmed current-source witness: fresh JVM, no repository test/reset fixture; replace only node/renderer with a synchronous renderer returning a tiny synthetic form. Before any explicit init, adapter/current-adapter is nil, GET / returns status 500, and render-call count remains 0. Call `(rf/init! ssr/adapter)` in the same process and invoke the SAME constructed handler: it returns status 200 and render-call count becomes 1. No socket or sidecar is needed to demonstrate this failure: it occurs before the renderer boundary.

Why existing coverage missed it: implementation/ssr-ring/test/re_frame/ssr/ring/login_host_crossing_test.clj:75-90,184-185 installs its reset-runtime fixture before request tests. That fixture supplies the SSR adapter (test_support.clj:85-96) that the advertised application startup omits. Requiring host successfully is a namespace-load witness, not a standalone boot witness.

Impact: following the native Fresco SSR example produces an error page even with a healthy, matching sidecar. The central teaching route does not reach server rendering.

Repair: add explicit JVM startup wiring, either a small host boot entry or a concrete README startup snippet requiring re-frame.core/re-frame.ssr and invoking rf/init! with ssr/adapter before serving requests. Keep initialization at the application lifecycle boundary; do not silently initialize the library's generic ssr-handler or reinstall the global adapter on every request/constructor call. Make the instruction to serve host/handler point at the complete boot.

Acceptance: exercise the documented host boot in a fresh process with no reset fixture installing an adapter for it. A first GET / reaches a controlled renderer and returns 200 with the login shell/payload; omitting the documented init must reproduce the 500 negative control. Retain the existing request-frame cleanup and separate Node/browser adapter installation.

Finding 2 — P2: the advertised SSR launch serves HTML at the client bootstrap URL

Owned sources: examples/substrates/fresco/login/host.clj:88-112, especially :script-src "/js/main.js" at 108 and the claim at 111 to hand handler to any Ring adapter; examples/substrates/fresco/login/README.md:233-254.

Trigger/reproducer: initialize the JVM adapter to pass finding 1, then serve the exported host/handler as instructed. GET / includes `<script src="/js/main.js">`. A browser then requests that URL from the same Ring host. The example's handler contains only ssr-handler; there is no static route/middleware, nor does the README instruct the reader to supply one.

Expected: that request serves the compiled Fresco client JavaScript, with its emitted dependency/asset URLs also reachable, so core/run installs the payload and hydrates the server markup.

Actual: ssr-handler renders a document for every request it receives. GET /js/main.js therefore returns HTTP 200 with `content-type: text/html; charset=utf-8` and another complete login HTML document. The compiled browser build actually emits `implementation/out/examples/login-fresco/main.js`, with :asset-path "." (implementation/shadow-cljs.edn:1709-1713); compiling that file creates no URL mapping on the Ring host. A Ring server adapter alone provides none. The script cannot execute and the SSR page remains inert. This is application wiring, not a defect in the general ssr-handler, whose own docs explicitly put static-asset middleware in front (ring.clj:342-370).

Confirmed witness: after the finding-1 positive control returned a 200 page, the SAME current-source handler received GET /js/main.js. It returned 200 text/html, contained the synthetic login form, and invoked the page renderer a second time. The witness asserts the page's script src and the asset request's HTML content/type. It does not claim a browser load or real compiled-client execution.

Impact: even after the JVM boot is repaired, the documented server/client build and serve sequence never produces an interactive hydrated login page. It also makes asset fetches perform extra SSR work.

Repair: show a concrete, minimal Ring composition or deployment mapping that serves this build's client output and forwards only page requests to host/handler. Align :script-src with that mapping; account for the dependency URLs generated by the documented development `compile` build and its :asset-path, not only a release main.js. It is sufficient to supply the missing application setup in the example README/host entry; no new general-purpose server framework is needed.

Acceptance: from the documented output, request the emitted script URL through the composed application and receive JavaScript rather than an SSR document; serve its generated runtime dependencies at the URLs it requests; verify an unknown asset does not become an HTML login document. A focused manual/browser check should then confirm the SSR page hydrates and its sign-in interactions work. Keep regression coverage centrally owned (extend the existing host witness or startup/asset contract); do not add per-example spec.cjs files.

Known history, overlaps and discarded candidates

- rf2-8arzr.5 is CLOSED. Read its current description/notes/close reason and latest three history entries. The previous merged audit fixed the commented-out model require, made model.cljc JVM-loadable, added the shared policy namespace and make-handler, and added the host crossing witness. Those repairs are present and are not refiled. The two findings here occur outside the initialized request fixture and outside the existing shell-only client-script assertions.
- rf2-fmns2 is CLOSED: the literal shared login model, native Fresco third arm and adapter-only bundle sentinel repair are present. This review does not reopen the earlier model/bundle comparison defects.
- rf2-kjx1 is CLOSED: the slim SSR fixture is isolated in its own non-runnable build; the runnable core no longer imports it. rf2-5x1xt is CLOSED: all three UIx consumer recipes explicitly name both com.pitch/uix.core and com.pitch/uix.dom at 1.4.4. These are fixed history, not new findings.
- rf2-fzbj.26-.30 already cover adapter reviews. In particular .29 owns missing shared ratom-spine derived-container observation activation; .30 owns slim sequence-output coercion and MetaFn callback conversion. This report does not count those shared runtime causes as fresh example defects. The slim counter uses Hiccup vectors and ordinary callbacks. UIx's imperative-resolution README correction is owned by .28; these example views use the recommended use-frame hook.
- rf2-fzbj.4 owns Fresco first-root failure cleanup and the test-kit hydrate setup-error channel. These are distinct from the host application's missing startup/asset composition.
- Render-visible but payload-excluded server notice mismatch is explicitly demonstrated and documented; host.clj ships no notice, and the React hydration mismatch is an intentional negative witness. Do not refile it as a shipped-page defect. The self-seeding machine's empty runtime partition on the default JVM host is likewise accurately explained.
- No quota-driven finding for intentionally absent per-example tests, generic multi-root/foreign-host reuse, invalid dashboard ranges unavailable through the UI, cosmetic wording, or every incidental source-comment drift. No unverified risk is promoted to an actionable finding.

Validation and limits

1. `ai/surface-review-20260912/review-examples-substrates-re-frame2-probe-3.clj`, same-stem .log/.exit: JVM exit 0, verified SOURCE_ROOT, both source-confirmed SSR defects plus explicit-init positive control. No test namespaces or fixture were required. The only test double is node/renderer; host, model registrations, frame setup, payload and shell are current production source. The synthetic renderer is intentionally insufficient to claim actual Node rendering or browser hydration.

These setup failures are not product findings.

Attempt 1 exited 1 on the probe's overly strict string-format assertion (JVM renders floating coordinates with .0); attempt 2 accepts equivalent numeric spelling.
4. All evidence paths are uniquely named and verified gitignored. Both successful probes ended, the JVM explicitly disposed its adapter and shut down agents, and no service was started or left running.
5. No broad gate, new CLJS compile, release/package build, fresh isolated consumer dependency resolution, real sidecar launch, browser/StrictMode/HMR run, visual layout, accessibility audit or repository-wide link validation was executed. Existing centralized tests/build entries were inspected only. Findings and coverage claims are bounded accordingly.

description:
Repair the conformance decoder and the source-reader boundary before relying on them as compatibility evidence. This review confirms three bounded P2 defects: valid JSON data is lost during dedup expansion, malformed dedup wrappers are silently normalized into acceptable results, and the JVM trace-key linter discards the ClojureScript branches it is intended to inspect. Keep this task OPEN until those repairs and discriminating regressions land. These are defects in the review/test surface; this report does not claim a production server currently emits the malformed wrapper or duplicate trace keys.

Review identity and scope

- Slice: tools_mcp_conformance. Parent: rf2-fzbj.
- Revision: 1c9ff9697b0fa3a018c7a4371e02983ad2e79b2f, checked again at completion.
- SOURCE_ROOT=C:/Users/miket/code/re-frame2.
- WORKTREE_ROOT=(none; read-only review).
- Owned scope is the 66 tracked paths listed at the end of this description, all under tools/mcp-conformance/. Neighboring mcp-base dedup implementation/spec and Story's Cheshire wire serialization were followed only to verify the owned decoder's contract.

Coverage and exclusions

Inspected the Node inventory and unit/live runner selection; SDK connection/watchdog and auxiliary-client ownership; descriptor classification and call-coverage ratchets; isError/ok? correlation; dedup, overflow, token and executable/path safety helpers; the hermetic runner's readiness, child-close grading, skip/sentinel checks, bounded cleanup and Windows process-identity ownership; the degraded Pair, Story and project-story workflows and fixture execution witness; and selected live overflow, redaction, coeffect, event-metadata, turn-observation and replace-app-db assertions. Inspected vocabulary fixture/source inventory helpers, wrapper schemas and their positive/negative/live-builder checks, and focused result, reply, event-bundle, operating-frame, egress-profile, verb and trace-catalogue checks. Some tests were sampled and the remaining assigned paths were inventoried; this is not a claim to have executed every file.

Existing good boundaries matter: live rows derive from one roster; the hermetic runner waits for child close and requires its success sentinel; classification and call coverage compare against authoritative catalogues; project-stories now requires a nonempty execution-only assertion witness; overflow validates both result slots and a closed wrapper. No broad suite was run merely to obtain green. No server, browser, build, dependency install or production edit was performed. The source slice and mcp-base had no git changes after these probes.

F1 — P2: dedup expansion silently loses the legal JSON key __proto__

Owned source: tools/mcp-conformance/lib/dedup-envelope.cjs:145-168 (plain-object allocation and out[jsKey] assignment). Consumer: tools/mcp-conformance/test/_runner.cjs:504-505. Existing unit coverage: tools/mcp-conformance/test/dedup-envelope.test.cjs.

Trigger/reproducer: an application payload contains an ordinary string map key "__proto__" and another repeated subtree makes dedup wrap the result. The process-local reproduction invoked the actual re-frame.mcp-base.dedup/dedup-value with enabled=true on:

  {"__proto__" {"marker" "payload"}
   "a" {"items" ["repeat" "the" "subtree"]}
   "b" {"items" ["repeat" "the" "subtree"]}}

It asserted a real :rf.mcp/dedup-table wrapper was created and that Clojure expand round-tripped the original, then used Cheshire to serialize both original and encoded values. The Node decoder consumed that actual serialized wire. JSON.parse preserved an own __proto__ key; decodeDedupEnvelope returned only a and b, with marker="payload" inherited through the decoded object's prototype. The actual round-trip comparison failed. Its a/b shared-subtree control still reconstructed correctly and retained identity.

Expected: decode(encode(JSON projection)) preserves all ordinary payload keys and values. The canonical dedup contract explicitly promises JSON-projection identity; __proto__ is not a reserved codec token. Actual: assignment invokes the inherited Object.prototype.__proto__ setter instead of creating the data property. The key disappears from Object.keys/JSON.stringify; object-valued data also changes the reconstructed object's prototype. A process-local hand-authored root with the same key showed the identical loss.

Impact: the conformance harness reasons about a different payload from the one emitted by a conforming server. This can produce wrong semantic assertions, and inherited values can satisfy consumers' `in`/property reads. This is a decoder correctness issue, not a claim of global prototype pollution or a production-server exploit.

Repair: build own enumerable data properties without invoking inherited setters, while preserving the helper's intended plain-object shape; Object.defineProperty for decoded keys is one small solution. Apply it to every recursively rebuilt object. Do not ban or drop programmer data keys.

Acceptance: a real encoder -> Cheshire -> Node boundary fixture with a root and nested own __proto__ key compares deeply equal to the JSON projection of the original; keys remain own properties and no payload value becomes a prototype. Retain normal repeated-subtree sharing, escaped-reference spelling, missing-reference and cycle rejection controls. A regression to out[jsKey] assignment must fail the new test.

F2 — P2: closed dedup wrappers accept siblings and erase them before semantic grading

Owned source: tools/mcp-conformance/lib/dedup-envelope.cjs:228-245. Downstream check: tools/mcp-conformance/test/_runner.cjs:504-530. Contract: tools/mcp-conformance/wire-vocab/test/re_frame/mcp_conformance/wire_vocab/schemas.clj:158-178; explicit rejection fixture at wire_vocab_test.clj:316-346.

Trigger/reproducer, using the actual shared Node helpers:

  const resp = {isError: false, structuredContent: {
    'rf.mcp/dedup-table': {'de-dupe.cache/cache-0': {'ok?': true, value: 42}},
    'ok?': false, reason: 'failure'
  }};
  structured(resp); // returns only {'ok?': true, value: 42}
  assertIsErrorMatchesOk('probe', resp); // returns successfully

Expected: a wrapper with any own sibling key is rejected as the malformed closed envelope it is. There is no precedence rule that permits either the inner or outer ok? to win. Actual: decodeDedupEnvelope checks that the marker exists and the table is an object, but never checks the wrapper's key set; returning expandCache erases all sibling fields. The semantic relation then accepts the sanitized shape. As a negative control, the same bare ok? false/isError false mismatch throws in assertIsErrorMatchesOk.

Impact: the Node path can grade a server response green that the canonical JVM wrapper schema explicitly rejects. A regression that adds metadata, status or another discriminator beside the marker is hidden rather than surfaced. The existing JVM fixture rejects its synthetic sibling, but does not feed each live Node response through that schema; it does not close this decoder gap.

Repair: before expansion, require the own-key set of a recognized dedup wrapper to be exactly ['rf.mcp/dedup-table'], with a diagnostic naming any siblings. Mirror the already established closed-overflow-wrapper approach. Keep normal unwrapped payloads untouched and permit ordinary additive fields inside the decoded root.

Acceptance: unit tests reject both harmless-looking and conflicting siblings, including the reproduction above through structured/assertIsErrorMatchesOk. Valid single-key wrappers and unwrapped ordinary payloads still pass; arbitrary root payload fields survive. A mutation removing the own-key check must fail these tests.

F3 — P2: trace-catalogue source parsing discards ClojureScript conditional branches

Owned source: tools/mcp-conformance/wire-vocab/test/re_frame/mcp_conformance/trace_catalogue_lint_test.clj:60-72 (read-all-forms) and :81-91 (duplicate-hits traversal); the current sanity check at :120-152 supplies already-read unconditional forms and therefore bypasses this boundary.

Trigger/reproducer: use ns-resolve to call the actual private read-all-forms and duplicate-hits from a fresh Clojure 1.12.0 JVM, with cached dependencies and no test runner/build. Input:

  #?(:clj {:rf.reply/work-id work-id}
     :cljs {:rf.reply/work-id work-id :work/id work-id})

Expected: the duplicate in the CLJS branch is reported, because the gate says it reads the production .cljc emitters as data and covers their reply fact vocabulary. Actual: opts is {:eof eof :read-cond :allow}, so the JVM reader chooses the CLJ arm before duplicate-hits can walk anything. The reproduction returned only [{:rf.reply/work-id work-id}], with zero hits. A standalone #?(:cljs {...duplicate...}) yielded no forms at all, and a #?@ CLJS-splicing example also produced zero hits. The same duplicate without a reader conditional produced one hit; a valid conditional produced zero. Babashka and the pinned Clojure 1.12.0 JVM independently agreed.

Impact: a platform-specific trace emission can gain either prohibited duplicate key without failing this cross-platform linter. Its comment claims :allow preserves reader conditionals as data, but that behavior belongs to :preserve. This is a confirmed coverage defect; the review does not assert that an owned emitter currently carries a duplicate in such a branch.

Repair: preserve reader conditionals and explicitly descend into their forms, or use another reader strategy that demonstrably visits every relevant platform arm and reader-conditional splice. Changing :allow to :preserve alone is insufficient unless the walker actually traverses ReaderConditional values. Test the composed read-all-forms -> duplicate-hits path, not only an already-read literal.

Acceptance: unconditional, CLJ-only, CLJS-only, nested #? and #?@ branches report the same prohibited pairs; valid alternatives, lone :work/id and nested carried/current identity maps remain accepted. The three concrete hidden-branch examples above become red under the detector, with no production file mutation required.

Known history and duplication check

Read current closed records for rf2-kjv05 (the earlier encoder namespace/reference collision fix), rf2-kzbf (Windows shadow descendant ownership), rf2-3n3dk (project-story nonvacuous execution witness), rf2-a9l6e (the command/profile entry point), and rf2-2qa7 (actual cold Windows watchdog evidence). These repairs are present and are not re-filed here. F1 concerns the JS object-key reconstruction, not rf2-kjv05's escaped reference grammar; F2 is the Node wrapper validation gap despite the JVM sibling rejection; F3 is the source reader, not the old duplicate-name cleanup. Relevant title/description searches did not identify an existing bead carrying these three defects. Source references rf2-6i2yi4, but bd show no longer resolves that legacy id; its implemented map-key/dangling-reference safeguards were inspected directly instead of treating old prose as current work.

Validation evidence and limits

Ignored artifacts under ai/surface-review-20260912 are uniquely named probe-tools_mcp_conformance-<attempt>.log with matching .exit files. Attempt 1 reproduced the decoder behaviors and valid/missing-reference controls (exit 0). Attempt 2 was an invalid Babashka stdin invocation and exited 1 before loading code; it supplies no semantic evidence. Attempt 3 ran the actual CLJC encoder plus Cheshire under Babashka and asserted the Clojure roundtrip and nonvacuous wrap (exit 0). Attempt 4 consumed that serialized result with the real Node decoder, demonstrated the failed roundtrip, and exercised the actual structured/isError helper plus its rejection control (exit 0). Attempt 5 exercised the reader defect under Babashka (exit 0); attempt 6 repeated and expanded it on Clojure 1.12.0, including standalone and spliced CLJS forms (exit 0). These zero exits mean the characterization probes observed the stated defects and controls, not that the conformance suite passed. No full JVM vocabulary suite, live MCP/browser workflow, or cleanup integration suite was executed in this read-only review. Runtime/platform behavior beyond those explicitly executed seams remains inspected evidence only.

notes:
VERDICT (mcpconf-a worker, 2026-09-13): FIXED in PR #9755, surface tools/mcp-conformance only. One finding set, five beads: rf2-fzbj.14 carries F1-F3, and rf2-gwye.36/.38/.40 are its per-finding splits. rf2-gwye.41 is the review's new finding on the same surface.

Every finding was re-verified before fixing, at tip e428126d87 (after #9752 merged), by re-running the review's own probes. All four reproduced. No tools/mcp-base change was needed: tools/mcp-base/spec/dedup.md already promises that encode-then-decode is the identity on the JSON projection.

- rf2-gwye.36, rf2-fzbj.14 F1 (own __proto__ keys). lib/dedup-envelope.cjs now creates each decoded key with Object.defineProperty instead of assigning it. An own "__proto__" key therefore survives expansion at the root and nested levels, and never becomes the rebuilt object's prototype. The regression is in test/dedup-envelope.test.cjs. Its fixture is transcribed from a real dedup-value plus Cheshire encode, re-run after #9752 merged; the wire is byte-identical.
- rf2-gwye.38, F2 (closed dedup wrapper). decodeDedupEnvelope rejects a rf.mcp/dedup-table wrapper carrying any sibling key before expansion can erase it, and names the siblings. This mirrors unwrapClosedOverflow and the JVM DedupTable schema. Regressions: dedup-envelope.test.cjs covers a harmless sibling and a conflicting one; is-error-matches-ok.test.cjs runs the review's reproduction through structured and assertIsErrorMatchesOk. Still accepted: the single-key wrapper, arbitrary root payload fields, and unwrapped payloads.
- rf2-gwye.40, F3 (every reader-conditional arm). trace_catalogue_lint_test.clj reads with :read-cond :preserve, and duplicate-hits replaces each preserved conditional with the vector of all its arms before walking. The new test every-reader-conditional-arm-is-inspected drives source text through read-all-forms and then duplicate-hits. These cases all report: unconditional, CLJ-only, CLJS-only, a CLJS arm beside a valid CLJ arm, a CLJS splice, and a nested conditional. Valid alternatives, a lone :work/id, and carried/current maps stay accepted. All 10 production emitters still read and pass. RECORDED RESIDUAL: preserve mode cannot read a splicing conditional placed directly inside a map literal. Such a file now fails the lint loudly at read time rather than being skipped. None of the 10 emitters has one; their splices all sit in let binding vectors and ns requires.
- rf2-gwye.41 (integer overflow fields). In overflow-marker.cjs, REQUIRED_FIELDS now uses Number.isInteger for cap-tokens and token-count, matching Malli :int. The two JVM source pins in wire_vocab_test.clj move with them. The schema is unchanged. The live path already emits integers: token-estimate is quot of the count by 4.

RED THEN GREEN. Against the pre-fix code, 4 of 47 Node tests failed, exactly the four new ones, and the JVM suite had 4 failures, the four hidden-arm cases. After the fix: Node 47 of 47, and JVM 92 tests, 1038 assertions, 0 failures. A planted mutation keeping :preserve but dropping the arm traversal produced 5 JVM failures. The restore was verified against the committed blob hash.

GATES, as captured exit codes:
- npm run test:unit: 0 (153 tests, 144 pass, 9 skipped, 0 fail).
- wire-vocab clojure -M:test: 0.
- npm run test:story, then test:flag-gates: 0.
- scripts/test-fast-pr.sh: 0, and its printed root was this worktree.
The pair-mcp end-to-end row and the hermetic live suite rely on CI, in the mcp-conformance-re-frame2-pair job.

SKIPPED SUGGESTIONS: none. Every F-finding is fixed and none was found already fixed. F1's instruction not to ban programmer keys was honoured.

title: surface-review(xray): capture current focus before pausing LIVE
description:
Recommendation: make the LIVE-to-paused transition capture the currently composed focus (dispatch id, frame and epoch id) before setting the pause flag. This focused review confirmed one P2 correctness defect. Keep this bead open for that repair; the rest of the inspected boundaries do not justify additional remediation from the evidence gathered here.

REVIEW IDENTITY AND SCOPE

Owned slice: tools/xray/**, reviewed at 1c9ff9697b0fa3a018c7a4371e02983ad2e79b2f (HEAD checked before and after inspection).
SOURCE_ROOT=C:/Users/miket/code/re-frame2
WORKTREE_ROOT=(none; read-only review)
Parent: rf2-fzbj. No production edits, builds, server startup, dependency installs, commits, checkout/rebase, or pushes were performed. The root reviewer owns the durable tracker checkpoint and push.

Coverage was deliberately concentrated on inspector capture/query/state/lifecycle integration:
- tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/{core.cljs,install.cljs,trace_collector.cljs,epoch.cljs,registry.cljs,mount.cljs,spine.cljs,focus.cljc,self_noise.cljc,config.cljc}: public/manual install versus preload, lazy seating/first-open seeding, coalesced trace and epoch delivery, per-frame trace harvesting, privacy suppression/scrub, target/history alignment, focus composition and transitions, inline/overlay/popout lifetime.
- tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/{egress.cljs,panels/local_render.cljc,panels/image_view_reads.cljs,panels/app_db_diff_subs.cljs}: inspected-frame selection, own-image seating, explicit frame/path egress, live versus epoch before/after values, and read dependency wiring.
- Sampled tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/{settings/effects.cljs,panels/resources.cljs,panels/resources_helpers.cljc,panels/reply_envelope.cljc,panels/routing.cljs}; followed keyboard and shell call sites in keybinding.cljs and shell.cljs. This was integration/read-contract inspection, not an exhaustive review of every renderer or every projection helper.
- tools/xray/{README.md,deps.edn,spec/API.md,spec/017-Test-Coverage-Matrix.md,spec/018-Event-Spine.md,spec/024-Resources-Panel.md}; testbed inventory and tools/xray/testbeds/feature_matrix/{README.md,scenarios.cjs}. The centralized browser scenarios and shared framework testbeds are valid coverage evidence. Their location outside individual example directories is not a defect.
- Read relevant coverage in tools/xray/test/day8/re_frame2_xray/{spine_cljs_test.cljs,epoch_pump_coalescing_cljs_test.cljs,scrub_retention_cljs_test.cljs,sensitive_trace_loop_cljs_test.cljs}, and located existing focus/frame-isolation, manual epoch, panel, and browser acceptance suites. These suites were inspected, not run.

Exclusions: exhaustive EDN tree/diff rendering, every static/dynamic panel projection, machines-viz internals, full Fresco substrate semantics, browser visual/accessibility QA, real popout-window execution, release/cold dependency resolution, and full performance/async-load behavior. No broad gate was run merely to obtain a green result.

CONFIRMED FINDING F1 - P2: Pausing LIVE does not pin the event being inspected

Primary source:
- tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/spine.cljs:747-757, toggle-live-pause-reducer, especially line 757: it only updates [:focus :paused?] with not.
- tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/spine.cljs:1147-1149, the registered event directly calls that reducer without resolving or storing current focus.
- tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/spine.cljs:396-530, compose-focus: LIVE derives the displayed head from event-bundles, while paused mode uses the stored pin; a nil pin takes the snap-to-head branch and a stale pin takes the old event.
- tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/spine.cljs:734-745, follow-head-reducer deliberately clears both stored :dispatch-id and :epoch-id, so the nil-pin path is a normal user action, not a malformed state.
- tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/keybinding.cljs:296 maps Space directly to :rf.xray/toggle-live-pause.

Contract/evidence:
The spine is the shared focus axis for Dynamic panels. spine.cljs:798ff is not relevant to the promise; the direct existing test spine_cljs_test.cljs:910-931 says: paused LIVE freezes auto-follow because the user paused to inspect, so arrivals must not pull focus away. compose-focus's own contract at spine.cljs:389-395 says LIVE-paused honors the stored epoch and is the explicit freeze-inspection gesture. Spec 018's Spine events table (line 1121) retains collecting while LIVE is paused; the pause must preserve the current inspection, not select a different historical event or lose its epoch.

Trigger / user reproducer:
1. Open Xray normally (or press L / Follow head) and let at least two host events settle. Do not click a historical row or step backward and forward first.
2. Press Space while focus is on the newest event, e.g. dispatch 2 / epoch 102.
3. Dispatch a third host event while Xray remains paused.
Expected: the buffer may grow to include event 3, but inspection remains pinned to dispatch 2 / epoch 102 until resume or an explicit new selection.
Actual: the fresh/follow-head slot has no stored dispatch id. Pause keeps the displayed dispatch at 2 initially but drops its composed epoch id to nil; after the new event, the displayed dispatch advances to 3 while :paused? is still true. Epoch-keyed panels can lose their selected record/diff and fall back to current data.

Second normal trigger, same root cause:
1. Click the current head event 1 (stores a LIVE pin), then let event 2 arrive; LIVE correctly displays event 2 even though the stored slot still carries 1.
2. Press Space.
Expected: freeze event 2 / its epoch.
Actual: focus jumps backward to stored event 1 / its old epoch at the instant of pause.

Nonmutating executable confirmation:
Babashka evaluated the original defn forms read directly from the absolute spine.cljs path, plus the original common_helpers.cljc dependency. No rewritten implementation or JavaScript port was used. Loaded functions were focusable-event-bundles, head-event-bundle, head-dispatch-id, event-bundle-by-id, epoch-id-for-event-bundle, compose-focus, toggle-live-pause-reducer and follow-head-reducer. Synthetic data only; no framework runtime was started.

The core probe, after loading those exact forms:

(def before [{:dispatch-id 1 :frame :app} {:dispatch-id 2 :frame :app}])
(def after (conj before {:dispatch-id 3 :frame :app}))
(def epochs [{:dispatch-id 1 :epoch-id 101}
             {:dispatch-id 2 :epoch-id 102}
             {:dispatch-id 3 :epoch-id 103}])
(def fresh {:focus {:frame :app}})
(def fresh-paused (toggle-live-pause-reducer fresh))
(compose-focus (:focus fresh) before false epochs)
; => dispatch 2, epoch 102, paused false
(compose-focus (:focus fresh-paused) before false epochs)
; => dispatch 2, epoch nil, paused true
(compose-focus (:focus fresh-paused) after false epochs)
; => dispatch 3, epoch nil, paused true
(def stale {:focus {:frame :app :dispatch-id 1 :epoch-id 101 :mode :live}})
(compose-focus (:focus stale) before false epochs)
; => dispatch 2, epoch 102, paused false
(compose-focus (:focus (toggle-live-pause-reducer stale)) before false epochs)
; => dispatch 1, epoch 101, paused true

Successful probe exit: 0, asserting both actual counterexamples. This exit means the defect was reproduced, not that Xray passes a gate. Two preceding harness attempts did not execute the probe (bb does not accept '-' as the script path here; then a scratch variable collided with clojure.repl/source). The successful attempt corrected those harness issues only and loaded unchanged source.

Why current tests miss this:
- spine_cljs_test.cljs:701-708, toggle-live-pause-event-flips-paused, follows the fresh path but asserts only :paused? and :mode.
- spine_cljs_test.cljs:910-931, focus-sub-paused-live-does-not-auto-follow, first dispatches prev and next to populate a pin equal to the current head, then pauses immediately. That setup prevents both the absent-pin and stale-pin defects from appearing.
- The pure paused-composer tests likewise start with a deliberately populated stored pin. They correctly establish what composition does given a pin, but do not establish that the pause gesture captures one.

Precise repair recommendation:
Resolve the current composed focus using the same frame-scoped event-bundle/epoch sources as :rf.xray/focus when entering paused LIVE. Store its dispatch id, epoch id and resolved frame atomically with :paused? true. Preserve resume behavior (LIVE follows the current head again) and the existing RETRO no-op. Keep capture in the transition/event path rather than making a query mutate state. Do not add a second panel selection model or stop capture of host events.

Acceptance criteria:
- Registered-event/sub regression: fresh mount/target plus two settled events, pause without a preliminary row click/step, append another event, assert both dispatch and epoch stay on the pre-pause head and the buffer still grows.
- The same test after follow-head, which clears the stored pin, must pass.
- Regression for a stored LIVE pin that lags a newer displayed head: pausing must retain the displayed newer dispatch/epoch without a backward jump.
- Resume must follow the newest event/epoch; RETRO Space must remain a no-op; frame ownership must remain on the observed frame.
- At least one browser keyboard witness using the real Space route should assert the focused row AND an epoch-keyed panel value/diff across a new host dispatch. Reuse the existing centralized testbed/feature or DOM harness; no new app-shaped testbed is needed.
- Existing spine and relevant panel-focus tests must continue to pass. The repair should include a failing-before/passing-after witness of F1, not only assertions on the boolean pause flag.

KNOWN ITEMS AND DISPOSITIONS

- rf2-chs7 is the closed epoch-pump overflow repair. The current install.cljs coalescer matches that remedy and has a dedicated queue-depth test. This review does not reopen it.
- rf2-6a4p was explicitly closed without code after measuring the custom-own-frame trace self-noise case, including the hardcoded tool-frame set in snapshot-from-rings. Its existing revisit trigger is shared with rf2-bgol. Those literals are not fresh findings and are not refiled here.
- rf2-bgol's default-plus-current-own-frame Fresco filter landed; its documented two-shell boundary remains a deliberate scope decision.
- rf2-l1jm already owns whether element-shaped host panel embedding should be supported. rf2-lect already owns bridge removal behind its unmet precondition. Neither is duplicated or widened by this review.
- deps.edn explicitly records the not-yet-publishable Fresco dependency and the release prerequisite owned by rf2-hic-008; the packaging precondition is acknowledged, not invented as a new defect.
- The source comments for LIVE auto-follow cite rf2-s0s5x and rf2-70tkv; bd show returned no current record for those two identities. They are historical source references, not independently verified tracker dispositions here. A current title/description search found no existing pause-remediation bead.

VALIDATION LIMITS / VERDICT

One confirmed P2 defect, zero P0/P1 findings, no additional unverified risk promoted to remediation. The proof is source-executed pure behavior plus inspected production keyboard/event/sub wiring. It is not a compiled CLJS or browser execution, and no complete suite is claimed green. Read-only source review left tracked files unchanged. This is the single review bead for tools/xray/** under rf2-fzbj; keep OPEN until F1's implementation and regression witnesses land.

title: xray: reg-view heads block the Fresco migration of trace/managed-fx; resizable-table needs a boundary
description:
MEASURED IN THE rf2-twil WORKTREE (base c6e008813d). rf2-twil folded in its two hazards and
found, on the way, that the migration it was folding into is blocked in both files by a class
the rf2-twil bead explicitly rated safe. This bead is that class.

=== THE CLAIM THAT DOES NOT HOLD ===

rf2-twil's description says, of `managed_fx_template.cljs`:

    "NOT EVERY HEAD IN THAT FILE IS AFFECTED, and the distinction is the useful half:
     `ei/edn-inspector` and `rt/resizable-table` are proper `reg-view` heads and are FINE."

A `reg-view` head is NOT fine in a Fresco body. `views/edn_inspector.cljs`'s own ns docstring
says so in terms:

    "Only `edn-inspector-view` is a head in a Fresco body."

And the mechanism agrees. `codec/boundary-head?` is one own-property read --
`(true? (unchecked-get f "frescoBoundary"))` -- and only `rf.fresco/defview` sets that slot.
`rf/reg-view` expands to `(def <sym> (re-frame.core/view <id>))`, i.e. the INSTALLED
SUBSTRATE's component head, which under a Reagent adapter is a plain fn. `head-kind` therefore
grades it `:invalid`, and `vec->element` raises `:rf.error/fresco-bad-head` down the SAME arm
that raises for a plain `defn` -- the message even branches on `(fn? head)` and takes the
plain-function wording.

So the two blocking classes are ONE class wearing two spellings, and the useful half of the
distinction is not the half the bead named. What IS true and useful: `inspect` was a
head-position outlier against six call-form callers, and fixing that is a one-file change
worth making on its own. That landed under rf2-twil.

=== WHAT IS ACTUALLY BLOCKING, PER FILE ===

`panels/managed_fx_template.cljs` -- pure hiccup folder, no view of its own. After rf2-twil
its ONLY non-native heads are the four vectors `edn/inspect` RETURNS, `[ei/edn-inspector v
opts]`. The fix is mechanical and the replacement already exists: `edn/inspect-view` (same
node-key, same opts, emits the `edn-inspector-view` boundary) has ZERO callers today and was
written for exactly this. It cannot be adopted before the mount migrates, because a Fresco
boundary in a Reagent head position is the mirror failure.

Its mount is `panels/ManagedFxList`, an `rf/reg-view` in `panels.cljs:430`. Migrating it is
NOT one file: `panel_enum.cljc:105` rosters it, `panel_enum_guard_cljs_test.cljs:76` asserts
in prose that it IS a reg-view, `panels_mount_cljs_test.cljs:190` pins the frame-provider
wrap, and two spec pages carry it (`tools/xray/spec/007-UX-IA.md:1895`,
`016-Auxiliary-Panels.md:45`). `panels.cljs` was held by a live worker
(`origin/worker/mountid-a`) while rf2-twil ran, which is why rf2-twil stopped at the hazard
fold rather than migrating the mount.

`panels/trace.cljs` -- `Panel` is an `rf/reg-view`. Two blockers in its subtree:

  1. `[rt/resizable-table ...]` at two sites (the feed's `ops-header` child and the one
     `flat-row-list` builds). `views/resizable_table.cljs:567` is `(rf/reg-view
     resizable-table)` and has NO Fresco sibling. It is SHARED -- `panels/epoch/view.cljs`
     uses it too -- so this is the epoch panel's blocker as well, and it belongs to whoever
     owns the shared-widget half of the fan-out rather than to either panel.

     Two things a migrator should know before starting on it. Its body reads the column-widths
     slot with the `reg-view`-injected `subscribe` and drives the drag flow with the injected
     `dispatch`, neither of which a `defview` binds -- the established replacement is
     `rf.fresco/sub` and `(:dispatch (rf/capture-frame))`. And its row vectors are keyed with
     `(with-meta ... {:key (row-key row i)})`, which is the SAME hazard class rf2-twil and
     rf2-hxfy just cleared twice: metadata Fresco reads nowhere, so every row in every
     consumer silently loses its key on migration. That one is worth fixing on its own terms
     -- it is correct today, it satisfies both substrates once moved into the attrs map, and
     it is invisible when it breaks.

  2. `[ei/edn-inspector raw ...]` at `trace.cljs:389`, the inline row-payload inspector.
     Replacement is `ei/edn-inspector-view` with a stable `:mount-id`; the row-id is the
     natural qualifier and each expanded row needs its own, per that boundary's own contract.

=== WHY THIS IS ONE BEAD AND NOT THREE ===

The `resizable-table` boundary is the only real work; the other two are one-line head swaps
that are unsafe UNTIL their mount is a boundary and mechanical the moment it is. Sequencing is
the whole content: shared widget first, then each panel's mount, then the heads inside it.

DO NOT dispatch the two panels in parallel with the widget -- and note that
`views/resizable_table.cljs` and `panels.cljs` are each single-toucher by conflict, not by
convention.

=== INSTRUMENT NOTE, WORTH MORE THAN THE FINDING ===

A census keyed on "plain `defn` in head position" finds the four `edn/inspect` sites and
reports the file clear. It cannot see `[ei/edn-inspector ...]`, because that head is a `def`,
not a `defn`, and it LOOKS like a component. Both are `:invalid` to the codec. Ask the codec
-- `head-kind` is one call and it is the renderer's own answer -- rather than pattern-matching
the authoring shape. rf2-twil's HD-016 regression row uses it as its positive control for
exactly this reason.
notes:
=== THE FOUR HD-016 SITES ARE UNREACHABLE AT RUNTIME TODAY, AND THAT IS WHY NOTHING GRADED THEM (measured under rf2-twil, base c6e008813d) ===

`record-panel` builds REQUEST, RESPONSE and HANDLER DISPATCHED with `:expanded? false`, and
`theme/section/section-row` renders its body under `(when expanded? ...)`. Nothing in this tree
wires a click: `section-row` takes no handler, `theme/section.cljc` holds no expansion state,
and `managed_fx_subs.cljs` registers none. The `▶` glyph the header draws therefore opens
nothing, and a collapsed body is EVALUATED (it is a positional argument) and then DISCARDED.

So all four `[edn/inspect ...]` vectors were constructed on every render and never reached any
rendered tree, in production or in a test. Consequences worth carrying:

  - The hazard was real in the SOURCE and latent behind a SECOND latency. Even post-migration
    the head form could not have thrown until the disclosure is wired, because the codec never
    walks a discarded body. That LOWERS the urgency and does not remove the defect.
  - It explains the blind spot completely. No tier missed these through bad luck; no rendered
    tree has ever contained them, so no walker, no codec and no DOM row could have.
  - A regression row over `record-panel`'s tree CANNOT go red on a revert to the head form.
    rf2-twil's first draft asserted the returned `[ei/edn-inspector ...]` was present so the
    pair would move red-to-green together; it read ZERO, which is how this was found. The
    shipped row says so in its own prose and stands as a floor over the REACHABLE tree only.

WHAT WOULD MAKE THEM GRADEABLE, cheapest first: wire the disclosure (which the panel's own
docstring already promises -- "one click reveals the payload -- keeps the panel scannable on
first paint" -- so this is arguably a live UX defect independent of Fresco), or give
`record-panel` an expansion override. Neither was in rf2-twil's scope; the first is the one
worth doing on its own merits, and it should be filed separately rather than folded into the
migration.

=== A SECOND FINDING IN THE SAME PLACE, INDEPENDENT OF FRESCO ===

Three sections of this panel draw a disclosure triangle that nothing can open. That is a
user-visible defect on its own terms and is not tracked anywhere I could find. Whoever picks
up the migration will be in this file anyway; wiring the toggle is the natural companion, and
it happens to be what turns the four HD-016 sites into gradeable render paths.
=== CORRECTION TO THE NOTE ABOVE (mayor, verified at source) ===

The note above concluded correctly and reasoned wrongly, which is the harder kind to catch.
It said the disclosure is unwired because "nothing in this tree wires a click: `section-row`
takes no handler, `theme/section.cljc` holds no expansion state, and `managed_fx_subs.cljs`
registers none." The second and third clauses do not hold as a statement about the TREE:

  - `theme/section.cljc` states the contract deliberately -- "No interactivity.
    Click-to-toggle wiring is the caller's responsibility -- the primitive only renders the
    visual state the caller passes via `:expanded?`." So `section-row` is non-interactive BY
    DESIGN, not by omission, and it is not the thing to fix.
  - Expansion state EXISTS and has a working caller: `panels/cancellation_cascade.cljs:689`
    feeds `:expanded?` from `(rf.fresco/sub [:rf.xray/cancellation-cascade-expanded?])`.

What is true is narrower and is all the note needed: `managed_fx_template` passes `:expanded?`
LITERALS -- `false` for REQUEST, RESPONSE and HANDLER DISPATCHED -- and never wrote the
caller's half. Everything the note concludes stands unchanged: those three bodies are computed
as positional arguments and discarded, the four head-position vectors have never reached a
rendered tree, and no regression row over `record-panel` can go red on a revert.

Note which register the working example is in: cancellation_cascade wires it with
`rf.fresco/sub` inside a `defview`, i.e. from the MIGRATED world. A pre-migration
managed_fx_template would wire it with `@(rf/subscribe …)` through its `reg-view` mount, and a
post-migration one with `rf.fresco/sub` -- so whoever does rf2-kfoq should know which side of
the migration they are on before choosing the read.

The dead-disclosure defect is tracked as rf2-kfoq (rf2-s6m6 was a duplicate of it, filed from
this worktree and closed into it).
== MAYOR, 2026-09-10: THE HOLD, WITH ITS REAL SURFACE — and a correction to my own reason ==

STILL HELD. Not dispatchable this tick, and the reason is a live collision rather than a
dependency, so it will not show up in any blocker query.

I HAD THE RIGHT ANSWER FOR THE WRONG REASON, and that is worth recording because it would have
mis-fenced the next dispatch. I had been holding this bead on the belief that its surface was
`panels/epoch/view.cljs` and `static/machines/persistence.cljs` — the consumers of
`resizable-table`. That is where the phrase stuck in my memory from, but it is not this bead's
surface. Re-read at source, the blocking surface this bead actually names is:

    tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/managed_fx_template.cljs
    tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels.cljs            <- `ManagedFxList` at :430
    tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panel_enum.cljc        <- :105 rosters it
    tools/xray/test/.../panel_enum_guard_cljs_test.cljs       <- :76 asserts in PROSE that it IS a reg-view
    tools/xray/test/.../panels_mount_cljs_test.cljs           <- :190

WHAT IS FREE NOW, and it is worth knowing because it changed this session:
`managed_fx_template.cljs` was held by `disclose-a` for rf2-s6m6; that PR (#9630) has MERGED and
the worker is reaped, so the file is free. `panel_enum.cljc` is free — `machtab-a` reported
leaving it untouched, and its branch diff confirms it.

WHAT IS NOT FREE: `panels.cljs`. Worker `panelfix-a` is live in it right now for rf2-hg3j
(`render-panel!` seats the default frame while providing `opts :frame`). `ManagedFxList` lives in
that same file at :430, so this bead cannot start until #9636's sibling PR from panelfix-a lands.

DISPATCH WHEN: panelfix-a's PR merges. Then the whole surface above is free at once and this is a
single coherent dispatch — do NOT split it across the five files, because the bead's own point is
that the migration is not one file and that the roster, the prose assertion and the mount test
all move together with the head.

ONE THING FOR THAT BRIEF, from the bead's own analysis: `edn/inspect-view` already exists, has
ZERO callers, and was written for exactly this — same node-key, same opts, emits the
`edn-inspector-view` boundary. It CANNOT be adopted before the mount migrates, because a Fresco
boundary in a Reagent head position is the mirror failure of the one being fixed. So the order is
fixed: migrate `ManagedFxList` first, adopt `inspect-view` second, in that sequence and not the
other.

AND A PROSE ASSERTION IS PART OF THE DIFF, which is easy to miss when fencing by source file:
`panel_enum_guard_cljs_test.cljs:76` asserts IN PROSE that `ManagedFxList` is a `reg-view`. That
sentence becomes false the moment the head migrates, and no compiler will say so.
== SLICE 1 (THE SHARED WIDGET) LANDED AS PR #9642 — worker restable-a, 2026-09-10 ==

Scope held to `views/resizable_table.cljs` plus one new test. The two consumer panels
were NOT touched, per this bead's own "DO NOT dispatch the two panels in parallel with
the widget".

=== THE METADATA-KEY HAZARD: FIXED, AND MEASURED RATHER THAN ASSUMED ===

Seven `with-meta` key sites (three in `weave-header`, three in `weave-body`, one in the
row weaver), all moved into the attrs map behind one `keyed` helper.

The hazard is now a measured number rather than an inference. With the source reverted to
`with-meta` and the new test kept, the Fresco codec's own hiccup-to-element door reads
`[nil nil nil]` for the three header cells — i.e. every row and header cell in both
consumer panels loses its key on migration, silently.

TWO FINDINGS FROM THAT RUN THAT OUTLIVE THIS PR:

(1) THE rf2-hxfy INSTRUMENT IS HOLLOW AGAINST THIS SUB-CASE. rf2-hxfy asserted at the
    renderer with `(.-key (r/as-element node))`, which was exactly right for ITS defect
    (meta on a call form, dead on every substrate). It cannot see THIS one: Reagent reads
    meta AND props, so it returns the same key before and after. Measured on the revert
    run — the Reagent assertion PASSED while the Fresco assertion on the next line failed.
    A worker told only "assert at the renderer" will reach for `r/as-element`, get green,
    and ship a hollow gate. The instrument that grades a meta-vs-attrs key is
    `(.-key (re-frame.fresco.impl.codec/as-element node))`, already used by
    `panels/cancellation_cascade_cljs_test`. Worth carrying into the briefs for slices 2
    and 3, which face the same class.

(2) A LATENT ROBUSTNESS BUG, INDEPENDENT OF FRESCO. The old weaver handed whatever the
    consumer's `:row-cells` returned straight to `with-meta`, which THROWS on a non-vector
    cell ("No protocol method IWithMeta.-with-meta defined for type string"). The helper's
    non-vector arm makes the weaver total. Not previously tracked anywhere.

=== DELIVERABLE 2 — THE FRESCO SIBLING IS MECHANICAL, BUT NOT WITHIN THIS FENCE ===

Measured at tip; no code written for this half.

COMPONENT-LOCAL STATE: exactly ONE site. `header-gutter` holds a boolean hover flag in a
Form-2 Reagent Ratom. The file's other two atoms are module-level `defonce` plain CLJS
atoms (the storage key, the drag-state bookkeeping) — non-reactive and substrate-neutral.
`r/` occurs exactly once in the file, and this is the ONLY file under all of
`tools/xray/src` using `r/atom`.

FRESCO'S REPLACEMENT: `rf.fresco/reg-state` (HD-009). But it CONSUMES an instance key and
does not mint one — `views/edn_inspector.cljs` says so outright, and enforces it:
`edn-inspector-view` REQUIRES a `:mount-id` and hard-throws without one, because a React
function component has no form-2 outer body. So keeping the hover as STATE would force the
widget to demand a stable instance key from all FIVE consumer call sites. That is an API
change across two panels, and it is the thing that would have needed a ruling.

IT DOES NOT NEED ONE, BECAUSE THE HOVER DOES NOT NEED STATE AT ALL. `theme/global_styles.cljs`
injects a global style block that already carries a family of hover rules for exactly this
problem, each commented that inline styles cannot carry a hover pseudo-class. One of them
is keyed on `rf-xray-event-list-col-divider-` and paints a COLUMN-DIVIDER DRAG HANDLE with
the accent colour on hover, in pure CSS, with no state anywhere — functionally the same
widget as this gutter. The sibling `resize_handle.cljs` solves it both ways (its vertical
handle deliberately drops hover for an always-visible accent; its seam handle delegates to
global-styles). The gutter already stamps a stable `data-testid`, so the selector exists
today with NO markup change.

AND IT REMOVES THE COMPONENT, NOT JUST THE STATE. With the Ratom gone `header-gutter`
becomes a pure function returning a native div, so it can be CALLED like its neighbour
`body-spacer` already is instead of sitting in head position. That deletes the only
codec-`:invalid` head inside the widget — so the gutter needs no boundary, no instance key,
and its key becomes codec-gradeable like the others. It also retires the file's only
`reagent.core` usage, which `tools/xray/deps.edn` names as the reason Xray declares the
stock Reagent dependency at all.

NOTHING ELSE RESISTS `defview`. Checked four things; three are free. The `:contextType`
frame-context injection is REPLACED (a defview resolves its frame through the boundary).
The injected `subscribe`/`dispatch` become the settled house idiom `rf.fresco/sub` plus
`(:dispatch (rf/capture-frame))` — two lines, and the nil-reaction guard can go. The raw
window-listener drag flow is ALREADY substrate-neutral: `on-pointer-down` takes
`dispatch-fn` as an explicit parameter (rf2-r0o63 made it so). And `install!` / `hydrate!`
have ZERO coupling to the view — they register an fx, a sub and four events and dispatch
into a frame, mentioning neither the view nor the registration id, so their call sites in
`registry.cljs` and `mount.cljs` need no change.

VERDICT: slice 1b is a MECHANICAL follow-on, not a ruling. Its one prerequisite is a CSS
hover rule in `theme/global_styles.cljs`, which was outside this dispatch's editable
surface — so the sibling was deliberately not built here. Whoever takes 1b should be
fenced to include that file.

=== A STALE CLAIM ON THIS BEAD, FOR WHOEVER BRIEFS SLICES 2 AND 3 ===

The description says `edn/inspect-view` "has ZERO callers today". That was true when
written and is FALSE at tip: `static/flows/panel.cljs` calls it twice and
`static/schemas/panel.cljs` once, both from panels already migrated to `defview`. The rest
of that paragraph stands — the replacement exists, and the order (migrate the mount, then
adopt) is unaffected. Only the caller count is stale, and a brief repeating it would send a
worker looking for an unadopted helper that has in fact been adopted three times.

== SLICE 1 DELIVERED (PR #9642). THREE CORRECTIONS, AND TWO OF THEM BIND SLICES 2 AND 3. ==

restable-a fixed the metadata-key hazard in `views/resizable_table.cljs` — seven `with-meta` sites,
my count confirmed by the worker's own re-count — plus a new test namespace. Hollow-gate check both
ways with the SAME test: fix present 11637 tests / 58351 assertions / 0 failures; fix reverted
11637 tests / 58337 assertions / 12 failures + 2 errors. TOTALS IDENTICAL at 11637, which is what
distinguishes a real runtime failure from a suite that merely got smaller. Source restored
byte-clean.

=== 1. MY GATE NOMINATION WAS INVERTED, AND IT FAILED OPEN. THE MAYOR'S ERROR. ===

I briefed: run `cd tools/xray && clojure -M:test`, and do NOT trust `npm run test:cljs` because
`implementation/shadow-cljs.edn`'s `:node-test` build "contains no `tools/` or `xray/` entry at
all". THAT IS BACKWARDS.

MAYOR-VERIFIED AT SOURCE after the worker challenged it: the `:node-test` section is 41,387
characters and carries 107 quoted paths, `../tools/xray/src` and `../tools/xray/test` among them,
under a comment saying the build exists so it picks up `tools/xray/test/**/*_cljs_test.cljs`. My
original check bounded the section at the first `:node-test-xray` string it met, read ~35 paths,
and reported an empty result — a plausible-looking `[]` from a window that never reached the
answer.

THE COST IS THE FAIL-OPEN DIRECTION, which is why this is worth a heading. The gate I named is a
JVM run that CANNOT LOAD A `.cljs` TEST: the worker ran it and got 1276 tests / 6118 assertions /
