title: no-rf-default-floor-lint-test flakes with a StackOverflowError that reads as a real lint finding
description:
`no-rf-default-floor-lint-test` CAN FAIL A PR WITH A STACKOVERFLOWERROR THAT HAS NOTHING
TO DO WITH THE DIFF. Measured on PR #9602 (rf2-twyh), 2026-09-10.

=== WHAT HAPPENED ===

`test.yml`'s job "JVM repo-wide source walks (clojure -M:test)" went RED on a
prose-only PR. The failing step is the FIRST one, "Absence-repair floor lint for
:rf/default", i.e. `clojure -M:test -n re-frame.no-rf-default-floor-lint-test`; the
six walks after it are then SKIPPED, so one flake takes the whole job and, through
`all-required-passed`, the aggregator too. The rollup read 2 failures where there was
one real one.

It is NOT an assertion failure, which is what makes it easy to misread:

    expected: (empty? offenders)
      actual: java.lang.StackOverflowError: null
     at java.util.regex.Pattern$CharProperty.match ...
        java.util.regex.Pattern$Branch.match ...
        java.util.regex.Pattern$GroupHead.match ...
        java.util.regex.Pattern$Loop.match ...
        (repeating to the frame limit)

The `expected:`/`actual:` framing makes it present as "the lint found offenders", and
the message printed immediately above it in the log is the lint's own explanatory prose
about `:rf/default` floors — so the natural reading is that the diff introduced a
forbidden floor. It did not; the assertion never evaluated.

=== THE MECHANISM ===

`implementation/core/test/re_frame/no_rf_default_floor_lint_test.clj` line 96:

    (def ^:private string-literal-re #"\"(?:\\.|[^\"\\])*\"")

`strip-string-literals` applies that per LINE across every `.clj{,c,s}` under
`implementation/**/src/` and `tools/**/src/`. Java's regex engine implements a
quantified GROUP by RECURSION — one `Loop.match` frame per iteration — so the stack
depth needed is proportional to the LENGTH OF THE LINE being scanned. It is not
catastrophic backtracking in the ambiguous-alternation sense (the two branches are
disjoint); it is plain recursion depth, which is why it is marginal rather than
hopeless, and therefore intermittent.

The corpus's longest lines, measured at trunk (unchanged by the PR that hit this):

    2898  tools/story-mcp/src/re_frame/story_mcp/tools/testing.cljc
    2829  implementation/core/src/re_frame/late_bind/directory.cljc
    2318  tools/story-mcp/src/re_frame/story_mcp/tools/dev.cljc
    1392  tools/story-mcp/src/re_frame/story_mcp/tools/docs.cljc

Those sit near whatever the runner's stack affords, so whether the job passes depends
on runner conditions rather than on the diff.

=== THE EVIDENCE THAT IT IS A FLAKE, NOT A DIFF ===

  * The PR's diff added NO long line to the corpus. It touched exactly one corpus file,
    `implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/html_helpers.cljc`, whose longest line measured
    89 characters BEFORE and 89 AFTER; the longest line the diff added anywhere under
    `implementation/` was 73 characters.
  * The same test passed LOCALLY on the same tree: exit 0, 1 test / 1 assertion,
    0 failures.
  * `main` at `03d4af871c` and `worker/listnest-a` at `074555347f` both ran the SAME job
    GREEN within minutes, on a corpus whose long-line files none of the three diffs
    touch.
  * DECISIVE: `gh run rerun --failed` on the identical commit, with no code change,
    turned the job GREEN. Final rollup 87 checks, 0 pending, 0 failed.

=== WHY IT IS WORTH RECORDING RATHER THAN SHRUGGING OFF ===

It fails in the direction that MANUFACTURES WORK, and it is well disguised. A
coordinator whose standing instruction is "dispatch a worker to fix any PR that is not
green" reads a named required check, a plausible `expected: (empty? offenders)` line
and the lint's own prose about forbidden `:rf/default` floors, and sends a worker after
a defect that does not exist. It also SKIPS the six walks behind it, so a genuine
finding in any of those is masked on the same run. This is the same class as the
rollup-reading traps CLAUDE.md item (p) catalogues, arriving through a test rather than
through `gh`.

=== POSSIBLE DISPOSITIONS (no recommendation ruled) ===

  1. Do nothing; re-run on sight. Cheapest, and the flake is rare — but the misreading
     above is the cost, and it is paid by whoever meets it next.
  2. Make the scan non-recursive: replace the `(?:\\.|[^\"\\])*` group with a possessive
     or character-class form whose Java implementation does not recurse per character,
     or hand-scan the line. Small, local, removes the class.
  3. Skip or chunk lines beyond some length before the regex runs. The lint's own
     docstrings say the strip can only REDUCE false positives, never mask a real floor,
     so declining to strip a 2900-character line is safe by the test's own argument —
     though it would then need to tolerate whatever that line contains.
  4. Reorder the job so a flake in step one does not skip the other six walks, or run
     the seven as independent steps with `if: always()`.

Option 2 is the one that removes the class rather than managing it, but this is a
`.github/workflows/**`-adjacent and core-test-tree change and deserves a deliberate
decision rather than a drive-by.
notes:
=== MAYOR'S DIAGNOSIS, MEASURED. IT IS NOT A FLAKE, AND CALLING IT ONE PICKS THE WRONG REMEDY. ===

**The overflow is DETERMINISTIC in the line length. What varies between runs is the JVM thread's
STACK SIZE, not luck.** That is why re-running the identical commit turned it green, and why
"re-run it" is a coin flip on stack allocation rather than a remedy.

MEASURED by the mayor on this box (Java 21.0.10, default stack), applying the lint's own pattern
`#"\"(?:\.|[^\"\])*\""` to a quoted span of N characters:

    content-len=100    greedy=ok        possessive=ok
    content-len=500    greedy=ok        possessive=ok
    content-len=1000   greedy=ok        possessive=ok
    content-len=1500   greedy=OVERFLOW  possessive=ok
    content-len=2000   greedy=OVERFLOW  possessive=ok
    content-len=2829   greedy=OVERFLOW  possessive=ok
    content-len=4000   greedy=OVERFLOW  possessive=ok

The threshold on THIS JVM sits between 1000 and 1500. **That number is not portable** — it is a
function of the stack the thread was given, so a CI runner with a different `-Xss` or a different
default lands elsewhere. Do not write 1500 into a test.

**THE MECHANISM.** `(?:A|B)*` compiles to a `Loop` node, and Java's engine matches a greedy loop by
RECURSING once per iteration — hence `java.util.regex.Pattern$Loop.match` in the trace. One frame
per character of string content. The POSSESSIVE form `(?:[^\"\]++|\.)*+` compiles to a different
node that iterates instead, and it did not overflow at any length tested. **That is a measurement,
not a prescription** — it may or may not be the repair you want, and possessive quantifiers change
backtracking semantics, so satisfy yourself the pattern still means what the lint needs before
adopting it. An index scan with no regex at all is the other obvious candidate.

**THE CORPUS THAT TRIGGERS IT, measured at trunk c123aa2889:** 18 lines exceed 1500 characters
across 3 files — **16 of them in `implementation/core/src/re_frame/late_bind/directory.cljc`**
(longest 2829 at line 1069), plus one each in `tools/story-mcp/.../tools/testing.cljc` and
`.../tools/dev.cljc`. So this is not a hypothetical: the walk crosses a file with sixteen
over-threshold lines every single run.

**AND THE FAILURE PRESENTS AS A REAL FINDING, WHICH IS THE EXPENSIVE PART.** The `StackOverflowError`
surfaces under `expected: (empty? offenders)` beneath the lint's own `:rf/default` prose, so a reader
sees what looks like a genuine floor violation. The `roster3-a` worker had to rule that out by hand —
its own longest line is 89 characters, before and after — before it could report its PR green.

=== THE SECOND HALF, WHICH IS THE FAIL-OPEN ONE, AND IT NEEDS CONFIRMING ===

The report states that because this step runs FIRST, **the six repo-wide source walks behind it were
SKIPPED** — so one stack overflow silently removes six checks from the run. The namespace itself
carries exactly ONE `deftest`, so the skipping is at the JOB or STEP level rather than within the
namespace.

**CONFIRM THAT AT SOURCE BEFORE BUILDING ANYTHING ON IT.** Read the job in `.github/workflows/` that
runs these walks and establish whether a failure in the first step actually prevents the rest, or
whether they merely reported nothing on that particular run. If it is real, say so plainly: it means
a green-after-re-run is not evidence that the other six passed on the FIRST attempt, and it is the
strongest argument for fixing the pattern rather than tolerating the intermittency.

=== SCOPE ===

`implementation/core/test/re_frame/no_rf_default_floor_lint_test.clj` — the pattern and, if the
walk-skipping is real, whatever ordering makes one failure hide six results.

**DO NOT reflow `late_bind/directory.cljc` to shorten its lines.** Those lines are the corpus, not
the defect; shortening them would hide this rather than fix it, and that file is nobody's to churn
for a lint's convenience.

**DO NOT widen the lint's subject.** It grades `:rf/default` positional floors; this bead is about
the instrument overflowing, not about what it looks for.

=== EVIDENCE ===

A regression row that applies the repaired pattern to a line comfortably past the threshold — 4000
characters, say — and asserts it returns rather than overflowing. **A row that only checks the
pattern still matches short strings is a HOLLOW GATE**: it passes today, with the bug. The mechanical
test is *delete the signal, keep the fault* — restore the greedy pattern and your row must go red.

The mayor's probe is reproducible in ten lines of Java or Clojure; build the equivalent in whatever
the suite already uses.

title: machines: a replaced/respawned parent reseeds :rf/spawn-counter and re-allocates a generated child address its live orphan still holds
description:
## Split out of rf2-dokz's ruling (2026-09-08). NOT cured by that bead's fix.

build-initial-snapshot seeds `:rf/spawn-counter {}` FRESH (implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines/parallel.cljc:395-397), while spec/005-StateMachines.md:2794 puts the declarative allocator's counter INSIDE the parent's snapshot. Ordinary destroy tears down the PARENT ONLY — run-active-exit-cascade (transition.cljc:2783) collects authored :exit action-refs and synthesises no child-destroy fx, and machine_reply_lowering_test.clj:250-262 pins a declaratively-spawned child SURVIVING an imperative parent destroy — which is the resolved 'teardown is explicit in v1' decision at 005:2618 working as designed.

So a parent that is destroyed and respawned at the same address starts counting from zero while its previously-spawned children are still live at `#1`, `#2`. Its first new child allocates `<type>#1` — an address its own orphaned predecessor still occupies — and installs over it through the same unguarded `assoc-in` at spawn.cljc:542. One replacement at the top manufactures a generated-address collision one level down, with no author involvement and no :fixed-actor-id anywhere in sight.

## Why it is filed separately rather than folded into rf2-dokz

MEASURED (Codex JVM probe, recorded in rf2-dokz's RULING note): the re-entered parent re-allocates the same `child#1` and loses the old marker in BOTH columns — after a silent overwrite AND after an explicit destroy-then-spawn. It is therefore a property of explicit-teardown semantics generally, NOT a symptom of the occupied-address overwrite and NOT something rf2-dokz's clean-teardown fix removes. Folding it in would have meant inventing an ownership cascade inside a bead that explicitly rejects one.

## The question, undecided

005:2618 already rules OUT an implicit ownership cascade, so 'destroy the orphans' is not on the table. What is open is narrower: should a fresh incarnation at an address inherit / advance the counter rather than reset it, so generated child addresses stay unique for the frame's lifetime? Options not yet weighed: seed :rf/spawn-counter from the outgoing incarnation; make generated ids incarnation-stamped; or rule the collision acceptable and document it. The orphan is reaped at frame destroy either way (spawn_order.cljc:50-57) — for an SPA's main frame, the page session.

## Do not start before rf2-dokz lands

Same file (spawn.cljc install path) and same spec section. Sequence behind it.
notes:
=== DECISION DOSSIER — 2026-09-09 01:0x AUSEST, worker spawncnt-a, read-only (no tracked file written, no PR) ===
=== THE HEADLINE IS THAT THIS BEAD IS SUBSTANTIALLY BIGGER THAN IT WAS FILED. RAISING P3 -> P2. ===

THE FILED DEFECT REPRODUCES EXACTLY, IN BOTH COLUMNS. A throwaway JVM probe drove the real runtime
(plain-atom substrate, `make-reset-runtime-fixture`). Column A (explicit destroy, then respawn at the same
address) and Column B (no destroy, spawn straight onto the live occupant) are identical line for line: the
re-incarnated parent's counter reads `{}` fresh, its first new child allocates `:pc/child#1`, and the
orphan's `:data :mark` goes `:FIRST -> :none` while the snapshot COUNT stays at 2. The old actor is
GONE, not detached. rf2-dokz's landed fix changed nothing here, exactly as it was scoped to.

BUT THE COLLISION DOES NOT NEED A RE-INCARNATION AT ALL, AND THAT IS THE FINDING. The counter is
snapshot-local to the parent while the address space is frame-global, so ANY TWO PARENTS SPAWNING THE SAME
CHILD TYPE COLLIDE ON `#1` IMMEDIATELY:
  (i)   two parents of the SAME type at DISTINCT addresses, no destroy, no re-incarnation:
        after A spawns -> `:pc/child#1` mark `:FROM-A`
        after B spawns -> addrs `(:pc/child#1 :pc/slotA :pc/slotB)`, `child#1` mark `:none`,
                          `child#2` does not exist, and slotA's AND slotB's `:rf/spawned` BOTH read
                          `{[:working] :pc/child#1}` — two parents addressing one child.
  (ii)  two parents of DIFFERENT types spawning the same child type: identical collapse.
  (iii) a declarative `:spawn` carrying an explicit `:id-prefix :pc/mine` still allocates `:pc/child#1`
        under counter key `:pc/child`. `:id-prefix` IS IGNORED on the declarative path.
  (iv)  CONTROL, two parents spawning two DIFFERENT child types: `(:pc/childX#1 :pc/childY#1 ...)`. PASSES.

So the ordinary "N rows, each an actor, each spawning a worker" shape silently collapses to one worker,
and the author has no workaround short of `:fixed-actor-id` — `:id-prefix` is accepted by
`validation.cljc:1501` and documented at `005:2798/2972/4558`, but `allocate-one`
(`transition.cljc:2358-2360`) reads `:machine-id`, and `:2402`/`:2471` overwrite `:id-prefix` with the
child's `:machine-id` anyway. THIS CONTRADICTS `spec/005:155` — "Inside one frame, the id is unique."

WHAT AN AUTHOR OBSERVES: NOTHING. Full trace stream captured across the colliding spawn — ZERO
destroyed-flavoured traces naming the orphan, ZERO error or warning traces. Two
`:rf.machine.spawn/spawned` traces carry the SAME `:spawned-id` with different `:parent-id` and no destroy
between them, which is precisely the invariant the PR #9508 comment at `spawn.cljc:1093-1096` claims
tooling can rely on. The `:rf.machine/snapshot-updated` trace reports `:before` as the FRESH initial
snapshot, not the orphan's, so even a snapshot-diff tool sees an install and never a deletion. The one
thing that does fire is `:rf.machine.timer/cancelled ... :reason :on-supersede` — the "re-armed its own
timer" reason, not a collision signal, though it does mean the host-clock handle is released.
A silently vanished actor with no announcement anywhere. That is what sets the priority.

A PREMISE ON THIS BEAD IS REFUTED: "the orphan is reaped at frame destroy either way
(`spawn_order.cljc:50-57`)" is FALSE. After the collision the orphan has no snapshot at all, and the
single `:spawn-order` entry for that address names the WINNER. There is nothing left to reap.

FILED LINE NUMBERS HAVE ALL DRIFTED AND ONE PATH IS WRONG — corrected here so nobody re-hunts:
  `parallel.cljc:395-397` (counter seed) -> :397;  `spec/005:2794` -> :2811;
  `spec/005:2618` -> :2635 AND THE TEXT CHANGED — it gained rf2-dokz's qualification, now saying a
  replacement "reaps NOTHING beyond the occupant itself";  `spawn.cljc:542` -> :557;
  `transition.cljc:2783` unchanged;  `machine_reply_lowering_test.clj` deftest :243, survival pin
  :282-283, and the bead's PATH is wrong — there is no `machines/` segment;
  `spawn_order.cljc:50-57` is docstring prose, the durable-order code is :84-172.
New anchors the dossier rests on: `allocate-spawned-id` `transition.cljc:561-570` (rationale :540-552);
`allocate-actor-id-in-runtime-db` `spawn.cljc:76-81`; `allocate-one` `transition.cljc:2350-2360`; the two
counter homes contrasted at `005:2811-2812`; `005:3902` (the `:spawn-all` silent-overwrite fail-closed);
`005:4556-4558` (spawn id format, marked RESOLVED).

THE OPTIONS, PRICED:
  (a) SEED THE COUNTER FROM THE OUTGOING INCARNATION — do not take it. It fixes a strict SUBSET and
      leaves (i)/(ii) broken while making the tree look fixed. Worse, in column A the outgoing snapshot is
      already gone when the replacement installs, so it needs a counter TOMBSTONE keyed by address: a new
      durable slot, a new lifecycle, a new thing to revert and to project through SSR.
  (b) INCARNATION-STAMPED IDS — fixes everything and reopens `005:4556` (marked RESOLVED) plus the 559
      literal `#n` pins, 8 conformance goldens and the Xray epoch projection. Spends a resolved decision
      to buy what (e) buys without one.
  (d) ACCEPT AND DOCUMENT — tenable for the bead AS FILED; not tenable now. Case (i) is the natural
      multi-actor program, it loses an actor silently, and the documented escape does not work. "We trust
      the programmer" cannot mean the programmer must know that two sibling actors share a child address.
  (e) RECOMMENDED — move the declarative allocator's counter to the frame runtime-db slot the
      hand-emitted path ALREADY uses (`[:rf.runtime/machines :spawn-counter <id-prefix>]`,
      `spawn.cljc:76-81`, `005:2812`). One home instead of two; `<type>#<n>` becomes frame-unique, which
      is what `005:155` already asserts; the id spelling does not change, so most of the 559 literals
      survive. Fixes all three measured shapes at once. The revert property is preserved — `005:2812` says
      a frame revert restores the runtime-db counter too.
  (f) CHEAP STOPGAP, ORTHOGONAL — refuse to install a GENERATED address over a live occupant: one
      `actor-live?` read at `spawn.cljc:557`, the same read the `:fixed-actor-id` path already pays, and
      raise the existing `:rf.error/machine-spawn-all-duplicate-id`, whose `005:3902` write-up already
      names this exact failure for the intra-`:spawn-all` case. Turns silent loss into a loud error today
      without touching the purity contract. NOTE: rf2-dokz's "no error, no warning trace" rejection was
      reasoned about an address the AUTHOR NAMED; here nobody named anything, so it is not obviously
      binding — but that is Mike's read to make.

THE RECOMMENDATION IN ONE LINE, AND THE HONEST CASE AGAINST IT:
  Take (e); land (f) first if the silence should stop this week.
  AGAINST: (e) spends the property the spec chose the in-snapshot home FOR — that `machine-transition` is
  pure in its spawn-id sequencing, the basis of the replay contract and of
  `machine_transition_purity_test.clj` — to fix a bug that bites only applications running several actors

  contract `005:2674`) needs re-siting into the fx handler, where the hand-emitted path already allocates

  load-bearing for replay/Xray in a way the worker could not measure, then (f) plus a documented

BLAST RADIUS, MEASURED, TWO AXES, WITH CONTROLS. Literal `<type>#<n>` pins: 559 occurrences across 65
files, 42 of them test files (`#1` 448, `#2` 63, `#7` 33, `#3` 21, `#0` 14, `#42` 11). The pattern used no
bracket expression, so CLAUDE.md item (j) does not apply; the two-directions control fired correctly and
produced no false positive on `fixed_actor_id_addressing_test.clj`. Direct counter reads:
100 lines across 23 files including 8 `spec/conformance/fixtures/*.edn` goldens and
`implementation/core/test/re_frame/smoke_test.clj:887-893`, which pins `:rf/spawn-counter {}` literally;
46 further sites across 9 `src/` files, 23 of them in `parallel.cljc`, plus 3 in `tools/xray`.

title: [implementation/core/subscriptions] Refresh affected cached subscriptions when a frame generation changes
description:
Reviewed snapshot: 7ffdacf24d797b67864af78a4625b2c1cb3ef8fd. Before filing, mayor HEAD e4d949e8e87893ad638ed97e3d087fda1f62f0d4 has no changes on the relevant subs, cache, frame, or live-frame paths.

Problem / expected behavior
A supported same-id make-frame call replaces the frame's image generation. Subsequent subscribe calls must resolve the changed definitions from that generation while preserving durable frame state and unaffected subscriptions. Instead, an already materialized query remains a cache hit and continues running the old body. This makes ordinary image replacement / Story behavior replacement appear not to take effect until the caller knows to clear the subscription cache manually.

Contract: docs/EP/EP-0023-image-loaded-frames.md:1538-1554 preserves subscription state that remains valid and explicitly permits targeted invalidation for changed registrations. EP-0024-unified-frame-identity-and-lifecycle.md:271-285 makes same-id construction update configuration and resolved generation without destroying durable state. The current public replacement is make-frame re-construction (live_frame.cljc:1227-1247); this does not request restoration of the retired reload-images! API.

Exact causal path
- implementation/core/src/re_frame/frame.cljc:3475-3522 stages the new :generation on the existing record, preserving the :sub-cache atom. set-generation! at :1651-1664 also only swaps :generation.
- implementation/core/src/re_frame/live_frame.cljc:1208-1219 and :1277-1298 swap a reprojected generation without invalidating affected subscription entries.
- implementation/core/src/re_frame/subs.cljc:1187-1232 captures :handler-fn and input topology from the resolved descriptor. The reaction/memo body retains those functions for its lifetime (:1327-1381).
- subscribe-in-frame enters current frame resolution, but its hit branch (:1756-1774) only increments ref-count and returns the cached reaction. It never compares the cache entry against the current descriptor/generation.
- implementation/core/src/re_frame/subs/cache.cljc:347-388 invalidates a transitive dependency closure only from registrar replacement hooks. Replacing inline images does not re-register those entries globally. First registration of a previously missing input also does not fire that hook (registrar.cljc:631-645).
- Existing subs_image_local_classification_cljs_test.cljc:284-289 explicitly calls clear-sub-cache! after changing the image to force a fresh reaction, so that coverage does not establish freshness without an extra cache clear.

Measured minimal reproduction (isolated JVM, actual core source + plain-atom adapter)
(require '[re-frame.core :as rf] '[re-frame.image :as image]
         '[re-frame.live-frame :as live] '[re-frame.subs :as subs]
         '[re-frame.substrate.plain-atom :as plain])
(rf/init! plain/adapter)
(defn img [id n]
  (image/image {:id id :registrations
                {:reg-sub [[:review/value {} (fn [_ _] n)]]}}))
(live/make-frame {:id :review/frame :images [(img :review/v1 1)]} [])
(def r1 (subs/subscribe [:review/value] {:frame :review/frame}))
@r1 ; => 1
(live/make-frame {:id :review/frame :images [(img :review/v2 2)]} [])
(def r2 (subs/subscribe [:review/value] {:frame :review/frame}))
@r2 ; ACTUAL 1, expected 2
(identical? r1 r2) ; => true
(live/call-with-frame-resolution :review/frame
  #(subs/compute-sub [:review/value] {})) ; => 2

Second supported variant: a late dependency becomes available in the live source store. Register :review/parent with {:inputs [[:review/late]]}, body (fn [[x] _] x); make a default-image frame and subscribe to the parent while :review/late is absent; then first-register :review/late with a constant-7 body. The next parent subscribe returns nil, while compute-sub inside call-with-frame-resolution returns 7. The read-time flush (live_frame.cljc:340-385) has updated the generation, but the parent's cached nil-yielding input remains. This is the same missing invalidation at a generation change, not a request for a new registration grammar.

Smallest repair
Use the existing generation-change boundary to invalidate only affected per-frame subscription entries and their transitive cached dependents, including parents that previously resolved an added input to nil. Reuse the existing cache disposal/closure machinery, preserve the cache atom and unaffected entries, and cover both same-id re-construction and source-store reprojection. Do not add a public cache-management ceremony or change always-vector input delivery. This finding requires correct newly requested subscriptions; it does not require retaining the identity of a reaction whose definition changed.

Dedupe / scope
Searched open and closed title/description matches for subscription, cache, sub-cache, no-such-sub, generation, and hot reload, plus relevant memories. No existing freshness owner found. The first-register miss contract in sub_cache_test.clj:376-408 covers only a top-level uncached miss. Lifecycle reviewer confirmed same-id surgical replacement is intentional and delegated subscription freshness to this bead.

Validation limits
One bounded java/clojure.main probe loaded only this worktree's core sources and installed Clojure jars, with process-local state. Exit 0; printed probe root matched WORKTREE_ROOT. It measured both sequences above, same-cache identity, and current-generation pure values. Initial attempt used a retired image key and failed before either scenario; the corrected second attempt is the evidence. No CLJS/browser run, compilation, full suite, implementation edits, or shared runtime mutations were performed.
acceptance_criteria: A same-id frame remake changing an inline sub from 1 to 2 makes the next subscribe and subscribe-once return 2 without clear-sub-cache!; changed declared-input parents rebuild too. A first-registered missing input becomes visible through an already cached parent on the next subscribe. Unchanged cached entries and other frames retain their identity/reference counts, and durable frame state survives. Exercise the shared paths on JVM and CLJS; verify removed or changed topology releases exactly the refs it owned. No requirement to preserve a changed reaction identity.
notes:
--- 2026-09-07 AUSEST — IMPLEMENTED on worker/core-a, PR #9373 (open, ready). Bead left OPEN for the mayor to close after merge. ---

PREMISE CHECK: the bead's causal path HELD at source in every particular. subscribe-in-frame's hit branch bumps the ref-count and returns the cached reaction with no comparison against the current generation; frame.cljc stages :generation on the existing record preserving the :sub-cache atom; live_frame.cljc swaps a reprojected generation without invalidating anything.

REPAIR. There are exactly TWO production writers of the :generation slot and BOTH are reachable from re-frame.live-frame: swap-frame-generation! (reprojection) and make-frame's upsert-frame! call (same-id re-construction). rf.frame/set-generation! has no other production caller, so no change to frame.cljc was needed. live-frame owns generation-diff, so it names exactly the :sub ids that moved (:changed / :removed / :added) and hands them to ONE new per-frame primitive, rf.subs.cache/invalidate-frame-subs!, which invalidate-sub-on-replace! now also routes through with a one-element set. transitive-dependent-closure was generalised from one id to a SET so a batch converges in one fixpoint pass.

:added is load-bearing rather than defensive — a cached parent holding a nil-yielding unregistered input is reached through its declared :inputs head even though the added id has no slot of its own. That is the bead's second variant.

DELIBERATELY NOT DONE: no new :rf.sub/reason enum value. The reason axis is a CLOSED set pinned in spec/009-Instrumentation.md, spec/006 and Xray's spec + view label map. A generation change IS the image hot-reload path (EP-0023 §Hot Reload), so it reuses :hot-reload and touches no spec or tool file.

ONE CORRECTION TO MY OWN FIRST TEST, worth recording because it looks like a bug and is not: two SEPARATELY-AUTHORED inline images declaring the same sub with the same body fn are NOT :retained — their lowered descriptors differ on :rf.provenance/image, so generation-diff honestly classes them :changed. Measured. The :retained scenario needs a SHARED image VALUE carried into both compositions; the test now does that.

FAILING-FIRST: implementation/core/test/re_frame/subs_generation_refresh_cljs_test.cljc (.cljc — runs on JVM and CLJS). clojure -M:test -n ... exit 1, 7 tests / 27 assertions, 11 failures / 0 errors BEFORE; exit 0, 7 / 27, 0 failures AFTER.

GATES (captured exit codes): fast-PR spine 0 (PASS fast PR spine); scripts/test-core-prod-gate.sh 0 under -Dre-frame.debug=false, 1976 tests / 8429 assertions / 187 namespaces — the new ns joined that lane automatically, the roster being an exclusion list, so the fix is posture-independent; npm run test:browser 0 (815/4466); test:browser-prod-elision 0 (92/292); test:adapter-smokes 0.
close_reason:
PR #9373 merged 2026-09-07T12:17:39Z; verified HEAD == origin/main == 2358c14a62. Merged on all five clauses (87 checks at the band, 0 fail, 0 non-terminal, four runs completed at head 542205d9f5, no workflow drift since 85f1eb1811). Closed by the mayor — the worker deliberately left all three beads open with verdicts appended for me to close after merge.

A DIFFERENT LAYER FROM ITS SIBLINGS, and the worker was explicit that they compose rather than overlap: rf2-1frc and rf2-kuky.57 are about WHAT a hook acquires and releases; this bead is about invalidation FIRING AT ALL when a frame generation changes. Separate commit.

NO ENUM WIDENING, deliberately: the generation path reuses :hot-reload rather than adding a :rf.sub/reason value, because that set is pinned in three places at once — spec/009, spec/006 and Xray — so widening it would have turned a core fix into a hot-zone change across all three. title: xray: :rf.xray/epoch-recorded floods :rf/xray's own queue under load — 4 :rf.error/drain-depth-exceeded in the Story feature-load gate
description:
Found while measuring rf2-avi7 (PR #9312). SEPARATE DEFECT — identical count with and without #9312, so it is neither caused nor fixed by that change, and it is NOT the frame-destroyed category rf2-avi7 is about.

npm run test:story-feature-load emits 4 :rf.error/drain-depth-exceeded console errors, all on :frame :rf/xray, all from Xray's own instrumentation loop. Two shapes (captured via a pr-str diagnostic planted in error_emit/report-unowned-error!, restored, blob cf828e0e6c167fd0d421c32de0e3b148f2b8e811 verified):

  {:error :rf.error/drain-depth-exceeded :frame :rf/xray :depth 100 :queue-size 101
   :last-event-id :rf.xray/epoch-recorded
   :dropped-event-ids [<101 x :rf.xray/epoch-recorded>]
   :tail-event-ids    [<16 x :rf.xray/epoch-recorded>]
   :rollback? false :recovery :no-recovery}

  {:error :rf.error/drain-depth-exceeded :frame :rf/xray :depth 100 :queue-size 1
   :last-event-id :rf.xray.edn-inspector/clear-width
   :dropped-event-ids [:rf.xray.edn-inspector/clear-width]
   :tail-event-ids [<9 x :rf.xray/epoch-recorded> <7 x :rf.xray.edn-inspector/clear-width>]}

MECHANISM (to confirm): preload/install-epoch-listener! dispatches :rf.xray/epoch-recorded into :rf/xray on EVERY epoch the framework records, on ANY frame. The gate's 20-event load burst produces epochs faster than :rf/xray's drain settles, so the queue passes the depth-100 cap and the router drops events with :recovery :no-recovery. The second shape shows an unrelated Xray chrome event (edn-inspector/clear-width) being the one dropped because the queue was already full of epoch-recorded — i.e. the flood costs Xray its OWN UI events, not just redundant refreshes.

Note the handler is already a cheap conditional re-read ((if (= frame-id target) (assoc db :epoch-history …) db)) — so for every frame that is NOT the target this is a full dispatch round-trip to compute . Coalescing is the obvious direction, and there is precedent in the same namespace: :rf.xray/sync-trace-buffer is deliberately task-coalesced (rf2-wq6gx) for exactly this reason — 'so the sub fires on every push without one dispatch per trace event'. epoch-recorded never got the same treatment.

PROPOSED (not ruled): coalesce :rf.xray/epoch-recorded the way sync-trace-buffer is coalesced, and/or drop the dispatch entirely for a frame-id that is not the current :target-frame (the listener can read the target without entering the queue).

WHY IT MATTERS NOW: this is a per-PR gate (test.yml, story_full_gate) and PR #9306 unmasks it by removing the Story shell's page-wide no-op :errors listener. After #9312 lands, the gate's remaining 6 console errors are these 4 plus the 2 on rf2-88f1.
notes:
TYPO CORRECTION (shell backtick substitution ate one word when this bead was created): the sentence "so for every frame that is NOT the target this is a full dispatch round-trip to compute ." should read "...to compute the SAME db value it already had". Nothing else in the description was affected.

CORRECTION, same session, ~20 minutes after the close above: that close reason says the residual acceptance measurement would be supplied by tonight nightly full gate. IT WILL NOT BE. PR #9306 is the change that removes the masking listener, and it is NOT merged — trunk still carries that listener (measured: 8 :errors hits in tools/story/src/re_frame/story/ui/shell.cljs on origin/main, control 26 for defn), so the nightly runs masked and cannot see these errors either way. The fix and its regression tests are on main and that part of the close stands; only the claimed instrument was wrong. The real instrument is a full-gate run on a tree carrying trunk PLUS #9306, and it is recorded as the release condition on rf2-kuky.18.
close_reason:
Merged as PR #9320 (rebased onto main at 816e9b82a2), same rollup and same five-clause verification as rf2-88f1.

:rf.xray/epoch-recorded is now coalesced, following the precedent already in the namespace (:rf.xray/sync-trace-buffer, task-coalesced under rf2-wq6gx for exactly this reason) rather than inventing a mechanism. New regression test epoch_pump_coalescing_cljs_test.cljs (162 lines) pins it.

THE REASON THIS MATTERED IS THE SECOND CAPTURED SHAPE, not the flood itself: an unrelated Xray chrome event (:rf.xray.edn-inspector/clear-width) was the event DROPPED, because the queue was already full of epoch-recorded. The flood cost Xray its OWN UI events, not merely redundant refreshes. A pure "too many dispatches" framing would have justified a cheaper fix that left that alive.

Confirmed separate from rf2-avi7 as the bead said: identical count with and without #9312, so it was neither caused nor fixed by that change.

SAME ACCEPTANCE CAVEAT AS rf2-88f1: the local npm run test:story-feature-load console-error count was never reported — the worker was killed by the session rate limit mid-verification. The 4 :rf.error/drain-depth-exceeded this bead owns are 4 of the 6 errors remaining after #9312, and the proof that they are gone now sits with tonight nightly full gate, folded into PR #9306 hold condition.

title: instrument: a 129-way grep -E alternation silently returns ZERO on this box, and a tail-spliced control passes anyway
description:
MEASURED 2026-09-05 by the mayor, after a read-only backlog audit refuted a sweep the mayor had run and believed.

THE FAILURE. The already-done sweep in loops.md section 3 ('for each open id, search the trunk's merged history for that id') was run as a single alternation of every open bead id:
  PAT=$(paste -sd'|' ids.txt)          # 129 ids, 1475 characters
  git log origin/main --format='%h %s' -1500 | grep -cE "($PAT)"
It returned 0. The true answer is 36.

MEASURED THREE WAYS ON THE SAME 1500 COMMITS, same shell, same box:
  single id, grep -c 'rf2-6g6e'          -> 1      (correct)
  129-way alternation, grep -cE          -> 0      (WRONG)
  grep -F -f ids.txt                     -> 36     (correct)
The falsifier that started this: commit c20d7ee62d, 'docs(009): frame-destroyed stops narrating the retired ui bundle as live, and :op is public (rf2-6g6e)', 268 commits from HEAD and therefore well inside the window, on a bead that is OPEN.

WHY THE CONTROL DID NOT CATCH IT, AND THIS IS THE PART WORTH KEEPING. A control WAS run at the time, and it passed. It spliced one known-present closed id onto the END of the same alternation and read 1. So it exercised the alternation's TAIL and proved nothing about its body — a control constructed so that it avoids the case it exists to catch, which is the exact defect class this project's own method tells you to hunt. Splicing at the end is the natural place to splice, which is what makes it dangerous.

WHAT TO DO INSTEAD, and it is one flag: pass the ids as a PATTERN FILE with fixed-string matching, grep -F -f <file>. It has no alternation to overflow, needs no escaping, and was measured correct here. If an alternation is genuinely wanted, splice the control id into the MIDDLE, never the end.

WHAT THE MISS COST: fifteen open beads had landed trunk commits naming them and the sweep reported none. It did not cause a wrong close — the audit caught it first — but the whole point of that sweep is to stop a worker being dispatched at finished work, and a silent zero is the one answer that reads as a clean bill of health.

RELATION TO WHAT IS ALREADY WRITTEN. CLAUDE.md already records that this box's GNU grep 3.0 under MSYS ABORTS on the flag pair -iF (SIGABRT, exit 134, nothing on stdout). This is a DIFFERENT failure on the same tool — no abort, exit 0, a confident zero — so the existing bullet does not cover it and would not have warned anybody. Whether the root cause is a regex-size limit, an MSYS argument-length limit, or something else was NOT established; establishing it is part of this bead, but the remedy above does not depend on the answer.

SCOPE: (1) reproduce the three measurements above and bisect roughly where the alternation starts failing (try 2, 10, 50, 100, 129 ids) so the failure has a stated shape rather than a folk rule; (2) add a bullet to CLAUDE.md's 'Four ways the INSTRUMENTS misreport on this machine' list — it will become five — carrying the measurement, the grep -F -f remedy, and the tail-splice trap; (3) grep the repo for other multi-id or multi-term alternations built the same way and report them, without necessarily fixing them. Do NOT weaken or remove the existing -iF bullet; both are real and they are different.
notes:
A SECOND INSTANCE OF THE SAME CLASS, measured 2026-09-05 by the mayor about half an hour after the first — and this bead should be read as being about the CLASS rather than about grep alternations specifically.

WHAT HAPPENED. A beads checkpoint aborted on a git index.lock collision (a concurrent process in the mayor checkout). To check whether four bd closes had survived into the pushed export, I read HEAD's .beads/issues.jsonl with:
  git show HEAD:.beads/issues.jsonl | grep -F "\"<id>\"" | head -1 | jq -r '.status'
It reported four beads as still OPEN. They were closed. I re-ran the checkpoint, the reading did not change, and for a moment that looked like a durability failure in the tracker — the most alarming class of finding available.

THE INSTRUMENT WAS WRONG, NOT THE DATA. The export is one JSON record per line, and a bead id appears in OTHER beads' records too — dependency lists, discovered-from edges, close-reason prose. So grep matched a record that MENTIONS the id and head -1 took it, and that record's own .status was reported as the target's. Control, run once the suspicion formed: 4 records MENTION rf2-s4dp, exactly 1 IS it. The correct read is a select on the identity field:
  git show HEAD:.beads/issues.jsonl | jq -r --arg i "<id>" 'select(.id==$i)|.status'
which reports all four closed, matching the live database.

WHY IT BELONGS ON THIS BEAD. Same shape as the 129-way alternation: an instrument returning a WELL-FORMED, PLAUSIBLE, WRONG answer with no error, where the failure is in how the question was asked rather than in what was asked about. And the same near-miss on the control — the first instance had a control that exercised the pattern's tail and proved nothing; this one had NO control until suspicion prompted one, and the control is what settled it in a single command.

THE GENERALISATION WORTH WRITING INTO WHATEVER LANDS: when reading a RECORD out of a line-oriented record file, match on the IDENTITY FIELD, never on the identifier appearing anywhere in the line. A grep for an id in a file where ids cross-reference each other answers 'some record containing this id', which is a different question and is right only when nothing cross-references. The mention-versus-is count is the one-line control that distinguishes them, and it is cheap enough to run every time.

ALSO WORTH RECORDING FOR THE SCOPE OF THIS BEAD: the git index.lock collision itself is normal contention in the mayor checkout, not corruption — CLAUDE.md already documents concurrent git processes there. The correct response was to inspect state (lock gone, tree clean, HEAD == origin/main, row counts equal) rather than to retry into it or to 'recover' by restoring an older export from history, which would have time-travelled the tracker. No recovery was needed and none was attempted.
DELIVERED 2026-09-05 by worker claudemd-a — PR #9283 (https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/9283), branch worker/claudemd-a, NOT closed, left in_progress.

ROOT CAUSE ESTABLISHED, and it is NOT a size or argument-length limit. jq on this box writes CRLF. paste -sd'|' therefore joins ids that each end in a carriage return, so every alternative except the LAST ends in \r and matches nothing.

REPRODUCED 2026-09-05, 1500 trunk commits, 99 open ids, one shell:
  grep -F -f ids.txt                     -> 22  (correct)
  paste -sd'|' alternation of same file  ->  1  (wrong)
  same alternation after tr -d '\r'      -> 22  (correct)
The one line the alternation matched named rf2-yo4s — the LAST id in the file, the only alternative without a trailing \r.

BISECT, alternation vs grep -F -f on the same first-N subset:
  N=10  (99 chars)   alt 0   -F -f 3
  N=50  (587 chars)  alt 0   -F -f 16
  N=90  (1078 chars) alt 0   -F -f 18
  N=99  (1169 chars) alt 1   -F -f 22
It already fails at 10 ids / 99 characters, so the size hypothesis in the description is refuted.

PRODUCER ISOLATED TO jq (jq-1.8.1), not bd and not the shell: bd list --json ends its lines LF; echo '[{"id":"aaa"}]' | jq -r '.[].id' ends them CRLF; a single-value $( ... | jq -r ... ) capture comes back clean. So the defect bites exactly where those lines are JOINED or read as patterns.

CORRECTION TO THIS BEAD'S PROPOSED REMEDY, by measurement. The description concludes 'splice the control id into the MIDDLE, never the end'. Measured: the tail splice reads 1 and passes, AND the middle splice also reads 1 and also passes — a spliced shell literal carries no \r wherever it sits, so position does not discriminate at all. The rule that DOES discriminate: the control must be drawn FROM the same file that produced the pattern, i.e. travel the same pipeline as the data. The landed text says that, not 'splice into the middle'.

SCOPE ITEM 3 (other alternations built the same way): swept the tracked tree for paste -sd, tr '\n' '|', join("|") and grep -E over a shell-built variable. The only hit outside CLAUDE.md is .beads/issues.jsonl (this bead's own text). No script in the repo builds a pattern this way; nothing to fix beyond the record.

THE ROOT CAUSE IS NOT WHAT THIS BEAD SAID, and the worker's measurement corrects me. It is NOT a size or argument-length limit. **jq on this box writes CRLF**, so `paste -sd'|'` joins ids each ending in `\r`, and every alternative but the LAST matches nothing. Measured over 1500 trunk commits, 99 open ids, one shell: `grep -F -f` 22, alternation 1, alternation after `tr -d '\r'` 22. The single line the alternation matched named rf2-yo4s — the LAST id in the file, which is the signature of exactly this mechanism. Bisected: it already fails at N=10, 99 characters. Producer isolated to jq-1.8.1 — `bd list --json` ends lines LF, `jq -r` ends them CRLF, and a single-value `$(...)` capture is clean.

MY PROPOSED REMEDY WAS REFUTED BY MEASUREMENT. This bead said: splice the control into the MIDDLE, never the end, because a tail splice exercises nothing of the alternation's body. The tail splice does read 1 and pass — AND SO DOES THE MIDDLE SPLICE, also 1, because a spliced shell literal carries no `\r` wherever it sits. The rule that actually discriminates is that THE CONTROL MUST BE DRAWN FROM THE SAME FILE THAT PRODUCED THE PATTERN. That is what landed, and it is a better rule than mine because it generalises past this one mechanism: a control constructed by hand shares none of the pipeline's corruptions.

description:
_Filed 2026-09-05 12:37:46 AUSEST by the API-review wave-3 coordinator from registry-introspection.md (ref registry-introspection.2); parent epic rf2-kuky. Local-only dossiers: ai/findings/API-review/{fable,codex}/ (gitignored; may be deleted)._

## Problem

The public registry read has two shapes whose documented meaning the tree contradicts. `re-frame.core/registrations` (`implementation/core/src/re_frame/core.cljc:1783`; arities `[arg]` / `[kind pred-fn]`) and `handler-meta` (`:1836`; `[arg]` map-only / `[kind id]`) document the positional-keyword arity as "the default source store" (`spec/API.md:520-521`, `core.cljc` docstrings), but they delegate to `rf.registrar/registrations` (`registrar.cljc:873`) and `rf.registrar/lookup` (`:828`), which consult the dynamic `*generation*` (`:224`) FIRST. `re-frame.live-frame/call-with-frame-resolution` (`live_frame.cljc:330`) binds it around every subscribe build / dispatch / fx / view resolution against an image-loaded frame — and since `make-frame` seals a generation unconditionally, every frame is one. So a "store" read issued inside a sub computation or handler silently reads THAT frame's image instead. Measured cost: Xray runs in its own `:rf/xray` frame and had to write `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/host_registry.cljs`, which derefs the private atom `re-frame.registrar/kind->id->metadata` to see the host app at all (its ns docstring explains the mechanism; 15 call lines in 7 files, required by 9); `spec/API.md:514` then BLESSES that private read ("reads the process source store directly via `re-frame.registrar`"). A public inspection request must say which source it means; a bare keyword cannot.

Second silent swallow on the same door: `:flow` and `:frame` sit in the closed `kinds` set (`registrar.cljc:98-146`) as reserved-EMPTY slots, so `(rf/registrations :flow)` returns `{}` while flows exist in `re-frame.flows`' per-frame store — it bit Xray (`tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/static/flows/panel.cljs:24-29` records the read going dead) and pair-MCP still offers `"flow"` / `"frame"` in its kind enum (`tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/src/re_frame2_pair_mcp/tools/descriptors_data.cljs:1709`, `:1775`).

## Target API

Two operations, one map grammar, exactly one source selector:

```clojure
;; store reads — the process-global registrar, NEVER routed through a bound *generation*
(rf/registrations {:source :store :kind :event})                 ; => {id meta} or {}
(rf/handler-meta  {:source :store :kind :event :id :cart/add})   ; => meta or nil
(rf/handler-meta  {:source :store :kind :machine-guard :id [:auth/login :form-valid?]}) ; derived, unchanged meaning

;; frame reads — resolved through live frame f's OWN sealed image generation (today's map form, unchanged)
(rf/registrations {:frame app-frame :kind :event})
(rf/handler-meta  {:frame app-frame :kind :resource :id :articles/list})

;; projections are Clojure, not library operations
(keys (rf/registrations {:source :store :kind :route}))
(into {} (filter (fn [[_ m]] (:rf/machine? m))) (rf/registrations {:source :store :kind :event}))
(:rf/resource (rf/handler-meta {:source :store :kind :resource :id :articles/list}))
```

Rules: a map with BOTH `:source` and `:frame`, or NEITHER, or a non-map argument, throws a catalogued error — rename today's `:rf.error/registrar-query-needs-frame` (`core.cljc:1672` `assert-registrar-query-has-frame!`; `spec/009-Instrumentation.md:2302`; 16 lines / 2 test files consume the id) to `:rf.error/registrar-query-needs-source`, since "needs frame" is no longer the truth. `:source` admits only `:store` (leave the door open for a future value; reject anything else). `:frame` keeps `resolve-live-frame-object` (`core.cljc:1632`) + `call-with-frame-resolution` and its `:rf.error/frame-no-generation` failure — no fallback. `:kind` outside `rf.registrar/kinds` → the existing `:rf.error/unknown-registry-kind` (`registrar.cljc:588`, currently thrown by `register-handler`; throw it from the query path too with `where` naming the query fn). `:kind :flow` or `:frame` (reserved-empty slots) → a new catalogued `:rf.error/registrar-kind-not-queryable` whose message names the real door (`re-frame.flows/flows-snapshot` / `flow-meta-at`; `rf/frame-ids` / `frame-meta`) — never `{}`. `:frame` + `:machine-guard` / `:machine-action` stays `nil` as documented today (pair-mcp refuses before emitting); codex: extending frame-targeted derived lookups is not required.

Implementation of `:source :store`: read the atom without consulting `*generation*` — add `rf.registrar/store-registrations` / `store-lookup` (`(get @(active-registrar) kind {})` / paired `get`) and call them from the facade. Do NOT change `rf.registrar/registrations` / `lookup` / `ids` / `handler-meta` themselves: 80 internal call lines in 35 files resolve events / fx / subs / views through them and MUST stay generation-routed (codex: "implement this distinction at the public inspection boundary, not by globally changing `registrar/lookup`"). Both facade fns are `.cljc`; the grammar is identical on the JVM.

## Corroboration

Two-reviewer. Codex `registration-inspection.md` §Proposed smaller API ("Give both the same map grammar with exactly one source selector: `:source :store`, or `:frame f` … Supplying both, or neither, is an invalid query … Retire positional reads, the generic predicate overloads"; §Codex Thoughts: "Reject reserved-but-empty query kinds clearly rather than silently returning an apparently authoritative empty catalogue"). Fable §Codex cross-check item 1 adopts it verbatim ("the positional keyword form goes with the aliases"; the map form was fable's own target). title: api(egress): one policy vocabulary — closed walker opts, `projected-record` reads `:rf.size/*`, fix teaching
description:
_Filed 2026-09-05 12:37:46 AUSEST by the API-review wave-3 coordinator from egress.md (ref egress.2); parent epic rf2-kuky. Local-only dossiers: ai/findings/API-review/{fable,codex}/ (gitignored; may be deleted)._

## Problem

On a privacy surface a RECOGNISED policy key can vanish without a signal, in both directions:

1. `rf/elide-wire-value` does not read `:rf.egress/profile` — the key does not occur in `implementation/core/src/re_frame/elision.cljc` (0 hits at tip); only `re-frame.projection/resolve-elision-opts` (`projection.cljc:190-221`) resolves it. Yet three normative teaching sites pass a profile to the walker, where it is silently dropped: `spec/015-Data-Classification.md:223-227` (the walker example carries `:rf.egress/profile :rf.egress/off-box-tool`), `skills/re-frame2/references/cross-cutting/privacy-and-elision.md:189-191` (same example), and `spec/Conventions.md:825` (`(rf/elide-wire-value v {:include-sensitive? false})` — a BARE key the walker does not read either; harmless only because `false` is the default).
2. `rf/projected-record` reads the bare spelling ONLY: `implementation/epoch/src/re_frame/epoch/tool_pair.cljc:1303-1320` (`egress-opts` destructures `{:keys [include-sensitive? include-large?]}` and re-spells them to `:rf.size/*` at :1319-1320). A caller passing `:rf.size/include-sensitive? true` — the spelling the walker, `project-egress`, `:rf/project-egress-opts`, Conventions §`:rf.size/*` and ~54 sites use — is silently dropped there. Pair-MCP's eval builder chose the bare spelling for exactly that reason (`tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/src/re_frame2_pair_mcp/tools/epoch_egress.cljs:146-149`: `"{:rf.egress/profile :rf.egress/off-box-tool :include-sensitive? true}"`).

Census at tip, non-test `implementation/*/src` + `tools/*/src` (`git grep -o`, re-measure): `:rf.egress/profile` 55, `:rf.size/include-sensitive?` 54, bare `include-sensitive?` 46, bare `include-large?` 26, `:rf.size/include-large?` 24, `:rf.size/include-digests?` 18. The MCP wire key `include-sensitive` (no `?`) is a fourth spelling on a different layer with a written reason (`tools/mcp-base/src/re_frame/mcp_base/sensitive.cljc:17-27`) and is NOT in scope.

## Evidence

- `elision.cljc:1108-1152` (the walker reads `:frame :path :query-v :as-of-epoch :rf.size/include-sensitive? :rf.size/include-large? :rf.size/include-digests? :rf.size/threshold-bytes` — `elide-against-frame` :1032-1066 enumerates them; `:rf.size/elision-policy`, reserved at `spec/Conventions.md:96`, has 0 readers in `implementation/*/src` and `tools/*/src`).
- `projection.cljc:186-221` (`size-override-keys`, `resolve-elision-opts`; the nil-profile "raw-flags" arm :207-210).
- `tool_pair.cljc:1282-1301` (`resolve-egress-profile`), :1303-1320 (`egress-opts`), and the bare epoch-only axes at :1364 (`include-runtime-db?`), :1957 (`include-fx-args?`), :2015 (`include-event-args?`), :1527/:1583/:1623/:1689/:1737/:1800 (trace-event / large helpers).
- `spec/Spec-Schemas.md:3662-3688` — `:rf/project-egress-opts` is `[:map {:closed false} …]` (:3672).
- `spec/Tool-Pair.md:885` teaches "the operator's `:include-sensitive` opt-in is passed as the `:include-sensitive? true` egress opt to `projected-record`"; `spec/Security.md:103, :105` and `spec/Privacy.md:499` spell the epoch defaults bare.

## Target API

Recommendation (of the two the review offered — fix the teaching vs make the walker honour the profile): **fix the teaching, and make both doors LOUD on the spelling they do not read.** Rationale: making the walker resolve profiles would require moving the profile table below `re-frame.projection` (which requires `re-frame.elision`), and it deepens the two-door equivalence that egress.5 exists to rule on; a thrown `:rf.error/bad-egress-opts` costs a `contains?` check, holds under every egress.5 outcome, and is codex's "loud diagnostics for retired / misspelled policy keys".

```clojure
;; 1. elide-wire-value — opts are CLOSED
;;    accepted: :frame :path :query-v :as-of-epoch
;;              :rf.size/include-sensitive? :rf.size/include-large?
;;              :rf.size/include-digests?   :rf.size/threshold-bytes
(rf/elide-wire-value v {:frame f :rf.egress/profile :rf.egress/off-box-tool})
;; => throws {:rf.error/id :rf.error/bad-egress-opts
;;            :recovery    :pass-the-profile-to-project-egress
;;            :extra       {:unknown-keys [:rf.egress/profile] :accepted [...]}}

;; 2. projected-record — one spelling for the two shared axes; opts CLOSED
;;    accepted: :rf.egress/profile
;;              :rf.size/include-sensitive? :rf.size/include-large?
;;              :include-fx-args? :include-runtime-db? :include-event-args?   ; epoch-local knobs, bare (API.md:919-922 discriminator)
(rf/projected-record r {:rf.egress/profile :rf.egress/off-box-tool :rf.size/include-sensitive? true})
(rf/projected-record r {:include-sensitive? true})   ; => throws :rf.error/bad-egress-opts

;; 3. project-egress — opts CLOSED (Spec-Schemas :rf/project-egress-opts {:closed true});
;;    an unknown key reaches the walker after resolve-elision-opts and throws there.
```

Teaching after the change: `spec/015:223-227` and `privacy-and-elision.md:189-191` show the walker with `:frame` / `:path` / `:rf.size/*` only, and say in one sentence that the profile belongs to `project-egress`; `spec/Conventions.md:825` shows `{:rf.size/include-sensitive? false}` (the bare form is deleted from the example; the paragraph's VERB rule — `include-` for off-box, `show-` for on-box — is unchanged). The three epoch-only axes stay bare pending egress.5 (which decides the `:rf.egress/include-*?` namespace question); do not rename `:rf.size/*` here (Grok: separable 50+ site churn).

## Corroboration

One-reviewer for the closed maps (Grok slice (2)-(3)); codex: "choose one inclusion-key vocabulary and one normalizer, with a documented default profile and loud diagnostics for retired / misspelled policy keys … retaining the current `:rf.size/*` spelling everywhere is also viable and cheaper. Renaming alone is not the benefit: identical interpretation at every boundary is." This bead is the identical-interpretation half; the rename is egress.5's.

## Deletion list

- `tool_pair.cljc:1316-1320` — the bare-key destructure and re-spelling in `egress-opts`; the bare `:include-sensitive?` / `:include-large?` reads in the slot helpers (:1527-1528, :1623-1624, :1689-1690, :1737-1738, :1800-1809) move to `:rf.size/*`.
- `epoch_egress.cljs:146-149` — the bare `:include-sensitive? true` literal (becomes `:rf.size/include-sensitive? true`).
- `spec/Conventions.md:825` — the `(rf/elide-wire-value v {:include-sensitive? false})` example form.
- `spec/Spec-Schemas.md:3672` — `{:closed false}`.

## Consumers to migrate

- pair-MCP: `epoch_egress.cljs:106-149` (`egress-opts-edn`) and the eval forms at :193 and :245; its pins `tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/test/re_frame2_pair_mcp/egress_elision_test.cljs` and `implementation/epoch/test/re_frame/epoch_mcp_egress_conformance_test.clj`. The direct-read builders (`elision.cljs:142-200` `elision-opts-edn`, `get_path.cljs:51-58`, `snapshot.cljs:167, :177`, `read_sub.cljs:117`, `dispatch_dry_run.cljs:222`) already render `:rf.size/*` + `:path` / `:frame` / `:query-v` — verify no other key is rendered (closed walker).
- Descriptor prose that spells the epoch opts bare: `tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/src/re_frame2_pair_mcp/tools/descriptors_data.cljs:777, :824` and `tool-descriptors.edn` (regenerate with the pair-MCP descriptor generator, `clojure -M:gen`, and its `--check` gate).
- Framework-internal walker callers (10 sites, listed in egress.1) pass only accepted keys today; `reply.cljc:661` and `routing/sub_egress.cljc:125` forward an `opts` map — verify the maps they forward carry nothing else. `projection.cljc:234-240` (`walk-slot`) passes `elision-opts` = opts minus the profile — after `project-egress`'s map is closed nothing else can reach it.
- Xray `local_render.cljc:251-253` passes `{:rf.egress/profile … :rf.size/include-large? true :frame …}` to `project-egress` (accepted); story-mcp `egress.cljc:157-166` (`posture->elision-opts`, `:rf.size/*` via the mcp-base mirror) and :209-211 / :332-337 (accepted); preload `runtime.cljs:3102-3108` merges MCP-supplied `elide-opts` — accepted keys only (verify with the pair-MCP builder).
- Test files touching the doors at tip (re-measure): `elide-wire-value` 53, `project-egress` 25, `projected-record` 20 — the closed maps will red any test passing a stray key; that is the point.

## Spec, docs, examples, skills, tests

- Spec (hot-zone, one-toucher): `spec/API.md:685` (walker row: enumerate the closed key set, name `:rf.error/bad-egress-opts`), `:697` (`project-egress` row: "opts conforms to `:rf/project-egress-opts`" now closed), `:907` (`:epoch-history` configure row is untouched — `:redact-fn` is egress.3); `spec/Conventions.md:825`; `spec/Tool-Pair.md:885` (`:include-sensitive? true` → `:rf.size/include-sensitive? true`; the orthogonal-axes sentence keeps the three bare epoch knobs); `spec/Spec-Schemas.md:3662-3688` (`{:closed true}`, the "with no profile the flags pass through verbatim" bullet stays); `spec/009-Instrumentation.md` — add `:rf.error/bad-egress-opts` to the error catalogue (single source of truth, §Error event catalogue :2936) and to the `:rf.error/*` conformance pin `implementation/core/test/re_frame/error_catalogue_channel_conformance_test.clj`.
- Spec (non-hot): `spec/015-Data-Classification.md:223-227` (walker example), `:229` ("sinks / tools should rarely call it directly" — keep); `spec/Security.md:103, :105, :264` (`:include-sensitive? false` → `:rf.size/…`); `spec/Privacy.md:499` and the `projected-record` row :122.
- Docs: `docs/api/re-frame.core.md:1253` (`projected-record` opts) and `docs/api/re-frame.epoch.md` `projected-record` section; `docs/core/how-to/keep-secrets-out-of-traces.md:293-304` (already teaches `project-egress` for direct reads — no change).
- Skills: `privacy-and-elision.md:173, :189-191`; `api-cheatsheet.md:158` (walker row lists `:include-large?` unqualified in prose — qualify).
- Code docstrings: `elision.cljc:1068-1107`; `epoch.cljc:701-731` (`projected-record` contract); `core_epoch.cljc:192-254`; `core.cljc:2480-2493`.
- Tests to add: walker throws on `:rf.egress/profile`, on a bare `:include-sensitive?`, and on an arbitrary unknown key, naming the offending keys; `projected-record` throws on the bare spelling and honours `:rf.size/include-sensitive? true` (the app-db axis lifts, fx-args / runtime-db / large stay closed — the `epoch_mcp_egress_conformance_test.clj` shape); `project-egress` throws on an unknown key for a kindless value AND for each `:rf.observe/*` kind; all six profiles still resolve (`projection_cljs_test.cljc`).
- `spec/api-manifest.edn`: no var added or removed; the keyword-drift gate (`test.yml` "Keyword drift gate", rf2-1nci83) will see the new `:rf.error/bad-egress-opts` — register it where that gate reads.
- Migration README: none.

## Sequencing and hot-zone

Touches `spec/API.md`, `spec/Conventions.md`, `spec/Tool-Pair.md`, `spec/Spec-Schemas.md`, `spec/009-Instrumentation.md` — one-toucher, serialise with egress.3 and egress.6. `rf2-qqn9` edits `elision.cljc` — rebase order as for egress.1.

## Risks

Throwing inside the trace chokepoint (`classification.cljc:755, :779`) on a stray key is a dev-time loud failure by design; the 10 internal sites pass only accepted keys at tip, and `error_emit.cljc:556` / `event_emit.cljc:140` already wrap the walk in try/catch. title: test(http,examples): deterministic overlap witness for Nine States newest-intent-wins
description:
Follow-up to rf2-t9va. That bead's fix landed the shared stable `:request-id`
(`nine-states.core/data-load-request-id`) on both live request shapes and both
Story twins, entirely inside `examples/patterns/**`. Its acceptance criteria
ALSO called for a deterministic CLJS regression proving newest-intent-wins.
That test cannot live in the example tree — examples are test-free (rf2-8cevm,
no `*.spec.cjs` under `examples/`) — and the worker's fence excluded
`implementation/**` (a peer was live on `implementation/adapters/reagent/test`
in the same wave), so the witness was deferred here rather than smuggled into a
locked/fenced tree.

## What to write

A single-frame CLJS test on a CONTROLLED/deferred managed-HTTP transport (not
the synchronous canned stub, and not a hand-dispatched `:fetch-succeeded`):

- hold request A open; issue B through the shipped example event
  (`:nine-states.demo/load`) before A settles;
- prove A's later success or failure reaches NO app target and cannot move or
  mutate the `:ui/nine-states` machine (supersession suppresses the superseded
  attempt's app reply — `registry/supersede!`, `:reason
  :request-id-superseded`);
- settle B and prove exactly B's `:items` / `:error`, the `:data` region state
  and tags, and the `:ui/render` result;
- include at least one CROSS-KIND row (old success vs new failure, or old
  failure vs new success) so `:nine-states.demo/load` and
  `:nine-states.demo/load-with-failure` are proven to share one replacement
  lane;
- cover reset-then-new-load: `:reset` alone does not abort the in-flight
  request, so the protection there is the same-id supersession on the reload,
  not the existing `reset`-to-`:nothing` test (which settles a completion while
  still at `:nothing`, where it is trivially ignored);
- a negative control: removing or changing the shared id makes the overlap
  witness FAIL.

## Where

Natural home is beside the existing example suite,
`implementation/adapters/reagent/test/re_frame/nine_states_cljs_test.cljs`
(reached by `npm run test:cljs` — `adapters/reagent/test` is on the `:node-test`
classpath). `implementation/http/test/re_frame/http_cljs_test.cljs` already
carries the transport-level same-id supersession regression and is the harness
precedent to follow rather than inventing a new controlled-fetch helper.

## Why the example alone is not enough

The shipped app routes `:rf.http/managed` through an `:fx-overrides` demo stub,
which REPLACES the effect outright — the framework's in-flight registry, and
with it supersession, never runs there, and canned replies settle
synchronously. So no gate currently executes the superseding path for this
example; the fix is compile-verified and contract-verified only.
close_reason: PR #9275. Witness landed at implementation/http/test/re_frame/nine_states_overlap_cljs_test.cljs — NOT under examples/ (test-free, rf2-8cevm) and NOT in the adapters/reagent tree the bead nominated, which was fenced to a peer worker this wave. The http artefact is the right shelf on the merits: the subject is the managed-HTTP in-flight registry and its same-:request-id supersession, this artefact's own contract, and http_managed_demo_frame_isolation_cljs_test.cljs is the standing precedent for an example-behaviour regression parked there. shadow-cljs.edn's own comment on the ../examples/* source roots states the rule outright. Deterministic by construction: js/fetch is stubbed with a transport that PARKS each attempt inside its own body read, so the test holds the resolver and PLACES the interleaving rather than racing for it — the multi-attempt form of re-frame.http-cljs-test's with-controlled-body-fetch. Frames carry no :fx-overrides so the real effect runs. Covers three overlap rows including cross-kind in BOTH directions; each settles the older attempt first and proves the machine did not move before settling the newer and proving exactly its :items/:error, data-region state, tag and :ui/render. Reset-then-reload asserts :reset does NOT abort the in-flight attempt, so the protection is the same-id supersession on the reload. Negative control is an executable assertion rather than a one-shot mutation: a test-local event issues the identical request under a DIFFERENT :request-id and the witness inverts (stale reply lands and clobbers the machine). Per-row isolation is inside the driver, not a fixture (a :each fixture resets once per deftest, not per table row); one row is additionally pinned running alone. Gates: http JVM 525/3969 exit 0; clj-kondo 0 errors 0 warnings; both ratchets exit 0, with the alias gate confirmed to SEE the new file (census 2793->2794 files, 10851->10857 edges, non-canonical unchanged at 2446, so all six re-frame aliases are canonical). npm run test:cljs deliberately NOT run — it is the only lane executing this file, but it compiles a shadow-cljs build and concurrent workers were live; CI owns it. Every framework API the file calls was verified against its definition first. No production or example change.

title: bug(mcp-base): sorted collection comparators crash default-on structural dedup when cache refs replace keys or elements
description:
## Scope

Make the shared structural-dedup walk in tools/mcp-base/src/re_frame/mcp_base/dedup.cljc safe for ordinary persistent sorted maps and sorted sets. Add focused cross-host base coverage and one small Story-MCP wire-boundary integration pin. Keep the dedup wire format, reference grammar, envelope, default-on posture, and public tool APIs unchanged.

## Correctness finding

The generic side-walk rebuilds each collection with (into (empty form) (map inner form)). During the substitution pass, process-element replaces a repeated cacheable subtree with a de-dupe.cache/cache-N symbol. If that subtree occurs as a sorted-map key or sorted-set element, the original collection comparator receives the temporary symbol.

A default sorted collection with one replaced vector key/element and one unreplaced vector key/element therefore compares a Symbol with an IPersistentVector and throws ClassCastException. This is valid persistent application data, not a malformed cache or hostile input. The default-on shrink step turns an otherwise successful AI/devtools read into a boundary failure.

## Evidence

- tools/mcp-base/src/re_frame/mcp_base/dedup.cljc:351-363 documents side-walk as recognizing every Clojure collection, then rebuilds the generic coll branch into (empty form).
- dedup.cljc:369-381 makes vectors longer than two elements cacheable.
- dedup.cljc:480-497 replaces a repeated cacheable subtree with a cache-element symbol before the enclosing collection is rebuilt.
- The measured stack reaches PersistentTreeMap.assoc through clojure.core/into and re_frame.mcp_base.dedup$side_walk at dedup.cljc:362.
- tools/mcp-base/spec/dedup.md:8-17 says the codec walks persistent data and expand reconstructs it exactly; lines 36-45 make de-dupe-eq and its exact inverse the owned surface.
- tools/mcp-base/test/re_frame/mcp_base/dedup_test.cljc:425-436 is named expand-round-trips-every-collection-kind, but covers list, seq, hash-set, and nested hash maps only. It never puts a cacheable repeat in a comparator-bearing key/element position.
- The real Story consumer reproduces the same throw through re-frame.story-mcp.tools.wire-pipeline/apply-dedup. tools/story-mcp/src/re_frame/story_mcp/tools/wire_pipeline.cljc:121-161 applies the base transform to structuredContent; lines 373-406 place it after the handler catch.
- Story run-variant and preview-variant are default-on dedup-eligible and carry app-db/snapshot values (tools/story-mcp/src/re_frame/story_mcp/tools/testing.cljc:305-319 and tools/story-mcp/src/re_frame/story_mcp/tools/dev.cljc:223-237).
- Pair-MCP's epoch/snapshot paths call the same default-on dedup-value (tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/src/re_frame2_pair_mcp/tools/wire_pipeline.cljs:167-200 and snapshot_pipeline.cljs:245-261).
- Sorted maps are explicitly legitimate SPA state in this repository: examples/core/todomvc/db.cljs:28-30,40-50,65-82 says its sorted map is non-incidental. That example's numeric keys do not trigger this exact comparator mismatch, but the collection class is deliberately supported application state.

## Steps to Reproduce

From tools/mcp-base, evaluate the real codec with shared-key [1 2 3], unique-key [4 5 6], and:

    {:index (sorted-map shared-key :old unique-key :new)
     :again shared-key}

Call (dedup/dedup-value payload true).

Observed controls and failure:

- The equivalent hash-map shape returns a real rf.mcp/dedup-table wrapper and expand round-trips true.
- The sorted-map shape with dedup disabled passes through and remains equal.
- The sorted-map shape with dedup enabled throws java.lang.ClassCastException: clojure.lang.Symbol cannot be cast to clojure.lang.IPersistentVector.
- Replacing sorted-map with sorted-set produces the same ClassCastException.
- Passing the sorted-map payload through Story-MCP wire-pipeline/apply-dedup with enabled true throws the identical exception.

## Failure scenario / invariant

An SPA stores an index in a sorted map keyed by path vectors. Across epoch snapshots, or across Story's app-db/snapshot/evidence duplication, an existing vector key repeats while a newly added vector key appears only once. Dedup substitutes the repeated key with a cache symbol, rebuilds it beside the unique vector key through the tree comparator, and the AI's read fails instead of returning state.

Invariant: default wire shrinking must accept ordinary persistent sorted maps/sets and either compress them or safely keep comparator-position values inline. It must never feed codec-only placeholders into a collection comparator that cannot compare them.

## Recommended minimal fix

Make the shared CLJC walk comparator-safe specifically for sorted maps and sorted sets. The smallest likely rule is to lower sorted collections to comparator-neutral wire maps/sets before placeholder substitution; EDN/JSON does not preserve a custom comparator in any case. Another acceptable small rule is to keep comparator positions inline while still handling their descendants, provided the existing reference-collision escaping remains correct.

Choose one local rule in the shared walker. Preserve semantic Clojure equality on expand and retain a real dedup win for repeated data. Do not add a fallback serialization framework or a second codec.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A cross-host dedup_test.cljc regression builds a default sorted-map with two vector keys and repeats only one key elsewhere, forcing the pre-fix mixed Symbol/vector comparator case. dedup-value with enabled true does not throw, produces a real dedup-table wrapper with a substitution beyond cache-0, and expand is equal to the input.
2. The same root cause is pinned compactly for sorted-set elements so both comparator-bearing core collection shapes cannot regress.
3. Story-MCP wire-pipeline/apply-dedup accepts the sorted-map structuredContent and keeps its text and structuredContent slots consistent rather than throwing. No consumer production logic should be needed.
4. An unordered-map control still wraps and round-trips, and enabled false remains strict pass-through. The de-dupe.cache/cache-N grammar, rf.mcp/dedup-table wrapper, cache-0 root, defaults, and tool names/arguments do not change.
5. Focused mcp-base JVM dedup, mcp-base CLJS, and Story-MCP dedup suites pass. A red control restoring the comparator-unsafe branch reproduces the focused failure before restore.

## Non-goals

- Preserving or serializing sorted comparator identity across EDN/JSON.
- A general serializer, arbitrary Java collection support, or an exhaustive exotic-collection taxonomy.
- Changing equality-vs-identity pooling, compression thresholds, default-on behavior, cache-id allocation, or the wire format.
- Optimizing compression ratios beyond retaining the existing real substitution.
- Combining malformed hand-authored cache hardening (dangling references or cycles); the earlier rf2-kjv05 explicitly left that separate case out of scope.

## Posture fit

This is one local correctness repair at an existing generic boundary: valid SPA state should be transparent to default-on AI tooling. It adds no public API and does not litigate every collection detail.

## Related / duplicate search

An all-status rg census covered all 938 issue records in .beads/issues.jsonl and was repeated against origin/main. Searches covered sorted-map, sorted map, sorted-set, sorted set, comparator, PersistentTreeMap, side-walk, empty form, cacheable map key, ClassCastException, dedup, de-dupe, and mcp-base across titles/descriptions/notes. No issue owns this outcome.

Closest records are not duplicates:

- rf2-kjv05 (closed) owns reference-token collisions between payload data and cache ids. Its implementation notes explicitly leave malformed dangling-cache behavior as a non-goal; it does not cover valid sorted collections or comparator failure.
- rf2-6r9j.238 (closed) only corrects the private cacheability predicate's spelling.
- rf2-ntbd1 (closed) proposed relocating the pair-only diff codec and was rejected as gold-plating; it does not concern dedup collection semantics.

Git history confirms the generic (into (empty form) ...) branch is unchanged since vendoring commit 9a4f5553f4 (2026-07-27). Later dedup commits change reference escaping and naming, not sorted-collection handling. No matching commit subject was found.

## Uncertainty

The failure is directly reproduced on the JVM in both mcp-base and the real Story wire adapter. CLJS was not executed during this read-only review because the dedicated worktree has no node_modules and the review explicitly prohibited creating a junction. The comparator-unsafe branch is shared CLJC, but the acceptance test must establish the CLJS result rather than treating that as proven.
acceptance_criteria: Cross-host base regressions cover mixed substituted/unsubstituted vector keys in a default sorted-map and elements in a sorted-set, force a real dedup wrapper, and prove expand equality without a comparator exception. Story apply-dedup returns consistent text/structured slots for the same payload. Unordered and disabled controls remain intact; wire grammar and tool API are unchanged. Focused JVM, CLJS, and Story dedup suites pass with a red control for the pre-fix branch.
close_reason: Fixed on worker/mcpbase-a, PR https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/9262. The shared side-walk now rebuilds sorted maps/sets into their unsorted counterparts (rebuild-into), so a de-dupe.cache/cache-N placeholder never reaches a tree comparator. Wire format, reference grammar, envelope, default-on posture and tool APIs unchanged; expand equality is exact by Clojure equality, which the bead's non-goals sanction (comparator identity is explicitly not preserved across EDN/JSON). Coverage: two focused cross-host regressions (pooled key beside an unpooled one; the same in sorted-set element position) with unordered and enabled-false controls, expand-round-trips-every-collection-kind extended to the two kinds its name claimed and now pinning the lowering, and one story-mcp apply-dedup integration pin (test only, no consumer production logic). Red control reproduced 2 failures + 2 errors on JVM and CLJS and 1 error in story-mcp before restore, restore verified by SHA-256. NEW FINDING answering the bead's stated Uncertainty: CLJS IS affected too, reporting 'Cannot compare [4 5 6] to de-dupe.cache/cache-1'.
