title: shadow-cljs compile server-test exits 0 with failing autorun tests - a fail-open gate signal
description:
`shadow-cljs compile server-test` in tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp exits 0 even when its autorun reports test FAILURES. Measured by the worker on PR #9121: the compile exited 0 with 4 test failures in the autorun output. Only the separate `node out/server-test.js` invocation is a verdict.

WHY THIS MATTERS BEYOND ONE SCRIPT: this is a fail-OPEN gate. Anything - a worker, a brief, a CI step, a script - that reads the compile's exit code as a test result reads a clean pass over real failures. It is the same class as the piped-gate hazard already in CLAUDE.md (a pipeline's exit status is its last command's), reached through a build tool instead of a shell.

WHAT TO DO. Establish first whether any CI job or local script actually reads that exit code as a test verdict - `git grep` for `compile server-test` and for the build id across `.github/workflows/`, `scripts/`, `tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/`, and any npm script. Two independent instruments plus a control that fires.

- If a real consumer reads it as a verdict: fix the consumer to run `node out/server-test.js` and read THAT exit code. Do not try to make shadow-cljs itself fail the compile on autorun failures unless that is genuinely configurable and cheap - the compile succeeded, which is what a compile exit code means.
- If no consumer reads it: this is documentation, not a defect. Record the trap where a reader will meet it (the pair-mcp README or its test docs) and close.

Either way say which, with the census that decided it.

NOT IN SCOPE: changing what the autorun does, or adding a new gate. The point is that an existing signal is being misread, or could be.
close_reason: Census settled it and a real consumer existed. The ONLY thing in the repo that turned `shadow-cljs compile server-test`'s exit code into a TEST VERDICT was tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/deps.edn's own `:test` alias (`-m shadow.cljs.devtools.cli compile server-test`, no node run) — a per-artefact deps.edn, so in fence. Fixed there: the alias now fails CLOSED (exit 2) naming `npm test`. Deleting it was measured to be WORSE (clojure -M:test on an ABSENT alias drops to a REPL and exits 0 on EOF). NO CI job or repo script read the compile exit as a verdict: test.yml's node-test-tools-re-frame2-pair-mcp runs `npm test`, expensive-tests.yml and test.yml's conformance job compile the `:server` bundle (a build step, not a suite), and implementation/scripts/test-mcp-conformance.cjs's row is {exe:'npm',args:['test']}. package.json's `test` chains with && and ends on node, so its status is Node's. Fail-open reproduced with captured exit codes on one unmodified build: compile printed 'Ran 1120 tests / 4068 assertions. 2 failures, 0 errors.' exit 0; node out/server-test.js printed the identical tally exit 1 (those 2 failures were LOCAL — a live nREPL the no-port harness found — not a repo red). Trap also documented in tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/test/README.md. PR: worker/gatetruth-a.

    git -C re-frame2 rev-parse HEAD    # record this in the log header

So each workspace lands on whatever `main` happened to be at the instant its
clone ran. Assembling the two pilots minutes apart therefore builds them on
DIFFERENT TREES, and nothing in the procedure notices.

MEASURED, not theorised. Two clones issued in the same tick during this run:
  pilot 1 -> ed0a0c29a7b761283eaf443c5f95f0f10d4d7c78
  pilot 2 -> 4893d007b6db5dbc2cb6f282f743429ae7d13a66

(error_emit.cljc, frame.cljc, core_artefact.cljc under rf2-6sqv). The operator
noticed only by reading both pins back and comparing them; step 1 as written
invites recording each pin independently into its own log header, where the
divergence is invisible.

WHY IT MATTERS. rf2-hic-063's ruling explicitly PERMITS the two pilots to run
in parallel, and the whole point of two pilots is two independent readings OF
THE SAME PRODUCT. Two pilots on different commits measure two different
products, and their friction logs are then not comparable with each other, nor
against the counted run that rf2-hic-063 says is read against them. It is the
same class of defect as rf2-v6l6 (a green check that measured the wrong thing)
reached through the clone rather than through the port.

it out in both workspaces, e.g. a third line `git -C re-frame2 checkout
--detach <sha>` with the surrounding prose saying the operator picks ONE sha
for both pilots and that `rev-parse HEAD` afterwards is a verification rather
than a discovery. The operator on this run did exactly that by hand and pinned
both at 4893d007b6db5dbc2cb6f282f743429ae7d13a66.

CLAIM

The Step 3 table (:70-92) has no row for the Reagent mount call.

TRUTH AT TIP
- Every v1 Reagent app mounts through `reagent.dom/render` (or `reagent.core/render`), not `ReactDOM.render`. Under the bridge (`day8/re-frame2-reagent` → stock `reagent/reagent 2.0.1`, `implementation/adapters/reagent/deps.edn:15`) that Var still resolves but `js/console.warn`s "react-dom/render function doesn't exist, you are likely trying to use the old DOM api with React 19. - The corpus already knows this: `migration/from-re-frame-v1/README.md` §M-42 ("on the bridge the Var warns and no-ops at runtime; the render call site needs the same `create-root` + `render` rewrite either way") and the sibling leaf `guided-handlers-state.md:446-472` carries the per-site recipe and the grep ("grep for call sites of `render` (`reagent.dom/render`, `reagent.core/render`)"). `sequencing.md:125` (Group 7 #30) sequences it.

Step 5's rule-driven backstop reaches M-42 only via `breaking-changes.md` row 71, whose trigger column reads "React-19-removed Reagent surfaces (specific list in MIGRATION.md)" — no grep target in the row.

IMPACT
The one v1 surface present in 100% of Reagent apps is the one the inventory never greps, and it fails the silent way (compiles, boots to a blank page). A migration that follows Steps 1-5 and the floor gate as written reaches Phase 4 with "compile clean, tests pass" and a dead mount. P2: missed breaking surface, silent.

No gate validates the regex — verify by hand against a v1 fixture: `rg` the widened pattern over any v1 Reagent app and confirm the root mount is a hit.

title: ssr-node crossing (E/6): native-Hicasso product witness — hicasso.server body-only entry + login example server bundle
description:
Slice E of the ssr-node crossing programme — the PRODUCT witness. Parent rf2-8arzr's RULING note (2026-09-02, delegated by Mike) is the canonical record: read its shared contract S1-S7 first; this description carries only E's own brief. Depends on D being MERGED. The ruling settled the witness question: it is native Hicasso; a Reagent example does NOT substitute (a Reagent root already renders on the JVM, so Reagent-over-Node proves machinery nobody would ship).

## Scope (fence)

- `implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/server.cljs`: ADD a body-only entry beside `render`; do NOT change `render`'s settled spellings (naming-ledger row 22, `docs/design/hicasso/product/naming-ledger.md`). Its CLJS test lives in `implementation/hicasso/test/` under the existing `:node-test-hicasso` build (no build change for the test).
- `examples/substrates/hicasso/login/`: extend the ONLY native-Hicasso example rather than start a new app — add `server.cljs` publishing the sidecar module contract (`{protocol, buildId, entries, render}`) with an entry table naming the login root, its `stateAllowlist` and the runtime-partition allowlist from slice C, and a small Clojure `server.clj` wiring `ssr-handler` + `re-frame.ssr.ring.node/renderer` + `:render-state` + `:payload`. Update the example README.
- `implementation/shadow-cljs.edn` (HOT-ZONE — queue): ONE `:examples/login-hicasso-server` `:node-library` build beside `:examples/login-hicasso` (~:1622).
- No Playwright spec under `examples/` (examples are test-free — rf2-8cevm); the witness lives under `implementation/hicasso/test/` or `implementation/ssr-ring/test/`.

## Do

`re-frame.hicasso.server/render-body` (name is the worker's within the naming ledger's rules): takes the restored snapshot via `render-state/restore!` (slice C) into a FRESH per-request frame — no boot-event replay, no `:snapshot`/`:initial-events` re-seeding — then `mount/tree` + `renderToString` with `:identifier-prefix`, returns the INNER markup only (no payload, no document), tears the frame down in a `finally`, and FAILS the render (throws, which the sidecar turns into a refusal) if the Hicasso runtime recorded a recovered render error during the pass — the JVM's post-render error accumulator cannot see inside the Node frame, so a swallowed error there would ship a wrong page as a success. The module wrapper publishes `render-body` as the entry's `render`. The client boots with `hydrate-root!` and the SAME `identifierPrefix`, reading the `__rf_payload` the JVM wrote.

## Acceptance

1. `npx shadow-cljs compile :examples/login-hicasso-server` and the `:examples/login-hicasso` client build both green; `npm run test:examples-compile` green.
2. An end-to-end test (CLJS in `implementation/hicasso/test`, or JVM in `implementation/ssr-ring/test` — worker's call) proving: the login page is server-rendered from a server-only value that is ABSENT from `__rf_payload`; route or machine runtime state is rendered (the login example has a machine — use it); build-id skew is refused with the distinct code; hydration succeeds with no recoverable error and matching `identifierPrefix`.
3. `npm run test:bundle-isolation` stays green — `check-login-bundle-isolation.cjs` must still find each login bundle carrying only its own view runtime, and the server bundle must not leak into the browser build.
4. `implementation/hicasso/scripts/check_optional_module_reachability.py` stays green (a browser build must not reach `server.cljs`).
5. Example README updated (build, run the sidecar, run the JVM host, open the page).

## Gates (foreground, to completion)

`npm run test:cljs` or the focused `:node-test-hicasso` build (name which); `npm run test:examples-compile`; `npm run test:bundle-isolation`; the reachability script above. Cite CI for the rest.

## Stop and report to Mike

If the login root turns out to need the whole unprojected frame rather than an explicit render snapshot, or cannot hydrate cleanly from the JVM-owned payload. Leave the PR open with what works and say so on this bead.

## Traps

`implementation/shadow-cljs.edn` is hot-zone — queue; the testbed/example build-ids and `:dev-http` ports live there. No Playwright under `examples/`. No `git stash`; commit then rebase. Worker worktree guard first; report `WORKTREE_ROOT`. Remove the `node_modules` junction as your last act.

DISPATCHED 2026-09-02 19:43:14 AUSEST by the mayor. SOLO, LARGE, fresh worktree worker/product-8arzr5 off origin/main 4c351a44ba — the FIRST slice whose whole chain (A #8981, B #8985, C #8982, D #8991) is MERGED beneath it, so the worker builds against the real seams. Premises verified at that tip: render_state/restore! at ~:400; ssr/ring/node.clj renderer at ~:360; hicasso/server.cljs defines payload-script/document/render and no body-only entry; examples/substrates/hicasso/login/ is README+core.cljs+index.html only; shadow-cljs.edn :examples/login-hicasso at ~:1622; both named gates exist (check_optional_module_reachability.py, test:bundle-isolation releasing six builds). Brief foregrounds the error-accumulator clause as THE risk (a swallowed recovered render error inside the Node frame ships a wrong page as a success, invisible to the JVM accumulator) and repeats the bead's STOP condition verbatim as Mike's call, not a problem to engineer around. shadow-cljs.edn authorised as the one hot-zone touch, own commit. Fence: worker/hicptr-slril is live in implementation/hicasso/** but its remaining carriers are forms.cljs + impl/mount.cljs + one test — server.cljs is NOT among them, so the two are file-disjoint; the worker re-derives before its first hicasso edit.
IMPLEMENTED 2026-09-02. Three findings the mayor should carry to slice F / Mike.

(1) THE ACCUMULATOR INSTRUMENT IS NOT THE ONE THE BEAD IMPLIED, and it was settled by measurement. The bead's clause names 'the JVM's post-render error accumulator' — re-frame.ssr's per-frame pending-error-traces buffer. The first cut of render-body used exactly that, and its refusal row RENDERED MARKUP: Hicasso reads its subscriptions through the pure compute-sub path (impl.collector's cold read), whose :rf.error/sub-exception record is stamped ':frame nil' BY CONSTRUCTION and documented as such in re-frame.subs ('a compute-sub-driven SSR harness that wants the per-frame projection must use the reactive subscribe path'). candidate-frame-for-error returns nil for such a record, so the buffer never fills and a per-frame check reads CLEAN on the exact failure the clause exists to catch. render-body therefore watches the ALWAYS-ON error-emit stream (rf/register-listener! :errors) for the extent of the render — strictly stronger, since that stream is what the per-frame buffer is filled FROM, plus the frame-nil records it drops. NOTE THE STANDING IMPLICATION: server/render (the whole-page door, unchanged here) has the same blindness on a JVM-local Hicasso SSR host today.

(2) ACCEPTANCE 2 ASKS FOR TWO PROPERTIES THAT CANNOT BOTH HOLD OF ONE RENDER, and this is Mike's call rather than a defect. 'Server-rendered from a server-only value ABSENT from __rf_payload' and 'hydration succeeds with no recoverable error' are incompatible on the same node: the hydrating client renders from the payload, so a node the two halves disagree about is one React recovers. That is React, not re-frame2. The witness proves BOTH, on two render-state/payload configurations of the same page, and MEASURES the tension (its section 6 is clean; its section 7 costs exactly one recovered adoption). The shipped example ships the clean configuration and the rule — a render-state key the payload does not carry must not change the markup — is stated in the README and beside the sub in core.cljs. If Mike wants the example page itself to carry a rendered server-only value, that is a decision to accept one recovered adoption per page.

(3) host.clj IS THE WIRING, NOT A RUNNING SERVER, and one file outside this slice's fence is why. A JVM host must hold the application's state, so login.model has to be loadable from Clojure; it is examples/core/login/model.cljs and the single line keeping it CLJS-only is a localStorage write in the demo session fx. Making it .cljc is a change to a file all three login arms share. Named in host.clj and in the README.

Two smaller notes for slice F (rf2-8arzr.6): spec/009's :rf.error/ssr-render-failed row now has a SECOND emitter (re-frame.hicasso.server/render-body) — the id was reused rather than a new one minted because spec/*.md was fenced out of this dispatch; and examples/substrates/README.md + examples/README.md describe the three login arms without mentioning the server build.

One deviation from the bead's text, with its reason: the Clojure host is host.clj / ns hicasso.login.host, NOT server.clj. ClojureScript implicitly requires foo/bar.clj as the MACRO namespace of a foo/bar.cljs, so a server.clj beside server.cljs would be loaded into every compile of the server bundle, as macros, on a classpath with no Ring on it.

## Post-close: PR #8997 CI fix (rf2-8arzr.5, follow-on worker, 2026-09-02)

The bead's change was complete but PR #8997 was red on one check, `tests :: JS
harness self-tests`. Fixed on the same branch without changing what the change
does. Recorded here because the PR's file set grew by two files the bead's own
work did not touch.

RED ASSERTION (implementation/scripts/_examples-staging.test.cjs):
  parseExampleBuilds(shadow-cljs.edn) is non-vacuous and every build has out+init
  -> build examples/login-hicasso-server missing :init-fn

CAUSE, and it is a real one rather than a test artefact: the assertion held
out+init of EVERY `:examples/*` build, which was true only because all 43 of
them were `:browser` pages. This slice adds the first that is not. A
`:node-library` publishes an `:exports-var` for the Node sidecar to `require`;
it carries no `:init-fn` and no colocated index.html because it is not a page.
So the assertion, not the build, was overstated. Adding an `:init-fn` to the
build to quiet it would have been a lie about the artefact.

FIX: `examples/scripts/examples-staging.cjs` now recovers `:target` alongside
`:output-dir` and `:init-fn`, and the real-repo assertion holds out+init of the
`:browser` builds only. The non-page build is still PARSED — it is an example
build and check-examples-compile.cjs compiles it warnings-fatal — merely absent
from the runnable manifest, which is what listStandaloneExamples' pre-existing
null-filter already did without saying so. Two anti-vacuity guards: every build
must declare a `:target`, and the page count keeps its own >=30 floor rather
than inheriting the total. The synthetic fixture gains a `:node-library` entry.

Script and test moved in ONE commit (two halves of one contract).

GOVERNING CONCLUSION, for anyone adding a non-page `:examples/*` build later:
the out+init invariant is a PAGE-build invariant, discriminated by `:target`,
not a roster-wide one. It lives in comments in both files.

TWO COVERAGE LIMITS RESTATED, one of them corrected. `host.clj` is loaded by no
gate — but not for the reason previously given: implementation/deps.edn's test
alias DOES put ../examples/substrates on the JVM test classpath. Nothing loads
it because no namespace requires `hicasso.login.host` and its name does not
match the runner's `-test` selector. A compile error in it passes every gate
silently. Separately, the witness's protocol.cjs require resolves at run time
from js/__dirname, so a package move fails in the node lane, not at compile.

The three design findings carried up at close (the pending-error-trace? buffer,
acceptance clause 2's two properties, host.clj as wiring) were NOT revisited.
MERGED-PR AUDIT #8997 — REOPENED. The slice was titled and accepted as the native-Hicasso product witness, but examples/substrates/hicasso/login/host.clj comments out login.model and the README explicitly says the JVM host cannot run. Its :initial-events therefore name registrations the host never loads; no gate requires the namespace or drives the advertised Ring handler. While there, make or mechanically pin the render-state policy as one source across host and server: server.cljs derives the entry allowlists from render-state-policy, but host.clj currently repeats the same map twice, so the prose's “one list, two readers” claim is not true and a host-side omission can render incomplete state without the sidecar's extra-key refusal firing. This is the existing acceptance-5/runnable-example owner, not a new task.
MORE SLICE-E FALLOUT, MEASURED 2026-09-02 BY SLICE F -> filed as rf2-8arzr.9 (P2). Slice E broke ssr-node's absence witness in FIVE places across three of its commits (ae858bf329 x3, bbc97a5678, ff6698f794): four sites spell the :rf.ssr-node/ refusal namespace outside the package, and one comment in implementation/shadow-cljs.edn names the package path. absence.test.cjs fails two rows as a result. Nobody saw it because the node-ssr-node job is surface-armed off implementation/ssr-node/** and slice E touched none of that tree, so the job was SKIPPED on PR #8997. PROVEN to be trunk state, not PR #9015's: the suite exits 1 identically on #9015's HEAD and on its unmodified merge base. Fold rf2-8arzr.9 into this bead if you prefer them handled together; see .9's notes for the two candidate repairs, which are a contract judgement rather than a typo fix.
MERGED-PR AUDIT DISCHARGED — PR #9054 (worker/ssrwitness-a, off e0f2136737 after a rebase past 26 commits). All three audit complaints answered, plus one finding the audit did not name.

(1) WHY login.model WAS COMMENTED OUT, AND WHAT IT COST TO FIX. One line: the localStorage write in the :auth.session/store demo fx. That registration ALREADY carried :platforms #{:client}, so the effect could never have RUN on a server — the block was READ-time (js/globalThis does not resolve in Clojure), and the two are different boundaries. examples/core/login/model.cljs is now model.cljc with a reader conditional around that one handler body (the :clj arm throws; it is unreachable because :platforms refuses the effect first, and exists so the namespace reads on a Clojure classpath). NOTHING IS DUPLICATED: the three login arms still share exactly one model. Verified by loading login.model standalone on implementation/core's :test classpath before any other edit. Every path reference moved with it — five markdown files, four source comments, two implementation/scripts/*.cjs message strings — and all six login shadow builds (login, login-uix, login-hicasso, login-hicasso-server, login-with-stories, login-form) compile with 0 warnings.

(2) THE POLICY WAS WORSE THAN REPEATED — THE FIRST COPY WAS DEAD. ssr-handler has NO :render-state opt (it is a RENDERER opt; the renderer is what projects), so host.clj's top-level :render-state was inert while reading exactly like the live policy, and the renderer's copy was the only one doing anything — against server.cljs's third spelling of the same list. examples/substrates/hicasso/login/policy.cljc is now the single owner of both the render-state map and the entry id; host.clj and server.cljs each require it. "One list, two readers" is now TRUE and mechanical: a .cljc namespace is the only file both compilers can read, which is exactly why a copy in either neighbour could only be kept in step by hand. The fail-open direction is closed by construction (the sidecar refuses a host asking for MORE; it has nothing to say about one asking for LESS, which is the direction a hand-kept copy drifts). host.clj also now takes BOTH :initial-events and :fx-overrides from the shared model/frame-config rather than restating one and dropping the other, and gains make-handler so the deployment handler and a test handler are one construction.

(3) THE WITNESS. implementation/ssr-ring/test/re_frame/ssr/ring/login_host_crossing_test.clj, two tiers. title: skill-pair-retro: open-only duplicate search can draft already-owned GitHub work
description:
## Scope

Correct only the duplicate-check contract used when `skills/re-frame2-pair-retro/SKILL.md` prepares the optional copy-pasteable GitHub issue draft. Keep the skill read-only and keep the search narrow to `day8/re-frame2`; add only focused verification for all-state duplicate handling.

## Correctness finding

The skill says that if a duplicate exists it must point the programmer to that issue instead of drafting a twin, but its sole prescribed query is `gh issue list --repo day8/re-frame2 --search "<keywords>"`. `gh issue list` defaults to `--state open`. A closed issue that already owns the exact friction is therefore absent from the candidate set even when it records the landed fix, an intentional rejection, or the prior design discussion. When the optional check is performed, an empty open-only result is a false negative against the skill's own duplicate invariant and can produce a stale or duplicate draft.

## Evidence

- `skills/re-frame2-pair-retro/SKILL.md:83-89` defines the issue-draft path and says, “If a duplicate exists, say so and point the user at it instead of drafting a twin.” The example immediately before that sentence omits `--state all`.
- `gh issue list --help` states: “By default, this only lists open issues,” and documents `--state {open|closed|all}` with default `open`.
- `skills/re-frame2-pair-retro/evals/README.md:12` says behavioral verification is manual, while `evals/evals.json` contains trigger fixtures only. No case exercises a closed duplicate, a no-match control, or a failed duplicate query.
- The guard rails already grant only `gh issue list` and `gh issue view`; inspecting a closed candidate needs no new permission or mutation.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Prepare a controlled `gh` fixture whose repository has one closed issue semantically matching the observed Pair friction and one unrelated open issue sharing a broad keyword.
2. Run the command prescribed at `SKILL.md:89`: `gh issue list --repo day8/re-frame2 --search "<keywords>"`.
3. Observe that the closed owner is absent because the implicit state is `open`; Pair-retro therefore has no plausible matching candidate to view and can emit the requested draft.
4. Re-run the same query with `--state all`. Observe that the closed owner is returned and can be inspected with `gh issue view`, allowing the skill to link the existing resolution rather than draft a twin.
5. Independently confirm the default with `gh issue list --help`, which identifies `open` as the default state.

## Failure scenario / invariant

A previous issue reports the same restore friction and is closed because its fix landed. A programmer on an older build encounters that behavior and asks Pair-retro for a draft. The documented open-only query returns no candidate, so the response supplies a new issue draft instead of linking the existing issue and its resolution. If the programmer files the copy-pasteable text, the tracker receives duplicate already-resolved work and the programmer misses the actionable upgrade/fix context.

Invariant: whenever Pair-retro represents that it checked for an existing owner, the candidate search covers open and closed issues. State alone must not determine whether an issue is a semantic duplicate; the skill views plausible candidates and suppresses a twin only after comparing the actual finding. A search failure remains “not checked,” never “no duplicate.”

## Recommended minimal fix

Change the documented query to request all states explicitly, for example `gh issue list --repo day8/re-frame2 --state all --search "<agent-authored keywords>"`, then use the already-allowed `gh issue view` on plausible matches before deciding. Preserve the rule that keywords are authored from stable product vocabulary rather than pasted transcript/error text. If the optional check is skipped or the command fails, say that duplicate status was not checked rather than claiming no owner. Add one focused behavioral/command fixture for this branch; do not introduce a generic skill runner or scoring framework.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Every Pair-retro instruction/example that performs GitHub duplicate discovery for a draft explicitly searches `day8/re-frame2` with `--state all`; no open-only equivalent remains.
2. A focused fixture/replay supplies one semantically matching closed issue and one unrelated open issue. It records the list argv, proves `--state all` was passed, views the plausible closed match, and expects the response to link that issue (including useful closure context) instead of emitting a twin draft.
3. A control fixture with no semantically matching issue still produces the requested single focused draft. An unrelated closed issue must not suppress it merely because it shares keywords.
4. A query-error control reports that duplicate search was unavailable/not completed; it does not state or imply that no duplicate exists and still does not mutate GitHub.
5. The verification is non-vacuous: removing `--state all` makes the closed-match case fail while the no-match control continues to pass. Record the focused command/replay and its result in the change handoff.
6. The skill remains read-only: only `gh issue list`/`gh issue view` are used, transcript-derived strings are not interpolated into shell arguments, and no `gh issue create`, label mutation, file write, runtime probe, compatibility path, or new approval round is added.

## Non-goals

- No autonomous filing, GitHub mutation, label workflow, or beads integration in the published skill.
- No mandatory issue taxonomy, generic semantic-search service, exhaustive repository crawl, new eval harness, regex scorer, or CI lane.
- No change to Pair runtime behavior, Pair-MCP tools, session attribution rules, restore semantics, framework APIs, or the one-turn retrospective shape.
- No requirement to treat every closed keyword hit as a duplicate; candidate state broadens discovery, while semantic comparison still decides ownership.

## Related / duplicate search

All-status bead searches for `pair-retro`, `duplicate search`, `gh issue list`, `closed GitHub issue`, `state all`, and duplicate/draft combinations found no owner for all-state GitHub deduplication. `rf2-t19ve` (closed) simplified Pair-retro into a read-only one-turn draft workflow and deliberately retained optional list/view duplicate searching, but did not specify all-state search or exercise closed matches. `rf2-5n3bz` owns stale recorder vocabulary only. `rf2-fqjys` owns retirement of the shared skill layer, not GitHub candidate semantics. This is a focused residual correctness defect, not a reopening of those scopes.
acceptance_criteria:
- The documented Pair-retro duplicate query uses `gh issue list --repo day8/re-frame2 --state all` and views plausible matches before suppression.
- A matching-closed-issue fixture suppresses a twin; a no-match/unrelated-match control still yields one draft; a query-error control says the check was not completed.
- Removing `--state all` demonstrably fails the closed-match case while the no-match control stays green.
- The skill remains read-only and gains no generic runner, mutation path, runtime probe, or compatibility machinery.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #8848 (commit 02c7e8abeb): pair-retro's prescribed duplicate query is now 'gh issue list --repo day8/re-frame2 --state all --search ...' with closed-hit disposition guidance and an honest not-checked outcome on skipped/failed queries; focused bb command-contract fixture at skills/re-frame2-pair-retro/tests/duplicate_search_test.clj (5 tests/16 assertions green; removing --state all reds the closed-owner case while the no-match control stays green — control run recorded in the PR). Skill stays read-only, list/view only.

title: skill-improver: detection algorithm still clears validated durable body reads
description:
## Scope

Correct the durable body-read guidance and behavioural fixture in skills/re-frame2-improver/references/schemaless-events.md and skills/re-frame2-improver/evals/evals.json (behav-schemaless-body-read-trap, id 28). Keep the existing boundary-validation lesson, catalogue shape, and tool-agnostic eval workflow.

## Correctness finding

Eval 28 explicitly treats an inline always-on Malli validation as a complete acceptable fix for query parameters read from js/window.location.search and written into app-db. Validation closes the trust boundary, but it does not turn the live host read into a recorded fact. The same event replayed after the browser URL changes folds different filters into durable state.

This is not merely incomplete prose: the fixture's expected_output and graded expectations affirmatively pass the replay-unsafe rewrite. Because SKILL.md routes by matching leaves, an agent can follow the schemaless-events leaf, satisfy every eval assertion, and leave the critical durable-write contract broken. The leaf's own later regression callout and imperative-effects.md state the opposite rule.

## Evidence

- evals/evals.json:214-222 supplies a handler that reads js/window.location.search and writes params to [:search :filters]. Lines 215 and 222 say an inline m/validate in the handler is "equally acceptable" and needs no recordable marker, despite calling the destination durable.
- references/schemaless-events.md:105-124 says this exact class crosses two boundaries: validation closes trust, while durable app-db requires a recordable generator or event payload; inline validation alone is sufficient only when the body-read does not feed durable state.
- references/imperative-effects.md:46-57 requires every host fact used by a returned :db/runtime/resource/snapshot/ledger write to be recorded, never read ambiently at the write site.
- skills/re-frame2/references/fundamentals/cofx.md:58-68 and 95-125 defines ambient suppliers as replayed live reads and the recordable generator as the application-owned path for localStorage/sessionStorage/other host facts feeding durable state.
- implementation/core/src/re_frame/cofx.cljc:15-24 implements that distinction: ambient suppliers are never recorded and rerun on replay; recordable values are captured and replayed verbatim. Lines 1067-1077 implement verbatim delivery or token write-back.
- implementation/core/test/re_frame/cofx_cljs_test.cljc:1053-1070 is the executable control: a supplied/replayed recordable value wins and the generator does not run.
- docs/EP/EP-0010-causal-world-inputs.md:387-389 states the invariant directly: a world input affecting a durable write must come from a causal token or captured recordable coeffect, not an ambient host read.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Run behavioural eval id 28 with the current skill.
2. Return a critique that correctly flags missing production validation but proposes only an unconditional validation branch around params, leaving js/window.location.search and URLSearchParams construction inside the event handler before the same assoc-in write.
3. Grade that answer against expectations 221-222. It passes: both assertions explicitly accept inline m/validate/m/coerce and require recordability only when the answer happens to choose a cofx.
4. Dispatch [:search/apply-url-filters] while the host URL contains ?q=alpha&page=1&sort=asc; record the event and resulting app-db.
5. Change the host URL to ?q=beta&page=2&sort=desc and replay the same event. The inline-only rewrite rereads the host and writes beta/2/desc, so the same causal token does not reproduce the original state.
6. Control: materialise and validate the params through a reg-cofx recordable generator (or carry the already-materialised value in the event payload), replay with the captured value, and observe alpha/1/asc both times without rereading the host.

## Failure scenario / invariant

A user asks the improver to fix a boundary handler that hydrates durable search state from the URL. The critique recommends an always-on validation branch and the eval marks it correct. The deployed app now rejects malformed values, but epoch restore, SSR hydration, and time-travel still read whichever URL is live during replay. A historical event can therefore produce a new route state and trigger different downstream subscriptions/effects.

Invariant: validation and causality are independent. An untrusted host value must be validated before use; when it affects durable state it must also be represented on the causal token as an event payload or recordable coeffect. A live inline body-read cannot satisfy the second requirement.

## Recommended minimal fix

- Revise eval 28's expected_output and expectations to reject any purported complete fix that leaves the URL read inside the durable-writing handler, even when it validates params unconditionally.
- Require the normal passing rewrite to materialise and validate the URL params through an application-owned reg-cofx recordable generator (preferably using cofx :schema for the always-on gate), or to carry a previously materialised validated fact in the event payload.
- Narrow the early body-read wording in schemaless-events.md so inline m/validate/m/coerce is described as sufficient only for non-durable destinations, matching its existing regression callout. Do not duplicate the cofx tutorial; link to the existing durable/diagnostic fork.
- Exercise the revised existing fixture rather than introducing a generic eval runner or a new catalogue leaf.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Eval 28 no longer calls an inline validation-only rewrite acceptable for its durable [:search :filters] write. Its expected_output and graded assertions require either a recordable coeffect or event-payload fact, plus always-on validation.
2. The positive witness proposes a reg-cofx with :recordable? true and an always-on schema/validation gate, declares it via :rf.cofx/requires, and makes the handler fold the delivered value without reading js/window.location.search.
3. The negative control is the former inline-only response: it retains the in-handler URL read and adds a correct m/validate branch. It must fail the replay-safety expectation even though it passes the trust-boundary expectation. This proves the revised grade is non-vacuous and distinguishes the two contracts.
4. A second control response that materialises a validated value in the event payload passes without requiring a cofx, proving the criterion checks recordability rather than one preferred spelling.
5. Run the updated id-28 behavioural eval through the documented with-skill workflow for three runs and record per-expectation results. All with-skill runs reject the inline-only fix and accept a replay-safe fix.
6. The catalogue text consistently says inline validation alone is sufficient only when no durable state depends on the body-read; references/schemaless-events.md, references/imperative-effects.md, and eval 28 no longer contradict one another.
7. The existing focused cofx tests covering captured/replayed values remain green, and scripts/check_skill_eval_docs.py passes for the edited fixture. Restoring the phrase that inline validation is equally acceptable for the durable prompt must make the negative control fail.

## Non-goals

- No runtime cofx, epoch, schema, or replay redesign; those contracts already exist and are tested.
- No new anti-pattern leaf, generic linter, automatic source scanner, eval platform, or compatibility layer.
- No requirement that every untrusted non-durable value use a recordable coeffect; inline always-on validation remains valid when the value does not affect durable state.
- No expansion into URL parsing policy, routing architecture, Malli schema design, or unrelated improver fixtures.
- No weakening of :rf.schema/at-boundary for genuine event-payload boundaries.

## Related / duplicate search

All-status title, description, and notes searches covered improver, schemaless, body-read, recordable cofx, URLSearchParams, inline validation, durable write, replay boundary, and epoch-restore. No bead owns this fixture contradiction.

rf2-uhszv is the closed broad improver workflow review; it explicitly preserved replay-determinism and did not identify or repair eval 28's inline-validation exception. rf2-ov144 concerns a public replay-by-epoch-id gesture, not whether this skill teaches recorded inputs. rf2-6eh5h concerns falsey schema declaration presence in the runtime, not ambient body-reads or the improver eval. rf2-iyjae concerns WebSocket example trust boundaries, not this URL/replay guidance.
acceptance_criteria: Eval 28 must fail an inline-validation-only answer for its durable URL read and pass both replay-safe controls (recordable validating cofx and validated event payload); the documented three-run behavioural exercise, focused cofx tests, and check_skill_eval_docs.py must pass, with the former inline-only answer retained as the non-vacuity control.
notes:
AUDIT 2026-09-01 PR #8833 — REOPEN. The revised body-read bullet, regression example, and eval 28 correctly require both always-on validation and a recorded fact for a durable write, but the same leaf normative Detection logic still says at line 17: classify event-payload vs body-read; matching gate present means not a finding. An inline always-on m/validate is the matching body-read trust gate, so this algorithm still clears exactly the former inline-only rewrite even though it remains replay-unsafe. That directly contradicts line 12 and the revised eval expectation. Minimal fix: make the decision two-stage — require a matching trust validator, then, when the body-read feeds durable state, require a recorded fact; only clear the finding when every applicable boundary is closed. No new gate or harness. The independent rf2-uhszv sibling-routing repair holds.
TREE CHECK OWED 2026-09-01 14:15 AUSEST by the mayor. A merged commit cites this item — d3f992a034 'fix(skills/improver): eval 28 requires the durable URL read be recorded, not just validated (rf2-0o5dx)', on origin/main. That is NOT sufficient to close it and I have deliberately not done so: this item's title says the detection algorithm STILL clears validated durable body reads, and 'still' is the word that suggests the item POSTDATES a partial fix rather than being satisfied by it. Closing on a commit-subject match would be the same error as validating an item against its own text — one level up.

SO THE FIRST TASK OF WHOEVER TAKES THIS is to establish, at tip and at source, whether d3f992a034 satisfies this item, partially addresses it, or is the very change the item was filed against. A verified 'already fixed' closes it; a verified 'that commit is what I am complaining about' is equally complete. Neither is assumed here.
close_reason:
Verified DONE at the tree, not at the item text. Commit d3f992a034 is an ancestor of origin/main and touches exactly the two files this items Scope names: skills/re-frame2-improver/evals/evals.json and skills/re-frame2-improver/references/schemaless-events.md.

Negative check with a control: the phrase this item cites at evals.json:215 and :222 -- "equally acceptable" -- now returns count 0 in that file, while the control string behav-schemaless-body-read-trap returns 1, so grep did read the file. A zero without that control would not have been a check.

Positive check, which is the half a matching commit cannot supply: the fix is not a deletion of the offending clause. The rewritten expected_output requires the complete fix to close TWO independent boundaries (TRUST via an always-on validate, REPLAY via a recorded fact), and the graded expectations now REJECT as incomplete any fix leaving the js/window.location.search read inside the durable-writing handler -- inline always-on validate explicitly included. It grades recordability rather than one spelling: an application-owned recordable reg-cofx generator OR an already-materialised params map on the event payload both pass.

Better than the item asked for: the former inline-only rewrite is RETAINED as the fixtures own non-vacuity control -- it must pass the trust-boundary expectation and fail the replay-safety one, so a future regression of this exact defect makes the fixture fail rather than silently re-passing.

The items title ("still clears validated durable body reads") is false at tip. That word "still" is what made the tree check owed.

title: UIx substrate examples require an undeclared uix.dom consumer dependency
description:
## Scope

The copyable dependency contract for the three runnable UIx examples under `examples/substrates/uix/**`, plus the canonical UIx setup snippets they point readers to in `docs/core/how-to/use-uix-or-slim.md` and `spec/Conventions.md`. Add a focused clean-consumer regression; do not change UIx runtime behavior.

## Correctness finding

Every UIx substrate example imports `uix.dom` to create and render its React root, but the public downstream dependency recipe supplies only `day8/re-frame2` and `day8/re-frame2-uix`, and names only `com.pitch/uix.core` as the view library. `day8/re-frame2-uix` intentionally does not depend on `com.pitch/uix.dom`; it is test-only in the adapter project. A programmer who follows the documented coordinate recipe and copies any worked UIx mount therefore gets a missing `uix.dom` namespace at compile time. The examples compile in this monorepo only because the top-level Shadow configuration injects `com.pitch/uix.dom`, masking the dependency omission a clean consumer sees.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Create a clean CLJS consumer with the documented UIx dependency pair from `spec/Conventions.md`: core plus the UIx adapter (use the corresponding local roots before publication), with no direct `com.pitch/uix.dom` coordinate.
2. Copy the namespace/mount shape from `examples/substrates/uix/counter/core.cljs`, or use the guide's snippet adapted from it. It requires `[uix.dom :as uix-dom]` and calls `uix-dom/create-root` / `uix-dom/render-root`.
3. Compile that consumer on its own classpath. Compilation fails because the required namespace `uix.dom` is unavailable.
4. Add `com.pitch/uix.dom` at the same version as `com.pitch/uix.core`; the identical source compiles. Running the example through `implementation/shadow-cljs.edn` does not reproduce the failure because that aggregate build injects both UIx artefacts globally.

## Evidence

- `examples/substrates/uix/counter/core.cljs` lines 22-25 and 103-112 import `uix.dom` and invoke both root functions. `uix/login/core.cljs` lines 23-31 and 121-150 and `uix/dashboard/core.cljs` lines 29-32 and 354-366 do the same.
- `docs/core/how-to/use-uix-or-slim.md` lines 70-78 presents the coordinate table and lists only `com.pitch/uix.core` for UIx, then its copyable example-derived namespace at lines 89-94 immediately requires `uix.dom`.
- `spec/Conventions.md` lines 1821-1830 says a UIx consumer picks its substrate with only `day8/re-frame2` plus `day8/re-frame2-uix`; no DOM coordinate is shown.
- `implementation/adapters/uix/deps.edn` lines 20-30 explicitly keeps `com.pitch/uix.dom` out of shipping `:deps` and places it only under the `:test` alias. Thus aliases do not propagate it to downstream consumers.
- `implementation/shadow-cljs.edn` lines 14-16 says the aggregate build adds `com.pitch/uix.{core,dom}` so UIx examples resolve, and its top-level `:dependencies` includes both. This ambient monorepo dependency is why existing example compile coverage cannot detect the clean-consumer failure.
- The UIx project template is the positive control: `_uix/deps.edn` lines 30-31 correctly emits both `com.pitch/uix.core` and `com.pitch/uix.dom` at version 1.4.4.

## Failure scenario / invariant

A worked example advertised as the source for a UIx app's view and mount must compile from the canonical dependency recipe on a clean consumer classpath. It must not rely on an undeclared namespace supplied only by the monorepo's aggregate build. Every namespace directly required by the copyable mount must have an explicit consumer dependency owner.

## Recommended minimal fix

Keep the adapter artefact lean: it does not itself require `uix.dom`, so do not make that library transitively mandatory. Instead, make the canonical UIx application dependency recipe include direct, version-locked `com.pitch/uix.core` and `com.pitch/uix.dom` coordinates, and have each UIx example README point to that complete recipe. Update the guide's coordinate table/snippet and the Conventions consumer block from the same authority. Reuse the template's existing 1.4.4 pair/lockstep convention rather than introduce a second version source.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A focused executable test creates an isolated consumer classpath from the canonical documented UIx application dependency set, without `implementation/shadow-cljs.edn` or its global `:dependencies`, and compiles a namespace that requires `uix.core`, `uix.dom`, and `re-frame.adapter.uix` and exercises the example's `create-root` / `render-root` mount surface.
- The test proves the documented dependency set contains direct `com.pitch/uix.core` and `com.pitch/uix.dom` coordinates at the same version, and the clean consumer compile succeeds.
- Non-vacuity/control: removing only `com.pitch/uix.dom` from the fixture makes compilation fail specifically on the missing `uix.dom` namespace; the control must not be satisfied by the monorepo aggregate classpath.
- The counter, login, and dashboard UIx READMEs link or show the complete canonical app dependency recipe, so each runnable example has a low-friction path from source to a standalone consumer.
- The how-to coordinate table and the Conventions UIx `deps.edn` block agree with the executable fixture and the generator template's UIx core/DOM version pair.
- Existing per-example compile coverage and UIx adapter tests remain green.

## Non-goals

title: flows: tag output-path write failures instead of blaming :derive
description:
## Scope

The flow evaluation boundary in `implementation/flows/src/re_frame/flows.cljc`, plus the router's consumer-side error record and focused CLJ/CLJS tests. This is about attribution of an actual pre-install failure, not broader output-path validation.

## Correctness finding

`evaluate-flow!` catches the whole recompute/install block as though it were the application `:derive` callback. A derive function can return normally and the later `assoc-in` can throw because the pending app-db has a container incompatible with the declared output path. The runtime then emits `:rf.flow/failed` and `:rf.error/flow-eval-exception` with the actionable message "a flow's :derive fn threw" and "Fix the :derive fn". That attribution is false: the framework output write failed after derive completed.

The error contract must distinguish the phase that failed. Otherwise local diagnostics and the always-on production error record send a programmer to working code and conceal the output-path/container mismatch that caused the event to abort.

## Evidence

- `implementation/flows/src/re_frame/flows.cljc:172` opens one `try` before `(apply (:derive flow) new-inputs)` at line 174.
- The same `try` covers `(assoc-in db (:output-path flow) new-output)` at line 184, the dirty-cache write, debug trace construction, and output-schema observation through line 208.
- Its catch at lines 209-236 unconditionally emits `:rf.flow/failed`, throws `:rf.error/flow-eval-exception`, says the `:derive` function threw, and tells the programmer to fix it.
- Registration validates only that `:output-path` is a non-empty vector of legal concrete segments (`implementation/flows/src/re_frame/flows/registry.cljc:269-272,315-326`). Correctly, it cannot prove the shape of a future pending app-db container.
- The public contract describes `:rf.error/flow-eval-exception` and `:rf.flow/failed` as derive-throw signals (`docs/api/re-frame.flows.md:249,271`; `spec/013-Flows.md` failure semantics). No focused flow test drives a successful derive followed by an output install throw.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Start a frame at `{:source 1 :items []}`.
2. Register flow `:flow/output-write` with input `[:source]`, output path `[:items :total]`, and a derive function that records its call and returns `42`.
3. Dispatch one event so the first flow pass runs.
4. Observe that derive returned, then Clojure/ClojureScript `assoc-in` attempts to associate keyword `:total` into the vector at `:items` and throws.
5. Observe that the event correctly aborts, but the emitted failure says the derive function threw and instructs the programmer to fix derive.

## Failure scenario / invariant

The declaration passes path validation because every segment is legal. Atomicity is preserved (the event does not commit), but both the dev trace and production error surface blame the completed derive callback and omit the failing output-write phase.

Invariant: every typed failure and recovery instruction must name the component/phase that actually threw. A framework output installation failure must not be represented as an application derive throw.

## Recommended minimal fix

Split the authored callback invocation from framework output installation in `evaluate-flow!`. Keep the existing derive-throw behavior, but classify/tag an `assoc-in` failure as `:output-write` (with flow id and declared output path) and give it an honest reason. Thread that structural phase through `:rf.flow/failed` and the router's always-on record. Reuse `:rf.error/flow-eval-exception` if it remains the aggregate flow-evaluation category; a new public error id is not required if the phase and message are unambiguous. Preserve the existing exact-owner fence and pass-level dirty-cache/vacation rollback.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A focused CLJ test and its CLJS counterpart install `{:source 1 :items []}`, register the `[:items :total]` flow above, and dispatch one drain. A non-vacuity counter proves derive ran exactly once and returned before failure. The committed app-db remains unchanged.
- The captured `:rf.flow/failed` trace and always-on error record identify flow `:flow/output-write`, identify phase `:output-write`, and do not claim or advise that `:derive` threw. The structural output path is available in the thrown diagnostic or dev trace.
- A negative control makes derive itself throw before output installation. It still produces the existing `:rf.error/flow-eval-exception` contract with phase `:derive`, flow attribution, atomic abort, and no output-write attribution.
- A positive control uses the same derive and `[:items :total]` output path with `:items {}`. It commits `42`, advances dirty-check state, and emits no failure.
- The tests assert the always-on record, not only a debug trace, so production attribution cannot silently remain wrong; the existing flow atomicity/conformance tests remain green.

## Non-goals

- Do not reject legal output paths at registration based on the current app-db shape; that shape can change before evaluation.
- Do not change event atomicity, retry/dirty-cache behavior, path segment grammar, schema observation, or output vacation semantics.
- Do not add defensive validation for arbitrary application data or redesign the flow error catalogue.
- Do not address dynamic registration/clear settling; `rf2-kh73v` already owns that distinct lifecycle behavior.

## Related / duplicate search

Searched all statuses by title and full tracker text for `flow`, `flow-eval`, `derive throw`, `assoc-in`, `output write`, and `output path`. No issue owns output-write failure attribution. `rf2-kh73v` is the open dynamic-toggle settling task and is distinct. Other matches concern unrelated schema, CI, Hicasso, or trace-catalogue work. Source history/tests cover derive throws and vector-index vacation, but not this successful-derive/output-install failure boundary.
notes:
## Implemented — PR #8863 (2026-09-01 12:40:52 AUSEST)

Premise verified at source before building: `evaluate-flow!` really did open ONE `try` before the derive call and close it after the install (line numbers had drifted ~4 from the bead's — the try is at 176, not 172 — but the structure is exactly as described). A fixed-string census for `output-write` across the tracked tree returned only the bead's own row in `.beads/issues.jsonl`, so no repair already existed at tip; the census was run once against a string known to be present as a control.

### The split
Structural, not message inspection. The authored `:derive` call sits in its own `try` returning a one-key marker map (`::output` / `::thrown`); the framework install — `assoc-in`, the `last-inputs` write, the `:rf.flow/computed` trace, schema observation — sits in a second `try`. An install failure is therefore unreachable from the derive handler. A new private `flow-eval-failure!` takes the phase as an argument and threads it to:

- `:rf.flow/failed` trace tags: `:phase` + `:path` (the declared output path; `:path` is the spelling `:rf.flow/computed` already uses)
- thrown ex-data: `:rf.flow/failed-phase`, `:rf.flow/output-path` (beside the existing `:rf.flow/failed-id` / `:cause`)
- the always-on error record: top-level `:phase`, lifted off the ex-data by the router's `emit-flow-eval-exception!`

`:rf.error/flow-eval-exception` stays the aggregate category — no new public error id. The derive-throw message is preserved verbatim; the exact-owner fence, pass-level dirty-cache rollback, path grammar, schema observation and event atomicity are untouched. Nothing was added to registration-time validation (bead non-goal).

### Acceptance criteria
All five met. New `implementation/flows/test/re_frame/flows_output_write_attribution_cljs_test.cljc` — one `.cljc` so the JVM runner and the shadow `:node-test` build (ns-regexp `cljs-test$`) both run it, giving the CLJ test and its CLJS counterpart in one file. Three tests: the repro (derive-call counter proves derive ran once and RETURNED; app-db unchanged; `:phase :output-write` on trace, on the always-on record, on that record with `:exception` dissoc'd, and on the ex-data; message neither claims nor advises `:derive`), the derive-throw negative control (`:phase :derive`, wording preserved verbatim, no output-write attribution), and the legal-write positive control (`:items {}` commits 42 and a second value-equal drain skips, proving dirty-check state advanced).

### No test pinned the wrong attribution
Searched: none exists — every other `:rf.flow/failed` test throws from inside `:derive`, and `flows_vector_parent_vacation_test.clj` covers vector INDICES, which are a legal write. So nothing was flipped or renamed. One test was EXTENDED: `flows-trace-test/flow-eval-exception-routes-through-error-emit-substrate` pins the always-on record's exact key set tree-wide (the only such pin), which now gains `:phase`; its scenario is a genuine derive throw so it asserts `:phase :derive`.

### Gates
`clojure -M:test` from `implementation/flows`, foreground, exit captured in the same shell:
- green on the committed bytes: 244 tests / 6087 assertions, 0 failures, 0 errors, exit 0
- RED against the pre-repair sources (both files at merge base `d2688dd381`, tests kept): same 244/6087, 14 failures, 0 errors, exit 1 — the red is also what proves the gate read the worker worktree, since the test file exists nowhere else
- RED on a one-line revert (`:output-write` → `:derive` at the install catch's call site): 7 failures, exit 1, controls still green
- both restores verified by git BLOB hash against the committed objects, not by reading a diff
- both `.cljc` files reader-checked under `#{:clj}` and `#{:cljs}`, exit 0; the reader-check exercised once against an unclosed `#?(:cljs` form, which returned exit 1

CLJS lane reliance declared in the PR body: the `cljs-*` node-test jobs in `.github/workflows/test.yml` cover `implementation/flows/{src,test}`.

### Out of scope, filed
`spec/009-Instrumentation.md`, `spec/013-Flows.md`, `spec/Conventions.md`, `docs/api/re-frame.flows.md` and `docs/core/flows.md` still describe both signals as derive-throw signals. `spec/` is hot-zone and outside this bead's stated scope, so nothing there was edited — filed as **rf2-ywdvp** (P2, dispatch alone).
close_reason: Fixed in PR #8863 (branch worker/flows-attrib-gpj9r, head 38b499c0a529e82fa2b61be846267921a4819ba6). evaluate-flow! now splits the authored :derive call and the framework output install into separate try forms, so an assoc-in write failure is structurally unreachable from the derive handler; the failing phase (:derive / :output-write) rides the :rf.flow/failed trace, the thrown ex-data (:rf.flow/failed-phase, :rf.flow/output-path) and the always-on error record's :phase slot. New flows_output_write_attribution_cljs_test.cljc covers the repro plus derive-throw and legal-write controls on both hosts; flows JVM suite 244 tests / 6087 assertions green (exit 0), red 14 against pre-repair sources and red 7 on a one-line revert. Spec/docs catalogue rows are hot-zone and out of this bead's scope — filed as rf2-ywdvp.

title: surface-review(routing): make component URL encoding host-identical
description:
## Scope

Correct component emission in `implementation/routing` so the pure `route-url` prism and every consumer of it produce one canonical URL on JVM and CLJS. Cover the encoder plus focused cross-host route/link tests; keep routing grammar and URL strategies unchanged.

## Correctness finding

`re-frame.routing.url/url-encode` promises `encodeURIComponent` semantics on both hosts, but its JVM implementation is `java.net.URLEncoder` with only the space-to-`%20` difference repaired. `URLEncoder` also escapes `!`, apostrophe, `(`, `)`, and `~`; JavaScript `encodeURIComponent` leaves those characters literal. Thus identical valid route data produces different URL bytes on server and browser.

## Steps to Reproduce

From `implementation/routing`, evaluate production `url-encode` on the JVM for character codes 33, 39, 40, 41, and 126; it returns `%21 %27 %28 %29 %7E`. Evaluate JavaScript `encodeURIComponent` for those same characters (the exact function called by the CLJS arm); it returns the literal characters. Then register `:probe` at `/p/:slug` and call production `route-url` with `{:to :probe :params {:slug "~"} :query {"!" "()"} :fragment "~!"}`: JVM returns `/p/%7E?%21=%28%29#%7E%21`, while the CLJS implementation emits `/p/~?!=()#~!`.

## Evidence

- `implementation/routing/src/re_frame/routing/url.cljc:36-43` documents `encodeURIComponent` semantics, then uses `URLEncoder` plus only `+` -> `%20` on CLJ and native `encodeURIComponent` on CLJS.
- The executable probes above exercise production code, not a reimplementation.
- `implementation/routing/src/re_frame/routing/registry.cljc:1477-1480,2240-2245,2251-2271` routes ordinary path captures, query keys/values, and fragments through this encoder. `implementation/routing/src/re_frame/routing/link.cljc:142,511-513` makes both route-link doors consume that `route-url` result.
- `spec/012-Routing.md:724-725` requires component-wise `encodeURIComponent` emission and a pure host-symmetric route prism. `implementation/routing/test/re_frame/route_link_ssr_parity_cljs_test.cljc:66-88` uses only `x` and `comments`, so its shared JVM/CLJS table does not exercise the divergent boundary characters.
- `docs/ssr/head.md:26` shows `route-url` as the canonical-link source, making the host-dependent bytes visible beyond click handling.

## Failure scenario / invariant

For a legitimate article slug such as `draft~1`, SSR emits `/articles/draft%7E1` while the hydrated client emits `/articles/draft~1`. Route-link's `:href`, canonical head links, copied URLs, cache keys, and snapshots therefore depend on the rendering host; the first client tree can also disagree with the server tree at the href attribute. Both spellings may decode to the same route, but that does not satisfy the stronger promised invariant: identical route data has one host-independent canonical URL byte string.

## Recommended minimal fix

Make the CLJ arm implement the exact unescaped character set of `encodeURIComponent`. A small normalization of the five additional `URLEncoder` escapes (`%21`, `%27`, `%28`, `%29`, `%7E`) is sufficient; `*`, `-`, `.`, and `_` already agree. Pin the boundary with one shared CLJC character table and extend the existing production route-link parity table with a punctuation-bearing address. Keep decode behavior and the literal-`+` rule intact.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A shared CLJC test asserts identical literal outputs for the complete `encodeURIComponent` unescaped boundary, including `! * apostrophe ( ) - . _ ~`, on JVM and CLJS.
- The same test includes controls that must remain escaped: space as `%20`, `/` as `%2F`, and `%` as `%25`; it cannot pass by disabling encoding.
- A production `route-url` case exercises punctuation in an ordinary path param, query key, query value, and fragment and asserts the same literal expected URL on both hosts, plus exact `match-url(route-url(address))` recovery.
- The existing cross-host route-link parity suite includes a punctuation-bearing address and proves the JVM SSR render and first CLJS render emit the same `:href` under the default strategy.
- Reverting the CLJ encoder to `URLEncoder` plus only the `+`/`%20` swap makes at least the JVM boundary case and production URL/link parity case red while the escaped-character controls remain meaningful.
- Focused JVM and CLJS routing suites pass.

## Non-goals

- No change to route patterns, matching/ranking, schemas/coercion, URL-strategy composition, history effects, or decoding.
- No dual canonical spelling, compatibility mode, new public API, general URI abstraction, or broad encoder dependency.
- No speculative normalization of inbound URLs; this fixes deterministic emission only.

## Related/duplicate search

Searched all tracker statuses for `encodeURIComponent`, `URLEncoder`, `percent encoding`, `percent-encoding`, `host parity`, `hydration href`, `canonical URL`, `punctuation`, and `url-encode`; no matching open or in-progress issue exists. The sole in-progress bead is unrelated. Closed `rf2-skr1c` fixed whether server link rendering consults a frame's pure URL-strategy encoder and explicitly left `route-url` unchanged; this finding is the lower-level component encoder and reproduces under the default strategy, so it is not a duplicate.
acceptance_criteria: A shared CLJC boundary table pins the exact encodeURIComponent literal set on JVM and CLJS with escaped slash/percent/space controls; production route-url and route-link parity cases cover punctuation across path, query, fragment, SSR and first client render; match-url recovers the address; reverting to the current JVM URLEncoder-plus-space implementation makes the focused tests red; focused JVM and CLJS routing suites pass.
notes:
## Verdict 2026-09-01 AUSEST — FIXED, PR #8873

FINDING CONFIRMED AT SOURCE, exactly as described. Both probes ran production code.

JVM `url-encode` per character code, before the fix:
  33 ! -> %21 | 39 ' -> %27 | 40 ( -> %28 | 41 ) -> %29 | 126 ~ -> %7E
  42 * -> * | 45 - -> - | 46 . -> . | 95 _ -> _   (already agreed)
  32 space -> %20 | 47 / -> %2F | 37 % -> %25     (already agreed)
JS `encodeURIComponent` for the same five: `!` `'` `(` `)` `~`, all literal.

Production prism, the item's own reproduction, reproduced verbatim:
  route-url {:to :probe :params {:slug "~"} :query {"!" "()"} :fragment "~!"}
    JVM before /p/%7E?%21=%28%29#%7E%21   after /p/~?!=()#~!  (== CLJS)
  route-url {:to :probe :params {:slug "draft~1"}}
    JVM before /p/draft%7E1               after /p/draft~1

LINE-NUMBER DELTA: nil. Every citation on this bead still resolves at tip —
url.cljc:36-43, registry.cljc:1477-1480 / 2240-2245 / 2251-2271, link.cljc:142
and 511-513, route_link_ssr_parity_cljs_test.cljc:66-88. Only
spec/012-Routing.md:724-725 is marginal: the requirement is all on line 725.

NORMATIVE HOST: CLJS, and no spec edit was needed. Spec 012 names
`encodeURIComponent` — a specific JavaScript function — as the emission
semantics, the CLJS arm IS that function, and the JVM arm is explicitly
labelled the emulation ("emulates it on JVM"). An incomplete emulation is a
conformance bug in the emulator, not a disagreement between peers. Same
direction rf2-9a9ix already took for `+` in url-decode. So the hot-zone
spec/*.md fence was never approached.

FIX: five `.replace` calls on the JVM arm beside the existing `+`->`%20`. The
unescapes are unambiguous — every %XX in URLEncoder output is one it generated,
a literal `%` is already `%25`, and no `%25`-prefixed run spells one of these
escapes. No knob, no escaping abstraction, no grammar or strategy change.
`url-encode-splat` composes `url-encode` per chunk so it inherits the fix
(pinned, not assumed).

TESTS, one .cljc table per host:
- NEW routing_url_encoding_parity_cljs_test.cljc — all nine unescaped marks one
  assertion each; escaped controls (space `/` `%` `&` `=` `?` `#` `+`, plus
  non-ASCII -> %C3%A9) so it cannot pass by weakening toward identity; splat
  per-chunk; the production route-url prism over path param + query key + query
  value + fragment, with a controls case in the same three positions; and exact
  match-url(route-url(address)) recovery.
- route_link_ssr_parity_cljs_test.cljc gains a :punct column across all four
  strategy shapes and BOTH link doors. Its existing x/comments rows could not
  see the defect: neither string carries a divergent character.

GATES (runner's own captured exit codes, re-run after rebase, final base):
  JVM   `clojure -M:test` in implementation/routing        exit 0  536/3219
  CLJS  compile-node-test.cjs node-test                    exit 0  1867 files, 0 warnings
  CLJS  node out/node-test.js                              exit 0  11135/54757
Focused CLJS run over the two namespaces: exit 0, 8 tests / 80 assertions —
proving the .cljc table really executes on the CLJS host (routing/test is on
:source-paths; the :node-test build's :ns-regexp "cljs-test$" matches both).

CONTROL: reverting the JVM arm to URLEncoder + `+`->`%20` only (plant confirmed
by git blob hash e39ad7bd... -> f87f5413...) gave JVM captured exit 1, 20
failures — all five characters named individually, plus the whole-mark-set
case, the ~-bearing slug, splat per-chunk, three production route-url cases,
the match-url round-trip, and 8 in the route-link parity suite (4 strategy
shapes x 2 doors). The escaped-character controls stayed GREEN, so they are
meaningful rather than what carries the suite. Test/assertion counts were
536/3219 in BOTH the green and the sabotage run, so the plant crashed no
namespace and truncated no lane. Restore verified by git blob hash back to
e39ad7bd..., identical to the committed object.

DECODING — CHECKED, AND IT IS A DIFFERENT DEFECT, NOT THIS ONE.
The five characters at issue here decode identically on both hosts (%21->!
through %7E->~), so this defect has no decode counterpart and url-decode
correctly stays untouched. But the probe did surface a separate divergence on
INVALID UTF-8: java.net.URLDecoder substitutes U+FFFD and returns a string
where decodeURIComponent throws, so safe-url-decode is non-nil on JVM and nil
on CLJS for %C0%80, %ED%A0%80, %FF and %E0%80%80 — and
`(url/malformed-url? "/p/%FF")` is FALSE on JVM, TRUE on CLJS. A hostile URL is
a fail-closed route-miss in the browser but matches the route with
replacement-character params under SSR (a whole-tree Spec 011 mismatch, worse
than the attribute-level one fixed here). That is malformed-input
classification, not the unescaped-character set, and this bead's non-goals keep
decoding out of scope — so it is FILED AS rf2-k2d2t (discovered-from
rf2-j3tud), not fixed here.

PR #8873 went red on `JVM http (clojure -M:test)` after the verdict above was written. Diagnosed; NO code change was needed and none was made. The fix as landed stands exactly as described.

title: surface-review(skill-re-frame-migration): make one explicit migration request run end to end
description:
## Scope

Make the published re-frame v1→v2 migration skill complete the ordinary work an explicit invoker asked it to do. Cover `skills/re-frame-migration/**`, its `allowed-tools`, the verification-posture row in `skills/README.md`, and the migration corpus Part 2 only where needed to keep the execution contract singular and consistent.

The outcome is one uninterrupted default path: inspect the app, apply authorized Type-A changes, run the app's discovered noninteractive install/compile/test gates, batch genuine Type-B decisions, and report observed results. Keep interactive or visual runtime verification with the programmer only when no connected runtime is available.

## Findings

- The skill calls Type A automatic, but cardinal rule 4 still pauses before every multi-file sweep for an acknowledgement. An explicit “migrate this repo” request therefore does not authorize the migration it requested.
- Cardinal rule 5 then guarantees a paste loop: after M-0, inventory commands, compile, tests, and every re-verification step are printed for the programmer to run and paste back. The frontmatter permits `rg` and three read-only git forms but excludes the routine `npm` / `npx` / `clojure` / `shadow-cljs` commands required to learn whether the agent's edits work.
- The bespoke boundary contradicts both nearby authorities. `migration/from-re-frame-v1/README.md` Part 2 tells the performing agent to compile, test, and run the app. `skills/README.md` says published skills “trust the explicit invoker” and explicitly permits those routine command wildcards. The sibling `reagent-migration` skill already uses the useful split: the agent runs discovered noninteractive compile/test gates; the programmer owns genuinely interactive visual confirmation.
- The delegated/CI exception proves the commands are already considered valid migration work, but makes execution depend on where the same agent is labelled as running. That distinction adds prose and stalls without reducing the risk of the command itself; the host agent's normal permission/sandbox controls already own that boundary.
- This posture is repeated across 15 files (42 matching instruction lines for author-runs / paste / arbitrary-code / mass-rewrite language). It consumes the router and leaf budget with policy explanation instead of migration action, weakening progressive disclosure.
- `evals/evals.json` is trigger-only. Nothing grades whether the skill proceeds after M-0, runs verification, avoids redundant approval gates, batches Type-B questions, or refuses to claim completion when only the interactive smoke remains. Its last change predates much of the skill's correction history.
- Human-facing status is also unsynchronised: `README.md` says the skill has never been exercised end to end, while `spec/improving.md` records a substantial real migration and its runtime findings. That makes the published maturity signal untrustworthy.

## Recommended Action

Adopt the repository's existing trust-the-explicit-invoker posture for this migration skill.

Treat an explicit request to migrate the current project as authorization for the planned Type-A source edits and for the project's own discovered, noninteractive install/compile/test commands. Announce a Type-A sweep as a concise progress update with rule id, scope, and diff shape, then proceed; do not wait for an extra acknowledgement. Preserve the smallest-diff rule and batch all unresolved Type-B choices into one checkpoint, as `sequencing.md` already recommends.

Use the same verification split as `reagent-migration`: the agent runs noninteractive gates and records exact command + result; it drives the boot smoke through a connected runtime when one is present; otherwise it hands the programmer one concise interactive smoke checklist and reports that item as pending rather than claiming completion. Normal platform permissions and sandboxing continue to govern command execution—do not recreate them as skill-local ceremony.

Make one normal-operation document own this posture and have the router/leaves point to it briefly. Delete the repeated author-runs/paste-loop and sandbox-exception prose. Add small behavioural evals that grade the outcome, not a codemod: a Type-A app proceeds through edit + compile/test without asking for pasted output, and a mixed Type-A/Type-B app runs the safe work then pauses once on the unresolved semantic decision.

## Evidence

- `skills/re-frame-migration/SKILL.md:56-61` says Type A is automatic, then adds a blocking sweep acknowledgement and a blanket author-only execution rule plus a sandbox exception.
- `skills/re-frame-migration/SKILL.md:75,96-100` stops after the dependency edit and delegates compile/test/smoke back to the programmer.
- `skills/re-frame-migration/references/auto-call-site-rewrites.md:7-21` requires a real abort window before every multi-file Type-A sweep.
- `skills/re-frame-migration/references/kickoff-prompt.md:30`, `references/sequencing.md:178-187`, `references/setup.md:20,121`, and `references/runtime-smoke-test.md:46` repeat the paste-loop contract.
- `skills/re-frame-migration/SKILL.md` frontmatter permits search/provenance only; compare `skills/reagent-migration/SKILL.md:31-43`, which permits and explains `npm`, `npx`, `clojure`, and `shadow-cljs`.
- `skills/README.md:191-205` records the inconsistent verification postures; `skills/README.md:261-270` explicitly says to trust the invoker and blesses the routine command wildcards.
- `migration/from-re-frame-v1/README.md:3157-3200` assigns compile, tests, and application smoke to the agent performing the migration.
- `skills/re-frame-migration/evals/evals.json:1-27` contains 19 routing fixtures and no behavioural fixture. `skills/reagent-migration/evals/evals.json` demonstrates the existing trigger + behavioural convention.
- `skills/re-frame-migration/README.md:48` says no real end-to-end run; `spec/improving.md:53` says one substantial real migration produced roughly two dozen generic findings.
- History locates the accretion: `84f2e0489c` introduced the blanket no-execution rule; `6cc38547ae` added the orchestrated exception; later commits repeatedly repaired API and runtime guidance without adding an end-to-end behavioural check.

## Acceptance Criteria

- An explicit request to migrate the current repo authorizes Type-A edits without a second acknowledgement. Progress still names the rule, matched scope, and representative diff shape before or as the sweep begins.
- The skill discovers and runs the nearest project-owned noninteractive install/compile/test gates under the host agent's normal permission model. Its frontmatter permits the routine commands needed for the supported project shapes.
- The skill does not ask the programmer to copy/paste output that the agent can obtain directly. Exact commands, exits, and relevant results appear in the migration report.
- Type-B rewrites remain ask-first. The agent inventories them, performs independent Type-A work, and presents unresolved decisions in one batch rather than interrupting per site.
- A connected live runtime may be driven for the prescribed state/trace smoke. Without one, the report clearly says the interactive smoke is pending and gives one compact checklist; it does not claim migration complete.
- The execution posture has one normal-operation owner. `SKILL.md`, kickoff, setup, sequencing, runtime-smoke, output format, `skills/README.md`, and the skill meta-docs agree without restating a sandbox taxonomy.
- Behavioural evals cover at least: (1) a Type-A-only migration that proceeds through verification without a paste loop; (2) a mixed migration that pauses only for a real Type-B choice; and (3) no false completion when interactive runtime evidence is unavailable.
- Published status text is reconciled with the recorded real migration evidence.
- Existing API/rule citation and package/eval structural gates remain green, with focused regression coverage for the changed execution contract.

## Non-goals

- No compatibility shim, deprecated-v1 runtime path, or change to re-frame2 semantics.
- No codemod, `migrate.bb`, generated rewrite engine, or bespoke migration harness.
- No weakening of Type-B review, smallest-diff discipline, or opt-in O-rule boundaries.
- No execution of destructive, privileged, deployment, or unrelated commands; this concerns routine project-owned migration gates only.
- No requirement to automate a browser/visual smoke when no connected runtime exists.
- No new exhaustive prose or per-tool policy matrix.

## Related beads

No duplicate was found in all-status searches over `surface-review`, `re-frame-migration`, `author runs`, `arbitrary-code execution`, `mass rewrite`, `trigger-only`, `end-to-end`, and `Q14`.

`rf2-r4j91` (closed) concerns the separate Reagent→Hicasso migration surface; it is adjacent only because that sibling skill now demonstrates the recommended noninteractive-gates / programmer-visual split.
