title: surface-review(epoch): make strict replay a one-call epoch-id gesture
description:
## Scope

Close the gap between the epoch runtime's recorded replay material and the public/Tool-Pair replay gesture. Cover the smallest coherent slice across `implementation/epoch/**`, the optional core facade/late-bind hook, Pair-MCP runtime/tool wiring, Tool-Pair/API/spec prose, descriptor manifest, and focused CLJ/CLJS/tool tests.

## Findings

- Every ordinary `:rf/epoch-record` already captures the complete ingredients for a faithful strict replay: `:trigger-event`, the post-generation `:rf.cofx` token (including mid-run minted facts), and the envelope's serializable `:fx-overrides` / `:interceptor-overrides`.
- The normative Tool-Pair replay contract requires replay to re-supply all of those fields and hard-wire `:rf.cofx/mint-policy :strict`; missing facts and `:rf/fn-override` must fail loud.
- No epoch public API or late-bind hook performs that gesture from an epoch id. `re-frame.epoch` exposes history, restore, replace, listeners, config, and egress projection; Pair-MCP exposes `restore-epoch`, while its `dispatch {replay true}` merely sets strict mode and requires the caller to copy the event/cofx/override fields manually.
- That manual route is not generally available to an off-box agent: `projected-record` deliberately replaces every `:trigger-event` argument with `:rf/redacted` by default, and `:include-sensitive?` is orthogonal to `:include-event-args?`. Pair-MCP's epoch egress threads only the app-db `include-sensitive` axis, so `trace-window` / `watch-epochs` cannot return the raw arguments needed to replay a normal argument-bearing event. The remaining escape is raw `eval-cljs` over `rf/epoch-history`, which bypasses the structured privacy and tool envelope.
- Existing replay tests prove the ingredients by hand-extracting a record and calling `rf/dispatch-sync`; none proves that a programmer or tool can name one retained epoch and replay it in one supported call.

## Recommended Action

Provide one dev-only replay-by-epoch-id operation, preferably `replay-epoch!`, owned by the epoch artefact. It should resolve the retained raw record in-process, build the strict dispatch opts from the record in one place, and dispatch the recorded event without exporting its arguments/coeffects/overrides. Make source-frame and target-frame semantics explicit (same frame by default; an optional explicit target only if needed), and make clear that replay runs against the target frame's current state/code unless the caller separately restores a starting epoch.

Expose the operation through the normal optional-artefact facade and as a dedicated Pair-MCP `replay-epoch` tool (or an equally direct epoch-id mode on the existing dispatch tool). Return a structured consequence/failure envelope. Fail before dispatch for an unknown/aged-out id, a non-replayable record (synthetic/halted/missing trigger or replay token), or any recorded `:rf/fn-override`; preserve the existing strict missing-cofx failure rather than minting. Use the existing dispatch authority/annotation posture—do not invent another permission system.

## Evidence

- `implementation/epoch/src/re_frame/epoch/assembly.cljc` builds `:trigger-event`, post-generation `:rf.cofx`, `:fx-overrides`, and `:interceptor-overrides` into each record specifically for Tool-Pair replay.
- `implementation/epoch/src/re_frame/epoch.cljc` publishes no replay hook or public replay function; its Tool-Pair mutations are restore and replace only.
- `implementation/epoch/src/re_frame/epoch/tool_pair.cljc` independently redacts trigger-event args; `implementation/epoch/test/re_frame/epoch_egress_redaction_cljs_test.cljc` pins that `:include-sensitive? true` still leaves them redacted unless the separate `:include-event-args?` opt is supplied.
- `tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/src/re_frame2_pair_mcp/tools/epoch_egress.cljs` threads only `:include-sensitive?` into projected epoch pages and explicitly leaves the orthogonal event-args axis closed.
- `tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/src/re_frame2_pair_mcp/tools/dispatch.cljs` accepts caller-supplied event/cofx/overrides plus `replay true`; it performs no epoch-id lookup. `registry.cljs` and generated `tool-descriptors.edn` contain restore but no replay-by-id tool.
- `spec/Tool-Pair.md` Replay and `tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/spec/003-Tool-Catalogue.md` Strict replay instruct callers to read and copy the four recorded fields manually.
- `implementation/epoch/test/re_frame/epoch_test.clj`, `epoch_override_capture_test.clj`, `machine_minted_cofx_replay_token_test.clj`, and `join_strict_mint_epoch_replay_test.clj` all demonstrate replay through manual record extraction/re-dispatch.
- `implementation/epoch/deps.edn` confirms epoch is an optional, dev-elided artefact with an existing real production-gate lane; the new seam belongs under that same boundary.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. From only a retained epoch id plus explicit frame targeting, a public dev API can replay an ordinary argument-bearing event using the raw in-process `:trigger-event`, recorded `:rf.cofx`, and both recorded override maps under hard-wired `:strict` mint policy.
2. An end-to-end test records a generator-backed/mid-run coeffect and serializable fx/interceptor overrides, then replays by id and proves the generator/host is not consulted and the recorded effective chain is used. Include an event argument that the off-box projected history exposes only as `:rf/redacted`.
3. Pair-MCP offers the same one-call epoch-id gesture without requiring raw event, cofx, or override payloads on the wire; the descriptor, generated manifest, catalogue, and skill routing all agree.
4. Unknown/aged-out ids, halted/synthetic/incomplete records, and `:rf/fn-override` records return stable structured failures and do not dispatch. Missing declared recordable facts remain the canonical strict `:rf.error/missing-required-cofx`; no live mint fallback is introduced.
5. Docs state the state semantics plainly: replay does not implicitly restore, external effects may fire again, the target's current code/frame config applies, and the replayed dispatch records a new ordinary epoch.
6. Existing `projected-record` privacy defaults remain unchanged; no raw event-argument egress knob is added to make replay work.
7. Focused JVM/CLJS epoch tests, Pair-MCP tool tests, descriptor-manifest drift checks, and the existing epoch production-elision lane pass with non-vacuous assertions.

## Non-goals

- A branching timeline, redo stack, or general event-log framework.
- Automatic restore-before-replay or a promise that replay matches the historical `:db-after` when starting state/code differs.
- Replaying opaque fn-valued overrides, virtualising/undoing external effects, or weakening off-box redaction.
- Compatibility aliases, a generic command abstraction, or a second permission/gating system.

## Related beads

No open duplicate was found after title and full-description searches for replay-by-epoch-id, strict replay, trigger-event replay, and `include-event-args`. Historical implementation lineage visible in source/commit history: rf2-1xdotm (post-generation cofx capture), rf2-yigokd (override capture), rf2-v52xsr (strict replay flag), rf2-m7x0qb (Pair-MCP override re-supply), rf2-s3qjlw (epoch/restore strict-replay composition proof), and rf2-nm611o (fail-closed trigger-event args).

## MEASURED BY THE MAYOR AT TRUNK 6b008b0df9 — AND THE PICTURE IS SHARPER THAN THE FLAG

### Row at `API.md:533` — `(rf/frame-ids)` / `(rf/frame-meta id)`, "The frame picker."

**THIS ROW IS HALF TRUE, WHICH IS THE INTERESTING PART AND THE REASON IT CANNOT BE SWEPT.**

`(rf/frame-ids)` **IS** consumed. Three executable call sites under `tools/xray/src`:

    palette/subs.cljs:145             :frame-ids (rf/frame-ids)
    static/schemas/panel.cljs:501     (rf/frame-ids)))
    trace_collector.cljs:212          (remove tool-frames (rf.frame/frame-ids))

Note the third is spelled **`rf.frame/frame-ids`**, a different alias from the one the row prints — so the
row's spelling under-describes its own true half.

`(rf/frame-meta id)` is **NOT** consumed: **0** call sites under `tools/xray/src`. Its four live call sites
are all in `tools/xray/testbeds/machine_epochs/core.cljs` (`:640`, `:699`, `:779`, plus `:692` in a
comment) — **a TESTBED, not `src`**, which is a different claim from "Xray consumes it".

**A TRAP THIS ROW WALKS YOU INTO, AND IT IS ITEM (g) EXACTLY.** A bare search for `frame-ids` under
`tools/xray/src` reads **32**, which looks like abundant consumption. Nearly all of it is the DOMAIN TERM
— `seeded-frame-ids`, a `frame-ids` fn parameter in `palette/sources.cljc`, a `:frame-ids` map key —
rather than a call to the API. **Match the CALL, not the word.** Controls: the munged CLJS spellings
`frame_ids`, `frame_meta_BANG` and `sub_cache_snapshot` all read **0** tree-wide, so no compiled spelling
is hiding anywhere.

### Row at `API.md:536` — `(rf.subs.tooling/sub-cache-snapshot frame-id)`, "The subscription graph."

**ZERO call sites anywhere in `tools/xray` — not in `src`, not in `test`, not in `testbeds`.** All three
occurrences in the tree are PROSE:

    tools/xray/spec/012-Views.md:425   the same surface, in 012's own table
    tools/xray/spec/012-Views.md:474   "The Views tab is CLJS-only in the same way ... sub-cache-snapshot"
    tools/xray/spec/API.md:536         the row itself

**SO THIS IS A TWO-CHAPTER ITEM, AND 012 IS THE ONE THAT MATTERS MORE**: `012-Views.md:425` says this
surface "Drives sub-status decoration", which is a behavioural claim about a surface nothing calls. Do not
correct API.md and leave 012 saying the stronger thing.

under `tools/xray/src`, so the zeros above are ABSENCE rather than a dead instrument. The `replace-frame-state!`
row that `rf2-o1r4m` corrected read 0 the same way, and its correction is the worked precedent.

**Decide per row, and the two rows will probably not get the same answer.**

`rf2-o1r4m` established the disposition that matters here: **the table already carries honest
documented-but-unconsumed rows** — the `:rf.event/origin` row says in terms that no view renders or
colour-codes by it — **so "documented but not consumed" is an existing, legitimate register and not a
defect.** The question for each row is therefore *which register does it belong in*, not *is it wrong*.

For the frame-picker row specifically: **do not delete a half-true row.** Either split the pair, or say
what is true of each half. And establish whether the frame picker actually exists and what it reads before
describing it — `palette/subs.cljs` and `static/schemas/panel.cljs` are where to look, and that is a
question for the code, not for the neighbouring prose.

**If a row cannot be made true without a code change, name it and STOP.** No call site is to be added to
make prose true — that was `rf2-o1r4m`'s central judgement and it is binding here.

The premise "an image or generation snapshot at make-frame" is only half right, and the brief's candidate explanation differs from what the source says. make-frame does seal a generation (live_frame.cljc make-frame, via assemble-default). But a reg-* made afterwards marks the projection dirty, and call-with-frame-resolution flushes it before the next resolution. Its docstring says a registration issued after make-frame "is deterministically visible to the very next dispatch / subscribe in the SAME tick".

The real cause is that the page's frame has no :id. re-frame.frame/image-loaded-frame-ids (frame.cljc:1607-1618) "EXCLUDES no-id (direct) frames" and names EP-0023 §Frame, "direct frames bypass auto-reprojection". - C: spy before anonymous frame: 1 denial.
- D: anonymous frame, spy after, forced synchronous flush-pending-reprojection!: the flush returned {} (no frame moved), image-loaded-frame-ids read [], and 0 denials.

The spy is registered before (rf/make-frame {}), and one sentence says why: a frame made without an :id keeps the registrations it was made with and does not pick up later ones.

title: docs(resources testing): sections 1 and 3 assert view-model booleans on durable snapshots
description:
Found while running docs/resources/testing.md's snippets verbatim on the JVM for rf2-6ddy0 item 4. Docs only.

## Defect

`docs/resources/testing.md` section 1 (`article-loads-into-the-cache`) and section 3 (`favorite-invalidates-the-article`) assert derived view-model booleans on `rf/resource-state` and `rf/mutation-state`:

- section 1: `(is (true? (:has-data? state)))`
- section 3: `(is (true? (:success? m)))` and `(is (true? (:stale? (rf/resource-state ...))))`

Both functions return the DURABLE runtime row, not the view-model: `implementation/resources/src/re_frame/resources.cljc:144` ("Return a resource instance's durable runtime ENTRY") and `:188` ("Return a mutation INSTANCE's durable runtime row"). The derived booleans (`:has-data?`, `:success?`, `:stale?`) live on the `:rf/resource` / `:rf/mutation` subscriptions. So those three assertions read nil and fail. The page's intro sentence calling the two functions the snapshots a test asserts on directly carries the same assumption.

## Evidence

Scratch JVM run (never committed) of sections 1 and 3 verbatim, under the fixture rf2-6ddy0 installs on that page (`{:adapter plain-atom/adapter :ambient-frame nil}`), with Conduit-shaped `:realworld/*` registrations mirroring tutorial Parts 2-4: 2 tests, 2 pass, 3 fail, all three `(not (true? nil))` at exactly those assertions. Identical with and without `:populates` on the favourite, so it is not about populate. `:status :loaded` in section 1 passes, which is the control that the entry is really there.

Before rf2-6ddy0 the page's fixture was `(ts/make-reset-runtime-fixture {})`, which installs no adapter, so every example on the page errored earlier with `:rf.error/no-adapter-installed` and these assertions were never reached.

## Repair shape (not decided here)

Either assert on durable fields that `resource-state` / `mutation-state` do carry (for example the entry `:status`, and a staleness fact such as `:invalidated-at`), or read the booleans through the subscription the page already names. Check the row shape at source before choosing; nothing above establishes which durable key names are stable public surface.

## Observed, not verified

`docs/routing/testing.md:26` and `docs/ssr/testing.md:28` use the same adapter-less `(ts/make-reset-runtime-fixture {})`. Not run; if their examples call `make-frame` they will meet the same `:rf.error/no-adapter-installed`.

title: docs(story): two honesty paragraphs the research asked for — frames isolate STATE, not CSS/focus/portals (chapter 02); the agent loop has TWO HOSTS, JVM story-mcp and the browser via re-frame2-pair, and chapter 09 must say which on its first screen
description:
From the reconciled Story-parity research (ai/findings/Story/{astra,grok,fable}/report.md, 2026-09-14; filed under rf2-rln91). Both paragraphs are docs-only, S, and both close a place where a Storybook user would form a wrong belief in their first session.

1. docs/story/02-every-state-side-by-side.md — ISOLATION HONESTY. Story's workspace cells are frames: each has its own app-db, registrar view, effect table and epoch tape (spec/002-Frames.md; `:preset :story` in tools/story/src/re_frame/story/frames.cljc). They do NOT isolate the document: the canvas is a stamped div in one page, so CSS, focus, React portals and timers are shared across cells, where Storybook's per-story iframe isolates them (and Storybook's inline docs stories do not). One paragraph saying exactly that, with the consequence: a design-system CSS job may need an iframe boundary, and today Story does not offer one. Do NOT build an iframe canvas on the strength of this paragraph; the research lists it under do-not-build until a CSS-isolation job is named by a real user.

2. docs/story/09-multi-substrate-and-agent-loop.md — TWO HOSTS. The agent loop runs in one of two hosts and the chapter must say which on its first screen: the standalone story-mcp server (tools/story-mcp) runs in its own JVM against the registrar — fail-closed, no browser, 19 tools, live-browser questions such as list-substrates and read-a11y-violations answer capability-unavailable by design — while the browser route drives the human's live frame through re-frame2-pair (skills/re-frame2-pair/references/stories.md). Name the host distinction and frame ownership in the first screen, say which skill runs which loop (the skills currently split it: skills/re-frame2/references/tooling/story-mcp-loop.md vs the pair skill), and cross-link the story-mcp README's own statement of the split. Two host transports are acceptable if choosing the right one is easy; today the reader finds out by getting a capability-unavailable error.

title: Incomplete: replay epoch correlation can capture another JVM thread's dispatch
description:
Merged-PR audit of #9769 (1b36a7ad6eb774c26396b7f591cd9ce944ddbfc2), discovered from closed rf2-fzbj.19. The own-dispatch correlation claim is incomplete on the JVM: an unrelated same-frame dispatch on another thread can become the replay result's epoch ID.

Mechanism: perform-replay! arms state/arm-commit-observation! before entering router/dispatch-sync!, without holding the frame's serialization boundary. state/note-observed-dispatch! takes the first :rf.event/dispatched ID for that frame. If the replay thread is preempted after arming and another thread dispatches, capture records the unrelated dispatch ID, note-commit! stores its epoch, and the subsequent successful replay returns that unrelated epoch. Moving observation into epoch capture fixes public-listener nesting but does not make frame-wide first-arrival identity belong to the calling replay.

Deterministic actual-source JVM witness (exit 0): start a frame, dispatch [:audit/add 1], and replay that first epoch on a future. Wrap the real arm-commit-observation! only with CountDownLatch scheduling pauses immediately AFTER real arming. From another thread dispatch [:audit/add 100] while the replay thread is paused, then release it. Both events execute, app-db is {:n 102}; history triggers are [[:audit/add 1] [:audit/add 100] [:audit/add 1]]. replay-epoch! returns {:ok? true, :source-epoch-id 1, :event-id :audit/add, :epoch-id 2}, but its own replay epoch is 3. A subsequent ordinary replay correctly names its own epoch after cleanup. No fabricated dispatch IDs, commits, history, or application results were used. This pause models an ordinary JVM scheduling gap; it is not a CLJS single-thread claim.

Evidence: C:/Users/miket/.codex/tmp/audit-re-frame2-pr9769-concurrent-replay-probe-1.clj and .log/.exit. The log identifies the actual epoch/state.cljc source; relevant production files match the audited merge. Relevant sites: implementation/epoch/src/re_frame/epoch/state.cljc:327-391, capture.cljc dispatch observation, and tool_pair.cljc perform-replay! arming before dispatch-sync!.

Required correction: associate the observation with the replay invocation's own dispatch identity, or serialize the arming-to-dispatch interval using the existing frame boundary without holding user callbacks under an inappropriate lock. Keep the public replay API and router dispatch return unchanged. Add a deterministic two-thread regression exercising the actual public replay/dispatch path and preserve listener-nesting (including same handler/different arguments), queued-child retention/eviction and exceptional cleanup behavior. Do not broaden into general replay concurrency policy or new public diagnostics.

Impact is incorrect dev-tool causal evidence on JVM concurrent use; both application dispatches still run. The 541-test JVM epoch and 12051-test CLJS CI lanes are green but do not exercise this interleaving. No exact open finding among the 28 literal-open Beads records this defect/correction. This new finding is separate from the closed original; no source status or closure fields are to be changed. No mayor notification or acknowledgment is inferred from filing/pushing.
acceptance_criteria: A deterministic JVM two-thread public replay test pauses after real observation arming, executes an unrelated same-frame dispatch on another thread, resumes replay, and proves the result names its own replay epoch or nil only when that epoch was evicted; both dispatches execute. Existing same-handler/different-argument listener nesting, ordinary replay, queued-child retained/evicted results and failed-dispatch observation cleanup remain correct. Use existing dispatch/frame machinery and preserve public API shapes.
notes:
VERDICT (rf2-k0nr), fixed in PR #9785.

CORRECTION TAKEN: option 1, associating the observation with the replay invocation's own dispatch identity. It is implemented as arming-thread identity. On the JVM, `arm-commit-observation!` records the thread that armed it, and `note-observed-dispatch!` accepts an `:rf.event/dispatched` id only from that thread. The replay's own `dispatch-sync!` emits synchronously on the calling thread, so the first id that thread reports is its own. A listener's nested dispatch on the same thread is still refused, as under rf2-fzbj.19.

WHY NOT OPTION 2: a foreign dispatch emits its `:rf.event/dispatched` on its own thread BEFORE any drain lock. `dispatch-sync!` emits ahead of `drain-block!`, and an async `dispatch!` emits at enqueue. Serializing on the frame boundary therefore cannot keep that emit out of the armed window.

SCOPE: the CLJS path is unchanged (the check sits under `#?(:clj ...)`). The public replay API and the router's dispatch return are unchanged, there is no core edit and no new diagnostics. Files touched: `implementation/epoch/src/re_frame/epoch/state.cljc` and `implementation/epoch/test/re_frame/epoch_replay_cljs_test.cljc`.

REGRESSION PINNED: `replay-result-names-its-own-dispatch-not-another-threads`, in `epoch_replay_cljs_test.cljc` under `#?(:clj ...)`. It runs the replay through the public path on a future, parked by a `CountDownLatch` immediately AFTER the real `arm-commit-observation!`. The test thread then dispatch-syncs `[:review/add 100]` into the same frame and releases the replay. It asserts that the reported epoch is the replay's own new record and resolves to `[:review/add 1]`; that app-db is `{:n 102}`, so both dispatches ran; and that the other thread's record is never reported. No sleeps. Companion: `replay-reports-nil-not-another-threads-epoch-when-its-own-was-evicted` pins the documented nil under the same interleave. It is not a tooth, because the other thread's record is older and so is always evicted first.

EVIDENCE:
- RED: with the pre-fix `state.cljc` planted (blob `02f542f6a3`, confirmed by content hash), the replay namespace exited 1 with 3 failures, all in the tooth. The reported epoch was 14, the other thread's; the replay's own was 15. The run was 18 tests / 136 assertions.
- Restore: verified by blob hash (`927e53d994`) and by `git diff --quiet`.
- GREEN: the epoch JVM lane (test.yml job `jvm-epoch`) exited 0 at 543 tests / 7328 assertions, against a baseline of 541 / 7315. `npm run test:cljs` exited 0 at 12065 tests / 60143 assertions.

The bead's preserved behaviours stay pinned by the unchanged neighbouring deftests: same-handler/different-argument listener nesting, ordinary replay, queued-child retained and evicted results, and failed-dispatch cleanup.

RESIDUAL, NAMED AND NOT FIXED: `note-commit!`'s `:fallback-epoch-id` still takes the frame's first commit from any thread. It is read only in the no-dispatch-id posture.
Merged-PR audit #9785: NEW open finding rf2-c74lr tracks the remaining uncorrelated fallback: after :rf.trace/no-emit? is applied to the replayed handler, a foreign same-frame commit can still be returned as replay evidence. Normal arming-thread correlation is verified fixed. Deterministic public JVM probe recorded foreign epoch 2 with db n=102, while the no-interleave control returns nil. Source status and closure are preserved. This pointer is not mayor notification or acknowledgment.

title: ssr-node: reject unrepresentable HTTP correlation IDs before rendering
description:
Validate the HTTP representation of requestId before dispatch, rather than turning a successfully rendered request into a misleading render-threw 500 when its correlation ID cannot be placed in a response header. Ownership: impl_ssr_node; implementation/ssr-node/src/protocol.cjs:615-616 accepts any string requestId; src/http.cjs:137-143 captures it, :168-177 and :198-206 interpolate it verbatim into x-rf-ssr-request, :209-210 translate the resulting header exception into RENDER_THREW. README.md:336 and :639-643 document a correlation string echoed in that header without a representability constraint. Baseline 9e8ca973767f4ecff455421e48e1765d59783261; reviewed HEAD 50abcab5ce674e5107b34834ebbfd81d1af7e2cd, owned source unchanged. SOURCE_ROOT=C:/Users/miket/code/re-frame2; WORKTREE_ROOT=(none; read-only review). Trigger: use the existing chunked fixture with {protocol:1, entry:'app/root', requestId:'correlation-\u2026', state:{':bytes':'["

ok

"]'}}. This is valid JSON and passes validateRequest. U+1F600 in the ID also reproduces it; the README's ellipsis example is itself outside Node's raw header character set. Expected: correlation metadata does not masquerade as a renderer failure. Either preserve it through an explicitly encoded transport representation, or reject an unsupported HTTP ID as BAD_REQUEST_FIELD before acquiring an isolate. Actual: renderToString returns '

ok

' and the unchanged requestId, but buffered and streamed HTTP both return 500 / :rf.ssr-node/render-threw with TypeError [ERR_INVALID_CHAR]: Invalid character in header content ["x-rf-ssr-request"]. The renderer is correct and has already run. ASCII requestId succeeds through both modes. Impact/severity: P3, a request-local contract mismatch for callers using non-Latin-1 correlation tokens (or other header-invalid strings). It wastes render work and reports a server render failure that a caller/operator may retry or diagnose incorrectly. No process-wide availability or data-disclosure claim is made. Suggested minimal repair: at the HTTP boundary, check a string requestId with Node's header-value validator before service.renderFrames and return the existing BAD_REQUEST_FIELD 400 with detail.field='requestId' when not representable; document the HTTP header constraint. Keep the in-process protocol's string domain unchanged. If preserving arbitrary Unicode across HTTP is preferred, define one reversible ASCII encoding and document it consistently for buffered and streaming responses. Do not silently drop correlation, and do not rely on catching writeHead after rendering. Acceptance criteria: - ASCII IDs keep their current echoed value in buffered and streaming HTTP. - Ellipsis, emoji, and CR/LF IDs get the documented HTTP behavior: either encoded success with recoverable correlation, or a BAD_REQUEST_FIELD 400 before renderer admission; never render-threw 500 caused by response headers. - In-process renderFrames/renderToString retain their string contract. - Add a discriminator proving an invalid HTTP ID does not invoke the renderer if choosing request-local rejection. Fresh validation: Node v24.13.0, actual createService with existing chunked fixture and actual serve over real loopback TCP. Both Unicode IDs succeeded in-process and returned 500 in each HTTP mode; ASCII control returned 200 in each. Exact responses are in ai/surface-review-20260913/impl_ssr_node/probe-impl_ssr_node-1.log; the matching .cjs and .exit contain reproduction and exit 0 (assertions of current behavior). All transports/workers closed. No package-wide suite, production bundle, browser or JVM crossing run. The buildId header has the same raw-header mechanism but is not separately claimed or dynamically tested here. Deduplication: independently discovered during the 2026-09-13 fresh review; not part of rf2-fzbj.22's three findings. Current tracker searches of ssr-node titles and requestId, x-rf-ssr-request, ERR_INVALID_CHAR descriptions found no matching dedicated open issue. Closed rf2-8arzr.4 covers the JVM adapter crossing; neither it nor prior identifier renaming work resolves this HTTP exception. Parent rf2-gwye. This is a review issue only, with no fixer dispatched or source remediation authorized.
notes:
HELD (mayor, 2026-09-13): remediation of rf2-gwye findings awaits Mike's ruling on who fixes them. The rf2-gwye review closed 2026-09-13T00:42:37Z saying "finding remediation remains open and all prior ownership fences remain in force", and its notes mark new findings as review deliverables, not fixer work. Do not dispatch until that ruling is recorded here or on rf2-gwye. CLEARS WHEN: Mike names who remediates the rf2-gwye findings.
VERDICT (worker ssrnode-a, 2026-09-13): FIXED in PR #9744 (one commit on implementation/ssr-node/**).

Re-verified at the branch base before fixing. implementation/ssr-node was byte-unchanged since the reviewed HEAD 50abcab5ce, and the rf2-gwye review probe, copied to scratch and re-rooted at the worktree, reproduced all four defects with exit 0:
- // and http://[::1 each killed the child process with ERR_INVALID_URL at http.cjs:236;
- boot-exit start() stayed pending at 1000 ms against bootTimeoutMs 500;
- the split surrogate streamed as hex 3c703eefbfbdefbfbd3c2f703e;
- non-Latin-1 requestIds came back 500 render-threw.

What landed, finding by finding:
- rf2-gwye.22 (fzbj.22 finding 1, malformed request target). src/http.cjs guards new URL() inside the request listener and answers with the existing MALFORMED_REQUEST refusal (400, x-rf-ssr-refusal). handleRender now receives the already-parsed URL, so the second, unguarded parse is gone.
- rf2-gwye.23 (fzbj.22 finding 2, worker exit before readiness). The worker exit handler in src/isolate.cjs rejects start() as MALFORMED_MODULE, with detail {modulePath, exitCode}. Once ready has resolved this is a no-op, as the error arm's reject already is. It adds no new state and no second timer. Pool.start's allSettled sibling cleanup and release()'s replacement-failure arm observe the rejection unchanged.
- rf2-gwye.24 (fzbj.22 finding 3, surrogate pair split across streamed chunks). The streaming writer holds back at most one trailing high surrogate (holdTrailingHighSurrogate) and writes it with the next chunk, or alone before res.end(). That matches the buffered join's encoding of an unmatched surrogate.
- rf2-gwye.25 (requestId that no header can carry). http.validateHeaderValue('x-rf-ssr-request', requestId) now runs before service.renderFrames. Failure is refused BAD_REQUEST_FIELD 400 with detail.field "requestId", and the JSON refusal body still echoes the token. The in-process string contract is unchanged, and the README documents the HTTP constraint.

Regression rows:
- test/bytes.test.cjs: the malformed-target row, the split-surrogate row (split pair, empty intervening chunk, several split pairs, unmatched control, compared against Buffer.from(parts.join(''),'utf8') in both modes), and the requestId row (the renderer-call spy reads zero; an ASCII control echoes in both modes).
- test/timeout.test.cjs: eval exit 7 and boot exit 0 each reject createService promptly with bootTimeoutMs at its 30 s default. A 2-isolate start where one sibling exits rejects, the healthy sibling is terminated, and both threadIds read -1. A replacement that exits before ready refuses its queued waiter with REPLACEMENT_FAILED_REFUSAL, writes the operator stderr line, and close() completes.
- test/fixtures/exits.cjs gains the env switch RF2_SSR_NODE_EXIT_AT (eval, boot, boot-even-thread). With it unset, the fixture behaves as before.

RED control: the pre-fix src/http.cjs and src/isolate.cjs were planted from the parent commit (planted blob hashes equal the parent's). All four RED runs exited 1, each on its intended assertion. After the restore, the blob hashes equal the commit's and git diff --quiet exits 0.

Gates:
- npm run test:ssr-node (CI job node-ssr-node) exits 0 on the final base, 9 suites green.
- check_readme_links.py --ci exits 0.
- The changed-surface classifier arms only ssr_node.
- The tree-wide ratchets I ran all exit 0.

Skipped on purpose, one sentence each:
- No timing witness for prompt delivery of completed chunks: the writer holds back at most one code unit, and only when a chunk ends in a high surrogate.
- x-rf-ssr-build shares the raw-header mechanism, and so does the render catch's String(err) wording a failure there would reach. The value is the module's own boot-time buildId rather than caller input, and no review claimed it, so both are left as they are.
- No global uncaughtException handler, and no extra boot timeout. Both beads ruled those out as substitutes.

spec/011-SSR.md needs no change. It names requestId as a field the JVM adapter sends but states no character set for it. The adapter sends (str (symbol frame-id)) and classifies any non-200 other than a 504 as ssr-node-refused, so a 500 that becomes a 400 lands in the same JVM error id.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #9744 with the request-local rejection. src/http.cjs checks requestId with http.validateHeaderValue before service.renderFrames, and refuses one that fails as BAD_REQUEST_FIELD 400 with detail.field requestId. The JSON body still echoes the token. The in-process string contract is unchanged, and the README documents the HTTP constraint. The regression row in test/bytes.test.cjs sends ellipsis, emoji and CR/LF IDs: 400 in both modes, with a renderer-call spy reading zero. An ASCII control is echoed in both modes. The row was RED (500 render-threw) before the fix. title: test: no floor in this repo counts EXECUTED assertions, so a namespace that runs nothing passes them all
description:
WHY THE rf2-6ppy / rf2-r51p CLASS WENT UNNOTICED: NO FLOOR IN THIS REPO COUNTS EXECUTED ASSERTIONS.
A NAMESPACE WITH N DEFTESTS AND ZERO EXECUTED ASSERTIONS PASSES EVERY ONE OF THEM.

Found by lanefix-a while repairing two such files (PR #9685), and recorded here rather than acted on
because building a gate is a judgement call rather than an obvious yes. This is the STRUCTURAL
reason a class of 16 files and ~106 assertions sat dead long enough to be discovered by audit.

=== THE THREE FLOORS, AND WHAT EACH ACTUALLY GRADES ===

  * check_test_lane_bijection.py, check B1 -- grades lane SELECTION, not EXECUTION. The old files
    WERE selected by :node-test. They simply skipped every row once selected, because each row sat
    behind a browser guard that is false on node. B1 is satisfied.
  * RF2_MIN_TESTS floor -- counts test VARS. A deftest that runs and asserts nothing still counts.
  * check-per-ns-isolation.cjs -- refuses only on `tests === 0`. N deftests is not 0.

So all three agree the namespace is healthy, and all three are answering a different question from
the one anybody cares about. That is the "instrument that is RIGHT and still answers a different
question" shape the method names: exercise any of them against a dead namespace and it comes back
green because nothing is malfunctioning.

=== WHY IT IS WORTH MORE THAN A TIDINESS ITEM ===

The failure is not merely absent coverage. Measured on xray_preset: a dead guarded row was a
PRECONDITION calling attach!, so the UNGUARDED assertion two lines below --
`(is (false? (attached?)))` -- passed vacuously on every PR, reporting a removed keyboard listener
to CI without one ever having been installed. lanefix-a then measured the inverse in a real
browser: with the bridge suppressed, attached? returned TRUE. A dead row hollowing a live one is a
false GREEN, not a gap.

=== THE SHAPE A GATE WOULD TAKE, IF ONE IS WANTED ===

Count assertions EXECUTED per namespace per lane and refuse zero, rather than counting test vars
declared. cljs.test already reports per-namespace assertion counts, so the signal exists; the work
is reading it and picking the floor. It is not obvious where the floor belongs -- a namespace whose
rows are all legitimately browser-only would read zero on node and must not fail there, so the
check is per-namespace-per-lane with an allowance, which is exactly the kind of rule that grows
teeth it should not have.

=== THE ARGUMENT AGAINST, STATED HONESTLY ===

Two workers have now flagged a lint rule for this class and neither filed one, both calling it a
judgement rather than a defect. The repo's stance is explicit about not over-engineering, and a gate
with a per-lane allowance table is a maintenance surface. The counter-argument is that this class
produced a false green, and a false green is the one thing a test suite must not do.

NOT DISPATCHABLE AS WRITTEN. Whoever picks this up should first decide whether the gate is wanted at
all; a verified "no gate, the class is closed by hand under rf2-r51p" is a complete outcome and
should be recorded as the close reason.
close_reason:
DECIDED: NO GATE. The three floors are characterised correctly and the gap is real, but the gate
this bead sketches CANNOT CATCH THE DEFECT THAT JUSTIFIES IT, and the repo already carries a
two-part answer to the class. Closed with no code change. Nothing to build; the residue is
rf2-r51p's.

=== 1. THE THREE PREMISES: ALL VERIFIED TRUE AT SOURCE ===

The universal negative holds — nothing in this repository counts EXECUTED assertions and refuses on
a floor. Searches for `assertions <`, `assertionCount`, `MIN_ASSERTIONS`, `min-assertions` return
zero code hits; the control (`tests\s*<\s*minTests|tests\s*===\s*0`) matches exactly two sites, so
the instrument finds test-count comparisons and there are no assertion-count ones to find.

  * check_test_lane_bijection.py B1 — STATIC SELECTION, never runs anything. `selected_by` is
    populated purely by `lane.selects(test_file.ns)` regex match. Confirmed by running it: exit 0,
    "1640 test-defining files, 45 lanes, every file selected and every selector reached".
  * RF2_MIN_TESTS — THREE implementations, all counting test VARS. runner.clj reads `(:test
    summary)`, never the sibling `:pass` key. shadow_node.cljs is weaker than this bead states: it
    counts `(count (env/get-test-vars))` — vars registered in the compiled build, BEFORE any test
    runs. run-browser-tests.cjs compares `ranCounts.tests < minTests` and discards the assertion
    member it parsed on the same regex.
  * check-per-ns-isolation.cjs:273 — `if (summary.tests === 0)`, confirmed. It parses `{tests,
    assertions}` off one regex (:226) and consumes `assertions` only for console display (:354,
    :371, :377). browser-test-report.cjs:155 says so outright: "RAN_RE has always captured both;
    nothing read them."

=== 2. WHY NO GATE: THE PROPOSED FLOOR IS GREEN ON ITS OWN MOTIVATING CASE ===

This is the decisive finding and it is structural, not incidental.

The false green is tools/story/test/re_frame/story/xray_preset_cljs_test.cljs. Its hollow row is at
:236 — `(when (exists? js/document) (xray-keybinding/attach!) (is (true? (attached?)) "precondition:
..."))`, an else-less guard. The vacuous assertion is at :248, UNGUARDED, two lines below the guard's
close. On node the guard is false, the precondition never runs, and :248 asserts `(false?
(attached?))` against a listener nothing installed.

But that namespace carries 17 deftests and 34 `is` forms, and the rest of them execute on node. A
census of "every assertion behind a node-false guard" does not classify this file as hollow. So a
per-namespace-per-lane "refuse zero executed assertions" floor reads NON-ZERO here and passes. So
does a per-deftest floor: the offending deftest itself executes two assertions on node — :246 and
the vacuous :248.

The floor therefore reaches only the WHOLLY-DEAD-NAMESPACE case, which is a coverage gap, and not
the FALSE GREEN, which is the thing this bead correctly calls the one failure a suite must not have.
Those are two different defects and the sketched gate reaches the weaker one.

=== 3. THE REPO ALREADY ANSWERS THIS CLASS, IN TWO PARTS, BOTH DOCUMENTED ===

(a) THE STATED-SKIP CONVENTION. implementation/fresco/test/re_frame/fresco/roots_frames_support.cljs
:97 defines `skip!` as `(is true (str "a multi-root claim needs a real React DOM — " why))`, and its
docstring gives the rule: ":node-test compiles these namespaces too ... every DOM claim in this arm
degrades to a stated skip there rather than to a false green." The same rule is stated independently
in the ns docstring of tools/xray/test/day8/re_frame2_xray/palette/recents_dom_cljs_test.cljs: "A
bare `(when ...)` body would leave the node lane holding a deftest with ZERO assertions, which is the
hollow shape rf2-6ppy exists to remove."

Adoption is high and measurable. Of the namespaces whose in-deftest assertions all sit behind
node-false guards, 58 of 61 already route the skip through `skip!` and so DO report assertions on
node. Teaching a census that `skip!` is an assertion drops the else-less-guard count from 911 sites
across 176 files to 321 across 97, and collapses fresco's `browser?` guards from 408 to 7. The
convention is not aspirational; it is the norm.

(b) THE CLASSIFIER ARM THAT MAKES THE OTHER LANE ACTUALLY RUN. TESTING.md:193 documents this exact
failure and its fix (rf2-8a6s): ":browser-test selects .*-dom-cljs-test$, so the package's three DOM
suites were already IN this lane — the lane just never ran on a diff that touched them, while the
consolidated :node-test build compiled the same namespaces and reported each DOM row as a stated
green skip. The surface passed having executed none of its DOM assertions." The remedy chosen there
was to arm `cljs_browser`, not to count assertions. TESTING.md:233-242 carries the general principle:
"Never treat a passing skip-ok diagnostic as evidence the behaviour was covered."

=== 4. THE REPO HAS A WRITTEN RULE AGAINST BUILDING IT ===

TESTING.md:24, carrying forward the lesson of the retired freeze gate: "A gate that hashes one side
of a claimed equality must reconstruct and compare the other; A HOLLOW GATE ADVERTISED AS PROOF IS
WORSE THAN NO GATE."

A per-namespace executed-assertion floor, advertised as closing the false-green class while being
structurally green on the only measured instance of that class, is precisely that shape.

=== 5. COST, MEASURED, SO THE TRADE IS ON THE RECORD ===

The runtime floor needs per-namespace assertion tallying added to
implementation/test-quiet/src/re_frame/test_quiet/shadow_node.cljs — a file whose own comments flag
its `:end-run-tests` defmethod as "the only thing that turns a RED cljs.test summary into a non-zero
node exit", hardened against two named hazards and pinned by its own contract-test suite — plus a
machine-readable emission, a checker, wiring on both lanes, and a new test.yml job, which moves the
check band the merge loop recomputes.

The static alternative that WOULD catch the false green (refuse an else-less guard wrapping
assertions inside a deftest) carries a residual baseline of roughly 110 lane-guard sites after
`skip!` is excluded — 31 `(browser?)`, 25 `(dom-available?)`, 20 window/localStorage, 16 `(exists?
js/document)`, 11 `bridge?`, 7 fresco `browser?` — plus 74 `rf.interop/debug-enabled?` sites on a
different axis. That is a migration across test trees, not a gate.

=== 6. RESIDUE, ALREADY OWNED ===

An independent census corroborates rf2-r51p rather than adding to it: the two files it singles out as
worst are exactly the two that survive as genuine defects — toolbar_persistence_cljs_test.cljs (a
plain `-cljs-test`, so node-only; every in-deftest assertion guarded, therefore executing nowhere)
and xray_preset (the false green above). rf2-r51p has already RULED the per-property convention, so
nothing here blocks it.

One observation NOT in rf2-r51p's scope, recorded rather than filed: three `-dom-cljs-test`
namespaces are silent on the node lane with no stated skip —
tools/story/test/re_frame/story/recorder/dom_capture_dom_cljs_test.cljs, its
dom_capture_stop_flush sibling, and tools/xray/test/day8/re_frame2_xray/theme/a11y_dom_cljs_test.cljs.
These are NOT coverage holes: the browser lane selects and runs them. They are convention gaps, worth
a `skip!` if anyone is in those files anyway, and not worth a dispatch of their own.

=== WHAT WAS NOT DONE, AND WHY ===

No gate, no fixture, no test.yml job, so the check band does not move. No test file was edited.

One cheap change was considered and declined: gating check-per-ns-isolation.cjs on the `assertions`
count it already parses and prints. It is about five lines, but its roster is a curated EP-0023
runtime-construction allowlist that deliberately rejects a blanket scan as too slow, so the floor
would police a set in which the hollow shape does not occur — near-zero value against a shared gate
whose surface arms the whole consolidated `cljs` job in CI. Trust the programmer; the convention is
the mechanism here, and it is already written down in three places.

title: False: Static panel API docs still describe migrated Fresco boundaries as reg-views
description:
Audited PR #9648 at 606ba24a190ee5b94ef7cb381f4f2d38163ca5de. Routes is now the fifth Static panel to export a Fresco boundary. tools/xray/spec/API.md around 415-431 still says each Static namespace exports a panel reg-view; docs/xray/api/reference.md carries the same obsolete Static inventory, and static/shell.cljs:114-117 and 495-499 still describe four bridges plus one Routes reg-view. These descriptions now misidentify the exported API and the registry's actual bridge values. The implementation Bead's notes identify the stale prose but no separate open correction owner exists.
Update the Static inventory and shell explanations to distinguish public boundary exports from the temporary callable registry bridges, and give the supported composition spelling if the reference describes composition. Preserve the existing valid symbol names and the fact that bridges remain until the registry contract changes. Scope this to the migrated Static surface; do not relabel unmigrated Dynamic panels or remove bridges as part of a documentation fix.
acceptance_criteria: Both public references correctly describe all five Static exports and their present registry composition; shell prose no longer calls Routes a reg-view. Validate links and relevant public symbols against the actual landed tree, without changing the runtime API.
notes:
== ALREADY IN FLIGHT AS OF 2026-09-11 ~09:56 AUSEST — DO NOT DISPATCH THIS SEPARATELY. ==

This bead was filed by the #9648 merge audit at 00:25Z. Two workers were dispatched against exactly
this surface roughly half an hour BEFORE it was filed, so the finding is independent corroboration
rather than new work. The audit and the dispatch agree on the fault, which is worth more than either
alone.

THE SURFACE SPLITS ACROSS TWO WORKERS BECAUSE ONE OF THE THREE FILES IS FENCED:

  docs/xray/api/reference.md      -> `routewit-a`  (worker/routewit-a)
  tools/xray/spec/API.md          -> `routewit-a`
  static/shell.cljs :114-117, :495-499 -> `dynshell-a` (worker/dynshell-a)

regions explicitly. `routewit-a`'s brief names the two markdown pages and explicitly tells it NOT to
touch `static/shell.cljs`.

WHAT THIS BEAD ADDS THAT MY BRIEFS DID NOT SAY, and it is worth keeping: the instruction to
distinguish PUBLIC BOUNDARY EXPORTS from the TEMPORARY CALLABLE REGISTRY BRIDGES, and to preserve the
fact that the bridges remain until the registry contract changes. My briefs said "correct them to the
shipped shape", which is weaker and could be satisfied by prose that flattens the two into one. The
bridges are not an implementation detail to paper over — the L4 registry holds a callable, and that is
exactly what blocks `[(:panel tab)]` from heading a boundary.

CLOSE THIS WHEN BOTH PRs LAND. It needs no dispatch of its own.

== TWO OF THREE SURFACES LANDED IN PR #9650 (merged, trunk e4563a126f). THIS BEAD STAYS OPEN FOR THE
== THIRD, AND CLOSING IT NOW WOULD SILENTLY DROP THAT SURFACE. ==

DONE:
  docs/xray/api/reference.md    corrected
  tools/xray/spec/API.md        corrected

STILL STALE AT TRUNK, verified just now rather than assumed:
  tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/static/shell.cljs:117 still reads

  :495-499 region carries the same shape. That file holds 12 `reg-view` mentions in total, not all of

WHY IT IS NOT DONE: `static/shell.cljs` is inside the Dynamic shell slice's require closure and is
fenced to `dynshell-a`, live now. That worker's brief names those two comment regions explicitly, so
the surface is dispatched, not forgotten. CLOSE THIS BEAD WHEN `dynshell-a`'s PR LANDS, not before.

== THE WORKER WIDENED SCOPE DELIBERATELY AND WAS RIGHT TO ==

The stale prose was wrong for ALL FIVE Static panels, not only Routes. `routewit-a` corrected the
Static inventory WHOLE rather than one row of five, on the reasoning that correcting a single row of
a shared table makes the corrected entry read as the odd one out — worse than a uniformly stale table.
That is a judgement I would not have thought to ask for and it is the right one.

landed and their spellings are still moving, so a correction now would be re-stale within a slice or

not from my brief — mine said only "correct them to the shipped shape", which prose flattening the two

that is exactly what stops `[(:panel tab)]` heading a boundary and what makes the Dynamic shell slice
hard. Whoever finishes the `static/shell.cljs` half should carry that same distinction into it.

Keep the existing dynshell-a sequencing; this is not a request for another migration. No status or closure fields changed; this note is not evidence of mayor notification or acknowledgment.

reconciliation. The repair is to move the key into the attrs map.

title: fresco/ssr: compare use(browser()) inside a :server :render host against the adoption window on the Node arm; docs paragraph only if it holds
description:
Blocked on rf2-4ale (React 19.3 on trunk). Discovered from rf2-3y09 and from a second, independent analysis of the same release (ai/findings/react19.md, since deleted; its substance is here and on rf2-4ale).

WHAT 19.3 ADDS: react-dom `browser(reason?)`, consumed as `use(browser())`. On the server it suspends -- the nearest Suspense fallback lands in the HTML, and with NO boundary the server render FAILS. In the browser, hydration included, it returns undefined without suspending. renderToString / renderToPipeableStream / renderToReadableStream gain `onBrowserBailout(error, errorInfo)` with componentStack and the reason as error.cause. Reference: https://react.dev/reference/react-dom/browser

WHAT FRESCO ALREADY HAS, AND KEEPS: `{:server :client-only :fallback ...}` through the per-root hydration adoption window, read as a `useSyncExternalStore` triple (implementation/fresco/src/re_frame/fresco/impl/codec.cljs:578-600; docs/core/fresco/18-ssr-and-hydration.md:217-236). It needs no Suspense boundary, agrees on hydration's first pass by construction, emits :rf.ssr/host-adopted, and ALSO covers the pure-CLJS SSR artefact (re-frame.ssr.suspense's own header: "Not React Suspense"), which browser() cannot reach. browser() reaches only Fresco's Node arm (implementation/fresco/src/re_frame/fresco/server.cljs:402 and :530, rdom-server/renderToString; its options object carries identifierPrefix only, :135-145). REPLACING the adoption gate is NOT on the table: fallback selection would become Suspense-boundary-dependent, siblings could disappear into a fallback, first-client-pass behaviour, instrumentation and error classification would all change -- product semantics, not a simplification to slip into a bump.

THE EXPERIMENT: one hosted browser-dependent widget with a useful declared placeholder. Compare (1) the current client-only policy with (2) a `:server :render` host that is server-safe except for one leaf, which bails that leaf with `use(browser())` under its own LOCAL Suspense boundary -- the finer-grained "third policy by composition", not a new :server value. Read: server bytes, first client render, adoption, sibling content, source attribution, and that no unintended recoverable error is raised.

DELIVERABLE: the comparison recorded on this bead. A short paragraph in 18-ssr-and-hydration.md under "Client-only components and fallbacks" ONLY if the composition holds cleanly on the Node arm. `onBrowserBailout` plumbing through render-options into the recovered-error stream ONLY if the recipe is adopted, under the existing bounded-diagnostics policy. Nothing in the SSR artefact.

close_reason:
CLOSED ON A REFUTED PREMISE, not on the experiment it asked for. PR #9583 carried the one paragraph that
survived, merged as 371c99d292. **This bead's own description contains a false claim, and that is the
finding.**

THE FALSE CLAIM: the description states that `renderToString` gained `onBrowserBailout` in React 19.3.
**It cannot reach this package at all.** Fresco's only server API is `renderToString`, which comes from
react-dom's LEGACY build, and `renderToStringImpl` reads exactly ONE caller option — `identifierPrefix`.
Measured 0 bailouts in development and 0 in production, agreeing with the source read. So the entire
`onBrowserBailout` half of this bead was conditional on a mechanism that is not reachable, and no plumbing
was built.

AND THE EXPERIMENT'S SUBJECT ALREADY EXISTS AT TIP. The composition the bead proposed to build and compare —
a `:server :render` host containing a `:client-only` leaf — is already there, and was measured working: clean
bytes, no Suspense machinery involved. There was nothing to compare against, because the "third policy by
composition" the bead wanted to demonstrate is the shipped behaviour.

SO BOTH DELIVERABLES WERE CONDITIONAL AND BOTH CONDITIONS FAILED — correctly. What landed instead is a short
paragraph in `docs/core/fresco/18-ssr-and-hydration.md` documenting the mechanism that DOES work, which is
the useful residue of the investigation rather than a consolation prize.

WHAT THIS BEAD REFUSED, AND THE REFUSAL STANDS UNCHANGED: replacing the adoption gate was never on the table.
Fresco's `{:server :client-only :fallback ...}` runs through the per-root hydration adoption window as a
useSyncExternalStore triple; it needs no Suspense boundary, agrees with hydration's first pass by
construction, emits `:rf.ssr/host-adopted`, and covers the pure-CLJS SSR artefact that `browser()` cannot
reach at all. Swapping it would make fallback selection Suspense-boundary-dependent, could make siblings
disappear into a fallback, and would change first-client-pass behaviour, instrumentation and error
classification. Nothing measured here disturbs that.

THE GENERAL LESSON, WHICH IS WHY THIS CLOSE REASON IS LONGER THAN THE WORK: a bead whose premise comes from
reading a release note rather than from reading the installed package can be internally coherent, well
specified, correctly fenced, and about nothing. This one was filed off a second independent analysis of the
same release and still carried the error. The check that caught it was reading `renderToStringImpl`'s option
handling at source — one file, minutes — and it should have happened at filing.

Gates and isolation are recorded on rf2-26hs, which shared this PR. AI attribution declined in both commits
and the PR body.

title: machines: settle the region-sourced CROSS-REGION target — reject at registration or support it (XState v6 alpha.17 supports it; re-frame2 silently reads it as an in-region path)
description:
Found while correcting spec/005-StateMachines.md's parallel-broadcast paragraph under rf2-uvby (the audit of PR #9388 flagged the overreach).

MEASURED AT SOURCE (2026-09-07, tip of origin/main):
- implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines/parallel.cljc build-region-machine constructs a SYNTHETIC single-machine spec from (get parent-machine [:regions region-name]) alone, and the SELECT/APPLY passes drive each region through that synthetic spec. A region-local :on / :always / :after :target is therefore resolved against THAT REGION'S OWN BODY.
- Only apply-root-region-target (the root :on / :after ancestor fallback) normalises region-qualified targets [[:a :x] [:b :y]].
- Consequence, per the rf2-uvby PR-audit probe: a root :on {:go {:target [:b :two]}} on {a:one, b:one} yields {a:one, b:two}, but the SAME target written under a region-:a state's :on yields {a:[:b :two], b:one} — the region name is consumed as an in-region path segment. No :rf.error/machine-unresolved-target is raised.

WHY THIS IS A GENUINE GAP RATHER THAN AN OBSERVATION: the author gets a nonsense configuration silently. Either spelling is defensible as the answer, but the present behaviour is neither.

TWO CANDIDATE DISPOSITIONS — this bead is the argument, not the implementation:
(a) REJECT at registration. A region-local :target whose head names a DECLARED SIBLING REGION fails with a dedicated :rf.error/* (sibling of :rf.error/machine-parallel-root-on-bad-target). Cheapest, fail-closed, and consistent with re-frame2's posture that cross-region coordination is expressed either through the root ancestor fallback or through tags-as-stateIn guards. Recommended.
(b) SUPPORT it, matching XState v6 alpha.17: 'A cross-region transition now only exits the region containing its targets. The source region and other sibling regions stay in their current states.' This needs its own argument — it widens the region abstraction (a region would stop being a self-contained synthetic machine) and touches target resolution, the root fallback and the Xray projection.

PRIMARY SOURCE for the v6 side: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/statelyai/xstate/refs/heads/next/packages/core/CHANGELOG.md (the v6 alpha entries live on the next branch only; the main-branch changelog tops out at 5.32.6 and has no v6 entries). Registry dist-tags re-read 2026-09-07: latest=5.32.6, alpha=6.0.0-alpha.52, no stable v6.

NOT A CITATION REFRESH. rf2-uvby corrected the SPEC PROSE so it no longer advertises the capability; this bead decides the RUNTIME answer. Per rf2-2qfi's frame, do not chase an alpha — v6 has 52 alphas and no stable release, and EP-0029 C17 (alpha-churn exactness) stays rejected. Decide (a) or (b) on re-frame2's own merits.
notes:
2026-09-08 (worker mach-a, PR #9404) — SETTLED as (a) REJECT at registration. Cross-region SUPPORT deliberately NOT implemented; the XState-v6-alpha parity question is left open and is recorded as open in spec/005.

PREMISE CORRECTION, measured at source on origin/main e2d1981990. The bead reports the case as neither rejected nor supported with no :rf.error/machine-unresolved-target. Half of that does not hold:
  - A region STATE-NODE's :on with {:target [:b :two]} was ALREADY rejected at registration — :rf.error/machine-unresolved-target, ex-data {:target [:b :two] :state :one :slot :on}. The filer's probe drove machine-transition on a RAW machine map, which bypasses registration validation entirely; that is why it observed the silent runtime {:a [:b :two], :b :one}.
  - The real unguarded slot is the REGION BODY's own root :on — that region's ancestor fallback, which does fire. validate-transition-targets! walks only nodes inside :states, so this slot was never reached. BOTH a cross-region [:b :two] and a plainly-missing [:nowhere] registered cleanly and the runtime committed the unresolved vector verbatim into the region's state slot: a nonsense configuration, no error, no trace.

DELIVERED (PR #9404):
  1. validate-transition-targets! now walks each region body's own :on, decl-path [] against that region's :states — the exact analog of the flat-machine-root branch beside it. (A region-root :after cannot reach that point; validate-non-parallel-root-after! rejects it.)
  2. The :rf.error/machine-unresolved-target message became actionable: when an unresolved vector target's head names a declared SIBLING REGION it says so, says what [:b :two] cannot mean, and gives the two spellings that DO express cross-region movement (the root :on/:after region-qualified target, and the :tags/:all-state sibling-state guard). :region/:regions join the ex-data. walk-state-nodes-with-scope carries the owning region name for this; diagnostic only, resolution unchanged.
  3. spec/005 §Cross-region coordination gains two paragraphs pinning the rule, the rejection, and that the v6 parity widening is NOT decided here.

NO NEW ERROR ID. :rf.error/machine-unresolved-target already names 'a well-shaped target that resolves to no declared state', which is exactly this — 009 catalogue and conformance fixtures unchanged. A sibling of :rf.error/machine-parallel-root-on-bad-target would have needed a 009 catalogue row, and 009 was fenced for this dispatch.

CONTROLS pinned so the rejection is not too broad: a nested in-region path whose head SHADOWS a sibling region's name (region :a declaring a real compound state :b) still registers and still resolves to {:a [:b :two], :b :one}; a resolvable region-root :on still registers and still fires. The check is region-scoped, not name-scoped.

GATES: full machines JVM suite exit 0 (1213 tests / 4415 assertions); check_doc_slugs.py exit 0, proved to read the worker tree by a planted bogus anchor going red at spec/005:1779 and restored under a verified git blob hash; keyword-catalogue-drift, retired-spellings and require-alias-dialect all exit 0. Merged-PR audit #9404 (1e852777cdc65c0da311119a56bbdb7ae221acbe, merged 2026-09-07T14:51:29Z). Registration implementation and its scoped positive/negative controls are accepted: the previously unvalidated region-root :on now rejects unresolved targets; real in-region paths shadowing sibling names still register; existing error taxonomy is reused. The raw machine-transition probe bypassing registration is correctly distinguished from the actual registration gap.

The new Cross-region coordination paragraphs at1783-1785, the implemented validator and this owner's close note instead settle rejection NOW and leave only future SUPPORT widening undecided. A reader of the earlier normative paragraph is explicitly told the current disposition is unresolved on this closed owner.

Align that earlier scope note with the decision this PR actually shipped: region-local unresolved cross-region targets are rejected at registration, valid shadowing in-region paths remain valid, and only a future cross-region-support widening is undecided. Link to the new section rather than leaving the reject-or-support choice open. title: [implementation/ssr-node] Preserve the torn-response count on timeout and isolate loss
description:
Source snapshot 7ffdacf24d797b67864af78a4625b2c1cb3ef8fd. implementation/ssr-node/README.md:374-378 and src/service.cjs:23-29 promise a failure after emitted chunks carries detail.afterChunks, including an isolate dying under a render. src/isolate.cjs counts chunks on pendingRender at :211-213 and attaches the count for worker-reported errors :232-235, but deadline rejection :179-189 and _failPendingRender :256-265 discard it. Service preserves those Refusals unchanged. Supported sequence: an async renderer emits a chunk and then exceeds its deadline (or an escaped callback crashes its worker). renderFrames yields the chunk, then throws render-timeout/isolate-lost without the documented torn-response count. A transport/consumer using that advertised discriminator sees undefined despite already-emitted body bytes. Existing HTTP remains safe because it independently checks res.headersSent and destroys the stream; this finding does not claim it serves truncated HTML. Tiny isolated source-method probe (Node exit 0, no worker/listener/build/files): require Isolate from src/isolate.cjs; instantiate it with modulePath unused; supply worker={postMessage:m=>setImmediate(()=>i._handleRenderMessage({t:'chunk',id:m.id,seq:0,html:'

first

'})),terminate:()=>Promise.resolve(0)}; call i.render({entry:'root'},{timeoutMs:15,onChunk:f=>seen.push(f)}) while a bounded keepalive timer permits deadline observation. Result: {chunks:1,code:':rf.ssr-node/render-timeout',detail:{timeoutMs:15,isolate:0,threadId:null,entry:'root'}}. The real timeout/count path executes; actual Worker crash and HTTP paths source-traced, not rerun. Smallest repair: preserve pendingRender.chunkCount as service-owned afterChunks on terminal timeout/lost/close refusals before clearing pending state. Keep refusal codes, sanitized wording, local diagnostics, hard termination and reuse/replacement unchanged. Dedupe: active+closed ssr-node/afterChunks searches and relevant memories; fully read rf2-c38b including async reopening/delivery and rf2-6r9j.77. Those own closed exception egress/unused stack fixes, not loss of the service-owned chunk count; preserve their boundary decisions. Latest mayor HEAD 90e9b0008ac96bb59e0e9f6ec03de8e1d650f21d has no relevant drift. No full suite/build run.
acceptance_criteria: Before/after-chunk timeout and escaped-worker-error cases expose afterChunks 0/exact count through renderFrames; no success completion follows failure. Streaming HTTP still destroys an already-committed response. Existing code distinctions, sanitized error wording, operator trace and replacement behavior remain intact.
close_reason: PR #9377, commit 958bb6143d. implementation/ssr-node/src/isolate.cjs now stamps the service-owned afterChunks onto every terminal refusal that ends an in-flight render, BEFORE pendingRender is cleared: the deadline rejection (via _settlePendingRender, which now hands the settler the pendingRender it is settling), _failPendingRender (a crashed or exited worker thread — the path where nothing else still knows the count, because the worker is gone and never posts an error message), and close(). title: [implementation/hicasso] Do not label a privacy-folded epoch sum as an exact React snapshot
description:
Snapshot 7ffdacf24d797b67864af78a4625b2c1cb3ef8fd; relevant source unchanged at mayor HEAD a7b6793a0d6a0614a1cc64d5988afa93d1e4c490.

Supported case: a frame uses a whole-value sensitive policy (an event returns :sensitive [[]]), and two mounted boundaries respectively read [:row "secret-a"] and [:row "secret-b"]. Each holds one raw readset, but both queries project to :rf/redacted and therefore both exported boundary identities are the same [frame :row :rf/redacted]. Advance the cells so their epochs are positive eA and eB.

Expected: keep the intentional privacy fold, but do not report a fabricated per-boundary React comparison as proven. Actual: explain-render reports :snapshot (+ eA eB). Boundary A's real snapshot is eA and B's is eB; no boundary compares the exported sum.

Exact cause in implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/tool.cljs:
- read-identity:94-112 deliberately folds arguments the egress policy removes. This is correct and must be preserved.
- entry-rows:188-233 groups entries by projected boundary identity and unions their RAW read keys at 214-218. The emitted :reads therefore contains both distinct raw cells' projected rows.
- explanation:466-524 builds epochs from those unioned :reads and emits their sum as :snapshot at 505. Its contract at 470-474 calls this the sum React compares.
- The actual collector make-snapshot, impl/collector.cljs:732-756, iterates ONE entry's keys, not the union of entries in a privacy group.

This is not merely a misleading internal comment: tools/xray/spec/027-Hicasso-Evidence.md:232-236 and tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/tool-descriptors.edn (explain-render entry) tell consumers that :snapshot is the exact individual React checkIfSnapshotChanged number. The folded explanation also loses :read-orders, so it carries no explicit distinction at the point this precise claim is made. Impact is a false debugging answer for applications correctly protecting sensitive queries, not an application render failure.

Smallest repair: preserve privacy-safe aggregation and honestly represent the snapshot as unknown/aggregate when a projected group contains distinct raw readsets. Keep exact individual snapshot semantics for truly identical raw sets (including different read orders). Do not reveal secret arguments, add synthetic occurrence IDs, or undo settled grouping. Align any affected consumer claim with the chosen honest representation.

Dedupe: searched all statuses for explain-render, read-orders, peak-epoch, projected edge, boundary key and relevant Hicasso snapshot/evidence records; relevant memories returned no matching ruling. Fully read rf2-6c12m.21 (envelope simplification and commit-owned view attribution) and rf2-6r9j.196 (lexical projection-role names). Intentional folding is explicitly settled in Xray spec027:207-214 and is NOT the requested change.

Execution limits: exact source causal trace, actual producer/consumer contracts and existing tests inspected. No CLJS/browser/build/test suite executed; no code changes.
acceptance_criteria: Mount two distinct single-read entries whose queries project identically; after positive epochs, the folded explanation must not claim their sum is an individual React snapshot. Assert no secret arguments escape. A group containing only two read orders of the same raw set must keep the exact snapshot. Pin the distinction at the producer and update affected consumer claims without changing privacy grouping.
close_reason: PR #9393. Premise verified at source post-#9375 and it held. entry-rows unions the RAW read keys of a projected group, and explanation summed that union's epochs and emitted it as :snapshot, whose contract called it the exact checkIfSnapshotChanged number — but make-snapshot (impl/collector) sums ONE entry's keys, so React held eA at one boundary and eB at the other and nothing compared (+ eA eB). description:

   PR #9305 therefore follows the `:url-bound?` precedent for value handling — an unrecognised member selects no listener — and DOES ship the artefact-missing preflight, which needed no new id (`:rf.error/resources-artefact-missing`, the mirror of the :url-strategy-without-routing rule, with a test pinning :where, :frame-id and zero residue).

Note the value-shape half is genuinely optional under the project stance ("trust the programmer", no nagging diagnostics) — decide it on merit rather than treating it as owed.

3. spec/Spec-Schemas.md FrameMeta — add `[:revalidate-on {:optional true} [:set [:enum :focus :reconnect]]]` beside `:url-bound?`. Documentation only: frame config is pass-through (re-frame.frame/frame-meta merges :config verbatim and core declares no closed key set), so nothing in core needs the key declared for it to work.

THE HUNK NO GATE INSPECTED, AND HOW IT WAS CHECKED INSTEAD. The FrameMeta edit lands INSIDE a fenced clojure block (fence opens at Spec-Schemas.md:4282).
