title: test(core): no :elide-asserts build exists anywhere, so the assertion-elided posture is proved by construction and never executed
description:
FILED BY THE MAYOR 2026-09-05, from worker coreguard-a's rf2-xn13 report. The worker DECLINED to claim a probe it could not execute, and this bead exists so that decline is recorded as work rather than lost as a caveat.

THE MEASUREMENT, from that worker: there is NO :elide-asserts build anywhere in this repository — zero hits across *.edn, *.cjs, *.yml, *.sh and *.md. Re-run that census at tip before acting; it is a count and counts go stale first.

WHY IT MATTERS. rf2-xn13's whole subject is that (assert (map? config-map) ...) is ELIDABLE, so a legitimate consumer build with assertions off silently accepted a non-map and applied nothing. The fix replaces the assert with an always-on when-not + throw-error!, and the accompanying dual-posture test is genuinely clever: it reads configure!'s ACTUAL source form and re-compiles it under *assert* false into a throwaway namespace, with an anti-vacuity control proving the harness really elides. That is a compile-time control on the JVM and it is the right test.

WHAT IS STILL NOT PROVEN, and it is a narrow gap rather than a hole: nothing in CI ever COMPILES this codebase with assertions elided, on either host. The rf2-xn13 criterion holds by construction — the source is host-neutral .cljc and no assert form remains in the guard — but 'by construction' is an argument, and every other guard in this repo that was believed by construction and never executed is why the method keeps saying a search returning zero is not a check that passed.

THE QUESTION FOR WHOEVER TAKES THIS, and it is a real fork rather than a foregone conclusion: is a permanent :elide-asserts build worth its cost? Arguments against are strong and the stance backs them — adding one touches implementation/shadow-cljs.edn, which is hot-zone and a standing serial bottleneck; it adds a compile to the matrix for a posture no shipped consumer has yet reported using; and 'not over-engineering or gold plating' is exactly the clause that rejects a whole build id to prove one guard. Arguments for: the elided posture is a REAL consumer configuration, it is the one this bug lived in, and it is currently unobserved on every artefact rather than just this one.

A CHEAPER MIDDLE OPTION worth costing first: assert the property by source inspection across the public boundary rather than by compilation — a gate that refuses a bare (assert ...) as the sole guard on a public-facing argument check. That catches the class rather than this instance, needs no new build, and touches no hot-zone file.

DO NOT dispatch this as an implementation task before that fork is settled. The deliverable of a first pass is the cost of each option, not a build.
notes:
=== FORK SETTLED 2026-09-05 19:30 AUSEST (worker elide-a, trunk 85d7b49fe5) ===
RULING: do NOT add an :elide-asserts build, and do NOT add a source-inspection
gate. Closing as not-worth-doing. No code change; no PR. Evidence below.

1. THE PREMISE HOLDS, re-measured at tip with biting controls.
   `git grep -F ':elide-asserts' -- '*.edn'` => 0 hits (control ':compiler-options'
   over the same file set via the same instrument => 5 files, so the instrument
   bites). `git grep -F 'elide-asserts' -- '*.yml' '*.sh' '*.cjs' '*.js' '*.json'`
   => 0 hits (control 'shadow-cljs' same set => hits). Carriers of the literal
   are 4 files and only 4: core.cljc (2, one of them a COMMENT quoting the
   retired form), configure_test.clj (1), spec/009-Instrumentation.md (1), and
   this bead's own export. Note 'elide' alone is a heavily overloaded DOMAIN word
   here (wire elision, trace elision, DCE) - that axis is noise, not signal.

2. BUT THE POSTURE IS ALREADY PROVEN BY EXECUTION, NOT BY CONSTRUCTION - and I
   PROVED THE TEST DISCRIMINATES rather than trusting it.
   `configure-non-map-guard-survives-assertion-elision` recompiles configure!'s
   ACTUAL source form under *assert* false and exercises it. I planted the
   original rf2-xn13 bug back into core.cljc as a one-line change - the bare
   `(assert (map? config-map))` restored as the SOLE guard with the throw-error!
   made dead code under `(when-not true ...)` - and the suite went RED with the
   original bug's exact signature:
     FAIL configure-non-map-guard-survives-assertion-elision (configure_test.clj:380)
     "assertion-elided build still fails loud on :trace-buffer"
     expected: (some? ex)   actual: (not (some? nil))
   i.e. the elided build silently returned nil, which IS the bug. Captured exit
   codes: baseline 0 (6 tests / 56 assertions, 0 failures); sabotage 1 (6
   failures, 1 error); restored 0 (6 tests / 56 assertions). Restore verified by
   blob hash, not by diff: working blob == committed object == pre-plant hash
   ed9ad8d8e9f81f56c018e6daf8d2d71653b92bd4.
   So the bead's "'by construction' is an argument" objection is DISCHARGED for
   the guard that actually had the bug. The CLJS half follows by source identity
   - one .cljc file, no reader conditional in the guard, no elidable construct in
   the form - with the sibling host's behaviour executed.

3. THE CLASS THE MIDDLE OPTION WOULD GATE IS STRUCTURALLY EMPTY, which is what
   kills that option rather than mere cost. Across ALL of implementation/*/src
   there are exactly TWO bare language `(assert ...)` forms, both in
   adapters/reagent-slim/src/reagent2/ratom.cljs (lines 230, 324). EVERY other
   `(assert` match is a call to a named always-on helper FUNCTION -
   assert-registrar-query-has-frame!, assert-path-equals, assert-url-value!,
   assert-fragment!, assert-app-schema-path!, assert-bulk-schemas-arg!,
   assert-roster-complete! - which are plain fns and not elidable at all. The
   repo's guard idiom is therefore already structurally non-elidable. Verified
   line-oriented AND flattened (whitespace-collapsed) over the same file set.

4. AND THE TWO SURVIVORS ARE CORRECT AS THEY STAND, so a gate's first act would
   be to allowlist 100% of its own findings. ratom.cljs's ns docstring states
   "RAtom and Reaction shapes match stock Reagent byte-for-byte"; both asserts
   are that byte-for-byte match with stock Reagent / cljs.core Atom, where
   matching the host IS the contract. Neither degrades to a silent wrong answer:
   the validator one mirrors cljs.core/atom's own elidable validator exactly (so
   diverging would be the fidelity BUG), and the read-only Reaction one becomes a
   loud TypeError under elision rather than a silent no-op.

5. THE REALISTIC ELISION VECTOR IN THIS REPO IS NOT :elide-asserts AT ALL, and it
   is clean. This codebase ships :advanced + goog.DEBUG=false, and core.cljc
   carries 17 goog.DEBUG / debug-enabled? gates. The configure! guard's whole
   throw path lives in error.cljc, which carries ZERO of them and zero asserts
   (control: the same grep reads 17 on core.cljc, so it bites). throw-error! is
   an unconditional defn -> thrown-ex-info -> ex-info + throw, reachable from a
   live call site and so not DCE-able. The guard therefore survives BOTH vectors,
   and the more probable one was never in question.

COSTING OF THE THREE OPTIONS, as the bead asked for.
 (a) New :elide-asserts build - REJECTED. Edits hot-zone shadow-cljs.edn, adds a
     permanent compile to every PR forever, and MOVES THE CHECK-COUNT BAND the
     merge criterion is measured against. It would prove by compilation a
     property already proven by a STRONGER instrument (execution of the real
     source form, with a planted-fault control). Textbook gold-plating.
 (b) Source-inspection gate refusing a bare assert on a public boundary -
     REJECTED, on evidence rather than on cost. Zero instances to catch (3), and
     its only two candidate matches are legitimate (4). A gate that must
     allowlist every finding it can make gates nothing, and "trust the
     programmer" plus "don't litigate the minutiae" both point away from it.
 (c) Close as not-worth-doing - CHOSEN.

CHECK-COUNT BAND: UNCHANGED. No new build id, no new CI job, no workflow edit.

NOTHING IS STALE AS A RESULT. spec/009-Instrumentation.md's :rf.error/configure-bad-arg
row (held by devcon-a this tick) remains accurate word-for-word - re-read and
confirmed, no follow-up needed. No spec, doc or catalogue edit is owed.

RESIDUAL RISK ACCEPTED: a future contributor could write a new elidable guard on
a new public boundary. Untested-for by choice. The teaching is already in two
tracked records - the 18-line comment above the guard in core.cljc, and the 009
catalogue row - and the surrounding idiom is visibly assert-*! named fns.
close_reason: Fork settled: no :elide-asserts build and no source-inspection gate. The elided posture is already proven BY EXECUTION (configure-non-map-guard-survives-assertion-elision recompiles configure!'s real source under *assert* false); a planted-fault run reproduced the original rf2-xn13 signature (elided build returned nil) and went red, so the test discriminates. The class a gate would catch is structurally empty: zero bare language asserts on any public boundary in implementation/*/src, the idiom being always-on assert-*! helper FNS; the only two language asserts are stock-Reagent byte-for-byte ports in reagent-slim/ratom.cljs, both correct. The realistic vector here is :advanced + goog.DEBUG=false, and error.cljc's throw path carries zero debug gates. A build would move the check-count band to prove a property a stronger instrument already proves. Full costing of all three options in the notes.

title: Clarify duplicated nine-states todo generator names
description:
## Finding
The live and Story variants of the nine-states pattern copy the same private todo generator but call it the abbreviated gen-todos, with one-letter count/index locals. The surrounding prose calls this a generator and the helper is example-facing teaching code, so the role should be explicit.

## Evidence
- examples/patterns/nine_states/core.cljs:148 mentions the demo server's gen-todos; :204 defines (defn- gen-todos [n]) and the for binding [i (range n)]; :229 invokes it from the managed demo stub.
- examples/patterns/nine_states/stories.cljs:108-113 defines the copied private (defn- gen-todos [n]) and [i (range n)]; :128 invokes it for the Story request value.
- Both helpers produce the same Todo shape, making the duplicated abbreviated name especially likely to be copied into future example code without communicating that it generates synthetic todos.

## Ambiguity cost
Readers must expand gen to generate and infer whether n is an item count and i is a row index in two parallel implementations; this is avoidable ambiguity in the canonical pattern example and its Story twin.

## Recommendation
Rename the two private helpers to generate-todos and their count/index locals to todo-count/index, updating only local references and the explanatory comment. Keep all event names, :n query keys, /api/todos URLs, :value payload slot, Todo schema, generated values, and control flow unchanged.

## Compatibility, exclusions, and Phase-1 fence
These helpers are private and have no public API or selector contract. Do not rename the public run/mount!/register-all! entry points, namespace/file paths (including nine_states), event/sub/machine IDs, DOM/test/build IDs, routes, serialized keys, or behavior. Do not migrate naming across other examples or touch any existing Phase-1 removal/vestigial target, shared pattern docs, or files outside examples/patterns/nine_states; risky cross-example/public migrations remain open work.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. Both private gen-todos definitions and all in-slice references become generate-todos; no stale token remains in this pattern.
2. The helper arguments and loops use todo-count/index consistently, with no change to generated Todo IDs/titles/counts.
3. A semantic review confirms :n, :value, event IDs, URLs, schemas, routes, DOM/build selectors, and test-facing entry points are unchanged.
4. Focused example CLJS/JVM/lint gates and git diff --check pass.
close_reason: Implemented in the two nine-states private helpers and verified: generate-todos replaces gen-todos in core.cljs and stories.cljs; todo-count/index clarify local roles; :n query keys, :value payloads, event IDs, URLs, schemas, routes, and behavior unchanged. Consolidated CLJS gate exit 0: 11,167 tests / 55,726 assertions, 0 failures/errors; compile 1,889 files / 432 compiled / 0 warnings; patterns clj-kondo exit 0 (0 errors; 2 pre-existing warnings); no-banner lint_kondo self-test exit 0; git diff --check clean.

title: Clarify private routed-edge geometry locals in machines-viz
description:
## Finding

The private SVG route helpers in `tools/machines-viz/src/day8/re_frame2_machines_viz/chart/edges.cljs` use generic geometry names at the points where multiple coordinate systems and path stages meet. `poly-path` (lines 70-108) calls the point count `n`, accumulator `sb`, points `a`/`b`, `prev`/`cur`/`nxt`, rounding radius `r`, entry/exit coordinates `ex`/`ey`/`xx`/`xy`, and terminal `last-pt`; `path-midpoint` (lines 115-124) repeats `n`/`i`/`a`/`b`; `cross-hierarchy-label-anchor` (lines 140-169) repeats `n`/`a`/`b` and uses `len`/`bx`/`by`. These helpers are the sole implementation of routed-edge path geometry, and the same short names recur across branches with different roles (route endpoints, bend points, label anchor, and SVG command accumulator).

## Ambiguity cost

A reader auditing route correctness must repeatedly reconstruct whether `a`/`b` are endpoints, incident points, or a segment; whether `r` is the configured corner radius or a clamped per-corner radius; and whether `bx`/`by` are a bend point or biased label coordinates. - The machines-viz artifact-owned CLJS test bundle and the proportional JVM/CLJS gates pass.

title: Clarify test-quiet CLJS selector, floor, and warning-buffer roles
description:
## Naming finding

The CLJS runtime and its pure CLI/warning helpers mix wire vocabulary with ambiguous implementation names. In `shadow_node.cljs`, `test-syms`/`test-var-syms` obscure that they are user selectors, `the-var` and `available` hide the selected value/count, and private `reject-empty-suite!` actually rejects every below-floor suite, including non-empty ones. In `shadow_node_cli.cljs`, `opts`, `test-arg`, `matched-ns`, `matched-fqn`, `v`, and `sym` repeat the ambiguity. In `warn_buffer.cljs`, `buf`/`buf'`/`n` hide the buffer, appended value, and entry count. The red-warning fixture has two independent arms but calls the first merely `armed?`.

## Proposed names

Retain wire key `:test-syms`, public functions, namespaces/files, CLI flags, env vars, and reporter IDs. Rename lexical roles to `test-selectors`, `test-var-symbols`, `test-var`, `discovered-test-count`, `cli-options`, `test-argument`, `matched-namespaces`, `matched-var-symbols`, `selector`, `buffer`, `entry`, `capacity`, `appended-buffer`, and `entry-count`. Rename private `reject-empty-suite!` to `reject-below-test-floor!`, with count-bearing arguments. Rename fixture booleans to identify the red-warning and large-replay arms explicitly.

## Ambiguity cost

`reject-empty-suite!` currently understates a behavior that can reject a non-empty lane, while `test-syms` conflates parsed selector tokens with discovered test Vars. These names make the CLI's parse -> match -> unmatched -> floor decision harder to verify and make two fixture feature flags easy to confuse.

## Compatibility / risk

The only function-level rename is private. Public helper Vars and their arities remain intact because this test-only artifact is consumed across multiple build coordinators. Preserve `:test-syms`, `:unknown-args`, RF2_* env names, `--test=`/`--list`/`--help`, output/exit codes, ordering, match semantics, warning cap/materialization, and compile-cycle boundary. Do not rename or restructure the copied selector test or exit-integrity/duplicate rows tracked by Phase-1 beads `.76`, `.89`, and `.92`.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Internal selector values are named distinctly from discovered/matched test Vars while all public map keys, flags, env names, functions, and namespaces remain compatible.
2. The below-floor rejection helper's name and arguments accurately cover both empty and non-empty under-floor suites.
3. Warning-buffer locals and the two fixture-arm predicates identify buffer/count/feature roles explicitly, with all references and prose updated.

title: Remove dead machines-viz bindings, helper, and no-op wrappers
description:

- layout_cljs_test.cljc wraps one predicate in a single-argument and.

A manual underscore-alias sweep also found unused :as _opts in ai_generate.cljc, :as _spec in after_rings.cljs, and :as _region in mermaid.cljc, which naming suppresses from ordinary unused-binding lint. Mermaid also wraps a string literal in str, and share wraps already-string current-version in str.

The unused ->elk-edges evaluation is especially misleading: it looks like coverage but its value is discarded and the assertion uses a different path.

Recommendation
Remove the unused aliases, helper, pure expression, imports, and redundant wrappers; rename the required Reagent form-2 outer argument to _props. Keep the readable unit-factor nesting in resolve-timeout-ms unless separately justified; those information-level arithmetic hints are not dead behavior.

Risks and contracts

title: Truth the template substrate spec to the adapter-owned Reagent root
description:
## Evidence

The normative substrate spec still describes the Reagent generated core as rf/frame-root rendered through reagent.dom.client and says the scaffold calls reagent.dom.client/create-root directly (tools/template/spec/001-Substrate-Variants.md, table and What each variant emits).

Commit 7f104b4de9 (rf2-k5r9t) deliberately replaced that path. The emitted _reagent/core.cljs now allocates an inert reagent-adapter/client-root handle and calls reagent-adapter/render!. The adapter owns the underlying React Root, lazily creates or hydrates it on first render, tracks it for destroy-adapter!, and reuses it across hot reloads. The resource comments and template_emission_test.clj were updated and pin this adapter-owned contract; spec/001 was not.

## Impact

The current capability document teaches consumers to bypass the ownership API the generated scaffold is specifically designed to demonstrate. It also hides the meaningful Reagent/UIx distinction: adapter-owned opaque handle versus caller-owned uix.dom root.

## Recommendation

Update both spec/001 descriptions to name reagent-adapter/client-root plus render!, and explain that direct reagent.dom.client construction is encapsulated by the adapter. Reconcile any nearby generated-shape wording that says the emitted source directly calls create-root.

## Risks and contracts

This is documentation truthing, not an API rename. Preserve UIx create-root/render-root wording and the shared one-root/hot-reload lifecycle contract.
acceptance_criteria:
- The substrate summary and detailed Reagent core description match the emitted _reagent/core.cljs byte-level API calls.
- Reagent is described as using the adapter-owned client-root/render! surface, not direct reagent.dom.client/create-root.
- UIx remains accurately described as owning a uix.dom root.
- Documentation link/slug checks pass for the touched spec pages.

Both the substrate table cell and the 'What each variant emits' core.cljs entry are updated, and the entry now states the Reagent/UIx ownership distinction the old wording hid. UIx wording preserved (uix.dom/create-root + render-root, caller-owned). spec/002-Generated-Shape.md's hot-reload contract and its 'exactly one create-root' pin reconciled to what template_emission_test.clj actually asserts per substrate. title: Synchronize reply-conformance inventory with its live suites
description:
## Finding

The reply-conformance implementation was deliberately narrowed to vocabulary plus egress projection, but several surrounding inventory comments still describe the deleted synthetic family functor suite or names that never exist. The changed-surface policy test also uses a nonexistent reply-conformance filename instead of a tracked file.

## Evidence

- Commit `540c8af134` deleted `reply_functor_law_cljs_test.cljc` because it only re-proved core laws with synthetic transforms. It updated `implementation/reply-conformance/deps.edn` and both surviving namespace docstrings to say core plus the timer probe own functor laws.
- `implementation/README.md:225-232` still says this surface holds “the family-level functor/naturality law at the target-relocating families.”
- `implementation/shadow-cljs.edn:223-240` carries the same retired ownership claim and names route-loader relay / machine-spawn `:on-done` even though the deleted suite never exercised production relocation seams.
- `implementation/scripts/_changed-surfaces.test.cjs:3706-3710` names `implementation/reply-conformance/test/re_frame/reply_vocabulary_conformance_cljs_test.cljc`; the tracked file is `reply_vocab_conformance_cljs_test.cljc`. History shows the phantom spelling entered in `863a00b85c` and was never a tracked path. The classifier glob still returns the expected flags, so this is a weak/stale fixture rather than current routing failure.
- `reply_vocab_conformance_cljs_test.cljc:99-111` documents an `:error-work-status` descriptor field, but no `families` row or executable consumer defines it; history shows it has been documentation-only since the surface was introduced.
- The live surface consists of exactly four tracked files: `deps.edn`, the shared completion-time fixture, the vocabulary suite, and the egress-projection suite. Both suites are enrolled in the consolidated Node build and JVM `clojure -M:test` lane (currently 27 tests / 533 assertions).
- Searches of all tracker text for the deleted suite, phantom filename, and descriptor key found no existing owner.

## Impact

Maintainers are told a conformance guarantee exists at a family integration seam that has no such test, while the CI policy pin demonstrates routing with a filename no developer can edit. The dead descriptor field also invites a future author to populate inert metadata. None changes runtime today, but together they make coverage and ownership harder to reason about.

## Recommendation

Synchronize the implementation layout, Shadow build commentary, CI classifier fixture, and descriptor documentation with the live two-suite surface. Name vocabulary and egress projection as the owned guarantees; point the classifier test at the tracked vocab filename (and optionally the tracked egress file as an additional real-path row); remove the nonexistent descriptor field from the matrix documentation. Keep functor-law ownership explicitly at core plus timer-probe.

## Risks and contracts

Do not restore the deleted synthetic functor suite or weaken the actual core/timer functor tests. Do not change changed-surface outputs: reply-conformance remains source-less and should arm JVM plus consolidated Node only. Do not rename the tracked namespace/file as part of this cleanup unless a separately justified naming migration covers every selector and reference.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. No implementation inventory/build comment claims reply-conformance owns family-level functor/naturality integration.
2. Core `re-frame.reply` plus timer-probe remain named as the functor-law owners where useful.
3. Changed-surface policy tests use tracked reply-conformance file paths and retain the same positive and negative outputs.
4. The descriptor documentation lists only keys the `families` matrix actually consumes.
5. Repository search finds no live reference to the deleted `reply_functor_law_cljs_test.cljc`, the phantom `reply_vocabulary_conformance_cljs_test.cljc`, or the inert `:error-work-status` descriptor.
6. Focused classifier tests and both reply-conformance runtime lanes pass.

title: Remove the post-Freehand JVM fallback from spec-resource
description:
Evidence
- implementation/spec-resource/src/re_frame/build/spec_resource.clj:114-120 selects the shadow recording read only when env carries :ns; otherwise it reaches private spec-file, classpath-root, and clojure.java.io.
- The only tracked production call is implementation/scripts/api-manifest/probe/src/re_frame/api_manifest/cljs_publics.clj:113. Both callers of read-sidecar are macros consumed only from .cljs test namespaces, so their &env carries the ClojureScript :ns. The classifier audit in commit 93b110c20b independently established this as the single current macro path.
- The last tracked no-:ns call was implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/freehand/unpublished_head_absence_jvm_test.clj, which passed nil. It and every other Freehand consumer were deleted in c951808b47.
- implementation/deps.edn:113 still adds day8/re-frame2-spec-resource to the root :test alias even though the Freehand test path that required it was removed in the same retirement; the only live API-probe consumer paths are not present in that alias.
- .github/workflows/test.yml:2560-2564 still says the reader is shared by the Freehand fixture loader and API probe, contradicting the current source and the 2026-08-18 singular-consumer cleanup.

Impact
The unpublished artifact retains an unreachable filesystem walk that can bind to the wrong ancestor spec/ tree if reused accidentally, keeps an unnecessary root test dependency, and leaves CI documentation asserting a deleted consumer.

Recommended disposition
Remove the non-ClojureScript fallback and its io/classpath-root/spec-file support, make slurp-resource explicitly require the ClojureScript macro-expansion environment, remove the unused root :test extra-dep, and update current-consumer prose. Preserve resolve-after-require, recording-slurp, and the deterministic cold-load race test: those protect the live shadow-cljs path.

Risks/contracts
The only plausible lost behavior is manually expanding the API-probe macros from a JVM REPL. This artifact is explicitly unpublished and no tracked caller or documented workflow does that. If maintainers intend that workflow as a contract, keep it only with a direct test and documentation naming the supported consumer.

5. implementation/spec-resource JVM tests and the consolidated CLJS node/API-manifest probe lane pass.

description:

- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/image_assembly.cljc:744` defines private `standard-descriptor?` as `(boolean (:standard d))`.
- A repository-wide exact search for `standard-descriptor?` finds only that definition, and clj-kondo reports it as an unused private var.
- Git history shows the helper was used by the EP-0023 `resolve-collision` implementation. Commit `4203e0f959` (EP-0026 layered collision resolution, 2026-06-23) replaced that path with `resolve-within-image` / `inline-descriptor?` and removed the last calls without removing the helper.
- Current standard-descriptor policy still exists, but it is expressed directly through `:standard` checks/stamps elsewhere in the same file; this predicate is not that policy's seam.

Why this is vestigial
The private helper is unreachable and represents the superseded collision algorithm. Keeping it suggests that current standard-vs-inline resolution still routes through a predicate that it never calls, adding noise to a security-sensitive image assembly policy.

Proposed disposition
Delete only `standard-descriptor?`. Preserve `inline-descriptor?`, the current `:standard` checks/stamps, collision diagnostics, precedence, and image assembly semantics.

Risks / constraints
This is intended to be behavior-neutral. Do not use the cleanup to simplify or change EP-0026 collision ordering, standard descriptor eligibility, framework-default supersession, or provenance checks.
acceptance_criteria:
- `standard-descriptor?` is absent from `implementation/core/src/re_frame/image_assembly.cljc`, and a repository-wide exact search returns no occurrence.
- Existing core image assembly coverage, including `image_assembly_cljs_test.cljc`, `image_assembly_default_cljs_test.cljc`, and `image_assembly_cache_cljs_test.cljc`, passes on the supported hosts.
- The targeted lint no longer reports the unused private var, and no collision/precedence behavior or public API changes.
close_reason: Done in PR #9083. Premise re-verified at tip and HELD, and the sibling question the brief raised is answered: there are NO siblings. Reachability: two text instruments (line-oriented and whitespace-flattened over 4818 tracked files, .beads excluded, plus hyphen-normalised) plus clj-kondo :analysis, each against a live control. TARGET standard-descriptor?: exactly ONE occurrence repository-wide, the definition at image_assembly.cljc:744 (line re-derived, held). CONTROL inline-descriptor?, the live sibling immediately below it in the same file: 3 hits INCLUDING two executable calls at :781 and :785. Analyser: both :name standard-descriptor? entries sit in :var-definitions (:defined-by clojure.core/defn- and cljs.core/defn-, the .cljc dual branch), ZERO in :var-usages. clj-kondo also named it directly as an unused private var. SIBLINGS ENUMERATED: image_assembly.cljc carries exactly ONE clj-kondo finding in total - this one - and there is no unused private var anywhere else in core/src, so the EP-0026 layered-collision rewrite left nothing else stranded in that file. Deleted only standard-descriptor?. inline-descriptor?, resolve-within-image, the current :standard checks/stamps, collision diagnostics, precedence and framework-default supersession are untouched; EP-0026 collision ordering and provenance checks unchanged. After the change a repository-wide exact search for standard-descriptor? returns ZERO, and the targeted lint no longer reports the unused private var (clj-kondo core/src+core/test --cache false: 641 warnings BEFORE, 640 AFTER, the single delta being exactly this finding; errors 0 both sides). Core JVM :test exit 0, 2176 tests / 11149 assertions, 0 failures, covering image_assembly_cljs_test.cljc, image_assembly_default_cljs_test.cljc and image_assembly_cache_cljs_test.cljc; test:cljs exit 0, 11209 tests / 55849 assertions, 0 failures. The gate was PROVED live against this tree by planting an inverted inline-descriptor? at the adjacent line: exit 1 with 22 failures naming within-image-two-selected-is-ambiguous, within-image-two-inline-is-malformed and both image-assembly test namespaces, with test counts UNCHANGED at 2176/11149; plant restored and verified by git blob hash against the committed object.

title: Remove vestigial states argument from machine cofx target resolver
description:
## Evidence

`implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines/cofx_attach.cljc` defines private helper `resolve-target-path` as `[states decl-path target]` (currently lines 345-357), but its body never reads `states`; it derives the result solely from `decl-path` and `target`. A focused clj-kondo run over `implementation/machines/src` reports `cofx_attach.cljc:352:4: warning: unused binding states`. Repository search finds exactly four call sites, all in the same namespace (currently lines 409, 524, 566, and 639), and each redundantly passes `states`. `git blame` / `git log -S"defn- resolve-target-path"` show the parameter has been unused since the helper was introduced in commit `9895cbd53d0` (2026-06-14), rather than being a recently disconnected input. The helper is private and has no external callers.

Searches for `resolve-target-path`, `cofx attach unused states`, `unused parameter machines cofx`, `unused binding`, and `cofx-attach` found no existing bead covering this cleanup.

## Impact

The unused argument is vestigial API inside the namespace: its name and the docstring phrase "within states" imply that target resolution validates or consults the state tree, while the function only normalises target coordinates. Every caller carries a value with no effect, and the stale parameter creates a standing lint warning that makes genuine unused bindings harder to notice.

## Proposed disposition

Remove `states` from the private helper's parameter vector, update its docstring to describe coordinate normalisation without implying a tree read, and update the four in-namespace call sites to pass only `decl-path` and `target`. Preserve the existing nil / `:same-state`, keyword sibling, vector absolute, and malformed-target cases exactly; this is a behavior-neutral arity cleanup, not a change to machine target semantics.

## Risks

The helper participates in static coeffect ensure-set closure calculation, including `:always`, `:on-done`, `:after`, and ordinary event candidates. An over-broad refactor could accidentally change those paths. Keep the change mechanical and retain all existing target branches and surrounding state-tree reads.
acceptance_criteria:
- `resolve-target-path` has two parameters (`decl-path`, `target`) and no caller passes the redundant state tree.
- `rg -n "resolve-target-path" implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines/cofx_attach.cljc` shows the definition plus the same four updated call sites and no three-argument use.
- A focused clj-kondo run over `implementation/machines/src` no longer reports `unused binding states` for `cofx_attach.cljc`.
- The machines JVM suite (`clojure -M:test` from `implementation/machines`) and consolidated CLJS suite (`npm run test:cljs` from `implementation`) pass, demonstrating unchanged ensure-set behavior on both runtimes.
close_reason: PR #9150: dropped the never-read `states` parameter from cofx_attach's private `resolve-target-path` and the redundant argument at its four in-namespace call sites; docstring reworded to describe coordinate normalisation rather than a state-tree read. Re-measured at branch tip: clj-kondo over implementation/machines/src went 37 warnings (incl. cofx_attach.cljc:352:4 unused binding states) to 35 with 0 unused bindings. Machines JVM suite exit 0 (1241 tests/4495 assertions); npm run test:cljs exit 0 (11173/55748, 0 compile warnings). A planted 3-arg call took the CLJS compile to exit 1 with 'Wrong number of args (3) passed to re-frame.machines.cofx-attach/resolve-target-path', confirming the gate catches a missed call site.

title: core(derivation/egress): dead-frame-sentinel is a registrable keyword, so a colliding live frame fails the graph egress open
description: implementation/core/src/re_frame/derivation/egress.cljc defines dead-frame-sentinel as ::no-egress-frame (the public keyword :re-frame.derivation.egress/no-egress-frame) and stamps it as elide-wire-value's :frame opt whenever project-graph's governing frame is nil or unreachable, so the walker takes its unresolvable-frame arm. Its docstring says the keyword is namespaced into this ns so it can never collide with a real frame id. That claim does not hold: make-frame validates no :id type and the frame registry is keyed by whatever public keyword it is handed, so an app that registers a frame under that literal id turns the fail-closed stamp into a live-frame walk under that frame's empty declaration registry, and the graph's value-bearing fields ship raw. This is exactly the class the rf2-7htk7 audit of PR #8972 named for Xray's ::no-frame, which the third pass (PR #8987) fixed by making the substitute a private identity value (a fresh host object) that no registration can equal, with a collision regression (register a live frame under the literal id, leave the target unselected, assert :rf/redacted). Not done in PR #8987 because that audit note scoped the completion to Xray and forbade widening. Remedy options, smallest first: (a) make dead-frame-sentinel a private identity value the same way, plus a collision regression in the derivation egress tests; (b) have elide-wire-value distinguish a present nil :frame key from an absent one, which retires both sentinels but changes the :frame opt's documented override semantics (spec/API.md elide-wire-value and project-egress rows, spec/015 §Projection promise fallback to the carried scope when the record's own :frame is unknown) and so drags hot-zone spec prose. Verify the premise first: register a frame under :re-frame.derivation.egress/no-egress-frame, call project-graph with a nil frame-id on a graph carrying a sensitive value under an ambient live frame, and observe whether the value egresses raw.
notes:
MAYOR RULING, 2026-09-03 02:4x AUSEST — OPTION (a), THE PRIVATE IDENTITY VALUE, PLUS THE COLLISION REGRESSION. Option (b) is refused.

WHY (a). It is not a new design decision — it is the SAME fix this repo already made for the SAME defect class one artefact over. The rf2-7htk7 audit of PR #8972 named this class for Xray's ::no-frame, and PR #8987 fixed it by making the substitute a private identity value (a fresh host object) that no registration can equal, with a collision regression that registers a live frame under the literal id, leaves the target unselected, and asserts :rf/redacted. That is a worked precedent with a shipped test shape, so this is applying a settled answer rather than choosing one. The bead itself records that (a) was not done then only because the audit note scoped the completion to Xray and forbade widening — the scope, not the reasoning, is what kept it out.

WHY NOT (b). Two reasons, and the second is what settles it. First, it changes the :frame opt's DOCUMENTED override semantics, which is a public-contract change made in service of an internal sentinel — the tail wagging the dog. Second, it drags hot-zone spec prose (spec/API.md's elide-wire-value and project-egress rows, and spec/015's Projection promise fallback), and a worker is live in spec/** right now, so (b) would be a lane collision on top of a larger change. Neither reason alone would be decisive; together they are.

VERIFY THE PREMISE FIRST, and the bead tells you exactly how, so do it rather than trusting the docstring's claim OR mine: register a frame under the literal :re-frame.derivation.egress/no-egress-frame, call project-graph with a nil frame-id on a graph carrying a sensitive value under an ambient live frame, and observe whether the value egresses raw. IF IT DOES NOT, the premise fails and saying so is the whole deliverable — the docstring's collision claim would then be true and there is nothing to fix.

THE REGRESSION IS NOT OPTIONAL. A private identity value with no test asserting the collision case is the same fix without the thing that keeps it fixed, and this defect has now been found twice in two artefacts because the first fix's scope was drawn too tight.
RESOLVED 2026-09-03 by PR #9043 (branch worker/code-a, commit 5276cf4b0a).

PREMISE REPRODUCED FIRST, exactly as the bead and the ruling required, and BEFORE any source
change: the collision regression was written against the unfixed tree and went RED —
"expected: (= privacy/redacted-sentinel (:value sub)) / actual: (not (= :rf/redacted
{:cart {:items \"tenant-jwt-9f3a-SECRET\"}}))", captured exit 1, 2 failing assertions. With a live
frame registered under the literal :re-frame.derivation.egress/no-egress-frame, project-graph with
a nil frame-id egressed the sensitive value RAW. The docstring collision claim was false.

OPTION (a) TAKEN per the mayor ruling. dead-frame-sentinel in
implementation/core/src/re_frame/derivation/egress.cljc is now a private identity value,
#?(:clj (Object.) :cljs (js/Object.)) — the .cljc reader conditional is the one difference from the
Xray precedent, which is .cljs. Checked before relying on it: frame/frame is a plain registry
lookup ((get @frames id) at frame.cljc:1347), so a host object misses cleanly with no validation
path that could throw. Docstring rewritten to state WHY a keyword cannot serve.

PRECEDENT FOLLOWED: commit 449bfd21c7 (PR #8987, rf2-7htk7 third pass) and its collision
regression at tools/xray/test/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/app_db_diff_cljs_test.cljs:559.

REGRESSION ADDED: g-graph-egress-nil-frame-fails-closed-under-sentinel-id-collision in
implementation/derivation-conformance/test/re_frame/derivation_algebra_conformance_cljs_test.cljc,
which is where project-graph tests live. Registers a live frame under the literal id, leaves the
governing frame nil, ALSO binds an ambient frame so a pass cannot be an accident of there being
nothing to borrow, asserts :rf/redacted plus a no-secret-anywhere sweep, and destroys the colliding
frame in a finally. The suite is .cljc and runs in BOTH runtimes, so the JVM alias exercises the
(Object.) arm and the :node-test bundle the (js/Object.) arm — the regression discriminates both.
Also extracted the fixture its sibling arm duplicated; pure extraction, no assertion removed
(22/522 -> 23/526 = exactly the four is forms of the new test).

FINDING, filed as rf2-ws60 (P2): a THIRD carrier of this class exists at
tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/local_render.cljc:106 — its own dead-frame-sentinel,
also ::no-egress-frame, also stamped as the :frame opt (:175), carrying the identical false
docstring claim. Out of this dispatch write fence (tools/xray/**), so filed not fixed. A near-miss
at implementation/core/src/re_frame/elision.cljc:1145 was inspected and CLEARED: it only applies
where the caller waived sensitive redaction, and a colliding registry there causes MORE elision, so
it fails closed.

GATES, exit codes captured on the runner own command line, all on the final rebased base:
test:cljs 11190 tests / 55778 assertions 0 failures exit 0; implementation/core JVM 2175 / 11144
exit 0; derivation-conformance JVM 23 / 526 exit 0; test-fast-pr.sh PASS exit 0.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #9043 (worker/code-a): dead-frame-sentinel is now a private identity value #?(:clj (Object.) :cljs (js/Object.)), following PR #8987 commit 449bfd21c7, with the collision regression g-graph-egress-nil-frame-fails-closed-under-sentinel-id-collision. Premise reproduced red before the fix (raw secret egressed) and green after. See the RESOLVED note.

title: spec/Spec-Schemas FixtureFile classification op-map schema does not enforce its exactly-one contract
description:
CLAIM. spec/conformance/README.md §Fixture format and spec/Spec-Schemas.md §:rf/fixture-file document neither the eight top-level :fixture/* keys live in the corpus nor :fixture/dynamic-host-only?; the capability conventions omit :identity/*, :data-classification/*, :flow/*, :derivation/*. rf2-9vbg3 is the skill-side half (harness fail-loud floors omit unknown keys).
IMPACT. A foreign-host harness written from the docs rejects or silently ignores live fixture keys.
FIX SHAPE. Derive the key roster mechanically from the corpus and document it once. Spec-Schemas.md is a fenced-schema page — check_doc_slugs does not read inside fences, so verify by hand and say so in the PR body. Spec-Schemas.md is HOT ZONE — sequence.
GATE. hand-verified.
Surfaced by the 2026-09-02 independent skills review (15 reviewers, tip 72df4dd915); routed out of the reviewing skill's scope. Re-verify line numbers at dispatch. Filed 2026-09-02 12:16:50 AUSEST. Reported by the implementor reviewer.
acceptance_criteria: FixtureFile’s :fixture/classification-effects element enforces exactly one known commit-plane axis per op-map. Empty maps, maps with multiple axes, and maps with unknown keys fail validation rather than silently no-op or partially apply; all live fixtures still validate; the fenced schema is parsed/checked by a discriminating hand or executable check.
notes:
MERGED-PR AUDIT #9001: corrected this open owner's census from an unanchored namespace search. Parsing every fixture EDN top-level map yields 18 fixture keys. spec/conformance/README.md omits 7: compute-subs, dynamic-host-only?, flow-bodies, frames, render-after-hydrate, runtime, wire-order. spec/Spec-Schemas.md omits those seven plus capabilities and classification-effects, for 9. interceptor-fired and clear-interceptor are event ids, not top-level keys. The existing acceptance remains the right future-proof target.
MERGED-PR AUDIT #9019 (2026-09-02): PR #9019 completed the 18-key roster, but its new FixtureFile projection still disagrees with the live corpus in two load-bearing ways. First, spec/Spec-Schemas.md declares :fixture/classification-effects as :map; every live occurrence is a VECTOR of operation maps (for example [{:sensitive [[:auth :token]]}]), and conformance_runner.cljc consumes it with doseq. A port generated from the schema will reject or misread all eight classification fixtures. Second, :fixture/registry and :fixture/handlers remain required entries in FixtureFile even though the PR's own parsed census finds them in only 237/247 and 218/247 fixtures respectively; both need {:optional true}. These are schema/corpus contradictions, not requests for a richer schema. Reopened the exact fixture-schema owner rather than filing a duplicate.
MERGED-PR AUDIT #9032 — REOPENED.

The vector correction is right, but the inner Malli schema does not express the contract it now states. spec/conformance/README.md:599 and the new Spec-Schemas comment both require each op-map to carry EXACTLY ONE of :sensitive, :large, :clear-sensitive, or :clear-large. The added form is an ordinary open [:map ...] with all four entries optional: it accepts {}, several recognized axes at once, and arbitrary unknown keys. This is observable, not theoretical. implementation/core/test/re_frame/conformance_runner.cljc:528-537 uses a priority-ordered cond: a multi-axis map applies only its first recognized axis, while an empty/unknown map silently does nothing.

Use the exact existing FixtureFile owner. Minimal fix shape: make the element a closed four-way :or of single-required-key maps, or add an equivalently fail-loud validation seam before the runner applies it. Keep the ordered vector and current live corpus unchanged; do not build new machinery.
MERGED-PR AUDIT #9052 — exact owner reopened for the missing durable negative. The closed four-way Malli schema and the runner's pre-apply key check are correct, but no committed test ever gives `run-fixture` an empty, multi-axis, or unknown-axis `:fixture/classification-effects` op-map. Every corpus op is valid, and the reported JVM conformance count was identical before and after; inverting the guard only proves valid fixtures reach it, not that deletion or loosening will red. The same runner already pins `unknown-expect-keys` directly on JVM and CLJS. Minimal completion: add the analogous table-driven `run-fixture` regression on both hosts for the three refused shapes (plus one valid single-axis control), asserting a failed result and the classification-op error. No new validator, fixture format, or gate.
close_reason: PR #9108 (worker/schemagate-a). THE BRIEFED PREMISE DID NOT HOLD: the schema does NOT permit zero-or-many. f0f2e40f9f already made the FixtureFile :fixture/classification-effects element a closed four-way :or of single-required-key maps, and realise-classification-effects! already checks the same contract before applying anything. Authoritative side: the exactly-one prose -- and both the schema and the harness already agree with it, so there was nothing to decide and nothing in the corpus would fail the tightened form. What audit #9052 actually asked for -- the missing durable negative -- is what landed: classification-op-map-guard (JVM) and classification-op-map-guard-cljs feed run-fixture an empty, a multi-axis, an unknown-axis and a known-beside-unknown op-map and assert a FAILED fixture naming the classification-op error, with a valid single-axis op as the control. Proved live rather than asserted: neutering the guard's condition reds 8 of the JVM test's 9 assertions (all four shapes, on both the :passed? and the error-message assertion) while the control stays green; the runner was then restored byte-identically (git hash-object == HEAD blob 37976da1a53efbe01243013fc646a3ede5dfbbf8). The acceptance criterion's second half -- 'the fenced schema is parsed/checked by a discriminating hand or executable check' -- was discharged by an EXECUTABLE parse, since neither doc gate reads inside a fence: the entry was read out of Spec-Schemas.md with clojure.edn and run through Malli, accepting 12 live ops across 8 fixtures and all 8 whole-vector values, rejecting all four refused shapes, accepting all four valid single-axis shapes. Spec-Schemas.md gains one comment naming the two tests so the fenced contract points at its own durable negative. OVERLAP DECLARED, not raced: draft PR #9103 (worker/aliasq-a, 401 files) renames the 'runner' require-alias in both leaf files; the new tests sit at EOF and change no ns form, so a rebase merges cleanly but that PR's rename pass must catch two more call sites. Gates: JVM guard test exit 0 (1 test, 9 assertions); api-manifest exit 0 (84/170); check_doc_slugs.py exit 0; check_readme_links.py --ci exit 0; mkdocs build --strict exit 0. CLJS not run locally (cold whole-suite compile, CI owns it); the CLJS test is a structural mirror of the passing derivation-graph-expect-graph-guard-cljs in the same file and was reader-checked.

The example does exist — in the spec: `spec/Pattern-Boot.md:297-330` "Semantic retry — state machine handles 401-vs-200-vs-fatal" (`:got-401?` guard L318-320; "`:failed` whose `:error` is `{:kind :rf.http/http-4xx :status 401}` → `:refreshing` … loops back to `:loading-me`" L300-306), and `spec/014-HTTPRequests.md:446` points at "Pattern-Boot §Worked example — auth-machine and the retry-ownership boundary" for it. description:
CLAIM. skills/re-frame2-setup/SKILL.md:43 -- "the skill is the **executor**: it writes the files, runs `npm install`, runs a terminating `npx shadow-cljs compile app`, starts the watch, and reports the URL". Step 6 (SKILL.md:74) and the Done checklist (:82) report `http://localhost:8280/`; references/shadow-cljs.md:25 fixes `:dev-http {8280 "resources/public"}`. Two or three lines, not a manual -- a precondition in step 6 (or a "Before you run" line above it): (a) `java -version` must succeed -- shadow-cljs runs on the JVM, the npm package only wraps it; if it fails, say so and stop (no version claim without a source; the template README's JDK 21 is one if the fixer wants a number); grant `Bash(java -version)` in allowed-tools. (b) Report the URL from the watch's own dev-http output line, never from the config: if 8280 is already bound, pick another `:dev-http` port, restart the watch, and report THAT URL. Node version: nothing, unless a source is cited.

GATE. `bb tests/setup_drift_test.clj` (Lock 12's executor pins remain green); otherwise no gate -- verify by hand.

title: fix(docs): repair link rot blocking mkdocs --strict
description:
mkdocs build --strict aborts on broken cross-doc links. Two distinct categories:

## Category A — skills/ file links into repo spec/ tree (~12 warnings)
skills/re-frame2-implementor.md uses '../spec/001-Registration.md', '../spec/002-Frames.md', '../spec/006-ReactiveSubstrate.md', '../spec/004-Views.md', '../spec/009-Instrumentation.md', '../spec/000-Vision.md', '../spec/Implementor-Checklist.md', '../spec/conformance/README.md' etc.

Root cause: skills/ is built INTO the mkdocs site (so mkdocs treats relative ../spec/ links as broken because repo spec/ is not in docs/ nav). 

Fix options:
- (a) Exclude skills/ from mkdocs build entirely (skills are AI-targeted source, not user docs)
- (b) Rewrite ../spec/ links to absolute GitHub URLs (e.g. https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/blob/main/spec/001-Registration.md)
- (c) Mirror or symlink spec/ into docs/spec/ so the links resolve

**Recommend A, with a purpose-based editorial boundary:** retain a useful human summary of each skill's outcome, triggers, prerequisites and kickoff, while removing copied leaf inventories and detailed execution instructions. Link those details to their authoritative source. This is a recommendation for Mike's ruling on rf2-y126v, not a ruling or authorization to implement it. **Corrections to the dossier's premises.** There are ten Markdown files in `docs/skills`: nine skill pages and one index. More importantly, 61/97 is not a measured defect rate: it includes all 31 authoring references because that page uses category words, and seven improver references on a page intentionally offering no inventory. A selective summary need not name every leaf. The two incorrect destinations above are stronger evidence than an omission percentage.

Likewise, “nothing gates the copies” is too broad: `skills/re-frame2-setup/tests/setup_drift_test.clj:850` loads the setup mirror and `:864–899` checks several claims, including the exact phrase `thirteen files`. Readers retain enough context to choose a skill; detailed procedures cost an extra click. B would provide more detail locally, but makes unrelated leaf splits and operational changes require another human-maintained account. A still requires updates when purpose, triggers or prerequisites change; it does not end every kind of documentation drift.

title: False claim after #10200: Xray init! persists :target-frame
description:
PR #10200 (eeb0056e12380e663bf41ea5078eb2e41b05f933) correctly removes the repeated-init no-op claim, but its new init! docstring says every supplied :target-frame / :theme / :density / :buffer-depths option is written AND PERSISTED through config/update-setting! (tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/core.cljs:170-174). The :target-frame part is false.

The same file:269-270 sends :target-frame through seat-and-set-target-frame!, whose body at :146-149 only seats the Xray frame and dispatches :rf.xray/set-target-frame. The three actual config/update-setting! calls at :272, :275 and :279 cover theme, density and epoch-history. tools/xray/spec/015-Configuration.md:943-947 explicitly excludes :target-frame from persisted Settings.

Consequence: an integrator reading the public docstring is told their inspected-frame choice survives as a Settings value when it is only reapplied to the running shell. The detailed option list below the new paragraph already makes the correct distinction.

Smallest correction: split current target selection from persisted theme/density/epoch-depth options in the new paragraph. Keep repeated-call behavior and runtime code unchanged; no new persistence feature, API, test harness or broader prose sweep. Source inspection of the function and existing settings contract is sufficient. The source Bead description also inherited the mistaken blanket persistence premise; this finding supplies the correction without rewriting its history.

Exact-open-match check: live open database contained only rf2-yh5pa for the neighboring test-name/comment cleanup. It does not record this defect or required correction, so it is not reused.
acceptance_criteria: The init! docstring distinguishes session target selection from persisted theme/density/epoch-history settings and agrees with the function body and configuration spec; runtime behavior is unchanged.
notes: Merged-PR audit #10239 (f6ad2bfdae7e20cafbad6344634801206fff047f; merged 2026-09-22T13:34:01Z). Completeness: Both scoped corrections landed: init! separates current target selection from persisted theme/density/epoch depth, and the repeated-call test name, testing prose and installation comment retire the no-op framing. Existing assertions remain. Correctness: Checked the seat-and-dispatch helper, all three config/update-setting! call sites and configuration spec ownership rule. After removing strings/comments and normalizing the intended test rename, executable forms in both files equal the merge parent. The old test name has zero tracked non-ledger references and the new name occurs once. Merged CI reports 35 successful checks including CLJS node/browser tests and clj-kondo, with 53 skipped. Implementation quality: Small documentation and test-label correction matches the existing behavior without adding persistence machinery or widening the API. No new actionable finding under the pre-alpha ergonomic posture. Actionable findings: none. Existing finding updates: none.
close_reason:
DONE — merged as PR #10239 at trunk `f6ad2bfdae`, clustered with rf2-yh5pa. Two files, 19 insertions
/ 9 deletions. This item's half corrects the `init!` docstring in
`tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/core.cljs`.

THE FALSE CLAIM AND ITS REFUTATION AT SOURCE. The merged #10200 text said `init!` *"writes and
PERSISTS each supplied `:target-frame` / `:theme` / `:density` / `:buffer-depths` opt through
`config/update-setting!`."* The `:target-frame` half of that is false. The worker read the function
body rather than the prose: `seat-and-set-target-frame!` is

    [frame-id]
    (mount/ensure-seated!)
    (rf/with-frame :rf/xray
      (rf/dispatch [:rf.xray/set-target-frame frame-id]))
    nil)

— no `config/update-setting!` anywhere in it — and `init!` reaches it through a plain
`(when target-frame (seat-and-set-target-frame! target-frame))`. A census of `config/update-setting!`
over the whole file returns **4** hits: one is the docstring sentence being corrected, and the other
**3** are the only executable sites — `:theme`, `(:general :density)`, `(:general :epoch-history)` —
**none of them `:target-frame`**. The spec agrees and was cited rather than edited:
`tools/xray/spec/015-Configuration.md` §`configure!` vs `init!` vs persisted Settings reads *"It does
not make `:target-frame` a persisted Settings field."*

The replacement therefore splits the sentence: a supplied `:target-frame` **selects the CURRENT
inspected target and nothing more — dispatched, not persisted**, with the spec section named inline;
`:theme` / `:density` / `:buffer-depths` are written AND persisted. The detailed option list below
the summary already drew the right distinction and was left alone.

MY DIRECTION TEST AT MERGE — a docstring change is one no gate can fail on, so the reading IS the
deliverable and the only thing I can check mechanically is that nothing executable moved with it.
Over `core.cljs`: `^(defn` **5 → 5**, `^(def` **17 → 17**, `config/update-setting!` sites **4 → 4**,
file **432 → 437 lines** (+5, the expanded docstring). Nothing executable moved, and the count of
update-setting! sites is unchanged — which is the tell that the prose was corrected around the same
three real sites rather than the sites themselves being touched.

NOT VERIFIED, AND DECLARED: `clj-kondo` was run in its PLAIN form (never `--fail-level error`, which
exits 0 on an unresolved symbol in this tree) and read **0 errors / 1 warning / exit 2 before and
after** — the honest pass condition being *unchanged from baseline*, not zero, with the warning
(`namespace re-frame.frame is required but never used`) established as pre-existing by restoring both
files to the merge base and re-linting. Local binary v2025.10.23 against CI's pinned 2026.04.15, and
the worker declared that skew rather than glossing it. The compile evidence is CI's: the worker never
held the shadow-cljs lane and ran nothing entering it.

Restores verified by blob hash rather than by diff — `git rev-parse HEAD:<path>` equals the default
`git hash-object` for both files, `--no-filters` correctly does NOT match (both are `i/lf`), and
`git diff --quiet HEAD` exit 0 as a second instrument. 51 of 51 static/ratchet gates green, re-run in
full on the final rebased base. eol: `core.cljs` cr=437 crlf=437 bare_lf=0; `core_cljs_test.cljs`
cr=222 crlf=222 bare_lf=0. No `sed -i`.

CI 88 rows, 0 pending, 0 failed at head `4cdcad0810`; 4 runs COMPLETED; merge base `33986947d3`
carries the matrix anchor `22d939a1d5` with 0 workflow files changed since.

ONE THING LEFT ALONE ON PURPOSE, and it is worth knowing:
`skills/re-frame2-xray/references/launch-modes.md:81` still carries *"Idempotency: every step is
`defonce`-guarded"* — the same framing this item retires from the spec side. It is out of fence

title: http(managed): emit the :rf.http/issued trace row and number anonymous issuances per (frame, event-id), never evicted — Managed-Effects §Tracing conformance; the exact join key rf2-6ooch builds on
description:
Filed 2026-09-23 by the delegated decider for rf2-6ooch (Mike delegated the ruling; dossier + independent Codex review weighed, disagreements verified at source at trunk 3b5faef172). This is STEP 1 of a two-step ruling: the framework-side conformance change that gives Xray an EXACT join key. rf2-6ooch (step 2, the Epoch-panel join) is blocked by this bead. Read rf2-6ooch's `== RULING` note for the full reasoning; this description is self-contained for dispatch.

## Project stance (verbatim, from CLAUDE.md; paste it into any dispatch preamble unchanged)

> Posture is that we are pre-alpha and focused on elegance, power and a masterpiece.
> But we are not over-engineering or gold plating. Also, we trust the programmer.
> We're trying to facilitate high productivity for them (and the AI they use) via a
> library with excellent ergonomics and low friction. We don't need to litigate every
> last fine detail and drown in the minutiae.

## What this is

Two small framework changes in the HTTP artefact, both owed to `spec/Managed-Effects.md:234` ("Managed async families MUST emit trace rows from the reply-envelope facts ... issuance/start (with `:work/id`, frame, owner/cause, target summary) ..."):

1. **Emit an HTTP ISSUANCE trace row, `:rf.http/issued`.** Today HTTP is the one managed family with none: the 17 `rf.trace/emit!` / `emit-error!` sites under `implementation/http/src` (rg at trunk) include no issuance row; resources emit `:rf.resource/work-started` (`implementation/resources/src/re_frame/resources/events.cljc:837-841`) and mutations `:rf.mutation/started`; Xray's op->phase table (`tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/reply_envelope.cljc:387-398`) lists both under `:issued` and records HTTP as having none. The generic `:rf.fx/handled` row (`implementation/core/src/re_frame/fx.cljc:1273-1278`) carries only `{:rf.fx/id :rf.fx/args :frame}` — the caller's raw args, never the allocated issuance — so nothing in the issuing bundle names the work-id that every completion row already carries.

2. **Count ANONYMOUS issuances so the work-id is unique.** `next-issuance!` returns 1 for every nil `:request-id` (`implementation/http/src/re_frame/http/registry.cljc:527-529`), and the anonymous `logical-id` is `(first origin-event)` — the event-id keyword (`implementation/http/src/re_frame/http/reply.cljc:97`). So two anonymous requests of one event-id in one frame carry the IDENTICAL work-id `[:rf.work/http :search/go 1 1]`, and nothing in the trace can tell their completions apart. Named requests already get a per-(frame, request-id) monotonic counter (:516-529) with conditional eviction on terminal completion (:531-563, rf2-k47b3d).

## The mechanism (exact)

**(a) Anonymous issuance numbering — per (frame, event-id), NEVER evicted.** Give `next-issuance!` what it needs to tell the two cases apart (e.g. a third argument `origin-event`, or pass the logical id plus an anonymous flag — worker's choice; the call site is `handlers.cljc:453`). Named requests: UNCHANGED — the existing per-(frame, request-id) counter, the existing conditional eviction, the existing "a frame's first issuance under an id is 1" contract (`spec/014-HTTPRequests.md:670-674`). Anonymous requests: a monotonic counter keyed by `[frame-id (first origin-event)]`, held in a SEPARATE atom from `issuance-counters` (so `issuance-counter-count`, the rf2-k47b3d leak instrument, keeps its meaning), never evicted — the key space is (frames x registered event-ids), which is bounded, unlike the `[:fetch-doc uuid]` request-id space rf2-k47b3d had to bound. Reset it in `reset-issuance-counters-for-test!` (:566-571) and, if it is one line, drop a frame's entries in the frame-destroy sweep (`abort-in-flight-on-frame-destroyed!` :1003 or wherever frame state is dropped); otherwise accept the bounded residue and say so.

**WHY NOT the dossier's shape ("count anonymous issuances exactly as named ones, same eviction")** — Codex's counterexample, verified at source: `evict-issuance-on-completion!` is a compare-and-drop `(if (= issuance (get counters k)) (dissoc counters k) counters)` (:559-562) that protects only a supersession's NEWER live successor. Two anonymous siblings A=1, B=2 with B completing first: B's evict sees counter==2, drops it, and the next anonymous request reads 1 while A is still live — `[1 2 1]`, a live collision. Never evicting anonymous counters closes it. NOTE the existing evict call sites (`transport.cljc:260, :783, :975, :1071`) pass `(:request-id ctx)`, which is nil for an anonymous request, and the guard `(when (and (some? request-id) ...))` at :557 already no-ops — keep it that way and pin it.

**WHY NOT a runtime-wide monotonic sequence for ALL requests** (Codex's stated preference, offered as a preference not a requirement): it would rewrite a normative contract at four spec sites (`014:581`, `014:670-674`, `014:816`, `Managed-Effects.md:189`) and move every one of the 146 literal `[:rf.work/http ...]` lines across 25 files for a property the Xray join does not need — sequential reuse of a named id (`[x 1 1]` then `[x 1 1]` after eviction) is disambiguated by the issue row's POSITION (rows carry a monotonic `:id`, `trace.cljc:713`), not by the number. Smallest change wins.

**WHY NOT an origin stamp (dispatch-id + frame + invocation index on every completion row)** — the shape rf2-6ooch originally asked for: a second identity for a fact the framework already names (`:rf.reply/work-id`), propagated through nine emit sites. Out.

**(b) The `:rf.http/issued` row.** In `managed-handler` (`implementation/http/src/re_frame/http/handlers.cljc:453-455`), immediately after `issuance` is allocated and BEFORE `supersede!` (:470-478) and `run-attempt!` (:479) — so the row precedes every row the issuance causes, including a synchronous body-prep failure. It runs inside the fx handler's `with-handler-scope`, so `build-event` (`implementation/core/src/re_frame/trace.cljc:673-716`) stamps the issuing run's dispatch-id and the row lands in the issuing bundle (in `:other`, as an `:info` row). Gate it on `rf.interop/debug-enabled?` exactly as the other `:rf.http/*` rows are (`transport.cljc:611`). Tags:

```clojure
(rf.trace/emit! :info :rf.http/issued
  (rf.http.privacy/prepare-emit-tags            ; the retry row's privacy path (transport.cljc:1108-1116) — :url rides redacted under :sensitive?
    {:rf.reply/work-id   (rf.http.reply/work-id {:request-id request-id :origin-event origin-event :issuance issuance :attempt 1})
     :rf.reply/work-kind :http
     :request-id         request-id             ; nil when anonymous
     :url                <the normalised url>   ; same slot the retry row reads as (:url ctx)
     :method             <the request method>
     :frame              frame-id
     :reply-to           <target summary: the target event-id(s), via the existing reply-target helper if it takes this map; otherwise omit>}
    (true? (:sensitive? normalised))))
```

Use the tag spelling `:rf.reply/work-id` — `reply_envelope.cljc:164-173` says it is the CANONICAL trace-tag spelling (`work-id-of` prefers it, falls back to bare `:work/id`). Do NOT capture a dispatch-id by hand, do NOT mint an invocation index, do NOT add any tag to any completion row, do NOT rewrite a completion row's dispatch-id.

**(c) One line in Xray's op table:** `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/reply_envelope.cljc:387-398` gains `:rf.http/issued :issued` and its :396-397 comment ("HTTP issues the request through the fx ...") is corrected. This is REQUIRED, not optional: the `suffix->phase` heuristic (:504-516) has needles for "started"/"work-started" but none for "issued", so the row would otherwise fall through unclassified.

**(d) Optional one-liner, take it only if it is one line:** the `:rf.http/retry-attempt` row (`transport.cljc:1107-1115`) carries no work-id at all (Codex traced it: the 5xx failure is built raw at :1512-1517, `self-identify` runs only on the terminal tail at :876). `ctx` at that site carries all four ingredients (`:request-id :origin-event :issuance :attempt`, see :374/:398), so `:rf.reply/work-id (rf.http.reply/work-id ctx)` is one line. Step 2 does NOT depend on it (it reads attempt counts off the terminal row's `:attempt`); if it would need a 009 row rewrite, skip it and say so.

**(e) Spec and docstrings (the owning docs, no waiver):**
- `spec/014-HTTPRequests.md`: the trace-events prose that documents `:rf.http/replied` (~:579-583) gains `:rf.http/issued` (when it fires, that it inherits the issuing run's dispatch-id, its tags, `:url` redaction under `:sensitive?`); the :581 sentence "issuance is the monotonic per-request-id re-issuance counter" gains the anonymous clause (per originating event-id within the frame, never reset, so two anonymous requests of one event never share a work id). :670-674 stays true as written (it is about named ids).
- `spec/Managed-Effects.md:189` (the HTTP work-id cell): the same anonymous clause.
- `spec/009-Instrumentation.md` — HOT-ZONE, the mayor sequences it: one catalogue row `:rf.http/issued | :info | diagnostic | ...` beside the four sibling HTTP lifecycle rows at :2292-2295 (`retry-attempt`, `aborted-on-actor-destroy`, `aborted`, `stale-suppressed`; `:rf.http/replied` alone is uncatalogued today — an omission, not a precedent), and the op added to the emit-site inventory line at :1078. If 009 is held by another worker at dispatch, the mayor drops it from this fence and files the row as a follow-on; do not edit it in parallel.
- Docstrings that state the old contract: `reply.cljc:93-95` ("issuance defaults to 1 ... the only value an anonymous / non-superseding request ever sees"), `registry.cljc:495-529` (the counter comment + `next-issuance!`), `handlers.cljc:441-452` (the allocation comment), `transport.cljc:595-599` if it reads wrong afterwards.

## Fence (files)

- `implementation/http/src/re_frame/http/handlers.cljc` (emit + call site + comment)
- `implementation/http/src/re_frame/http/registry.cljc` (anonymous counter, reset, docstrings; optional frame-destroy drop)
- `implementation/http/src/re_frame/http/reply.cljc` (docstring only)
- `implementation/http/src/re_frame/http/transport.cljc` (ONLY the optional retry one-liner (d); otherwise untouched — do NOT reorder the evict/emit teardown, see Traps)
- `implementation/http/test/re_frame/**` (new + updated tests)
- `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/reply_envelope.cljc` (one table line + comment)
- `spec/014-HTTPRequests.md`, `spec/Managed-Effects.md`, `spec/009-Instrumentation.md` (HOT-ZONE, sequenced)
- Test files outside `implementation/http/test` ONLY where a pin legitimately reddens (see Pins).
Nothing else in `tools/xray` — the panel join is rf2-6ooch.

## Acceptance bar (RED first, then GREEN; every zero beside a control)

RED (before the change), measured and quoted in the PR body:
- R1: two anonymous `:rf.http/managed` requests of one event-id in one frame produce the SAME work-id on their completion rows (control: two NAMED requests under distinct ids produce distinct ones).
- R2: a managed request's issuing bundle carries 0 `:rf.http/issued` rows (control: it carries 1 `:rf.fx/handled` with `:rf.fx/id :rf.http/managed`).

GREEN (after), as JVM tests under `implementation/http/test` capturing trace rows through the existing listener/projection machinery the lowering tests already use (e.g. `http_reply_lowering_test.clj` names `:rf.http/replied`) — derive fixtures from the producer, never by hand:
- G1 named request: the issuing bundle holds exactly one `:rf.http/issued` row carrying the issuing run's `:rf.trace/dispatch-id` (NOT filed under `[nil :ungrouped]`), and `(subvec work-id 0 3)` on it equals the same on the one `:rf.http/replied` row.
- G2 named request superseded and re-issued: two issued rows `[.. x 1]` and `[.. x 2]`; the `:rf.http/stale-suppressed` row's `:rf.reply/carried` names `[.. x 1 1]` and the `:rf.http/replied` names `[.. x 2 1]`.
- G3 two OVERLAPPING anonymous requests of one event-id from two runs, completing in REVERSE order: issued rows `[.. ev 1]`, `[.. ev 2]`; each completion carries its own.
- G4 two anonymous requests in ONE run: two issued rows, each with `:id` less than its own `:rf.fx/handled` row's `:id` and greater than the previous pair's (the ordinal pairing step 2 relies on: issued(k) precedes handled(k), `fx.cljc:1273` emits handled after the handler returns).
- G5 Codex's schedule as a pin (registry level): anonymous a=1, b=2; b completes (call the evict exactly as the transport does — with a nil request-id); the next anonymous issuance reads 3, not 1. Control: the existing `issuance-counter-eviction-preserves-live-successor` for named ids stays green as written.
- G6 sibling frames: each frame's anonymous counter for the same event-id starts at 1.
- G7 a synchronous body-prep failure: the issued row precedes the failure row in the same bundle (by `:id`).
- G8 boundedness: `issuance-counter-count` unchanged in meaning (the 500-distinct-named-ids test stays green); the anonymous map holds at most one entry per (frame, event-id) after N requests of one event (assert `<= 1` per pair, not `= N`).
- G9 zero change to any delivered reply map for a NAMED request (the existing lowering pins prove it by staying green); anonymous replies differ only in the issuance digit from the second issuance on.
- G10 `:rf.http/issued` classifies as `:issued` through `reply_envelope/phase-of` (control: a nonsense op reads nil).

## Gates (by path — say which lane compiled the changed forms)

- `handlers.cljc`, `registry.cljc`, `reply.cljc`, `transport.cljc` are `.cljc`. State which reader branch the changed forms sit in; they should be outside any `#?(:cljs ...)`, in which case BOTH lanes compile them. A change confined to a `:cljs` branch is graded by `npm run test:cljs` only — a JVM green is not evidence about it (CLAUDE.md § Build & Test).
- `implementation/http`: `clojure -M:test` (RED then GREEN, counts quoted red and green).
- `scripts/test-jvm-implementation.sh` — the whole roster, because work-id literals are pinned outside http too (`implementation/core/test/re_frame/reply_cljs_test.cljc` 9 lines, `implementation/security/test/.../reply_envelope_egress_security_cljs_test.cljc` 18, `reply-conformance` 1, `resources` 1).
- `scripts/test-jvm-tools.sh` — xray (`reply_envelope_cljs_test.cljc` 33 lines, `resources_cljs_test.cljs` 4, `managed_fx_helpers_cljs_test.cljc` 1, `typed_predicates_cljs_test.cljc` 2) and mcp-conformance (`reply_envelope_test.clj` 3).
- `npm run test:cljs` — the node lane grades every `-cljs-test` namespace above and the CLJS transport path. The shadow-cljs lane is a MACHINE-WIDE EXCLUSIVE (CLAUDE.md § Workflow): ask the mayor for the lane, take it once, release it.
- clj-kondo WITHOUT `--fail-level error` (CLAUDE.md instrument item (w): the flag is blind to unresolved symbols in this tree's config).
- Spec edits: `python scripts/check_doc_slugs.py` and `python -m mkdocs build --strict` (the hook stages `spec/` into the build).
- Surface classifier: hand `.github/scripts/report-changed-surfaces.sh` PATHS, never revisions (item (v)).

## Pins that legitimately redden (measure, do not guess)

Named work-id pins: ZERO movement by construction. | Bead | P | Title |
|---|---|---|
| rf2-3x7nj.18.1 | 2 | a sensitive flow output that fails its `:schema` ships raw in the validation trace's `:explain` (`:value` is redacted, no top-level `:sensitive?` stamp) |

- 18.1: failure `:value :rf/redacted`, `:explain {:value {:token "hunter2-SECRET"} :errors ({... :value "hunter2-SECRET"})}`, top-level `:sensitive? nil`. Control, with `{:sensitive? true}` in the schema: everything redacted, `:sensitive? true`.

**Considered and rejected** (one line each, so nobody re-litigates them)
1. The `:output-write` `try` (`flows.cljc:337-371`) also wraps the computed-trace emit and `validate-output!`, so a throw there would be misattributed. It is unreachable: the validator and explainer seams catch (`schemas/validate.cljc:1315-1330`) and listener throws are swallowed. rf2-pk4i6.13 already recorded this under "considered".
2. A malformed flow `:schema` reads as a value failure. Dismissed as item #3 on rf2-pk4i6.13.
3. The topology graph is rebuilt every drain, O(n²) `prefix?`. Spec 013:250 sanctions the unmemoised sort at v1 node counts.
4. The router skips stashing flow snapshots when there is no `:db` effect and the pass returned an identical db (`router.cljc:1916-1920`). A rejected runtime-only candidate then leaves advanced rows, but the output was identical and the next pass re-derives from the committed inputs, so it is harmless.
5. `elide-inputs` strips the `:rf.db/runtime` qualifier (`flows.cljc:86-98`). This is correct: runtime subsystems declare partition-relative paths, e.g. `routing/classification.cljc:41-44` re-roots to `[:rf.runtime/routing :current ...]`.
6. Take an app-db schema that REQUIRES a flow's output path, then `:rf.fx/clear-flow` that flow. The settle's candidate is rejected, the restore re-queues the vacation, and every later event on the frame re-vacates and is rejected in turn, so the frame wedges in dev. I rejected this: the app's own schema contradicts the spec'd leaf vacation, and every rejection names the path loudly. Trust the programmer.
7. An out-of-drain `reg-flow` that moves `:output-path` vacates the old leaf without settling dependents of the old path. Ruled: a direct reg-flow must not settle (spec 013:498, rf2-f3yl). A hot-reload edge.
8. Right after a cold re-registration the slot holds the previous definition's value. Ruled "stale but owned" (spec 013:506).
9. `capture-flow-pass-state` calls `ensure-*` between its two liveness checks and could recreate atoms for a dead frame. Unreachable: destroy's liveness flip serializes on the drain lock the pass holds, and no callback runs in that window.
10. The `:rf.flow/failed` `:exception-message` is not projected. It is author-controlled text, the same posture as handler exceptions, and `:exception-data` IS redacted (`classification.cljc:1045-1060`).
11. `flows/tooling.cljc:4-6` still says JVM consumers get a facade alias, which rf2-kuky.86 retired. Comment drift, and following it fails loudly.
12. A direct clear in a handler body followed by a handler throw leaves the queued vacation for a later drain, where it could remove a later legitimate write to that path. Contrived: it needs an impure handler that also throws.
13. `:inputs []` passes validation (`every?` over an empty vector), giving a constant flow that is evaluated once. Harmless.

**Out-of-slice observation, NOT filed and NOT probed.** The machines lifecycle fx (spawn / destroy / `:rf.machine/update-snapshot`) write runtime-db directly during the `:fx` walk (`core/frame.cljc:2113-2129` docstring, `machines/lifecycle_fx/*`). That is after the flow pass, and they request no settle. So a flow reading `[:rf.db/runtime :rf.runtime/machines :snapshots <id> ...]`, which is Spec 013:94's own example input, would lag until the next drain on that frame. It is the same class as 18.3 but belongs to the machines/core fence. It is left for the machines owner to measure.

- The CLJS host: no shadow-cljs, per the brief. All three findings sit in shared `.cljc` with no reader-conditional branch at the implicated sites, so the JVM probe ran the same code, but the CLJS arm is inferred.
