title: adapters: reagent-slim render-to-static-markup emits attacker-controlled attribute/tag names raw and misses oncommand (the XSS vectors re-frame.ssr closed)
description:
## Defect `reagent2.dom.server/render-to-static-markup` (the reagent-slim artefact's pure-CLJS static-markup serializer) is missing both halves of the SSR emitter's attribute-name injection defence. It emits attribute NAMES and tag NAMES verbatim with no grammar check, and its lowercase event-handler allowlist lacks `oncommand`. The serializer says it copies its XSS filtering "by intent" from `re-frame.ssr.html-helpers` ("Curated to match ... If HTML5 extends the event-handler list, both copies update"). But it never copied `validate-attr-name!`, the gate that closed the rf2-vl8ir vector, and it missed the later `oncommand` fix (rf2-51tgp, P1). The threat model is the one `re-frame.ssr` already accepts: an app splats an attacker-controlled attribute map into hiccup, for example a CMS or JSON payload with `:keywordize-keys`. That app gets an inline event handler in the HTML this function returns. ## Where Frozen tree `034d0c8fc8`, all under `implementation/adapters/reagent-slim/src/reagent2/dom/server.cljs` unless noted: - `:1188-1199` `render-to-static-markup` is the public entry point. It is a published `day8/reagent-slim` var, documented at `:1192` as "suitable for HTML email, static-export, or as the initial seed for the SSR seam". Its output is what `reagent2.dom.client/hydrate-root` hydrates. - `:786-858` `emit-attribute`: the only drops are `:key`, `:ref`, `:dangerouslySetInnerHTML`, `event-handler-prop?` and fn values. The `:else` arm at `:838-858` appends `(attribute-name k)` raw at `:855`. - `:468-492` `attribute-name`: `(str k)` for a string key, `cached-prop-name` for a keyword. Neither is checked against any grammar. - `:709-730` `event-handler-prop?`: this is structural (`on-` / `on[A-Z]`) plus the allowlist. A key like `onclick=alert(1) x` has a lowercase char after `on` and is not an allowlist member, so it passes. - `:679-707` `event-handler-allowlist`: `oncommand` is absent. `implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/html_helpers.cljc:459` carries it. - `:990-1009` `emit-dom-element` appends `tag-str` raw at `:1008`. The tag comes from `template/parse-tag`, whose `re-tag` (`implementation/adapters/reagent-slim/src/reagent2/impl/template.cljs:68`, `([^\s\.#]+)…`) admits `/ = " < >`. - For contrast, the defence this lacks: `implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/html_helpers.cljc:378-399` (`attr-name-grammar` `[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_:-]*`, `validate-attr-name!`) and `implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/emit.cljc:112-149` (the tag-name gate). ## Failure scenario 1. `(render-to-static-markup [:div {(keyword "onclick=alert(1) x") "y"} "hi"])`. `event-handler-prop?` is false. `cached-prop-name` finds no `-` to camelCase, and `attribute-name` sees an already-lowercase name, so the key survives verbatim and is emitted unescaped: `
hi
`. The browser installs a live `onclick`. A string key `"onclick=alert(1) x"` takes the same path through `(str k)`. 2. `(render-to-static-markup [:div {:oncommand "alert(1)"}])` gives `
`. rf2-51tgp measured that bundled Chromium executes `oncommand` on a `command` event. 3. A lower-probability case: a string head built from data, such as `"img/src=\"x\"/onerror=alert(1)"`, passes `re-tag` and is emitted as ``. ## Evidence - **Slim side: inspected.** The code is CLJS-only and shadow-cljs is out of bounds. The trace is short and has no branch that consults a grammar. Grep shows `oncommand` appears nowhere under `implementation/adapters/reagent-slim/src` and exactly once under `implementation/ssr/src`. The slim test tree has no hostile-attribute-key case. - **Reference side: executed.** A bounded JVM probe was run from a scratch `deps.edn` with `:local/root` pointing at the frozen `implementation/ssr`, so nothing was written into the tree. Results: - `(h/attr-string {:oncommand "alert(1)"})` returned `""`. - `(h/attr-string {(keyword "onclick=alert(1) x") "y"})` threw `:rf.error/ssr-invalid-attribute-name`. - So the house emitter refuses exactly the inputs the slim emitter passes through. - **Precedent:** rf2-51tgp priced the identical `oncommand` class P1 on the SSR emitter. rf2-4hjw established that the slim serializer's rosters are separate copies that drift from SSR. ## Smallest fix Duplicate by intent, as this namespace already does for its other rosters, because bundle isolation forbids `:require`-ing `re-frame.ssr`: - Add `"oncommand"` to `event-handler-allowlist`. - Gate every emitted attribute name through the same `[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_:-]*` grammar, and every DOM tag through the SSR tag grammar. - A failing name or tag should throw a catalogued id (or reuse `:rf.error/ssr-invalid-attribute-name` / `:rf.error/invalid-tag-name`) rather than being emitted. - Add a hostile-key corpus to `implementation/adapters/reagent-slim/test/reagent2/dom/server_cljs_test.cljs`. Fence: `implementation/adapters/reagent-slim/src/reagent2/dom/server.cljs` plus that test. There is no hot-zone file. The fence overlaps the sibling raw-text finding filed in this wave, so sequence the two. ## Gates `npm run test:cljs` (the node lane). `server_cljs_test.cljs` ends in `-cljs-test` and is a `.cljs` file, so no JVM artefact compiles it and a JVM green says nothing about it. ## Decision needed Only the refusal shape: throw, which matches `re-frame.ssr`, or silently drop the offending attribute. Recommendation: throw, for parity with the SSR emitter.

A one-word ruling suffices. Decisive findings: 1. Only the attribute-NAME cell is contested. oncommand = silent drop, settled by rf2-51tgp (one allowlist word; slim server.cljs:679-707 lacks it, html_helpers.cljc:459 has it). Tag names = throw in every precedent: re-frame.ssr emit.cljc:129-148; react-dom/server 19.3.0 throws "Invalid tag" (react-dom-server-legacy.node.production.js:943); slim already throws :rf.error/static-markup-bad-tag (server.cljs:1141). 2. An honest "drop" therefore has to copy React's much wider name regex rather than the SSR grammar [A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_:-]*. Otherwise names like :x.y or :_foo would vanish where React paints them. 3. So `{"data-x onclick=alert(1) x" true}` still produces a live onclick handler under a gate placed on the ordinary attribute path alone. For the fixing worker: gate BOTH the ordinary and the boolean attribute paths, and the tag name. Put a RED case on each path (a hostile name through an ordinary value AND through a boolean true) before the fix, with the ordinary-name control passing throughout. The dossier file ai/decisions/rf2-3x7nj.6.1.slim-static-markup-refusal-shape.md (local-only) carries the corrected text. == RULING (delegated by Mike; mayor-dispatched ruling agent, 2026-09-23 23:01:31 AUSEST) == RULING: THROW. A malformed attribute name or tag name in reagent-slim's render-to-static-markup throws a catalogued error, reusing :rf.error/ssr-invalid-attribute-name (attribute names, on BOTH the ordinary and the boolean path) and :rf.error/invalid-tag-name (tag names). The grammar tested is React 19.3.0's OWN name predicates, copied by intent, NOT re-frame.ssr's narrower [A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_:-]* grammar. "oncommand" joins the silent-drop event-handler allowlist. Verified at trunk ca03830caa (= origin/main when this was written). `git diff --stat 034d0c8fc8 ca03830caa` over reagent-slim/src, ssr/src, core subs.cljc, spec/006, spec/009, spec/011 and slim IMPL-SPEC.md is EMPTY (control: the same range unfiltered from 51494841d9 reads 8 files), so every line cited on this bead and below reads identically at the frozen review tree and at trunk. --- WHY --- The dossier author and the independent Codex review AGREED on throw, on reusing the two existing ids, and on gating the boolean path too. They differed only on the grammar: the dossier left it open ("reasonable default for slim"), Codex favoured React's predicate. I rule React's predicate. What decides each part: 1. Throw beats drop because a drop in THIS serializer would be completely silent. React itself is not silent: react-dom drops an invalid attribute name but prints a dev-only console.error (isAttributeNameSafe, react-dom-server-legacy.node.development.js:321-331; the client does the same). reagent2.dom.server has "no goog.DEBUG branches; nothing to elide" (its ns docstring, server.cljs:93-94), so a drop here would be quieter than React, and a splatted attack or a data bug would vanish without trace. One disposition for one hazard across the repo avoids the auditor trap Spec 011's "two dispositions, both correct, not interchangeable" paragraph exists to defuse. Cost accepted: one bad key aborts the whole static render, the same trade rf2-vl8ir accepted for re-frame.ssr. 2. React's grammar beats the SSR grammar because of slim's stated contract, and because of the stance. implementation/adapters/reagent-slim/IMPL-SPEC.md §8.4 says this artefact has "one contract only — byte-parity with react-dom/server.renderToStaticMarkup", and that is already why slim follows react-dom on `value` where re-frame.ssr differs. Test React's own predicate and the throw fires ONLY on names React itself refuses (dropped plus a dev error), so byte-parity still holds on every input React renders without error. The SSR grammar would make slim throw on valid names that React paints on both server and client — refusing programmer markup rather than an attack, which is what "trust the programmer" rules out. The security property is identical: React's predicate rejects every breakout character that Spec 011's rule lists. Spec 011 binds re-frame.ssr only and is NOT edited. Tags, React-VALID_TAG_REGEX / SSR tag-name-re: img/src="x"/onerror=alert(1) F/F; div my-element svg:rect font-face h1 T/T; a_b T/F. So oncommand is the ONLY drift. `event-handler-prop?` (:709-730) lower-cases before the allowlist lookup, so every casing is covered. B. Attribute-name gate. title: epoch: restore-epoch! / replace-frame-state! validate app-db with Malli directly, bypassing set-schema-fns! (validation off still refuses; a substituted validator's rejections are admitted)
description:
## Defect

`restore-epoch!` and `replace-frame-state!` check the app-db partition with Malli directly. The check goes through the `:schemas/malli-validate` hook, not the validator the app installed with `set-schema-fns!`. So the substitution seam does not reach time-travel. This fails both ways:

- **Validation switched off.** With `{:validate nil}`, the documented way to keep schemas as inert data, the app freely commits states that violate its schemas. Restore then refuses to rewind to those same states, with `:rf.epoch/restore-schema-mismatch`.
- **Substituted validator.** With a non-Malli validator (a `clojure.spec` bridge, say), restore admits states the installed validator rejects. Malli throws on the foreign schema token, and the probe treats the throw as a pass.

Intended parent: the epoch surface rf2-3x7nj.17. Filed from the schemas reviewer's follow-up (rf2-3x7nj.19), which flagged it as out of slice. The epoch review did not consider it; its considered-and-rejected list covers only runtime-db scoping of the schema check.

## Where

At `034d0c8fc8`:

- `implementation/epoch/src/re_frame/epoch/tool_pair.cljc:62-72`: `malli-validate-fn` returns `(rf.late-bind/get-fn :schemas/malli-validate)`.
- `tool_pair.cljc:86-106`: `failing-schema-paths` calls `(validate-schema schema schema-value)` and treats a throw as valid (`(catch ... true)`).
- Callers: `tool_pair.cljc:472-487` (restore precondition 4, `:rf.epoch/restore-schema-mismatch`) and `tool_pair.cljc:1334-1338` (`replace-frame-state!` precondition 4, `:rf.epoch/replace-schema-mismatch`).
- Public entries: `rf/restore-epoch!` and `rf/replace-frame-state!`. These are the Xray and pair-tool time-travel writes, dev builds only (`implementation/epoch/src/re_frame/epoch.cljc:472`).
- The runtime-db sibling (`failing-runtime-paths`) goes through the machines validator and is not affected.

## Failure scenario

Scenario 1, validation switched off:

1. `(set-schema-fns! {:validate nil})`, `(reg-app-schema [:n] {:frame :p/off} :int)`.
2. Dispatch `:seed` (`{:n 0}`), then `:set-str` (`{:n "not-an-int"}`), then `:seed`. The hot path honours nil, so `{:n "not-an-int"}` commits.
3. `(restore-epoch! :p/off <the :set-str epoch>)` returns `false` and emits `:rf.epoch/restore-schema-mismatch`. The app cannot time-travel to a state it legitimately produced.
4. `(replace-frame-state! :p/off {:rf.db/app {:n "not-an-int"}})` returns `false`.

Scenario 2, substituted validator:

1. `(s/def ::pos pos-int?)`, `(set-schema-fns! {:validate (fn [s v] (s/valid? s v)) ...})`, `(reg-app-schema [:n] {:frame :p/spec} ::pos)`.
2. Dispatching `{:n -5}` is REJECTED by the installed validator on the hot path (app-db stays `{:n 1}`).
3. `(replace-frame-state! :p/spec {:rf.db/app {:n -5}})` returns `true` and installs `{:n -5}`.

## Evidence

Executed: a bounded JVM probe (probe5.clj on the schemas `:test` classpath plus `../epoch/src`, run from the frozen tree's `implementation/schemas`) through the real `dispatch-sync`, `epoch-history`, `restore-epoch!`, `replace-frame-state!` and a trace listener. Measured:

- Scenario 1: the hot path committed `{:n "not-an-int"}`; `restore-epoch!` returned false with `:rf.epoch/restore-schema-mismatch`; `replace-frame-state!` returned false with `:rf.epoch/replace-schema-mismatch`; `failing-schema-paths` returned `[[:n]]`.
- Scenario 2: the hot path kept `{:n 1}`, rejecting -5; `replace-frame-state!` returned true, `:rf.epoch/db-replaced`, and app-db became `{:n -5}`; `failing-schema-paths` returned `[]`.
- Control, default Malli bundle, same shape as scenario 1: `replace-frame-state! {:n "not-an-int"}` returned false (mismatch) and `{:n 7}` returned true. So the probe itself is correct under the default validator.

Contract:

- spec/010-Schemas.md:23: "No validation site interprets a schema itself; every one routes through the registered validator fn ... Substituting a different validator is a single registration call; the rest of this Spec (when validation runs, what happens on failure, ...) is unchanged."
- :556 (claim 2): "The runtime never inspects `:schema` directly; every validation site routes through the registered validator fn."
- :640: "`nil` validator means no validation, not 'every value fails'."
- :686: a no-op validator "disables every validation call site."
- spec/Tool-Pair.md:127 and :262 define the restore and replace checks as "validates against the currently-registered app-schemas set", which names the same app-schema validation, not a separate Malli check.

No tracker bead covers this: the export was searched for `malli-validate-fn`, `restore-schema-mismatch` and `replace-schema-mismatch` (0 hits each), and `:schemas/malli-validate` (3 unrelated hits).

## Smallest fix

In `failing-schema-paths`, resolve `:schemas/validate-with-registered-fn` instead of `:schemas/malli-validate`. That seam returns true under a nil validator, routes through the installed validator, and fails closed on a throw. Keep the absent-hook soft pass for when the schemas artefact is not loaded. Update the `failing-schema-paths` / `malli-validate-fn` docstrings. Fence: `implementation/epoch/src/re_frame/epoch/tool_pair.cljc`, plus a test beside `restore-failure-schema-mismatch` in `implementation/epoch/test/re_frame/epoch_test.clj`. No hot-zone file.

## Gates

- JVM: `clojure -M:test` in `implementation/epoch`. Its `:test` alias pulls in schemas.
- CLJS: the code is plain `.cljc`, so also `npm run test:cljs`.

## Decision needed

A small one. The current probe treats a throwing validator as "valid" (restore proceeds). The registered seam treats it as a failure (restore refused, matching the hot path's fail-closed posture for malformed schemas). The recommendation is to take the seam's behaviour. Keeping throw-as-pass needs a wrapper.

== RULING (delegated by Mike; mayor-dispatched ruling agent, 2026-09-24 01:08:41 AUSEST) ==

RULING: option (1), REFUSE. `failing-schema-paths` routes through the registered validator seam `:schemas/validate-with-registered-fn`, so time-travel restore / replace obey `set-schema-fns!` exactly as the hot path does: a `nil` validator passes, a substituted validator's verdict stands (its acceptances AND its rejections), and a validator that THROWS (including a malformed schema such as a childless `[:vector]`) REFUSES the restore/replace. The `(catch ... true)` throw-as-pass arm is deleted. No new op, no new trace, no public API.

WHY
- Routing through the seam is not a choice: spec/010-Schemas.md :23 ("No validation site interprets a schema itself; every one routes through the registered validator fn"), :556 (same, claim 2), :640 (`nil` validator = no validation, every site passes) and :686 (a no-op validator "disables every validation call site"). spec/Tool-Pair.md :127 / :262 define both checks as validation against "the currently-registered app-schemas set" — the same validation, not a second Malli pass. rf2-6eh5h (PR #8832) moved "every Spec 010 validation seam" to the registered validator and its census missed epoch.
- The one real choice was the THROW case. Refusing matches Spec 010:100 ("fails CLOSED (REJECTS the candidate transition — the unvalidated state is never installed)"), the core cofx check (cofx.cljc: "coercing the throw to a PASS would fold an unvalidated value into the durable ledger, the exact fail-OPEN class this check exists to close"), and the runtime-db half of the SAME `replace-frame-state!` (machine-data boundary, same seam). Keeping throw-as-pass would need a wrapper whose only job is to be the framework's single fail-open validation site, plus a Spec 010 carve-out sentence — extra machinery to preserve an inconsistency, which the stance rules out. Programmers who want unchecked exploration already have `(set-schema-fns! {:validate nil})`.
- A distinct "the validator threw" refusal op was considered and rejected as gold plating: the failing path is named in `:failing-paths`.
- The dossier and the independent Codex review AGREED on refuse. Codex's two qualifications are adopted: (i) the seam itself emits NO trace, so a prior `:rf.error/malformed-schema` on the hot path is NOT guaranteed when a tool is the first caller after a configuration change — the existing mismatch op + `:failing-paths` is the adequate failure surface, no richer diagnostic now; (ii) wrapping the seam cannot recover throw-as-pass anyway (it already returns `false` on a throw), so "keep throw-as-pass" would need a different path, not a wrapper — one more reason it loses.

- Substituted `clojure.spec` validator (`(fn [s v] (s/valid? s v))`, schema `::pos`): the hot path REJECTS `{:n -5}` (app-db stays `{:n 1}`); `replace-frame-state! {:rf.db/app {:n -5}}` returns TRUE and installs it (Malli throws on the spec keyword; the throw counts as a pass). Seam: FALSE.

- Throwing custom validator, `:int`, `7` (Codex): dispatch REJECTS; restore and replace ACCEPT today; seam REFUSES.

title: flows: a direct clear-flow's settle force-evaluates unrelated never-run flows - a boot-time clear throws flow-eval-exception for a flow the caller never touched (contradicts the direct reg-flow deferral rule)
description:
## Defect

A direct `(rf/clear :flow id)` called outside a drain settles the frame's remaining flows by running the whole ordinary pass (`run-flows-on-db`) over the committed app-db. That pass evaluates every flow whose inputs differ from its dirty-check row, not just the cleared flow's dependents. A flow registered cold since the last drain has no row, so a clear of any unrelated flow forces that flow's FIRST evaluation. So the clear does what Spec 013 says a direct `reg-flow` must never cause: evaluation at a moment the caller did not choose, often against an unseeded app-db. If that `:derive` is not total on nil, the clear throws `:rf.error/flow-eval-exception` blaming a flow the caller never touched. Boot and per-tenant setup code ("register the flow set, clear the ones this tenant doesn't use, then seed") fails. Before this settle existed, and whenever no clear happens, the same code works. Registration is no longer order-independent with respect to seeding.

## Where

At `034d0c8fc8`:
- `implementation/flows/src/re_frame/flows/registry.cljc:966-967`: `clear-flow*` calls the settle out of drain. The docstring at `:976-982` says it "settles the frame's remaining flows".
- `implementation/flows/src/re_frame/flows.cljc:446-506`: `settle-frame-flows!` runs the full `run-flows-on-db` pass. `flows.cljc:306-307`: the dirty check reads the row, and a flow with no row has old-inputs nil, which never equals the input vector, so it always evaluates.
- Contract it contradicts: `spec/013-Flows.md:498` (NORMATIVE: a direct `reg-flow` "registers the flow without evaluating it", and its output "is materialised by the next drain"). `:504`: "Registration is a declaration; evaluation is the drain's job, and that is what keeps registration order-independent with respect to seeding." `:502`: the clear settle "is unconditionally safe, because the dependents it recomputes are flows that were already running against inputs that are already present". `:488` point 1: "Only dependents are recomputed".
- Public entry points: `rf/reg-flow` (cold, out of drain) followed by `(rf/clear :flow <other-id>)` (out of drain) on the same frame before any drain.

## Failure scenario

```clojure
(rf/reg-flow :p1/greeting {:inputs [[:user :name]] :output-path [:greeting]}
  (fn [n] (when (nil? n) (throw (ex-info "derive refuses nil" {}))) (str "Hi " n)))
(rf/reg-flow :p1/legacy {:inputs [[:x]] :output-path [:legacy]} identity)
(rf/clear :flow :p1/legacy)   ; tenant setup disables an unrelated flow
```

The clear throws `:rf.error/flow-eval-exception` with `:rf.flow/failed-id :p1/greeting`, `:phase :derive`: "a flow's :derive fn threw while recomputing flow :p1/greeting during the settle a direct clear-flow runs before it returns". `:p1/greeting`'s derive was called once, with nil. Without the clear, the same code evaluates nothing until the seeding drain and then produces `"Hi Ada"`.

## Evidence

EXECUTED. I ran a bounded JVM probe from a scratch deps project with `:local/root` pointing at the frozen tree (plain-atom substrate, standard `make-reset-runtime-fixture`), exit 0. Output:
- CONTROL (the same two cold registrations, no clear): derive calls `[]`. After the seeding drain: `{:user {:name "Ada"}, :legacy nil, :greeting "Hi Ada"}`, calls `["Ada"]`. So the reg-flow contract holds on its own.
- CASE (then `(rf/clear :flow :p1/legacy)`): calls stay `[]` after the two registrations. The clear result is `[:threw {:rf.error/id :rf.error/flow-eval-exception, :failed-id :p1/greeting, :phase :derive, ...}]`. Derive calls during the clear: `[nil]`. `:p1/legacy` is deregistered and `:p1/greeting` stays registered. The next seeding drain recovers.

Probe source (supporting only): `scratchpad/review-wave/flows/probe/src/flowprobe.clj`, cases P1-control and P1.

Not pinned: `implementation/flows/test/re_frame/flows_direct_clear_settle_cljs_test.cljc` always seeds before clearing, and `flows_direct_reg_deferral_cljs_test.cljc` never clears. The closed beads rf2-g1zb (the settle was added) and rf2-f3yl (direct reg-flow must not settle) each rule their own half. Neither addresses the interaction.

## Smallest fix

Two options, and either works. (A) Code: in the direct-clear settle only, skip flows that have no dirty-check row, i.e. never evaluated or cold-replaced since the last drain. Those are exactly the flows the reg-flow rule defers to "the next drain". Leave the drain pass untouched. That is a flag threaded from `settle-frame-flows!` into `run-flows-on-db*` / `evaluate-flow!`, about 10 lines in `implementation/flows/src/re_frame/flows.cljc`. (B) Spec: amend `spec/013-Flows.md:488/:502` to say the direct-clear settle also performs the first evaluation of any not-yet-evaluated flow and can throw for it, so the reg-flow deferral holds only until the next clear. `spec/013-Flows.md` is not a hot-zone file.

## Gates

(A) is shared `.cljc` with no reader-conditional branch, so the JVM flows lane (`clojure -M:test` from `implementation/flows`) grades it. The natural pin is a cross-host case in `flows_direct_clear_settle_cljs_test.cljc`, whose CLJS arm is graded by `npm run test:cljs` only. (B) is docs: `check_doc_slugs.py` and `mkdocs build --strict` stage `spec/`, but neither checks prose, so verify by hand.

## Decision needed

Yes: the direct-clear settle either (A) skips never-evaluated flows so the reg-flow deferral holds, or (B) keeps evaluating them and the spec is amended to say a direct clear can throw for a flow it did not touch.

== RULING (delegated by Mike; mayor-dispatched ruling agent, 2026-09-24 00:31:40 AUSEST) ==

RULING: option (A). The settle a direct (out-of-drain) `clear-flow` runs evaluates only flows that have ALREADY EVALUATED since their registration or re-registration — i.e. flows that hold a dirty-check row. A flow with no row (registered or re-registered since its last successful evaluation) is left untouched, row still absent, and its first evaluation belongs to the next drain, exactly as the direct `reg-flow` rule says. The drain path is untouched; no option, no trace, no public API, no lifecycle registry.

WHY
- It makes both NORMATIVE rules true together. spec/013-Flows.md :498 (ruled via PR #9222, rf2-f3yl): a direct `reg-flow` "registers the flow without evaluating it ... materialised by the next drain". :504: a `:derive` "is not required to be total on nil, and requiring it to be would be a breaking widening of the derive contract for every flow in every application. Registration is a declaration; evaluation is the drain's job, and that is what keeps registration order-independent with respect to seeding." Today a direct clear of ANY flow forces the first evaluation of every never-run flow on the frame, so :498 holds only until the next direct clear, and :488 point 1 ("Only dependents are recomputed; nothing else cascades") is false.
- (B) "keep evaluating, amend the spec" reintroduces through a side door the nil-total `:derive` requirement :504 rejects, scoped only by an unrelated call; the failure arrives at the wrong call site, blaming a flow the caller never touched; and even a nil-total derive writes a boot-time placeholder into an unseeded app-db (S2 below). It is honest documentation of a wart, and it costs about as much prose as (A) costs code.
- The two closed beads each ruled one half — rf2-g1zb added the direct-clear settle (PR #9204, refined in #9257; commit 080c3b749d removed the established dependent's lag) and rf2-f3yl records that #9222 made "a direct reg-flow MUST NOT settle" normative (commit fc306b82b6) — and neither ruled the interaction. Those changes solve different programmer problems; (A) keeps both.
- The dossier and the independent Codex review AGREED on (A). Codex's refinements are all adopted: (1) it is a LIFECYCLE rule, not an empty-db exemption — a flow whose inputs were seeded before it was registered is deferred too; (2) the S4 re-registration corner reaches DOWNSTREAM, so the normative boundary itself (:482) must carry the qualifier, not only a subordinate bullet; (3) the dossier's claim that skipping cold flows makes the settle "unconditionally safe" is wrong — a WARM dependent can still throw when its producer is cleared (that is :488 point 2, pinned by an existing test), so :502's safety sentence must be REPLACED, and (A) is justified by predictable evaluation timing, not by a promise that cleanup cannot fail; (4) the missing-row criterion also correctly treats a flow whose last evaluation was rolled back as not yet established.

MEASUREMENTS (decisive, inline; JVM, plain-atom substrate, standard reset fixture, run against the mayor checkout at trunk f6bb999d6e; option A SIMULATED by `with-redefs` over the private `re-frame.flows/evaluate-flow!` returning the db unchanged when `*pass-caller*` is `:direct-clear` and the flow has no row — not a real edit; two independent probes, the dossier's and Codex's)

Under (A): the clear returns, calls `[]`, the seed gives "Hi Ada" with calls `["Ada"]`. (Codex, independent fixture: clear returns with zero derivation calls and an unchanged empty db; the seeding event yields `{:n 7 :answer 14}` in both versions, but today only after the unwanted failing call.)
- S1b (Codex): with the input ALREADY seeded before registration, today's clear still performs the new flow's first evaluation; (A) defers it. Clearing an UNKNOWN id evaluates nothing in either version.
- S2 today, nil-total derive ("Hi stranger" on nil): the clear returns but writes `{:greeting "Hi stranger"}` into an unseeded app-db before any event. Under (A) app-db stays `{}` until the seed.
- S3, the spec's own case (control — (A) must not disable the settle): `:a` then `:b` seeded, clear `:a` -> `{:x 2, :b nil}` at return under BOTH. Codex's established `A -> B -> C` chain: clearing A leaves both B and C derived from its absence before returning, under both.
- S4, the corner: `:a` then `:b` seeded, `:b` cold RE-registered, then clear `:a`. Today `{:x 2, :b nil}` at return (the NEW definition's first evaluation, forced by the clear). Under (A) `{:x 2, :b 20}` at return (the OLD definition's value — the "stale but owned" state :506 already accepts after any cold re-registration), `{:x 2, :b nil}` after the next drain. Codex's three-flow version: B re-registered after the chain ran, clear A -> simulated (A) returned `{:n 7 :b 7 :c 7}` — established C stays derived from B's retained value — and the next drain produced `{:n 7 :b nil :c nil}`.

- `clear-flow*` calls the settle whenever not in a drain: `(when-let [settle! (and (not in-drain?) @settle-frame-flows-fn)] (settle! frame-id pinned))` (implementation/flows/src/re_frame/flows/registry.cljc :966-967).

The replacement justifies the settle by WHEN it evaluates: it re-evaluates only flows that have already run, so it never chooses a first-evaluation moment for the caller; it can still fail, per point 2.

title: schemas: an app-db failure at a non-sensitive leaf inside a :set element ships the whole element (with its :sensitive? sibling) verbatim in :path and :reason
description:
## Defect

An app-db validation failure at a NON-sensitive leaf inside a `:set` element ships the WHOLE failing set element, including a conforming `:sensitive?` sibling, verbatim in the trace's `:path` and `:reason`. Malli reports a `:set` failure's `:in` segment as the element VALUE itself. `validate-app-schema!` only runs the `:path` sanitizer when the failing LEAF is sensitive (`leaf-sensitive?`), on the stated premise that "a conforming sibling's secret never appears in THIS leaf's path". That premise is false for a `:set` segment: the segment is the whole element, so it carries the siblings. The trace is stamped `:sensitive? true` and `:explain` is correctly redacted, while the secret rides out in `:path` and `:reason`.

## Where

At `034d0c8fc8`:

- `implementation/schemas/src/re_frame/schemas/validate.cljc:1051` computes `leaf-sensitive?` (leaf-precise). Line 1052 computes `whole-sensitive?`.
- `validate.cljc:1083-1088`: `trace-in-path` is sanitized only `(if (and in-path leaf-sensitive?) ...)`. The comment at 1074-1078 states the false premise.
- `validate.cljc:1097-1107`: the unsanitized `trace-path` goes into both `:path` and the `:reason` string.
- `implementation/schemas/src/re_frame/schemas/walker.cljc:705-706,863-867`: `align-in-path` drops the `:set` segment and descends into the element schema. For a non-sensitive leaf, `schema-sensitive-at?` (walker.cljc:1227-1234) therefore resolves `:ok` with no matching declaration and returns false.
- `walker.cljc:1019-1025`: the scrub that would have removed the element (`sanitize-sensitive-path`'s `:set` arm) exists but is never reached on this path.
- Public entry: `re-frame.schemas/validate-app-schema!` (schemas.cljc:85). It is reached on every `:db`-producing dispatch in a dev build through `:schemas/validate-app-schema!` (core router.cljc:1283).

## Failure scenario

```clojure
(rf/reg-app-schema [:sessions]
  [:set [:map [:uid :int] [:token {:sensitive? true} :string]]])
;; a handler commits:
{:sessions #{{:uid "not-an-int" :token "SECRET-TOKEN-A1"}}}
```

The emitted `:rf.error/schema-validation-failure` carries:

- `:path [:sessions {:uid "not-an-int", :token "SECRET-TOKEN-A1"} :uid]`
- `:reason "App-db at path [:sessions {:uid \"not-an-int\", :token \"SECRET-TOKEN-A1\"} :uid] failed schema ..."`
- `:explain :rf/redacted`, top-level `:sensitive? true`

So the secret token reaches every trace listener: Xray, the epoch recorder, pair and MCP forwarders.

## Evidence

Executed: a bounded JVM probe (`java -cp <schemas :test classpath> clojure.main probe1.clj`, run from the frozen tree's `implementation/schemas`) went through the real `reg-app-schema`, `validate-app-schema!` and `with-trace-recorder!`.

- Case A (above): `schema-sensitive-at?` returned false, and the secret appeared in both `:path` and `:reason`.
- Control B (same schema, the SENSITIVE `:token` leaf fails): `:path [:sessions2 :rf/redacted :token]`, secret absent.
- Control C (same shape as a `:vector`, non-sensitive leaf fails): `:path [:sessions3 0 :uid]`, secret absent.

The existing pin `app-db-validation-set-path-carries-no-secret` (schemas_sensitive_test.clj:377) only exercises a failing SENSITIVE leaf, so it cannot see this case. `rf2-fzbj.20` lists "set-element path segments" as inspected, but it did not cover a non-sensitive leaf beside a sensitive sibling. No tracker bead covers this: the export was searched for `set-element`, `sanitize-sensitive-path` and `leaf-sensitive?`, and the control needle `sanitize-sensitive-path` returned 4 hits.

Spec contract: spec/010-Schemas.md:405 ("On a `:sensitive?` `:set`-nested failure the runtime therefore scrubs the `:set`-element segment") and :374/:401. This failure IS stamped sensitive.

## Smallest fix

Key the `:set`-segment scrub to whether the set ELEMENT can carry a sensitive value, not to whether the leaf is sensitive. Two options:

- Simplest: run the sanitizer when `whole-sensitive?`, not only when `leaf-sensitive?`. Over-redaction of a tail past an ambiguous wrapper is the documented acceptable direction.
- Narrower: always scrub a `:set` segment whose element schema has any sensitive or opaque descendant.

Add the non-sensitive-leaf/sensitive-sibling case to the shared `walker_sanitize_path_fixtures.cljc` corpus and to `schemas_sensitive_test.clj`. Fence: `implementation/schemas/src/re_frame/schemas/validate.cljc` (and possibly `walker.cljc`), plus those tests. No hot-zone file.

## Gates

- JVM: `clojure -M:test` in `implementation/schemas`.
- CLJS: the code is plain `.cljc` with no reader conditional, and the shared fixture corpus has a CLJS half (`schemas_sensitive_path_cljs_test.cljs`), so also `npm run test:cljs`.

## Decision needed

No.
notes:
## FIXED — PR #10303 (worker/schemas-3x7nj), 2026-09-24

Reproduced at trunk 328b6bd194 (schemas tree unchanged since the frozen 034d0c8fc8): `:path [:sessions {:uid "not-an-int", :token "SECRET-TOKEN-A1"} :uid]`, with the secret in `:reason` too, `:explain :rf/redacted`, top-level `:sensitive? true`.

Fix: the bead's SIMPLEST option. In `validate-app-schema!`, `trace-in-path` now runs `sanitize-sensitive-path` whenever `whole-sensitive?` holds, not only when `leaf-sensitive?` does. The comments that stated the false premise are corrected, and so is the `emit-app-db-rejection-record!` docstring. spec/010-Schemas.md §`:sensitive?` (the `:set` carve-out) now says "sensitive" means the whole-schema decision. Existing pins needed no change: the navigable locators (`:vector` / `:tuple` / declared `:map` / non-sensitive `:map-of` keys) are kept by the sanitizer itself. The full schemas JVM suite stayed green.

Regression: `app-db-validation-set-non-sensitive-leaf-sensitive-sibling-path-carries-no-secret` (schemas_sensitive_test.clj) asserts `:path [:sessions :rf/redacted :uid]`, the secret absent from `:reason`, and the sentinel "SECRET-TOKEN-A1" absent from `(pr-str trace)`. Also a new case in the shared `walker_sanitize_path_fixtures.cljc` corpus (JVM + CLJS parity).

Control: red at trunk (3 assertions, secret present). Removing the fix again by planting `leaf-sensitive?` back into the `trace-in-path` condition made the same 3 assertions red; the restore was verified with a git blob hash equal to the committed blob. Schemas JVM green after: 416 tests / 19473 assertions, 0 failures.
Merged-PR audit #10303 (2ec17584d2d39d232abf709d2ecf45a98d23a109; merged 2026-09-23T20:38:43Z). Completeness: All four findings addressed: whole-schema path sanitization, slot-specific large-value elision without overwriting query identity, explainer-owned failing values and nonmemoized per-request schema extraction. Correctness: Reviewed source changes and regression coverage including sensitive siblings, map-of keys versus values, absent explainer values, multi-error fallback and hook/public memo distinction. Accepted reported 21-artifact JVM run, schemas 416/19473, HTTP 524/4125, measured heap probe and targeted negative controls; CI 62 successful checks. Implementation quality: Keeps existing late-bind key and registered-schema memo, avoids an LRU or another public API, and distinguishes lookup identity from payload. No material additional finding. Actionable findings: none. Existing finding updates: none.

Now it reads [:sessions :rf/redacted :uid] and the secret is nowhere in the trace. The case is added to walker_sanitize_path_fixtures.cljc and schemas_sensitive_test.clj. title: story-ui-evidence: recorder export auto-assert (on by default) has no seed db, so it asserts the first 5 top-level keys (incl. Story's own :rf.story/assertions run records) instead of the changed paths it advertises; the pasted test fails or does not compile
description:
## Defect

The recorder export dialog ("export as play script") turns on "Auto-assert app-db at end" by default, and labels it "(top-5 changed paths; trim manually after pasting)". But the dialog never passes a `:seed-db`, because the recorder never captures one. So `auto-assert-steps` takes its no-seed branch, which asserts the FIRST five top-level keys of the final app-db in iteration order, whatever they are. Those keys are not the paths the recording changed. They include Story's own run bookkeeping: `:rf.story/lifecycle`, and `:rf.story/assertions`, which is the vector of run records carrying `:dispatch-id`, `:elapsed-ms` and `:source-coord` (with an unquoted `:ns` symbol). The generated regression test is therefore wrong by construction:

- On a db with more than a few keys, it asserts unchanged static keys and never the recorded behaviour.
- When the source variant declares any assertion, it asserts a copy of the previous run's records. The pasted form refuses to compile on the JVM, and it can never pass when registered.

## Where

- `tools/story/src/re_frame/story/ui/recorder_export_dialog.cljs:77`: `initial-state :auto-assert? true`.
- `tools/story/src/re_frame/story/ui/recorder_export_dialog.cljs:134-147`: `build-export-from-dialog` passes `:final-db` and never `:seed-db`.
- `tools/story/src/re_frame/story/ui/recorder_export_dialog.cljs:366-369`: the "top-5 changed paths" hint.
- `tools/story/src/re_frame/story/ui/recorder_export_dialog.cljs:403-417`: `open-from-recorder-dialog!` snapshots the live frame db as `:final-db`.
- `tools/story/src/re_frame/story/recorder/play_export.cljc:341-367`: `top-paths` / `auto-assert-steps` use `(or (and seed-db (changed-top-paths ...)) (top-paths final-db))`. Even the seeded branch would keep a changed `:rf.story/*` key.
- `tools/story/src/re_frame/story/recorder.cljc:546-560` and `:803-826`: `start` / `start-recording!` capture no db snapshot.
- `tools/story/src/re_frame/story/recorder/play_export.cljc:490-503`: `render-variant-form`'s docstring promises the form "survives read-string round-trip and registers cleanly".
- Entry point: recorder toolbar REC, then stop, then the save dialog's "export" button, which opens the export dialog with auto-assert on.

## Failure scenario

A. A source variant declares `:assertions [[:rf.assert/path-equals [:submits] nil]]`. The user records two `[:probe/submit]` and exports with the defaults.

- The final-db keys are `(:rf.story/lifecycle :rf.story/assertions :submits)`.
- The script gains `[:assert-db [:rf.story/assertions] [{... :dispatch-id 5 ... :source-coord {:ns probe.export2 ...} ...}]]`.
- Pasting the rendered form into a stories namespace fails with `ClassNotFoundException probe.export2` (the ns symbol is evaluated).
- Registered as data, the test runs `:fail` on `[:rf.story/assertions]`, while `[:submits] 2` passes.

B. The app-db has 10 static keys plus lifecycle, and only `:submits` changed. The dialog path asserts `[:static-9] [:static-5] [:static-4] [:static-2] [:static-7]` and never `:submits`, so the test cannot fail when the recorded behaviour regresses. With a seed, the same function asserts exactly `[[:assert-db [:submits] 2]]`.

## Evidence

EXECUTED as bounded JVM probes on the tools/story `:test` classpath, in the frozen tree at `034d0c8fc8`; the tree stayed clean.

- `probe_export2`: uses `play-export-events/build-export` with exactly the dialog's options (`:auto-run? true :auto-assert? true :final-db <snapshot-frame-db>`, no seed). Output is scenario A above, verbatim:
  - `PASTE ... REFUSED: java.lang.ClassNotFoundException probe.export2`;
  - `DATA-REGISTERED fresh run status: :fail`, with `:rf.assert/path-equals :fail [:rf.story/assertions]`.
- `probe_autoassert`: `auto-assert-steps` without and with `:seed-db` gives scenario B. The control is the seeded call producing the changed path.

The dialog wiring (a `.cljs` file) was INSPECTED: `build-export-from-dialog` has no `:seed-db` key anywhere, and `open-from-recorder-dialog!` supplies only `:final-db`.

On CLJS a dotted `:ns` symbol would compile as a reference rather than throw. That is inspected only, and it still cannot equal the recorded symbol.

Dedup: rf2-0ae7o.11 (closed) fixed auto-run/click issues in the same dialog, not auto-assert. There is no open bead.

## Smallest fix

1. Snapshot the variant frame's app-db at `start-recording!` and carry it as `:seed-db` into the export dialog, so the diff branch the hint describes actually runs.
2. Drop `:rf.story/*` keys from `auto-assert-steps` in both branches. Story's own run bookkeeping is never app behaviour.

Optionally, when there is no seed, emit nothing rather than guessing.

Fence:
- `tools/story/src/re_frame/story/recorder.cljc`;
- `tools/story/src/re_frame/story/recorder/play_export.cljc`;
- `tools/story/src/re_frame/story/ui/recorder_export_dialog.cljs` (and the `:on-export` caller in `ui/recorder.cljs:815-819`).

No hot-zone file. `recorder/play_export.cljc` is in the story-execution slice (rf2-3x7nj.30) fence, so check there for a sibling before dispatch.

## Gates

- `play_export.cljc` and `recorder.cljc` are JVM-gradeable: run `clojure -M:test` in `tools/story`. Pin that a db carrying `:rf.story/assertions` yields no assertion on it, and that the rendered form round-trips through `read-string` + `eval`.
- The dialog change is a `.cljs` file, compiled only by the CLJS lane (`npm run test:cljs`).

## Decision needed

No.

Premise reproduced at trunk 6fb4c99638 (this worker's starting trunk) (JVM probe with the dialog's exact build-export options, no seed): a source variant declaring an assertion, two recorded [:probe/submit], exported with the defaults, gave [:assert-db [:rf.story/lifecycle] :ready] [:assert-db [:rf.story/assertions] [{... :source-coord {:ns probe2 ...}}]] [:assert-db [:submits] 2]; and auto-assert-steps without a seed over 10 static keys + :submits asserted five static keys and never :submits.

The save dialog's :on-export (ui/recorder.cljs) passes (:seed-db (current-state)) only when the recorder is not recording and still holds THIS dialog's source-id, so a later recording's start is never paired with this one; the export dialog carries :seed-db through open-from-recorder-dialog! -> open-dialog! -> build-export-from-dialog -> build-export (which already accepted it).

RED before (asserted five static keys).
- JVM pure (play_export_test.cljc auto-assert-never-asserts-story-bookkeeping): seeded and unseeded, a changed :rf.story/assertions and :rf.story/lifecycle yield only [[:assert-db [:n] 1]]. RED before.

Merged-PR audit #10315 (43bf4ee37ce115e4cfae1382989dc8c5f9df00ab; merged 2026-09-23T22:51:57Z). Completeness: Recorder root dispatch filtering, seed-db handoff, bookkeeping exclusion, Docs arg layers and typed scalar controls are implemented. Two acknowledged bare-compile residues need separate open tracking: schema loss before props validation and a share report losing plan-derived downgrade reasons. title: story-ui-workspace: Docs and the Controls/Schema-validation schema read compile the plan without :run-args, so a variant that relies on its story's :args shows 'plan unavailable' and gets no schema-derived controls
description:
## Defect

Two read paths compile the variant plan bare, as `(rf.story.plan/variant-plan vid)` with no `:run-args`:
- Docs' plan read, `ui/docs.cljc` `variant-plan-quietly`;
- the shared view-args schema resolver, `view_args.cljc` `compile-schema`.

The Controls panel and the Schema-validation panel both get their schema from the second.

Without `:run-args` the compile sees only the `:extends`-merged VARIANT arg layer. The story's `:args`, the globals and the modes are absent from that layer. The plan's view-args validation then fails with `:rf.error/story-view-args-invalid` whenever the variant leaves a required prop to its story. That is the spec's own flagship authoring pattern: required props on the story's `:args`, with variants overriding one or two.

Both readers swallow the throw and return nil, so for every such variant:
- Docs shows "plan unavailable — this variant does not compile to a plan" and drops the status/fidelity section, the schema table and their TOC entries.
- Controls derives no widgets from the schema. It falls back to value-shape inference: an `[:enum ...]` prop becomes a plain text box writing strings, the inline schema-violation rows disappear, and the Schema-validation panel reports "no schema registered".

The variant itself compiles, runs `:pass` and renders fine. Only these tooling reads disagree, because they omit the layers that every other keyword-target reader now passes (rf2-noxox, rf2-851t0).

## Where

- `tools/story/src/re_frame/story/ui/docs.cljc:204-215`, `variant-plan-quietly`, has a bare compile at `:214`. It feeds `docs-view` (`:1143-1182`; the "plan unavailable" branch is at `:1169-1174`) and `visible-toc-entries` (`:1008-1029`).
- `tools/story/src/re_frame/story/view_args.cljc:85-96`, `compile-schema`, has a bare compile at `:95`. It sits behind `compiled-view-args-schema` (`:98-120`). This file is outside this slice's scope; it is the shared root.
- Consumers:
  - `ui/controls.cljs:291`, `resolve-argtypes` `derive-schema`;
  - `ui/schema_validation.cljc:321-340`, `resolve-component-schema` (CLJS);
  - `ui/controls.cljs:970-972`, the args-editor inline violations.
- Sibling bare site, same class: `ui/share.cljs:288` (outside scope). All three are listed as direct keyword compiles in `rf2-1myb2`'s close reason, recorded there and not ruled.
- Contract:
  - `tools/story/spec/001-Authoring.md:262-304` is the flagship: story `:args` carry `:label :variant :size :disabled?` and `:story.ui.button/*` variants override one.
  - `:1607-1625` says the controls schema comes "through the compiled variant-plan's `[:world :view-args-schema]`".
  - `tools/story/spec/014-Chrome-Features.md:70-82` makes the same statement.
- Public entry: select a variant, then the Docs tab, or the Controls panel on the canvas.

## Failure scenario

Take `001-Authoring.md`'s button example verbatim: the view's `:rf/props` requires all four keys, the story supplies all four in `:args`, and variant `:story.ui.button/danger` sets only `{:args {:variant :danger}}`.

1. Open its Docs tab. It says "plan unavailable" with no fidelity/status section and no schema table.
2. Open Controls. `:variant` renders as a free-text box showing `:danger`; editing it writes a STRING (e.g. `":secondary"`), which the view's enum rejects. `:size` gets no bounds, and no row shows a schema violation.

The canvas, `run-variant` and the View-State panel all compile this variant fine.

## Evidence

EXECUTED as bounded JVM probes from `tools/story` at `034d0c8fc8`, using the reset-fixture boot.

Probe 3, the 001-Authoring button example verbatim:

| variant | `compiled-view-args-schema` | `variant-plan-quietly` | `effective-args` | `run-variant` `:status` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `:story.ui.button/default` | nil | nil | full four-key map | `:pass` |
| `:story.ui.button/danger` | nil | nil | full four-key map | `:pass` |
| `:story.ui.button/restated` (control: every prop restated on the variant) | the full `[:map ...]` | present | — | — |

Probe 2 used a two-prop view with a story-level `:args` and a variant `:story.btn/big {:args {:size 48}}`:
- bare `variant-plan` throws `:rf.error/story-view-args-invalid`;
- `visible-toc-entries` = `[docs-args docs-decorators docs-parameters docs-evidence docs-tags]`, with no `docs-status` and no `docs-schema`;
- `view-state/compile-model` (which passes `:run-args`) = `:ok`;
- `run-variant` = `:pass`.

Control, `:story.btn/all-own`: the TOC includes `docs-status` and `docs-schema`.

The Controls fallback (`infer-value-shape`, `controls.cljs:199-218`; a keyword value becomes `{:widget :text}` with no `:coerce`) was INSPECTED, since `controls.cljs` is CLJS-only.

Tracker: `variant-plan-quietly` returns 0 beads. `compiled-view-args-schema` appears only in closed rf2-gwye.* notes about other defects. rf2-1myb2 lists the sites, but as prose bookkeeping, and rules nothing.

## Smallest fix

Pass `{:run-args (rf.story.args/run-arg-layers vid opts)}` at `docs.cljc:214` and `view_args.cljc:95`. `share.cljs:288` wants the same.

For the schema resolver, note that the schema is not arg-dependent: it is the component's `:rf/props`. Better to read the schema off a compile that cannot be vetoed by args validation, or at least not to let an args-validation failure erase the schema that validation used. Otherwise any genuinely invalid cell-override value would still blank the Controls panel.

`compiled-view-args-schema`'s memo key (`[vid tick]`) stays valid if the read is made arg-independent. If run-args are threaded instead, the key must include them.

Fence: `ui/docs.cljc`, `view_args.cljc`, optionally `ui/share.cljs`. No hot-zone files.

## Gates

- `docs.cljc` `variant-plan-quietly` and `view_args.cljc` are CLJC and pure. The tools/story JVM artefact grades them (`clojure -M:test` from `tools/story`); a JVM pin for the flagship shape is cheap.
- The Controls and Schema-validation consequences sit in `.cljs` or a `#?(:cljs ...)` branch, so only `npm run test:cljs` exercises them.

## Decision needed

No. Optionally, decide whether the schema read should be arg-independent (recommended) or should thread run-args.

title: xray-chrome-config: rf/destroy-adapter! drains Xray's own Fresco roots and nothing repaints them - Xray is blank after the documented custom-adapter after-load recipe
description:
## Defect

`rf/destroy-adapter!` drains every Fresco client root at the process teardown boundary, through the `:fresco/drain-client-roots!` hook added in rf2-kuky.59. Xray paints its shell through two Fresco client-root handles of its own, `xray-root` and `xray-popout-root`. So a `destroy-adapter!` unmounts Xray's shell as well.

Nothing in Xray notices or repaints:

- `mount-state` still reads `{:visible? true …}` with the now-empty node.
- `open!`, `open-overlay!`, `toggle!` and `close!` see a populated `mount-state` and only flip CSS.
- `boot-on-runtime-ready!` is a run-once CAS.

After the host re-runs `init!`, the host app repaints, because its own `render!` "mounts afresh" as Spec 006 promises. Xray stays an empty panel until a full page reload.

The docs publish a recipe that hits this on every hot reload. For a custom adapter with no canonical `:kind`, `docs/api/re-frame.core.md:727` and `spec/006-ReactiveSubstrate.md:2131` say to "hold it in a `defonce`, or call `destroy-adapter!` in the after-load fn". A host that takes the second option and runs Xray loses Xray on the first save.

## Where

Cited at `034d0c8fc8` (frozen tree):

- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/substrate/adapter.cljc:227-249` is `drain-fresco-client-roots!`. `:251-287` is `dispose-adapter!`, which drains the Fresco roots first.
- `implementation/fresco/src/re_frame/fresco/impl/mount.cljs:498-519` is `drain-active-roots!`, published at :528. It unmounts every handle's Root and leaves the handle to "mount afresh" on its next `render!`.
- `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/mount.cljs:371` and `:375` define the `defonce` `xray-root` and `xray-popout-root` Fresco handles.
- `mount.cljs:377-387`: `render-shell!` is the only place Xray calls `render!`. It is reached from `mount-shell-into!` (:389-421), `switch-surface!` and `popout!`.
- `mount.cljs:1039-1072`, `open!`: when `mount-state` is populated, it runs `set-visible!` only (:1063-1066).
- `mount.cljs:1089-1097`, `open-overlay!`: the same pattern.
- `mount.cljs:1098-1107` (`close!`) and `:1109-1140` (`toggle!`) flip CSS only.
- `mount.cljs:1280-1380`: `boot-on-runtime-ready!` is CAS-guarded (:1327).
- Public entry point: `rf/destroy-adapter!` (`implementation/core/src/re_frame/core.cljc:3019`), called from a host's `^:dev/after-load` as `core.cljc:3070`, `docs/api/re-frame.core.md:727` and `spec/006-ReactiveSubstrate.md:2131` describe.

## Failure scenario

1. The host installs a custom adapter, which has no canonical `:rf.adapter/*` kind. It follows the documented option: `(defn ^:dev/after-load reload! [] (rf/destroy-adapter!) (rf/init! my-adapter) (render-app!))`. It runs Xray through the standard preload.
2. Xray opens and shows events.
3. The developer saves a file. The after-load hook runs, `destroy-adapter!` drains Fresco's active roots, and Xray's shell root is unmounted. `init!` installs the adapter again and the host app repaints.
4. The Xray panel is now empty: its frame and styles are still in the page, and its content is gone. The toggle key hides and shows the empty panel. Only a full page reload brings Xray back.

The same happens to an open pop-out through `xray-popout-root`.

## Evidence

**Inspected only.** The failing half is CLJS-only (a React root unmount), and a shadow-cljs build is out of bounds for this review.

The chain is direct:

1. The drain empties the set and unmounts each handle (fresco `mount.cljs:512-518`).
2. Xray's handles are ordinary members of that set, created through `rf.fresco/render!`.
3. Xray has no code path that calls `render!` again while `mount-state` is populated, except `switch-surface!`, which runs only when the surface kind changes.

A grep of `mount.cljs`, `preload.cljs`, `install.cljs` and `core.cljs` for `after-load`, `destroy-adapter` or `drain` finds only comments and the epoch-drain helpers in `install.cljs`. None of them is an adapter-teardown reaction. For the control, the same kind of search does find `render-shell!`: its definition at :377 and its two callers, :410 (`mount-shell-into!`, which `switch-surface!` reaches at :1022 and :1037) and :1759 (`popout!`, which returns early while `popout-state` is populated).

No shipped caller of `destroy-adapter!` exists in `tools/`, `examples/` or `testbeds/`. `git grep` finds only adapter docstrings and `core.cljc`. So reaching this takes a host that follows the documented custom-adapter hot-reload option, which is why this is P4.

Tracker: `drain-client-roots` appears in 1 record of the tracker export, rf2-kuky.59, which moved the drain and does not mention Xray. A `bd search "destroy-adapter"` finds 1 bead, rf2-3x7nj.2.2, an unrelated UIx spine teardown throw.

## Smallest fix

Make Xray's show verbs repaint when its root is no longer live. In `open!` and `open-overlay!`, when `mount-state` is populated, call `render-shell!` again with the same tree and node instead of only flipping CSS. On a live root, Fresco's `render!` is an update. On a drained handle it mounts afresh, which is exactly the recovery needed.

If the unconditional update costs too much against the CSS-only toggle target (<80ms, spec 007), add a cheap liveness check instead. Either way the user would still have to toggle once after the reload. Repainting automatically would need a hook on adapter install, which is a larger change.

Fence: `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/mount.cljs`, plus an arm in `mount_cljs_test.cljs`. No hot-zone files.

## Gates

`mount.cljs` is `.cljs`, so the node lane grades it with `npm run test:cljs`. A JVM green says nothing about it.

## Decision needed

Should Xray survive `destroy-adapter!`?

- **(a)** Repaint on the next show, as above. This is small.
- **(b)** Rule it out and add one sentence to `tools/xray/spec/011-Launch-Modes.md`: the custom-adapter `destroy-adapter!`-in-after-load recipe unmounts Xray until a page reload, so hold such an adapter in a `defonce` instead.
notes:
== DOSSIER WRITTEN 2026-09-24 01:16:17 AUSEST (analysis only — no status change, no dispatch, no edit) ==
Dossier: ai/decisions/rf2-3x7nj.27.4.xray-blank-after-destroy-adapter.md. ai/ is local-only and gitignored, so that path is a convenience that can rot; the decisive findings are restated inline below.
Read at trunk f7f96cb1c7 (equal to origin/main). Since the review tree 034d0c8fc8, the only change to a cited file is eda3cd4c14, a spec/006 prose edit that moved the recipe line from :2131 to :2132. No code cite moved.

RECOMMENDATION: (b). Rule the case out with one sentence at the end of the "Idempotency under hot-reload" paragraph in tools/xray/spec/011-Launch-Modes.md (:722-734). The sentence: the custom-adapter recipe that calls destroy-adapter! in an after-load hook releases Xray's Fresco roots too, so Xray stays blank until a page reload; hold such an adapter in a defonce instead. Then close the bead with this reasoning. Why not (a): it recovers only for a user who knows to toggle Xray twice, and that user could just reload. It also adds a special case to a toggle path that spec 011 keeps CSS-only (:712-716), and it leaves the pop-out uncovered. It remains a ready, bounded upgrade if a real custom-adapter host ever appears.

DECISIVE FINDINGS
1. The chain holds at trunk. dispose-adapter! drains every Fresco root first (implementation/core/src/re_frame/substrate/adapter.cljc:227-287). The drain empties fresco's active set (implementation/fresco/src/re_frame/fresco/impl/mount.cljs:498-519). Xray's shell sits in two ordinary Fresco handles (tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/mount.cljs:371, :375). open!, open-overlay!, close! and toggle! only flip CSS once mount-state is populated (mount.cljs:1039-1140), so nothing re-renders.
2. Real-host census: zero known.
   - All seven in-tree adapters carry a canonical :rf.adapter/* :kind (reagent, reagent-slim, uix, fresco, plain-atom, ssr, test-react).
   - Every rf/init! call in examples and testbeds passes a canonical adapter.
   - git grep -l -F destroy-adapter! -- examples testbeds tools finds 4 files: 3 Story tests and 1 template-spec sentence. None is non-test code (control: rf/init! appears in 41 example files).
   - Only a hand-written adapter that also takes the second recipe option (docs/api/re-frame.core.md:727, spec/006:2132) hits this.
3. Spec 011:731 ("panel MUST remain open across an :after-load, with its internal state intact") is false under that recipe today. That is why a one-sentence carve-out is worth doing rather than closing with no edit at all. The gate is python scripts/check_doc_slugs.py, which is vacuous unless the sentence carries a link. There is no code change and no hot-zone file.
== RULING (delegated by Mike; mayor-dispatched ruling agent, 2026-09-24 04:12:39 AUSEST) ==

RULING: option (b), with Codex's refinements. Xray does NOT survive `rf/destroy-adapter!` and gets no repaint machinery: the hot-reload promise in tools/xray/spec/011-Launch-Modes.md is narrowed to an ordinary `:after-load`, with one explicit sentence saying that `rf/destroy-adapter!` (under ANY adapter) releases Xray's roots and a page reload is the supported restart; and the caveat is also made visible where the programmer actually meets the recipe, as one clause beside the custom-adapter hot-reload recipe in docs/api/re-frame.core.md. Docs only; no code, no test, no hot-zone file.

== WHY ==

Chain re-verified at trunk 51cb069bd8 (= origin/main). Since the review tree 034d0c8fc8 the only commit touching a cited file is eda3cd4c14 (spec/006 prose; moved the recipe line :2131 -> :2132). No code cite moved.
1. `rf/destroy-adapter!` is `rf.substrate.adapter/dispose-adapter!` (implementation/core/src/re_frame/core.cljc:3019). `dispose-adapter!` (implementation/core/src/re_frame/substrate/adapter.cljc:251-287) runs `drain-fresco-client-roots!` (:227-249) FIRST, in a `finally` over the installed adapter's own disposer, whatever adapter is installed. Deliberate, per rf2-kuky.59 (commit 1c944d0910): a Fresco root is the package's, not any adapter's, so the drain sits at the process boundary.
2. `drain-active-roots!` (implementation/fresco/src/re_frame/fresco/impl/mount.cljs:498-519, published as `:fresco/drain-client-roots!` at :528) empties the active set FIRST, then unmounts every Root; a retained handle is inert and "a `render!` through it mounts afresh".
3. Xray paints through two ordinary Fresco handles, `defonce` `xray-root` and `xray-popout-root` (tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/mount.cljs:371, :375). `render-shell!` (:377-387) is Xray's only `rf.fresco/render!` call; its callers are `mount-shell-into!` (:410, reached from first open and `switch-surface!`) and `popout!` (:1759, which returns early while `popout-state` is populated).
4. After the drain, `mount-state` still reads populated with `:visible? true`. `open!` (:1039-1072) and `open-overlay!` (:1074-1097) on a populated same-mode state only call `set-visible!` (CSS); `close!`/`toggle!` are CSS-only; `boot-on-runtime-ready!` is a run-once CAS. Nothing renders again, so the panel frame stays and its contents are gone until a page reload.
5. Spec 011 today overpromises: :730-732 "the user's currently-open Xray panel MUST remain open across an `:after-load`, with its internal state intact" is false under this recipe; :713-716 "Close MUST be a CSS-only `display: none` ... Re-open MUST be a CSS-only `display: block`" is what option (a) would have to carve an exception into.

Who reaches it (census at trunk, with controls):
- `init!` treats a re-call with a canonical `:rf.adapter/*` kind as a no-op, so hot reload is safe for every shipped adapter. All seven in-tree adapters carry a canonical kind: `git grep -h -o -E ':kind\s+:rf\.adapter/[a-z-]+' -- 'implementation/**/src/**'` reads reagent, reagent-slim, uix, fresco, plain-atom, ssr, test-react (9 lines, fresco and uix twice).
- `git grep -l -F 'destroy-adapter!' -- examples testbeds tools` reads 4 files: 3 Story TEST files (tools/story/test/.../invariants_cljs_test.cljs, play/run_loop_settle_cljs_test.cljs, play/substrate_boundary_cljs_test.cljc) and 1 prose sentence (tools/template/spec/001-Substrate-Variants.md); 0 non-test code. Control: `rf/init!` appears in 41 example files. Every `rf/init!` in examples/testbeds passes a shipped adapter (dossier: reagent 43, uix 4, fresco 3, ssr 1, reagent-slim 1; 0 custom).
- So the one host that hits this has written its own substrate adapter, chose the second recipe option ("hold it in a `defonce`, or call `destroy-adapter!` in the after-load fn": docs/api/re-frame.core.md:727, spec/006-ReactiveSubstrate.md:2132, core.cljc:3070 docstring) over `defonce`, and runs Xray. That person is developing an adapter and already accepts a full remount on every save (the same drain releases their own Fresco roots too). Real-host count today: zero known in-tree; external users unknown.

Why (a) loses: the repaint-on-next-show fix recovers only for a user who knows to toggle Xray twice (hide, show), and that user can simply reload. It needs a liveness test Fresco deliberately does not offer ("liveness is never read off" the handle, implementation/fresco/src/re_frame/fresco.cljc:676-683, the phrase at :680), so the cheap proxy would be DOM emptiness; it carves a special case into the CSS-only toggle path; it does not cover the pop-out (`popout!` returns early on a populated `popout-state`) without more code; automatic recovery would need an "adapter installed" framework callback that does not exist; and repainting alone does not show the `:rf/xray` frame's subscriptions are sound across an adapter generation change. Exempting Xray from the drain instead would invent a second root-lifetime policy against rf2-kuky.59, and implementation/fresco/test/re_frame/fresco/client_root_lifecycle_dom_cljs_test.cljs pins exactly that lifetime: `destroy-adapter-releases-fresco-roots-under-uix-and-reagent` (:557) and `destroy-adapter-releases-a-live-handle-once-and-a-later-render-mounts-afresh` (:272). Why (c) (leave both alone) loses: spec 011's MUST stays silently false for a documented recipe when one sentence fixes it.

Where the two recommendations agreed and differed:
- AGREED on (b), no repaint machinery, no liveness API, no install callback; (a) stays a ready, bounded upgrade if a real custom-adapter host ever appears (design notes kept below).
- REFINEMENTS ADOPTED from Codex: (1) the boundary is `destroy-adapter!` under ANY installed adapter, not only custom ones, so the sentence must not scope it to custom adapters; (2) do not say a page reload is the ONLY way back — `switch-surface!` (mount.cljs:994-1037) does reach a fresh render, but full recovery through it is unverified, so name the page reload as the SUPPORTED restart and advertise no workaround; (3) `defonce` is not equivalent for a programmer who needs edits to the adapter's own functions to take effect — for that workflow the page reload is the supported path, so the guidance names both.
- DIFFERED on placement, and resolved for Codex: the dossier kept the caveat to Xray spec 011 alone ("a framework doc bending around one tool"); Codex asked for visibility beside the public recipe. What decides it is who reads what: the adapter developer following the recipe reads docs/api/re-frame.core.md, never Xray's implementation spec, so an 011-only sentence fixes the spec's truth but leaves that programmer with an unexplained blank tool. And the fact is a FRAMEWORK fact, not an Xray special case: spec/006-ReactiveSubstrate.md:261 (§"The client root (adapter-owned, reusable)", Teardown) already states normatively that the package's Fresco root set "is drained at the PROCESS teardown boundary, by `(rf/destroy-adapter!)` itself before it invokes the installed adapter's disposer. The guarantee therefore carries no adapter qualifier". docs/api/re-frame.core.md is not a hot-zone file and is hand-written (0 GENERATED/hand-edit markers). spec/006 (hot zone) is NOT edited: it already carries the drain at :261.
- Codex's caution kept: do not claim a repeated render necessarily loses state or blows the 80 ms toggle budget; no timing evidence exists either way, and neither is part of the reasoning above.

== WHAT TO BUILD (trunk 51cb069bd8) ==

Two sentences, docs only. Fence: `tools/xray/spec/011-Launch-Modes.md` and `docs/api/re-frame.core.md`. No hot-zone file; no file shared with the in-flight xray workers (.24.1/.23.5/.22.3) or with siblings .27.1/.27.2/.27.3, so it can go at any time, or ride with any other 011 edit already queued (the mayor may do it inline).

1. tools/xray/spec/011-Launch-Modes.md, end of the "**Idempotency under hot-reload.**" paragraph (:722-734), a sentence to this effect: the promise covers an ordinary `:after-load`; it does not survive an explicit `(rf/destroy-adapter!)`, under any adapter, because that call releases every Fresco root in the page (spec/006 §The client root, Teardown) — Xray's `xray-root` and `xray-popout-root` included — and Xray does not repaint itself, so the panel (and an open pop-out) stays blank until a page reload, which is the supported restart. A host running Xray with a custom adapter should hold that adapter in a `defonce` (the other documented hot-reload option) where that suits, and reload the page when it needs edits to the adapter's own functions to take effect. Do NOT add a carve-out to the CSS-only toggle MUST (:713-716); under this ruling nothing changes there.
2. docs/api/re-frame.core.md, the `init!` "**Hot reload is safe.**" bullet (:727), after "call `destroy-adapter!` in the after-load fn": one clause saying the latter also releases every Fresco root in the page, whatever adapter is installed, so a root whose owner does not render again (Xray's panel is the in-repo instance) stays empty until a page reload. Keep it tool-neutral in substance; naming Xray as the example is fine.

Gates: tools/xray/spec is outside `docs_dir` and not staged, so `mkdocs build --strict` does not see edit 1; `python scripts/check_doc_slugs.py` covers tools/*/spec and docs/ but is VACUOUS unless a sentence carries a link or anchor. If edit 1 links spec/006, the anchor to verify is `#the-client-root-adapter-owned-reusable` (heading at spec/006:244) and then check_doc_slugs grades it for real. docs/api/re-frame.core.md is inside the strict build, but a prose clause with no link gives neither gate anything to grade: say so in the PR body and check the rendering by hand. There is no RED/GREEN; nothing executable changes.

After the edits land the bead closes as "limitation ruled and documented by design", carrying the census above (0 custom adapters in-tree, 0 non-test `destroy-adapter!` callers under examples/testbeds/tools) in its close reason.

== IF A REAL CUSTOM-ADAPTER HOST EVER APPEARS: option (a)'s design, kept so nothing is lost ==
- In `open!` and `open-overlay!`, when `mount-state` is populated but the root has been released, call `render-shell!` again with the same tree and node. Fresco offers no liveness read, so the proxy is DOM emptiness (React's unmount leaves the container childless). An unconditional re-render on every show would break 011's CSS-only MUST and the pin stated in mount_cljs_test.cljs's ns docstring (:22-27, "no second `rf.fresco/render!` call").
- Test trap: that node-lane suite stubs `rf.fresco/render!` via `with-redefs` (e.g. mount_cljs_test.cljs:212-219, :306-311), so the stub must put a child into the node, or a DOM-emptiness guard re-renders on every open and turns that pin red. mount_cljs_test.cljs has 87 `deftest`s at trunk and `grep -c -E 'drain|destroy-adapter'` over it reads 0.
- RED: mount, empty the node to simulate the drain, then `close!` + `open!` must call `render!` a second time with the same node. CONTROL: without the drain, `close!` + `open!` keep the call count at 1. The pop-out needs the equivalent (`popout!` returns early on a populated `popout-state`), and it would collide with rf2-3x7nj.27.3 in the pop-out branch of mount.cljs, so sequence them.
- A real browser witness (destroy, reinstall, render, and renewed reactivity) would be needed to claim recovery; a stub call count is not enough. Lane: mount.cljs is `.cljs`, so only `npm run test:cljs` grades it.

## Decision needed
No. Ruled above.
WORKER (xray-fu-3x7nj, 2026-09-24): RULING (b) BUILT in PR #10318 (commit "docs: destroy-adapter! releases Xray's roots; a page reload is the supported restart (rf2-3x7nj.27.4)"). Docs only, no code.
- tools/xray/spec/011-Launch-Modes.md, end of "Idempotency under hot-reload": the promise covers an ordinary :after-load and does not survive an explicit (rf/destroy-adapter!) under any adapter, which releases every Fresco root in the page (linked to spec/006 #the-client-root-adapter-owned-reusable), xray-root and xray-popout-root included; the panel and any pop-out stay blank until a page reload, the supported restart; a custom-adapter host should hold the adapter in a defonce where that suits and reload when it needs adapter edits to take effect. No carve-out added to the CSS-only toggle MUST.

title: core-reactive: egress opaque resource handles are a 32-bit String.hashCode digest - they collide (merging nodes) and are not one-way
description:
## Defect

The off-box egress projection replaces a live resource's scope and params with "stable opaque handles". It mints each handle as `(hash (canonical-bytes v))`, a 32-bit non-cryptographic hash of the CEDN-1 token. On the JVM that is `Murmur3.hashInt(String.hashCode())`, and the CLJS string hash is the same shape. The result breaks both properties the spec asks of the handle:

- **It is not one-way.** A low-entropy parameter (a user id, a tenant id, an email address from a known list) can be recovered by enumerating candidates through the public projection.
- **It collides.** `String.hashCode` collides trivially: substituting "Aa" for "BB" at the same position leaves the hash unchanged. Two DISTINCT live resource identities can therefore project to one node key, and `project-graph`'s `into {}` then silently drops one of the two nodes from the egressed graph.

## Where

Frozen tree `034d0c8fc8`.

- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/derivation/egress.cljc:147-171` — `opaque-handle`, `:166-169`: `token (canonical-bytes v)`, then `digest #?(:clj (Integer/toHexString (hash token)) :cljs (.toString (bit-and (hash token) 0xffffffff) 16))`.
- `egress.cljc:423-428` — node keys are re-keyed through `project-resource-node-key` into a map, so colliding projected keys merge.
- `spec/Derivations.md:369` (§Redaction metadata) — the handles are "deterministic so the same key maps to the same handle — connectivity survives; one-way so the raw scope/params never cross the wire".
- Public entry point: `re-frame.derivation.egress/project-graph`, which Xray's `redact-graph-for-egress` aliases for shipping a live graph off-box.

## Failure scenario

1. **Collision.** Two live entries of one resource, `[:rf.scope/global :search/results {:q "Aa"}]` and `[:rf.scope/global :search/results {:q "BB"}]`, both project to `[:resource [[:rf.resource/opaque "ba1c2bb0"] :search/results [:rf.resource/opaque "838f7741"]]]`. The egressed graph has one resource node where the app has two.
2. **Not one-way.** `[:rf.scope/global :account/profile {:user/id 424242}]` projects to params handle `[:rf.resource/opaque "ea66d584"]`. Anyone holding the graph can enumerate ids through `project-graph` until the handle matches, and recovers `424242`.

## Evidence

Executed: `scratchpad/review-wave/core-reactive/probe_egress.clj`, one-shot `clojure -M` over the frozen `implementation/core/src`, run from the scratch dir, `frame-id` nil (the fail-closed branch).

- **Collision:** nodes before 2, after 1. Control: `{:q "Aa"}` vs `{:q "Ab"}` stay two nodes.
- **Recovery:** the id 424242 was recovered by enumerating `0..10^6` through the full public `project-graph` in about 22 s. Hashing the token directly would take a fraction of that.
- **Mechanism:** the probe confirmed the handle string equals `(Integer/toHexString (hash (canonical-bytes {:user/id 424242})))`.

The tracker export has no bead discussing the handle's hash strength: the search for `opaque` with `hash` returned only unrelated schema, SSR and websocket beads.

## Smallest fix

Mint the handle from a keyed cryptographic digest of the CEDN-1 token. For example, HMAC-SHA-256 under a per-process random key, truncated to 64 bits or more: JVM `javax.crypto.Mac`, CLJS `goog.crypt.Hmac` with `goog.crypt.Sha256`, both synchronous. That keeps both properties the code relies on:

- deterministic within a process, so connectivity survives;
- idempotent, because the `already-projected?` short-circuit is unchanged.

Fail closed to `:rf/redacted` exactly as today. The fence is `implementation/core/src/re_frame/derivation/egress.cljc`. No hot-zone file.

## Gates

`.cljc`, so both lanes:

- JVM: the `implementation/derivation-conformance` egress arms (the `g-*` witnesses) and `implementation/core`;
- CLJS: `npm run test:cljs`.

Nothing should pin the literal handle values across processes. Check that before choosing a per-process key.

## Decision needed

Does the off-box threat model include a recipient who dictionary-attacks low-entropy params?

- If yes: the keyed digest above.
- If no: widen the digest only enough to stop node collisions, and reword Derivations §Redaction metadata's "one-way" as "opaque, not cryptographic".

It costs the same as the unkeyed fix, needs no configuration, keeps spec/Derivations.md:369's "one-way so the raw scope/params never cross the wire" true, and fixes collisions in the same stroke. 2. Collisions are real but population-dependent.
