== RULING (delegated by Mike; mayor-dispatched ruling agent, 2026-09-23 23:07:20 AUSEST) ==

RULING: Option (a). The off-box contract already promises one-way handles, and that promise is kept.
- New minting: each opaque resource handle becomes HMAC-SHA-256 over the UTF-8 bytes of the value's CEDN-1 token.
- The key: private, cryptographically random, 32 bytes, generated once per runtime.
- The output: the FULL digest as 64 lowercase hex chars, with no truncation.
- Unchanged: the handle shape `[:rf.resource/opaque <hex>]`, the fail-closed fallback to :rf/redacted, and idempotence.
- spec/Derivations.md:369 (not hot-zone) gets a clause stating the bounded one-way property and that handles are stable only within one runtime.
- Sequence this behind rf2-3x7nj.3.5, which is in_progress on the same egress.cljc.

WHY
- This does not need Mike. The existing record already settles the security posture.
  - spec/Derivations.md:369 already requires the handles to be "one-way so the raw scope/params never cross the wire".
  - spec/Security.md:285 states the normative stance: "Trust the explicit invoker; gate accidents not theoretical attacks; programmer ergonomics matter; secure by default but not at the cost of friction". It points the same way:
    - The accident being guarded against is a developer shipping a graph they were TOLD was one-way.
    - The attack is a `filter` over `range`, so it is not theoretical.
  - Option (b) would WEAKEN a normative promise. Option (a) keeps it with zero friction for the programmer: no config, and the same call.
- The dossier and Codex both chose (a). They differed on two points, resolved as follows.
  - (1) Truncation: the dossier said ">= 64 bits"; Codex said "full digest". RULED: the full 256-bit output.
    - It removes a parameter nobody needs to defend.
    - Any finite digest can collide, but with a cryptographic digest the chance is negligible either way.
    - Handles only travel in debug exports.
    - A shorter encoding can come later if a measured need appears.
  - (2) Spec clarification: the dossier said "optional"; Codex said "required". RULED: required.
    - The spec's unqualified "deterministic so the same key maps to the same handle" must now say "within one runtime".
    - "One-way" must be stated as the bounded property below, not as unconditional anonymity.
    - Derivations.md is not hot-zone, so this is cheap.
- Codex's bounded property is adopted for both the docstring and the spec clause.
  - It protects against someone who receives an exported snapshot but has neither the runtime key nor a live projection oracle.
  - It does NOT protect against the trusted programmer, against anyone with local evaluation access, or against what the graph topology itself reveals.
  - Equal values still get equal handles within a runtime, so equality remains visible.
  - Replace the docstring's "IRREVERSIBLE" with this statement.
- Why (b) loses. (b) is an unkeyed SHA-256 with "one-way" reworded to "opaque, not cryptographic". It fixes collisions but not reversibility. Measured: an unkeyed SHA-256/64 still gave up user id 424242 to enumeration in 2.8 s.
- Why (c) loses. (c) keeps the 32-bit hash and rewords the spec. Collisions then keep silently dropping nodes, which breaks "a redacted resource node is still a node".
- Codex's correction on cost is accepted. The change does not cost literally the same as the unkeyed option: it adds random-key initialisation, private state that lives as long as the runtime, and host crypto calls. The cost to the programmer stays zero.

THE DEFECT, VERIFIED AT TRUNK 5d74c334bb (egress.cljc is unchanged since 4b627ee9e2)
- implementation/core/src/re_frame/derivation/egress.cljc:147-171, opaque-handle, computes `token (rf.identity/canonical-bytes v)` and `digest #?(:clj (Integer/toHexString (hash token)) :cljs (.toString (bit-and (hash token) 0xffffffff) 16))` at :166-169.
  - That is a 32-bit non-cryptographic hash: Murmur3 over String.hashCode on the JVM, and the same shape on CLJS.
  - CLJS also renders a negative value as signed hex. That JVM/CLJS mismatch goes away with the fix.
  - Node keys are rebuilt into a map (:~423-428), so equal handles merge nodes.
- Executed evidence. The dossier and Codex probed independently on the JVM, at 4b627ee9e2 source.
  - Collision: `{:q "Aa"}` and `{:q "BB"}` through project-graph went from 2 nodes to 1. Control: `{:q "Aa"}` and `{:q "Ab"}` stayed at 2.
  - Reversal: `{:user/id 424242}` gets handle "ea66d584", equal to `(Integer/toHexString (hash (canonical-bytes {:user/id 424242})))`. Enumeration recovered the id in 0.77 s by hashing the token directly, and in 8.1 s through the public project-graph.
  - Natural collision rates:
    - integer ids 0..10^6: 1,000,000 distinct handles of 1,000,000;
    - every lowercase query of 1-4 chars: 475,254 of 475,254;
    - every [a-zA-Z] query of 1-3 chars: only 42,114 distinct of 143,364. The gap 'a'-'A' = 32 = 31+1 lines up with String.hashCode's weights.
  - Cost per handle, 200k calls on the JVM (both figures include canonical-bytes): 1.8 us for the 32-bit hash, 8.0 us for SHA-256/64.

1. A pure helper, hmac-sha256-hex [key-bytes s], returning the 64-char lowercase hex HMAC-SHA-256 of s's UTF-8 bytes.
   - JVM: javax.crypto.Mac "HmacSHA256" with a SecretKeySpec; get UTF-8 via StandardCharsets/UTF_8.
   - CLJS: goog.crypt.Hmac with goog.crypt.Sha256. Build the input with goog.crypt/stringToUtf8ByteArray (UTF-8 matters for non-ASCII values) and the hex with goog.crypt/byteArrayToHex.

title: http: anonymous issuance counters grow without bound for actor-issued requests (one permanent entry per spawned :rf.http/managed#N address) until frame destroy
description:
## Defect

The new anonymous issuance counters (rf2-x8oz5) are keyed `[frame-id (first origin-event)]` and are never evicted, except when the frame itself is destroyed. They were justified as bounded because "the key space is (frames × registered event-ids)". That premise fails for requests issued from inside a spawned state-machine actor. There the originating event-id is the actor's ADDRESS, `<prefix>#<n>`, and `n` comes from a counter that only goes up. Every spawn that issues an anonymous request therefore leaves one permanent counter entry behind. After the actor completes and is destroyed, nothing ever reads that entry again. The shipped `:rf.http/managed` machine wrapper is exactly this shape: each `:spawn {:machine-id :rf.http/managed …}` mints `:rf.http/managed#N` and issues one anonymous request. A long-lived frame (the ordinary browser app, a long-running JVM process) whose machine re-enters a spawning state grows the map by one entry per spawn, for ever. That is the unbounded-distinct-id leak rf2-k47b3d closed for named request-ids, reintroduced through actor addresses.

## Where

At `034d0c8fc8` (frozen tree), host: both (shared `.cljc`).

- `implementation/http/src/re_frame/http/registry.cljc:521-535`: the `anonymous-issuance-counters` atom and the "bounded" rationale.
- `registry.cljc:553-556`: the anonymous branch of `next-issuance!`, keyed by `(first origin-event)`.
- `registry.cljc:1067-1073`: the only removal, a frame-destroy drop.
- `registry.cljc:893-917`: `abort-on-actor-destroy` (2-arity), which runs on every actor destroy but does not touch the counter.
- `implementation/http/src/re_frame/http/handlers.cljc:494`: the allocation site.
- `implementation/http/src/re_frame/http/machine_wrapper.cljc:127-139`: the wrapper issues its request anonymously from its own actor.
- `implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines/transition.cljc:563-579`: spawn addresses `<id-prefix>#<n>` with an only-increasing `n`.
- `implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines/lifecycle_fx/finalize.cljc:692` and `lifecycle_fx/destroy.cljc:246`: the destroy hook fires on every actor teardown, so it is the natural eviction point.
- Entry point: a parent machine with `:spawn {:machine-id :rf.http/managed …}` (or any spawned actor that issues `:rf.http/managed` without `:request-id`), re-entered repeatedly in a frame that lives a long time.

## Failure scenario

A poller machine, `:idle --:go--> :fetching (:spawn :rf.http/managed) --:succeeded/:failed--> :idle`, driven every 5 s in `:rf/default`. Each cycle completes, the wrapper is destroyed, and in-flight and actor indexes return to empty. `anonymous-issuance-counter-count` nevertheless climbs by one per cycle: 17,280 permanent entries a day, released only if the frame is destroyed.

## Evidence

EXECUTED. JVM probe against the frozen tree (http `:test` classpath: machines and a local HttpServer).
- CONTROL: 25 anonymous requests from ONE ordinary event (`:probe/plain`) gave `anonymous-issuance-counter-count` 1, key `[[:rf/default :probe/plain]]`. The design works for ordinary events.
- SUBJECT: 25 poller cycles, each spawning the `:rf.http/managed` wrapper, 25 of 25 completed. Afterwards in-flight 0, actor-in-flight 0, live wrapper snapshots 0, but anonymous counters **26**, with keys `[:rf/default :rf.http/managed#10]`, `[:rf/default :rf.http/managed#11]`, … one per spawned address. The named counter count stayed 0.
- rf2-x8oz5's description states the bounded-key-space premise ("(frames x registered event-ids), which is bounded"). Its tests (`implementation/http/test/re_frame/http_issued_trace_test.clj:459-477`) only ever use a fixed event-id (`[:ev/go]`). Tracker full-text search (anonymous-issuance-counters; spawn + issuance) found no bead on actor addresses.

## Smallest fix

In `abort-on-actor-destroy`'s 2-arity, also `(swap! anonymous-issuance-counters dissoc [frame-id actor-id])` once the actor's handles are aborted. The hook already runs on every destroy trigger, including natural completion. A destroyed address's requests are all terminal by then, so restarting its count is collision-free; the only exception is a same-address re-mint by another parent snapshot, which is also safe for the same reason. Update the "bounded" comment to name the actor case. Fence: `implementation/http/src/re_frame/http/registry.cljc` plus a spawn-loop case in `implementation/http/test/re_frame/http_issued_trace_test.clj` (or the machine-wrapper test). No hot-zone file, and no machines change.

## Gates

JVM: `clojure -M:test` in `implementation/http`, which has the machines artefact on its test classpath. The change is shared `.cljc` outside any reader conditional, so the node lane `npm run test:cljs` compiles it too.

## Decision needed

No.
notes:
== FIXED, PR #10320 (branch worker/http-3x7nj), 2026-09-24 10:00 AUSEST ==

Premise held at trunk 24cfb3141a: `anonymous-issuance-counters` was dropped only in `abort-in-flight-on-frame-destroyed!`.

Reproduced producer-derived: new test `spawn-loop-leaves-no-anonymous-issuance-counters` (http_managed_machine_test.clj) drives five `:go` cycles of a parent machine whose `:fetching` state spawns the shipped `:rf.http/managed` wrapper against a local 200 server, waiting each cycle for the parent back at `:idle`, no live `:rf.http/managed#N` snapshot and an empty actor index. At trunk source: "5 completed spawns left 5 anonymous issuance counters behind".

Fix (registry.cljc): `abort-on-actor-destroy`'s 2-arity, after aborting the actor's handles, runs `(swap! anonymous-issuance-counters dissoc [frame-id actor-id])`. The hook runs on every actor destroy including natural completion (machines finalize step 6, destroy step 2). Every request the address issued is terminal by then, so restarting its count cannot collide, even on a re-mint of the address. The counter comment, `next-issuance!`, `evict-issuance-on-completion!` and the frame-destroy docstring now name the actor case, and Spec 014's work-id paragraph says the count is "never reset by completion" and is dropped when its owner (frame, or spawned actor whose address is the event-id) is destroyed. No machines change.

Control: a one-line plant removing the `dissoc` turned the test red again (5 left behind); restored, the blob hash equalled the committed blob. Green: 31 tests / 166 assertions across the machine-wrapper, issued-trace and both actor-destroy namespaces; the http JVM suite 530 / 4155 / 0.

Implementation quality: Uses existing policy and indexes, narrows retry ownership atomically and reclaims counters at owner teardown. No new author API or additional runtime finding. Completeness: Ruled option 1 is implemented at both abort emit paths, by kind for every reason; catalog and producer-shaped Xray/testbed mirrors agree. title: xray-shell-views: handler-source unescape rewrites backslash-n outside string literals, mangling regex and char literals
description:
## Defect

`edn_widget/unescape-source-newlines` turns every backslash-n pair anywhere in the captured handler source into a real line break, so the handler-source block shows code that was never written. Its docstring justifies this with the premise that "`pr-str` only ever emits the `\n` escape INSIDE string literals — a bare `\n` two-char sequence never occurs elsewhere in printed Clojure source". That premise is false. `pr-str` also prints backslash-n in three non-string forms that are common in handler bodies: a regex literal `#"\n"` (its pattern source is printed verbatim), the character literal `\n` (the letter n), and the character literal `\newline`. After `format-source` runs zprint and then this unescape, the Epoch handler-source block shows `(str/split s #"\n")` as `#"`, a line break, then `")`. It shows `(= c \n)` as `(= c \`, a line break, then `))`, so the character literal is gone. It shows `(str/join \newline …)` as `(str/join \`, a line break, then `ewline …`, which is not even readable Clojure. The operator uses this block to see what the handler actually does, and it misstates the code.

## Where

Frozen tree `034d0c8fc8`:

- `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/views/edn_widget.cljs:183-225`: `unescape-source-newlines`. The false premise is at `:205-208`, and the whole-string `str/replace` is at `:224-225`.
- `…/edn_widget.cljs:227-252`: `format-source` runs zprint and then the unescape over the WHOLE string. `code-block` at `:391-394` then tokenises the result.
- Callers: `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/epoch/view.cljs:3520` (the handler source) and `:4151`.
- Source capture: `implementation/core/src/re_frame/core_reg_macros.cljc:304`, `(pr-str whole-form)` at compile time on the JVM.
- Tests: `tools/xray/test/day8/re_frame2_xray/views/edn_widget_cljs_test.cljs:232-264` cover the string-literal case and escaped backslashes only, with no regex or char-literal case.

## Failure scenario

`(rf/reg-event :lines/split (fn [{:keys [db]} [_ s]] {:db (assoc db :lines (str/split s #"\n"))}))`. Fire it, open the Epoch panel, and look at the handler source: the regex is split across two lines. Swap the body for `(str/join \newline lines)` and the source shows `\` at the end of one line and `ewline lines)` at the start of the next.

## Evidence

**Executed** as bounded JVM probes, scratch `probe.clj` and `probe3.clj`. The regex is copied verbatim from `edn_widget.cljs:224`, and the input is `pr-str` of the whole form, as the capture does:

| Input form | Lines in | Lines out | Damaged output |
|---|---|---|---|
| `#"\n"` | 1 | 2 | the regex is split |
| `\newline` | 1 | 2 | `(str/join \` then line break then `ewline (:lines db))` |
| `(= c \n)` | 1 | 2 | `(= c ` then line break then `))}))` |

Controls, both ways:

- `{:doc "line one\nline two"}` goes from 1 line to 2. That is the intended unescape, and it works.
- A form with no backslash-n is returned unchanged.

JVM and CLJS agree here because the capture is JVM `pr-str` and the replace regex means the same thing in both.

**Not executed: the zprint step between capture and unescape.** zprint is expected to keep regex and character tokens as written, since they are source-preserving tokens, but no CLJS build could be run to confirm it. It could only remove the damage by rewriting those literals, and it has no reason to.

## Smallest fix

Unescape only inside string tokens. `code-block` already tokenises (`tokenize-clojure`, `edn_widget.cljs:317-366`), so the fix is to apply the backslash-n rewrite to `:string` tokens' literals after tokenising, instead of to the whole formatted string before it.

- **Skip regex strings.** The tokenizer splits a regex into a `#` symbol token followed by a `:string` token, so a `:string` token immediately preceded by `#` must be left alone.
- **Character literals are already safe.** They tokenise as a `\` token plus a symbol, never as `:string`, so they cannot reach the rewrite.

Add regex-literal, `\n` char and `\newline` char cases to the existing tests.

Fence: `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/views/edn_widget.cljs` and `tools/xray/test/day8/re_frame2_xray/views/edn_widget_cljs_test.cljs`. No hot-zone file.

## Gates

`npm run test:cljs`, the node lane (`.cljs` only).

## Decision needed

No.
notes:
## Fixed — PR #10334 (worker xshell-3x7nj, 2026-09-24)

Implemented the "Smallest fix". `format-source` is now zprint alone. `code-block` runs `(unescape-string-tokens (tokenize-clojure formatted))`, which rewrites only `:string` tokens and skips one straight after a `#` token (a regex).

DIFFERS FROM THE DESCRIPTION'S PREMISE: "Character literals are already safe" holds for `\n` and `\newline` but NOT for `\"`. The tokenizer read `\"` as `\` followed by an opening quote, so a :string token ran to the next quote. A JVM probe of the new per-token pipeline WITHOUT a fix for this, on `(if (= c \") {:db (assoc db :sep \n)} {:db db, :doc "a\nb"})`, rewrote the `\n` char into a line break and left the real docstring escaped. So the tokenizer now lexes a character literal as ONE `:symbol` token: named chars, `\uXXXX`, `\oNNN`, or any single char. Colours are unchanged. This also stops `\;` reading as a comment.

The JVM probe also measured the two unexecuted premises:
- JVM `pr-str` prints `#"\n"`, `\newline` and `\n` verbatim.
- zprint 1.3.0 `zprint-file-str` at width 72 leaves all three as printed.

Controls, in `views/edn_widget_cljs_test.cljs`: regex, `\newline`, `\n`, and the `\"` case, each as its exact JVM pr-str shape. Also one-token char lexing, and `unescape-string-tokens` directly.
- CI red at the tests-only head b5561d4640 (node-test job 107451484594): 5 failures, all in the new tests. The `unescape-string-tokens` unit test was held back from that commit.
- Local JVM probe loading the real edited fns from source: the pre-fix source planted over the file gave 6 failures; the fix gave 0. Both runs covered 12 tests and 23 assertions, and the restore matched the committed blob hash.
Merged-PR audit #10334 (11a2287c93e9fe43f505602b185b22be15228254; merged 2026-09-24T01:52:48Z). Completeness: All four shell/view findings addressed: added-subtree zoom uses missing before rather than whole-root fallback; leak predicate catches embedded strings and printed leaves; source unescape is token-local with regex and character handling; both React Flow overrides are scoped. Removed-side zoom was explicitly checked and does not enter the affected path. Correctness: Accepted tests-only CI control with 12 node failures and 2 JVM failures, final green CI 36 successes, local redaction 6 tests/48 assertions and tokenizer/style controls. Read all source and test changes against source Beads. Character quote lexing closes the premise gap the implementer discovered. No rerun or residual defect found. Implementation quality: Small fixes reuse the inspector absence sentinel, existing token stream and shell root attribute. No new rendering framework, parser dependency or global style policy; test-only predicate mirrors its already-corrected counterpart. Actionable findings: none. Existing finding updates: none.

rf2-3x7nj.25.6: fixed, with one PREMISE CORRECTED — the item said character literals already tokenise safely; true for 
 and 
ewline but NOT for " , which the tokenizer read as the start of a string running to the next quote. A JVM probe showed that with only the item's fix, a later

So tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/views/edn_widget.cljs now (a) applies the backslash-n rewrite to :string tokens only, skipping a regex (a :string preceded by #), and (b) reads each character literal as ONE token, same colour as before. The probe also confirmed JVM pr-str and zprint 1.3.0 leave #"
", 
 and

title: examples-core: login/stories.cljs's :login.story/submit :doc (and two docstrings) promise the :preset :story generic stub drives a submit to :authed; the same file records that stub is refused at :auth.login/succeeded's schema
description:
## Defect

`examples/core/login/stories.cljs` states two opposite things about the Story success path. Its own comment blocks, which record rf2-hz8u (`:103-111`, `:347-358`), say correctly that the `:preset :story` frame's GENERIC canned-success stub answers `{:stubbed true}`. That reply is refused at `:auth.login/succeeded`'s `[:value :token]` schema, so a submit through the real form path "never leaves `:submitting`" unless the variant supplies its own `:network` fixture.

Three other passages in the same file promise the reverse:

- The registered `:doc` of the story driver `:login.story/submit` (`:114-121`) says "Under the `:preset :story` frame the canned-success stub resolves it and the `:auth.login/success` follow-on lands the flow at `:authed`." This also skips the real hop through `:auth.login/succeeded`.
- The `good-creds` docstring (`:136-141`) says "the canned-success stub doesn't even look at them, it just answers `:ok`".
- The ns docstring (`:38-41`) says each variant's `:preset :story` frame "quietly redirects `:rf.http/managed` to the framework's canned-success stub. So a submit isn't a mock — it's the real cascade, running end to end".

The first of these is REGISTRATION METADATA rather than a comment. `:doc` is what Story, Xray and `handler-meta` show a reader or an agent about `:login.story/submit`. So the tool-facing description of the driver is the wrong half of the file.

rf2-fn0kx.2 finding 1 corrected three other comments in this file (the cascade header, `:85` and `:331`). These three survived that sweep.

## Where

All cites are at `034d0c8fc8`.

- `examples/core/login/stories.cljs:114-121`: the `:doc` on `(rf/reg-event :login.story/submit …)`.
- `examples/core/login/stories.cljs:136-141`: the `good-creds` docstring.
- `examples/core/login/stories.cljs:38-41`: the ns docstring.
- Against `examples/core/login/stories.cljs:103-111` and `:347-358` (the correct account), `examples/core/login/model.cljc:671-672` (the `:auth.login/succeeded` schema requiring `[:value [:map [:token :string]]]`), `implementation/core/src/re_frame/frame.cljc:2396` (`:preset :story` remaps `:rf.http/managed` to `:rf.http/managed-canned-success`), and `implementation/http/src/re_frame/http/test_support.cljc:202`, where the generic canned success value defaults to `{:stubbed true}`.
- Public entry point: `rf.story/reg-variant` with `:setup [[:login.story/submit …]]`.

## Failure scenario

A Story author reads the driver's `:doc`, either in the file or through the tool, and adds a variant `{:compose [:fragment.login/form-base] :setup [[:login.story/submit good-creds]]}` without a `:network` route, expecting the Welcome banner. The generic stub replies `{:status :ok :value {:stubbed true}}`. `[:auth.login/succeeded …]` fails its event schema and is skipped, the machine is never nudged, and the canvas sits in `:submitting` with "Signing in…". That is precisely the symptom rf2-hz8u was filed for.

## Evidence

INSPECTED; the behaviour itself was EXECUTED elsewhere. The contradiction is between passages of one file at one sha. The behavioural half is on record from CI: rf2-hz8u's close reason cites rf2-cckg's failing-first run, which drove the registered `:story.login/success` with its `:network` slot removed and reproduced "machine `:submitting`, `:auth/authenticated` false, empty storage". The source half, the `{:stubbed true}` default and the token schema, was read at the cites above. Tracker: `login.story/submit` appears in exactly one bead (rf2-hz8u, closed), which fixed the variant and not the driver's `:doc`.

## Smallest fix

Rewrite the three passages to say what `:103-111` already says. The generic preset stub is refused at `:auth.login/succeeded`'s schema, so the driver only walks the form path, and each variant decides what the server said: `:network` for success, hand-driven replies for the failures. Name `:auth.login/succeeded` as the hop before the machine's `:success`. The fence is `examples/core/login/stories.cljs` only. It is not a hot-zone file, and examples stay test-free.

## Gates

This changes docstrings and a `:doc` string only. No gate can fail on it (the vacuity rule under CLAUDE.md § Build & Test). Say so in the PR body. The file is compiled only by the `:examples/login-with-stories` build in CI's derived compile sweep, and by the node lane that co-loads login. Neither grades prose.

## Decision needed

no

title: core-images-and-rest: an explicit :select-ns image frame cannot resolve routing, managed-HTTP or resources handlers (nil-provenance, not standards) - :rf.route/navigate fails :rf.error/no-such-handler with no workaround
description:
## Defect

A frame built from an EXPLICIT `:select-ns` image cannot resolve any handler that a feature artefact registers for itself, apart from those registered as framework standards. The unresolvable handlers are:

- **routing:** `:rf.route/navigate`, `:rf.route/url-requested`, the `:rf.route/entry-denied` default, and `:rf/route`
- **http:** `:rf.http/managed` / `:rf.http/managed-abort`
- **resources:** `:rf/resource` and the `:rf.resource/*` subs, and `:rf/mutation`

The mechanism:
- Those registrations go through the fn-alias registration path (`rf.events/reg-event`, `rf.fx/reg-fx`, `rf.subs/reg-*`), which captures no provenance, so the source store records them under nil provenance.
- An explicit image selects only by provenance namespace, so no `:include` glob can ever match them.
- They are not framework standards either, so the standard union does not supply them.

The one feature that got this right is machines. `install-machine-runtime!` dual-registers its reserved fx and subs into BOTH the registrar and `register-standard!`. Its own comment states the rule the other artefacts miss: "Reserved machine effects and subscriptions must resolve in every image generation. They have no namespace provenance, so image selection cannot discover them; the framework-standard union is their generation path."

The user has NO workaround:
- They cannot stamp `:ns` on the framework's registrations; the rf2-nrc93 remedy applies to their own.
- They cannot glob-select nil provenance.
- They cannot inline the framework's handlers, which are not public values.

So routing, managed HTTP and resources are unusable in any explicit-image frame. The frame fails at the first dispatch with `:rf.error/no-such-handler`. ```clojure

For an explicit :images composition, assembly layers an implicit FRAMEWORK BASE beneath the app images: every source-store descriptor with NIL provenance whose id sits under the reserved :rf root (:rf/* and :rf.<x>/*), plus the one public framework id outside that root (:route/link), minus the protected standards. Hot-zone spec edits are required (spec/002-Frames.md and one clause in spec/Conventions.md), so the mayor must sequence this.

WHY
- The gap is a design hole, not a slip. EP-0023 defined an image as "a collection of your registrations, plus framework standard registrations" and used :rf.nav/push-url and :rf/time-ms as its replaceable-standard examples. EP-0026 then narrowed "standard" to a PROTECTED execution invariant (EP-0026:395-410; spec/002-Frames.md:1055) and removed replaceability, and nothing replaced the path for the rest. Explicit selection only matches :rf.provenance/ns, and every framework feature registers through the fn aliases with no provenance, so no image can select them and no user remedy exists (the :ns stamp of rf2-nrc93 reaches only the user's own registrations). B restores EP-0023's model without reopening EP-0026's protected-standard rule.
- A (per-artefact standards) loses, measured. (1) It silently defeats the stub idiom: with :rf.http/managed dual-registered as a standard, (fx/reg-fx :rf.http/managed stub) in a DEFAULT frame ran the REAL handler (:REAL, no error), because the default image drops the nil-provenance copy of a standard key and unions the load-time standard. That idiom appears in ~80 test files (82 files under implementation/ and tools/ at 5d74c334bb matching (rf\.)?fx/reg-fx\s+:rf\.(http|nav|route|resource|server|ssr)/ outside src/; the dossier counted 76 over a narrower scope). (2) EP-0026 use case 3, an overrides image inlining :rf.http/managed, THREW :rf.error/image-standard-replacement-forbidden. - C (library images the user composes) loses: ~97 :ns stamps, a new public image var per artefact (spec/API.md + both api-manifest sidecars, hot zone), a redesign of framework-default-descriptor? (which recognises the framework copy BY its nil provenance, image_assembly.cljc:568-578), and a "core image" for :rf/time-ms - all boilerplate for plumbing the programmer never authored, and forgetting one image reproduces today's first-dispatch failure.
- D ("features are default-image only") loses: it withdraws isolation for any app loading routing, resources, http or SSR, and because :rf/time-ms is CORE, for any handler taking the canonical durable-time fact at all. title: xstate-parity: spec/Pattern-LongRunningWork.md teaches :after 0 as the yield idiom but registration rejects a zero delay (pinned), and the skill page's explanation of why is stale too
description:
## Gap

XState v6: `after: { 0: 'b' }` is legal and fires at +0 on the simulated clock (`xs/A-14.out`: `after {0: b} -> status active value "a"` then `after 0 fired at +0: b`; `xs-docs/delays.md`).

re-frame2: a zero `:after` key is refused at REGISTRATION — `:rf.error/machine-bad-after-delay` (`jvm/A/A-1.out`: `after-zero`), by `validate-after-delays!` (`implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines/lifecycle_fx/validation.cljc:1272-1300`: "a POSITIVE integer (literal ms), a NON-EMPTY subscription vector, or a function"), pinned by `implementation/machines/test/re_frame/after_delay_validation_test.clj:53` (`zero-delay-key-rejected`). Yet `spec/Pattern-LongRunningWork.md` — the normative pattern page — teaches `:after 0` as THE yield mechanism at lines 27 ("yields to the browser between batches via `:after 0`"), 36, 87 (`{:after {0 :processing} ;; one browser tick, then next chunk` — a code sample that will not register), 100, 167 ("`:always` cycles without `:after 0` between batches …") and 188. The skill page `skills/re-frame2/patterns/long-running-work.md:128` and `:151` already moved to `:after {1 …}` but explains it with the PRE-validation mechanism — "a non-positive `:after` delay never schedules (the runtime emits `:rf.warning/no-clock-configured` and skips), so a zero-delay chunk loop silently stalls" — which is no longer what happens: it fails at `reg-machine`. Both records are wrong in the direction that sends a reader to "fix" the validator. (Trunk `20d5050bdc`.)

## XState evidence

Executed: `xs/A-14.mjs` → `xs/A-14.out` line 1-2. Docs: `xs-docs/delays.md`.

## re-frame2 evidence

Executed: `jvm/A/A-1.clj` → `jvm/A/A-1.out` (`after-zero` → `:rf.error/machine-bad-after-delay`; controls on the lines beside it: `after-fn-key OK`, `after-sub-vector-key OK`). Records: `spec/Pattern-LongRunningWork.md:27,36,87,100,167,188` (`rg -n ':after 0|:after \{0' spec/Pattern-LongRunningWork.md` — 6 lines; control: the same pattern over `spec/005-StateMachines.md` reads 0, and `skills/re-frame2/patterns/long-running-work.md` reads 2, both naming `:after {0 …}` as the thing NOT to write). Code: `validation.cljc:1248` (`valid-after-delay-key?`), `:1272`. Pin: `after_delay_validation_test.clj:53`.

## Why it matters

A reader following the spec's pattern page writes a machine that throws at registration; a reader following the skill believes the runtime silently swallows zero and may argue the validator is a regression. Underneath the record fix there is a small real parity question — XState treats `after: 0` as "next tick after the macrostep" — but the validator's docstring records the choice ("gated at registration rather than degrading to an fx-time no-op") and the skill's `1` is a perfectly good spelling, so the record fix is the whole of what is needed unless the XState reading is wanted.

## Options

1. Record fix only (spec + skill, no runtime): replace `:after 0` with `:after 1` on the six pattern-page lines and rewrite the skill's mechanism sentence to "a zero or negative `:after` key is refused at registration (`:rf.error/machine-bad-after-delay`)". No machine breaks.
2. Accept `0` as "fire on the next timer tick" for XState parity (runtime + `spec/005` §`:after` + flipping the `zero-delay-key-rejected` pin): touches the clock arm in `timer.cljc` and the validator.

## Recommendation

Option 1 — the pin is deliberate and documented, and `1` is the idiom the skill already teaches.

## Fence

`spec/Pattern-LongRunningWork.md` (not hot-zone); `skills/re-frame2/patterns/long-running-work.md`. Option 2 only: `spec/005-StateMachines.md` (HOT ZONE) §Delayed `:after` transitions `:2365-2369`, `implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines/{timer.cljc,lifecycle_fx/validation.cljc}`, `after_delay_validation_test.clj`.

## Gates

Option 1: `scripts/check_doc_slugs.py` (covers `spec/` and `skills/`) and `python -m mkdocs build --strict` (`spec/` is staged into the docs build); neither validates prose, so the six replaced lines are checked by hand and said so in the PR body. Option 2: `clojure -M:test` in `implementation/machines`.

## Decision needed

No for option 1. Say so if the XState next-tick reading (option 2) is wanted instead.

`skills/re-frame2/patterns/long-running-work.md`:128 now gives the mechanism as "a zero or negative `:after` key is refused at registration (`:rf.error/machine-bad-after-delay`)", and :151 says "which registration refuses". title: xstate-parity: the out-of-definition snapshot reset emits :rf.machine/started with :cause :spawned on a SINGLETON (spec/009 fixes :spawned as spawn-fx pre-seeded)
description:
## Gap

When the runtime reconciles an out-of-definition snapshot (spec/005 §Snapshot shape invariant 3 — a hot reload that dropped the occupied state, or a restored snapshot naming a state the definition lacks), it emits the always-on `:rf.error/machine-state-not-in-definition`, rebuilds the snapshot from the definition's initial and runs the initial-entry cascade — and that cascade's `:rf.machine/started` trace carries **`:cause :spawned` on a SINGLETON**. spec/009 defines the `:cause` enum `{:explicit :lazy :spawned}` and fixes `:spawned` as "snapshot pre-seeded `:rf/bootstrap-pending?` by a spawn fx"; the reset path reuses that same marker to make `:entry` fire, so `cause-of` reads the marker and reports a spawn that never happened. Xray's epoch panel renders `:rf.machine/started` as its `[START]` badge, so a reset singleton presents as spawned, and a tool pairing `:rf.machine.spawn/spawned` with `:rf.machine/started :cause :spawned` finds a birth with no spawn. XState has no analogue to compare (its restore of a stale snapshot is a terminal `status error`, C-11); the row is graded against re-frame2's own record.

## XState evidence

- Executed: `xs/C-11.mjs` → `xs/C-11.out`: `restore stale state: no throw; status error value undefined error Persisted snapshot references state 'b' which does not exist on machine 'm'.` — no birth event exists on the XState side to mis-attribute; this gap is about re-frame2's trace record only.

## re-frame2 evidence

- Executed: `jvm/C/c9.clj` → `jvm/C/c9.out` (trunk fe8de195bd), singleton `:c/st` (registered with `reg-machine`, never spawned):
  - B2 (installed stale `:vanished`, then `[:go]`): ops `[:rf.error/machine-state-not-in-definition {:machine-id :c/st, :state :vanished}]` then `[:rf.machine/started {:machine-id :c/st, :state :a, :cause :spawned}]`.
  - D2 (hot re-registration dropping the occupied `:b`, then `[:go]`): same shape, `:cause :spawned` on the same singleton.
  - Controls: the singleton's genuine births in the same run read `:cause :explicit` / `:lazy` (c1.out); a real spawned child's birth reads `:cause :spawned` (c4.out).
- `implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines/lifecycle_fx/registration.cljc:364-406` (`rebuild-incompatible-snapshot` stamps `:rf/bootstrap-pending? true`) and `:519-532` (`cause-of`: "present + `:rf/bootstrap-pending?` → spawn-pre-seeded (`:spawned`)").
- spec/009-Instrumentation.md:222 and :2313 — the `:cause` enum and its three meanings; neither names a reset.
- spec/005 invariants 3/4 (lines 60-63) and "Recovery replaces user state, never actor IDENTITY" (line 65) — the reset is described, its `:rf.machine/started` attribution is not.

## Why it matters

Small and record-level: the error record beside it (`:rf.error/machine-state-not-in-definition` with `:recovery :reset-to-initial`) tells the truth, so nobody is misled about WHAT happened, only about how the machine came to life again. The cost lands on tooling that groups births by cause (Xray's `[START]` badge, lifecycle pairing) and on anyone reading a trace to decide whether a singleton was spawned.

## Options

1. **Add `:reset` to the cause enum (spec/009 + spec/005 §The `:rf.machine/started` trace + `cause-of`).** The reset path stamps a distinct marker (or `rebuild-incompatible-snapshot` passes the cause explicitly) and `:rf.machine/started` reads `:cause :reset` with the triggering error id in tags. Honest and additive; the enum is documented as the tag's closed set, so it is a spec change.
2. **Reuse `:explicit` / `:lazy` per the triggering path** — no enum change, but it hides the reset in a cause that means "first birth", and the singleton's SECOND `:rf.machine/started` in one lifetime then looks like a duplicate birth.
3. Leave it and document that a reset presents as `:spawned` — cheapest, but it makes the `:spawned` meaning in spec/009 false as written.

## Recommendation

Option 1. Tiny code change (`cause-of` already switches on the marker; the reset path is one call site), one enum member in two spec pages.

- test beside `implementation/machines/test/re_frame/machine_started_trace_test.clj` (or wherever `:cause` is pinned — grep `:rf.machine.start/cause` under `implementation/machines/test`)

## Gates

- `clojure -M:test` in `implementation/machines`; `npm run test:cljs` if a CLJS-only test pins the cause enum; `spec/conformance` corpus if a fixture pins the started trace's tags.

## Decision needed

No.

title: FALSE: parent destroy can reap an unrelated replacement through a stale spawn-all slot
description:
PR #10384 (4f543982971f6a061d65bff35eddfd7d7371ed96) promises to destroy tracked children while leaving a same-id replacement unowned by the parent alive. Its new reap-tracked-children! dispatches join maps to destroy-spawn-all-children!; that helper iterates the old :children addresses without confirming that the CURRENT occupant still belongs to this exact join. prepare-join-child-teardown! authenticates membership only to classify/cancel it: an unauthenticated occupant still returns {:reason :explicit}, and destroy-single-actor! then kills it. The single-:spawn branch does have slot-owned-incarnation?, so the new single-child replacement control misses this join case.
Public reproduction on the exact merge: start :audit/parent with a :spawn-all join containing :audit/kid, creating :audit/kid#1. Hand-spawn the same type with :fixed-actor-id :audit/kid#1, replacing the original child. The live replacement has no :rf/join-child or :rf/parent-id and accepts a ping setting :marker :replacement; the old join still names that address. Destroy the parent. The replacement disappears and a false owned-child :rf.machine/destroyed trace attributes it to the old parent/invoke. A normal still-owned join child is correctly reaped as the control.
Evidence: ai/probe-join-replacement-audit-sep23-monitor-1.log and .exit, correct worker gate root, exit 0 asserting the defect witness and healthy control. Existing implementation test results were accepted; only this concrete concern was probed.
Required correction: authenticate each join slot's current occupant against the exact parent, invoke path, logical child and attempt before teardown, reusing the existing membership data. Prune stale bookkeeping while preserving a replacement. Apply at the shared join teardown so parent destruction and normal join exit agree. No new public actor address or lifecycle API.
acceptance_criteria: Add a bounded public-sequence regression: join child is replaced by an untracked actor at its address, parent is destroyed, replacement remains live and untouched with no destroyed trace, and stale join bookkeeping is cleared. A still-owned join child must still be destroyed exactly once. Preserve the existing join cancellation/terminal semantics and single-spawn replacement control.
notes:

title: FALSE: caught SSR boot failures preserve the original stack in operator diagnostics
description:
Merged-PR audit #10374 at 1542717d09be48d682b3b9b46eabb2bb02c823ff, correctness/diagnosability. Revised worker.cjs:111-117 says a caught module-load/boot exception retains its real stack through the parent worker error handler, and isolate.cjs:192-198 repeats that claim. But boot() catches the exception, posts only {t: boot-error, code, message}, and returns. Caught exceptions emit no worker error event. The parent message receiver at isolate.cjs:153-156 terminates the worker and constructs a new Refusal with only modulePath; the application's original stack is lost. This also deprives replacement-boot diagnostics of the application call site, even though they log the reconstructed refusal.

Focused Node witness at the exact merge, using the existing flaky-boot.cjs fixture, compared a healthy ready control with an armed module-load failure. Observed: failed=boot-error, error events=0, stderr bytes=0, no stack in the message, and the original error-message sentinel present. The probe printed the correct worktree root and exited 0 after asserting this defect witness. Evidence: ai/probe-boot-stack-audit-sep23-monitor-1.log and .exit. No full suite rerun or new fixture/script was needed.

Preserve the original caught boot exception on an operator-owned diagnostic path (for example the existing sidecar stderr convention), then make the two comments describe that actual path. Keep public render/replacement refusals sanitized; this is not a request to expose an application stack to HTTP callers or to add a logging framework.
acceptance_criteria: An existing fixture that throws during module evaluation or boot leaves the original application stack/call-site in the operator diagnostic channel. A healthy boot remains clean. A focused regression distinguishes the original stack from a newly constructed Refusal stack and verifies replacement/public response sanitization remains intact. worker.cjs and isolate.cjs comments describe the actual caught-boot path, without claiming it reaches worker.on(error).

Eventless :always passes nil for the event, also confirmed by the implementer's accepted producer-derived control. A consumer built from the 009 row can look up a nonexistent machine-id or discard exceptional rows. The implementer accurately reported this outside the action-ran-only fence; this new open finding tracks the necessary follow-up.

Required correction: align the guard-evaluated rows in 005 and 009 with the producer and corrected schema, including actor identity, frame, state, thrown outcome/exception and the nil event. title: docs/api re-frame.resources: :gc-after-ms is timed from load settle, not from last-owner release
description:
From GitHub issue #10491 (closed into this bead). Original text:

**Type:** bug (reference docs) · **Priority:** P3 · **Size:** small, one sentence

## Gap

`docs/api/re-frame.resources.md` line 55 (at `92c6b29960`) says:

> An owned entry is kept …; once its last owner is released, it is garbage-collected after `:gc-after-ms`.

That reads as "the clock starts at release". The spec and implementation agree on something different:
- `spec/016-Resources.md` §Stale and GC scheduling (~line 1238): "a GC timer arms on every load settle". At ~line 1228: "a fire while the entry is still owned or in flight re-arms it instead of collecting, a later owner release does not restart an armed timer".
- `implementation/resources/src/re_frame/resources/timers.cljc` line 88: `gc-kind` "arms `:gc-after-ms` after `:loaded-at`". `cancel-for-key!` notes: "Last-owner release does not use it — the entry stays alive and keeps its GC reaper".

So a released entry is removed when its already-armed GC timer next fires. That is at most `:gc-after-ms` after the release, and possibly sooner. It is not exactly `:gc-after-ms` after the release.

## What to do

1. Confirm the delay used when a GC fire finds the entry still owned and re-arms. Read the `gc-fired` handler in `events.cljc` (~line 3500) and the re-arm path in `timers.cljc`. It is probably `:gc-after-ms` from the fire.
2. Reword line 55 to match, for example: "once its last owner is released, it is removed the next time its GC timer fires, which is at most `:gc-after-ms` later."
3. Check the `:gc-after-ms` bullet at line ~116 ("how long an entry with no owner is kept") for the same implication, and adjust it if needed.

The tutorial and the TanStack comparison in `docs/resources` already describe this correctly ("armed when the entry settles"), so after this fix the two pages will agree.

## Acceptance

- The API page states the timing that `spec/016` and `timers.cljc` describe.
- The doc gates (`check_doc_slugs.py`, `mkdocs build --strict`) exit 0.

## Context

Found during the `docs/resources` correctness pass (day8/re-frame2#10480), and left out of it because the file is outside `docs/resources`.
notes:
== FIXED (worker/apirev12-elnoo, PR #10549, commit f1383e553f, 2026-09-26 20:3x AUSEST)
Re-arm delay confirmed: events.cljc gc-fired-handler removes the entry only when it has no active owner and no :current-work; on a :has-owner or :in-flight skip it computes gc-delay from the resource's own :gc-after-ms (rf.resources.state/positive-or-nil over resource-meta) and emits :rf.resource/schedule-timers with :timers {:gc gc-delay}, a partial cancel-then-arm of the GC timer only. So the re-arm is :gc-after-ms from the fire. The timer is armed on each load settle (timers.cljc gc-kind "arms :gc-after-ms after :loaded-at") and on a fresh-skip that revives an owner-free entry; last-owner release arms nothing.
docs/api/re-frame.resources.md changed in both places: the owner bullet now says a released entry is garbage-collected the next time its GC check runs, at most :gc-after-ms later, because the timer arms when a load settles, not at the release; the :gc-after-ms key now reads as the interval of the GC check that removes an entry with no owner and no load in flight, armed at load settle and re-armed while the entry is still owned or loading, so an idle entry goes at most that long after its last owner is released, and possibly sooner.
Gates: check_doc_slugs.py exit 0; mkdocs build --strict exit 0; line endings cr=crlf, bare_lf=0.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #10549 (merged, trunk a55df1a1e3; CI 88/88). Confirmed at source: the GC timer arms when a load settles, not at last-owner release, and a fire that finds the entry still owned or in flight re-arms :gc-after-ms from that fire. Both :gc-after-ms lines in docs/api/re-frame.resources.md are reworded to match: a released entry is removed when its already-armed timer next fires, at most :gc-after-ms later.

title: docs/machines review in four serial steps: completeness, correctness, quality, holistic structure
description:
Mike asked (2026-09-26) for a review of docs/machines/ (13 pages), in FOUR SERIAL steps. Each step reviews the tree the previous step left. It produces a read-only report, which is triaged, and then its accepted findings are applied as one commit. Step N+1 starts only on the tree step N produced.

1. COMPLETENESS: compare what is taught with the full API.
   - Are the happy path AND the unhappy paths discussed?
   - Are errors explained: which error ids a reader can meet, what each means, and how to recover?
   - Are values fully enumerated, each with the explanation it needs (option keys, states, statuses, enum values)?
   - Are the likely use cases covered?
   The source of truth for "the full API" is the implementation and spec/api-manifest.edn; the spec comes second.
2. CORRECTNESS: check every factual claim and every code sample against the implementation (then the spec). Evaluate samples where the code is portable. A spec or implementation defect found along the way is filed as its own bead, not fixed here.
3. QUALITY: review for a human senior developer, against docs/AUTHORING.md.
   - Do the docs make a good tutorial, with progressive disclosure?
   - Are they cohesive and consistent?
   - Are they human-friendly?
   - Do they use good, simple examples that build progressively?
4. HOLISTIC QUALITY: repeat step 3, taking a view of the folder as a whole.
   - Is the current set of pages the right way to teach this?
   - Do they have the right structure? Should the tutorial structure be improved?
   - Should new pages be created, content be moved between pages, or pages be removed?
   Step 4's report states each structural proposal with its reasons. The mayor rules on them under the stance before any page is created, moved, split or removed. Keep or update every inbound anchor, and grep the repo for links into a page before moving or removing it.

How it runs: one worktree and one worker per step (or one worker running the steps in order), with one PR per step, or one PR for the whole bead if the steps are small. Every step names the gates that actually cover what it changed. Per CLAUDE.md § Build & Test, check_doc_slugs.py, mkdocs build --strict and the fenced-block and zero-link caveats all apply. The worker verifies anchors and table column counts by hand and says so. Prose follows AUTHORING.md and the present-tense rule.

title: spec(016)/EP-0016: a default retry policy in the managed-HTTP interceptor seam is specified but cannot work
description:
From GitHub issue #10541 (closed into this bead). Original text:

**Type:** spec/implementation disagreement · **Priority:** P3 · **Needs a ruling:** correct the spec, or implement a frame-level HTTP defaults slot

## Gap
`spec/016-Resources.md` (~L1155–1160, "managed-HTTP interceptor/defaults seam … default retry policy") and EP-0016 Rider 3 describe setting a default retry policy through the managed-HTTP interceptor seam.

That cannot work. In `implementation/http/src/re_frame/http/handlers.cljc`, after the interceptor chain runs, only `(:request ctx)` is carried forward:

```clojure
args-map' (assoc args-map :request (:request ctx))   ; ~L434
```

So a `:retry` set in an interceptor's `:before` is silently dropped. Retry works only per request: it is returned from the request fn, and it passes through the resources transport (`implementation/resources/src/re_frame/resources/transport/http.cljc:118-119`).

The `re-frame2` skill told agents to put default retry in the interceptor seam. That is corrected in day8/re-frame2#10534, but the spec still says it.

## Options
- **A (smaller):** correct spec 016 and EP-0016 to say that interceptors decorate `:request` only, and that retry is per request.
- **B:** implement a frame-level HTTP defaults slot that includes `:retry`, with tests. The spec then describes that slot.

## Acceptance
The spec and the implementation agree on where a default retry policy can live, and no guide or skill promises a seam that drops the key.

MAYOR RULING (2026-09-26): OPTION A. Correct spec/016-Resources.md (~L1155-1160) and EP-0016 Rider 3 so that managed-HTTP interceptors decorate :request only, and a retry policy is per request: returned from the request fn, and carried through the resources transport. Do not build a frame-level HTTP defaults slot. Nothing needs it today, and the per-request route works. Re-check at tip that no guide or skill still promises the interceptor seam for :retry.
notes:
== FENCE (mayor, 2026-09-27)
HELD — SEQUENCED BEHIND worker/ssrfix-ysb2m (rf2-ysb2m item 8: it edits one sentence of spec/016 §Freshness clock contract, stating the domain of :stale-after-ms). Dispatch once that PR MERGES.
HELD — SEQUENCED BEHIND worker/ssrfix-ysb2m: DISCHARGED — PR #10565 merged at trunk 072b57fd62 on 2026-09-27.
== WORKER (worker/specres-9ktox, PR #10571), 2026-09-27: fixed per option A, prose only
The premise holds at tip: re-frame.http.handlers carries only (:request ctx) forward after the interceptor chain (args-map' assoc :request), and the resources transport passes the request fn's top-level :retry through unchanged (build-managed-args).
Corrected:
- spec/016 §Request decoration: interceptors decorate the nested :request only; retry is a top-level :retry the request fn returns; reads retry, and writes retry only when their own request declares it.
- spec/API.md request-decoration note: it said "Auth/tracing/base-URL/retry decoration"; the retry part is removed.
- EP-0016 Rider 3, plus the finding-4 doctrine sentence and three plan/acceptance lines that repeated the promise.
Re-check at tip, using a sentence-scoped scan of docs/** and skills/** for retry near interceptor or decoration seam: no guide or skill promises the seam for :retry. skills/re-frame2/patterns/resources.md already says retry is per request; its section heading still reads "Request decoration — auth headers, retry (the managed-HTTP seam)", and the body corrects it. The heading anchor is cited from two other skill files, so it was left alone. The realworld_resources example already returns rh/data-fetch-retry from each read's request fn.

title: :rf.error/http-interceptor-bad-return is unobservable: re-wrapped as http-interceptor-failed (middleware.cljc run-chain*)
description:
:rf.error/http-interceptor-bad-return (spec/009-Instrumentation.md ~:2328) is unobservable. The bad-return throw sits inside run-chain*'s try, and is re-wrapped as :rf.error/http-interceptor-failed, so the bad-return id never reaches a trace. It only appears inside the failed error's :cause. Code: implementation/http/src/re_frame/http/middleware.cljc:360-417.

Measured by the docs/async correctness review (rf2-s0i3z step 2) at trunk f89e28ec64: a :before returning nil surfaced only as :rf.error/http-interceptor-failed, with the bad return named in :cause.

Decide one of two fixes. Either the code lets bad-return escape the wrapper as its own trace id, or spec 009 describes it as the :cause of http-interceptor-failed. docs/async now names the observable id.
notes:
== MAYOR RULING (2026-09-26): option 1, code-side
The spec is the artefact, and spec/009 catalogues :rf.error/http-interceptor-bad-return as its own id. A bad return is a programmer error distinct from an interceptor THROWING, and a precise id is the better diagnostic. So the bad-return check must sit where run-chain*'s try does not re-wrap it (middleware.cljc:360-417): the id reaches the trace as itself, and :rf.error/http-interceptor-failed stays for genuine throws. Add a regression both ways:
- a :before returning nil emits bad-return and NOT failed;
- a :before that throws still emits failed.
spec/009 stands as written. Follow-on: docs/async currently names the observable id as http-interceptor-failed. That page belongs to rf2-s0i3z (session re-frame2-f8), so it is routed there to update once this PR merges. The worker must NOT edit docs/async. Dispatched in the http cluster with rf2-k3v1o and rf2-ntuvc.

== WORKER VERDICT (httpfix-k3v1o, PR #10522, 2026-09-26): FIXED per ruling option 1
Reproduced at trunk c7d1190398: a :before returning nil raised :rf.error/http-interceptor-failed and the trace stream carried only that id.
Fix: in re-frame.http.middleware/run-chain* the map? check now sits OUTSIDE the slot fn's try. A non-map return builds :rf.error/http-interceptor-bad-return (ex-data :id, :returned), emits it via emit-error! through privacy/prepare-emit-failure under the same effective sensitivity (dev-gated like failed), and throws it. :rf.error/http-interceptor-failed stays for genuine throws. The fix applies to :before and :after alike (shared walker); on the response side the reply-tail fence now reports :reply-error-id :rf.error/http-interceptor-bad-return.
Regressions (http_interceptors_test.clj): before-returning-nil-emits-bad-return-not-failed (5 assertions, all red at trunk and red with the fix planted out) and before-that-throws-still-emits-failed (green both ways). docs/api/re-frame.http.md gained a bad-return trace-table row plus one sentence under reg-http-interceptor. spec/009 untouched.
FOLLOW-ON for rf2-s0i3z's docs/async owner: docs/async/http-going-further.md:64 still says a non-map return fails with :rf.error/http-interceptor-failed; after PR #10522 merges it fires :rf.error/http-interceptor-bad-return carrying :id and :returned.
Forward pointer from PR #10522 audit: new OPEN bead rf2-sdeze confirms a sensitive bad-return diagnostic carries the interceptor value and textual echo raw in trace tags on current main. See its JVM reproduction. Original status/content preserved.

title: docs/core review in four serial steps: completeness, correctness, quality, holistic structure
description:
Mike asked (2026-09-26) for a review of docs/core/ (64 pages), in FOUR SERIAL steps. Each step reviews the tree the previous step left. It produces a read-only report, which is triaged, and then its accepted findings are applied as one commit. Step N+1 starts only on the tree step N produced.

1. COMPLETENESS: compare what is taught with the full API.
   - Are the happy path AND the unhappy paths discussed?
   - Are errors explained: which error ids a reader can meet, what each means, and how to recover?
   - Are values fully enumerated, each with the explanation it needs (option keys, states, statuses, enum values)?
   - Are the likely use cases covered?
   The source of truth for "the full API" is the implementation and spec/api-manifest.edn; the spec comes second.
2. CORRECTNESS: check every factual claim and every code sample against the implementation (then the spec). Evaluate samples where the code is portable. A spec or implementation defect found along the way is filed as its own bead, not fixed here.
3. QUALITY: review for a human senior developer, against docs/AUTHORING.md.
   - Do the docs make a good tutorial, with progressive disclosure?
   - Are they cohesive and consistent?
   - Are they human-friendly?
   - Do they use good, simple examples that build progressively?
4. HOLISTIC QUALITY: repeat step 3, taking a view of the folder as a whole.
   - Is the current set of pages the right way to teach this?
   - Do they have the right structure? Should the tutorial structure be improved?
   - Should new pages be created, content be moved between pages, or pages be removed?
   Step 4's report states each structural proposal with its reasons. The mayor rules on them under the stance before any page is created, moved, split or removed. Keep or update every inbound anchor, and grep the repo for links into a page before moving or removing it.

How it runs: one worktree and one worker per step (or one worker running the steps in order), with one PR per step, or one PR for the whole bead if the steps are small. Every step names the gates that actually cover what it changed. Per CLAUDE.md § Build & Test, check_doc_slugs.py, mkdocs build --strict and the fenced-block and zero-link caveats all apply. The worker verifies anchors and table column counts by hand and says so. Prose follows AUTHORING.md and the present-tense rule.

Scope: The core guide, the largest folder: tutorial, how-tos, concepts, Fresco, glossary.

SEQUENCING: the docs/core single-reader pass (rf2-csxab, PR #10478, merged) already weighed page splits (see rf2-yo6fq's close reason: no split). Step 4 may revisit that, with reasons. Open items touching docs/core: rf2-x7uj7 items 6+ (observability.md, subscriptions.md and others) and rf2-8n7ke (fresco/api-reference.md). Fold them into step 2 or land them first. Given the size, the steps may be split by sub-area (tutorial / how-to / concepts / fresco), with each sub-area running its steps in order.

- a fn, a Thread or a float (1.5) in MUTATION params raises :rf.error/resource-non-edn-params, with the mutation id in :resource-id, :kind :params — not :rf.error/mutation-invalid-params;
- the payload lint warned on #inst at path [1 :at], ignored a java.time.Instant (it was never in host-handle?), and warned on a Thread;
- re-frame.reply/walk-find-host-handle refuses #inst.

FLOATS: the rejection is DELIBERATE, not accidental, so float behaviour is unchanged. Conventions §Canonical EDN identity makes CEDN-1 "MUST reject by default ... floating-point values, ratios, arbitrary-precision decimals, NaN, and infinities". re-frame.identity/bad-number? admits only safe-range integers, and spec/016 §Resource identity calls it "Conventions' deliberate fail-closed stance". The reason stated in spec/009: the hosts disagree about floats (2.0 is a double on the JVM and the integer 2 on CLJS, and NaN is not equal to itself), so a float has no single identity.

MAYOR GRANT, 2026-09-26, mid-task: spec/Conventions.md §Event payloads SHOULD be serialisable data, the two sentences only, plus spec/009's :rf.warning/non-serialisable-event-payload row. The lint only changes; host-handle? stays.

The instance-id scalar list reads keyword / string / safe-range integer / UUID / instant, where it used to say "number" although a float is refused. No test asserts either text; tests branch on :rf.error/id.
(4) core's lint: re-frame.router.diagnostics/payload-host-handle? is (and (rf.reply/host-handle? v) (not (inst? v))), and walk-find-host-handle-bounded takes the predicate as an optional third argument (its only caller is the lint). host-handle? is UNCHANGED; its docstring now gives the reply-side reason for Date (EP-0010 epoch-ms durable timestamps) instead of the false "does not round-trip through the EDN reader". The warning's :reason and the router.cljc comment drop Date. The lint spec row and both Conventions sentences state the split, one reason each.

- fires-on-host-object-payload-beside-an-instant: {:at <inst> :pattern #"x"} fires exactly one warning, at path [1 :pattern].

Line endings cr=crlf, bare_lf=0.

title: Spec 011: reconcile the :rf/hydrate re-registration paragraph with the locked replace-frame-state decision
description:
spec/011-SSR.md disagrees with itself about client-only state across hydration. Measured at trunk 954e86a4fe.

- Section "The :rf/hydrate event" says: "If the user wants client-only transient state to survive hydration: the customisation point is re-registering :rf/hydrate with a custom handler that performs an explicit merge in the user's intended order." The server-hash paragraph just above it also expects implementations that override the reference handler with their own merge policy.
- Resolved decisions, "`:replace-frame-state` is the locked hydration merge policy", says a merge policy is rejected and "Apps that want client-only seeded state run it after the hydration event, not before". The data-classification passage near the top of the spec teaches the same thing: re-seed after hydration.

The SSR guide (docs/ssr/concepts.md "Why replace, not merge" and tutorial Step 4) followed the re-registration sentence. rf2-04uim removed that advice and now teaches seeding after hydrate! returns, so the guide matches the resolved decision. The spec still carries both readings.

Decide one of these:
(a) delete the re-registration paragraph and reword the server-hash override clause, or
(b) keep re-registration as an at-your-own-risk escape hatch and name what a replacement handler must preserve. Reading re_frame/ssr/hydrate.cljc, that list is: the fail-closed malformed-payload and frame-id-mismatch guards, the runtime-db install (:rf.db/runtime is framework-authority), the [:rf.runtime/ssr :hydration] metadata, the compatibility-check fx, and the resources and machines rearm hooks.

hydrate! has no after-hydration hook option (its opts are frame, payload, render-tree-fn, element-id, manifest, container and root-id), so (a) needs no new API.
notes:
== MAYOR RULING (2026-10-01 23:45 AUSEST): option (a) ==
Not an operator call: Spec 011's own Resolved decisions entry already locks :replace-frame-state and says apps seed client-only state AFTER the hydration event, and the stance rejects an at-your-own-risk escape hatch that would need a maintained preservation list (option b). So: delete the re-registration paragraph in "The :rf/hydrate event" and reword the server-hash clause so it no longer expects implementations to override the reference handler with their own merge policy. No new API (hydrate! has no after-hydration hook and none is wanted). Prose only; spec/011-SSR.md is not a CLAUDE.md hot-zone file, but it is the one i/crlf file (CLAUDE.md instrument (u)), so edit with Write/Edit or Python bytes, never sed -i.
== WORKER RESULT (2026-10-01 23:59 AUSEST): option (a) applied, PR #10682 (draft until gates done) ==
Commit 6edbf6335b on worker/docs-misc-ryi2z-dtjjw, based on 27c39601ab.
- spec/011-SSR.md "The :rf/hydrate event": deleted the paragraph that offered re-registering :rf/hydrate with a custom merge handler.
- The server-hash clause is restated as what verify-hydration! reads. It reads the [:rf.runtime/ssr :hydration :server-hash] slot unless a :server-hash opt supplies the value, and with neither it silently no-ops. No mention of an override remains.
- A search of the whole of spec/011-SSR.md for re-regist / overrid / custom handler / own merge / merge policy / reference handler found no other sentence assuming a user-replaced :rf/hydrate. Lines 109, 744 and 1836 already teach seeding after hydration, or the locked policy.
- Scope beyond the brief: spec/Runtime-Subsystems.md:149, the :rf.runtime/ssr "3 Read API" row, carried the same rule ("Apps that override the reference :rf/hydrate handler MUST preserve the :server-hash write ..."). It is reworded to "verify-hydration! also accepts the value directly as a :server-hash opt." That file is not a hot-zone file. The column count is unchanged, and check_runtime_subsystem_grading.py exits 0.
- Not changed: the verify-hydration! docstring (implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/hydrate.cljc:616-620) gives "fixture-overridden handlers" as the opt's use case. A test fixture stubbing a handler is legitimate, so nothing there contradicts the ruling.
- Line endings: spec/011-SSR.md (i/crlf) has 1924 CR, 1924 CRLF and 0 bare LF after the edit. It was edited with the Edit tool only.

title: epoch: no test tells a :halted-destroy record's :db-after from its :db-before
description:
Owner: rf2-98kzs.14 (found while pruning implementation/epoch/test; not fixed there).

No epoch test can tell a `:halted-destroy` record's destroy-time `:db-after` apart from its pre-cascade `:db-before`.

`re-frame.epoch-test/live-halted-destroy-fires-partial-record-with-real-snapshots` uses a handler that destroys its own frame before committing any db write. Its own comment notes that destroy-time db therefore equals pre-cascade db, and the test asserts `{:n 7 :live true}` for both. The sibling `live-halted-destroy-db-before-reflects-committed-cascade-writes` has a nearby comment that promises non-equal snapshots, but its two values are equal too. A regression that copied `:db-before` into `:db-after` would pass both of these tests and the privacy rollup tests. A search of the epoch and core test trees for `halted-destroy` found no other `:db-after` witness.

Fix shape: commit an app-db change earlier in the same drain (for example, a parent event that writes, then a queued child that destroys the frame), and assert `:db-after` differs from `:db-before` and equals the destroy-time value.
notes:
== FENCE (mayor, 2026-10-02 00:44 AUSEST): dispatch only after PR #10687 (rf2-98kzs.14) MERGES == That open PR prunes implementation/epoch/test and scripts/test-epoch-prod-gate.sh, the surface this bead edits. Clears when #10687 is merged into main.

live-halted-destroy-db-before-reflects-committed-cascade-writes reworked: the child now returns {:db (assoc db :phase :child-wrote) :fx [[:destroy-main]]} and a test fx destroys the frame, so the child's :db commit lands before the destroy. :db-before = {:phase :parent-done :marker 42} (unchanged), :db-after = {:phase :child-wrote :marker 42}, plus an explicit (not= :db-before :db-after). +1 assertion. The bead's suggested shape (parent writes, child destroys from its handler) alone keeps the two equal, because the child's pre-cascade snapshot is already post-parent; the divergence needs a write committed inside the destroying event, which an fx-side destroy gives.
CONTROL: plant = listeners.cljc snapshot-terminal-destroy-evidence! passes fs-before in the fs-after slot (:db-after copied from :db-before). Both old halted-destroy tests under the plant: GREEN (exit 0, the bead's premise confirmed). New test under the plant: RED on the :db-after equality and the not=, exit 1. title: Coverage gap: story-mcp's cap accounting of :structuredContent is never asserted (story-mcp)
description:
Found by rf2-3h7v2.13 (owner), not fixed there: a pruning PR adds no tests.

`re-frame.story-mcp.tools.wire-pipeline/result-io` sums `:content[*].text` AND the `pr-edn` of `:structuredContent` under one token budget, because `text-result` writes the same payload into both slots and counting only the text would underestimate the wire by about half. No story-mcp test can see that second term.

The test that named it, `cap-counts-structured-content-size` (removed in rf2-3h7v2.13's PR), compared two TEST-side `ResultIO` reifies against each other, so its verdict never depended on production code. `cap-trips-on-structured-content-alone` (also removed) used a 1-token cap, which the text slot alone already exceeds.

Measured at the rf2-3h7v2.13 branch: replacing the structuredContent term of `result-io`'s `wire-payload-strings` with `(conj "")` left the whole story-mcp JVM lane green at head (267 tests / 1663 assertions, 0 failures, exit 0), and left `re-frame.story-mcp.tools-test` green with the base `tools_test.clj` restored for the run (235 / 1367, 0 failures, exit 0). mcp-base's `structured-content-counted-toward-budget` pins the same rule for mcp-base's own reify, not story-mcp's.

A test that fails on that plant needs a response whose text slot fits a cap that the text plus the structured slot exceeds.
notes:
== RESULT (worker, 2026-10-02 02:15:41 AUSEST): PR #10701 (draft), head 0edfeea888 ==
Witness added: tools_test.clj `cap-counts-the-structured-slot-beside-the-text`, through production `invoke-tool` (so the real wire-pipeline `result-io`). It sizes list-tags' two slots at `:max-tokens 0`, then caps at the text slot's token estimate: production trips the overflow marker and reports `:token-count` = text tokens + structured tokens. A control row with a cap both slots fit stays intact.
Control: the bead's plant (structured term of `wire-payload-strings` -> `(conj "")`) turned the test red with 2 failures (overflow + token-count), the control row green, tools-test alone exit 1. Restore verified by blob hash against the committed object.
Counts (whole JVM lane, tests/assertions): 265/1657 -> 268/1688 for the whole cluster; this bead's share is +1/+5.

title: api-manifest: no test drives build-manifest with a :cljs-only row colliding with a JVM-derived row
description:
Owner: rf2-98kzs.21 (api-manifest suite pruning), which found this gap and did not fix it, because adding tests is outside a pruning PR.

THE GAP. `re-frame.api-manifest.gen/build-manifest` refuses a duplicate `[namespace var]` by calling `duplicate-rows` on the CONCATENATED rows (JVM-derived rows plus the verbatim `:cljs-only` sidecar rows). The gen ns docstring, `duplicate-rows`' docstring and the throw's own message each name two hazards: a duplicated `:cljs-only` entry, and a `:cljs-only` row colliding with a JVM-derived row. Only the first is driven through `build-manifest`. `gen_test/build-manifest-throws-on-duplicate` and `build-manifest-duplicate-ex-data-lists-the-key` both duplicate a `:cljs-only` row against another `:cljs-only` row.

THE FAULT NOTHING CATCHES.
