title: re-frame2-pair: reconcile the running MCP server's tools with the loaded skill revision before diagnosing (gh-10787)
description:
GitHub issue #10787: https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/issues/10787 (opened 2026-10-03T05:47:32Z under mike-thompson-day8). The body below is the issue's, verbatim. Mike's standing rule (2026-10-03): the worker that does this bead also closes issue #10787 as its last act, with a comment naming the PR.

---

## Problem

The Pair skill's source/document drift gate can pass while the configured, long-lived MCP process still runs an older compiled artifact. The skill does not explicitly reconcile that process's capabilities with the revision of the instructions it is about to apply.

This can send an agent to tools absent from its real session, or lead it to interpret the older view-evidence model using the new Fresco boundary semantics.

## Verified evidence

At source revision 412f86be3d07009cc45927ed495673f454b37f23:

- [The skill](https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/blob/412f86be3d07009cc45927ed495673f454b37f23/skills/re-frame2-pair/SKILL.md) and [source registry](https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/blob/412f86be3d07009cc45927ed495673f454b37f23/tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/src/re_frame2_pair_mcp/tools/registry.cljs) describe 30 tools, including read-mounted-boundaries, read-read-attribution and replay-epoch.
- The actual tools advertised to the inspected session number 35. Those three source tools are absent. Eight older tools are present: get-stream-controls, list-streams, read-mounted-views, read-view-dependencies, read-view-event-sites, read-view-manifest, subscribe and unsubscribe.
- Calling the actual get-re-frame2-pair-instructions tool succeeds and returns the older read-mounted-views onboarding text; it does not mention read-mounted-boundaries. This corroborates the host catalog rather than relying on artifact timestamps.
- [Current server source](https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/blob/412f86be3d07009cc45927ed495673f454b37f23/tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/src/re_frame2_pair_mcp/server.cljs#L75) and the older generated server module both identify version 0.1.0. That value does not distinguish these contracts.

No browser runtime was connected, read or modified. Current evidence files matched their committed Git blobs.

## Proposed improvement

Before the live discover/orient sequence, reconcile the required tool names and schemas for the loaded skill with the host's actual tools/list descriptors. Surface a clear capability/version mismatch with a scoped rebuild/restart/reconnect recipe. Do not alias an older view tool into a Fresco boundary tool: their evidence contracts differ.

Expose an identifiable build revision or descriptor fingerprint through initialization metadata or the existing stateless onboarding surface, so an agent can distinguish installed binary, checked-out source, loaded skill and browser preload.

Keep the current source/document drift gate. Add coverage for a stale configured server paired with current instructions, since rebuilding source in CI does not refresh an already-running MCP process.

Acceptance: the stale/current pairing is detected before missing tools are treated as an application diagnosis, while a matching supported pairing still proceeds normally.

Related closed #10544 concerns source-manifest argument drift, not a configured running artifact. Open and closed searches for Pair binary/version/stale/capability and tools/list found no duplicate.
close_reason: Done in PR #10793 (GitHub issue #10787). get-re-frame2-pair-instructions now returns :tool-contract, which is registry/tool-contract: the tool count, a dash, then the first 8 hex of a sha256 over every tool name with its inputSchema argument keys, sorted. The current value is 30-c1c787a3. SKILL.md section "Connect first" now opens with a one-time check before discover-app. If the value is absent or different, the server is stale: rebuild it and start a fresh session, never treat a missing tool as an app finding, and never swap in an older view tool. tool_contract_test checks the skill's stated value against the registry's through the real pre-connection path. It also checks that the issue's measured 35-tool stale catalogue and the current catalogue with one argument key dropped both read as a different contract. Local :server-test exit 0: 799 tests, 3578 assertions, against a main CI baseline of 797 and 3573. Red with the fingerprint dropped (1 failure), with it collapsed to 0.1.0 (3 failures), and with the skill's stated value removed (1 failure). Every restore matched the committed blob hash. The drift gate check_skill_mcp_drift.py is unchanged. The brief's premise of an npm lockfile did not hold, so CI's npm install was used.

title: Live in-memory routing examples in docs/routing/
description:
## This section

`docs/routing/` teaches `reg-route`, navigation and route subs with static code only. Routing is in the engine now.

**Hard constraint:** a cell must never create a `:url-bound? true` frame, because it would take over the docs site's address bar. A frame without `:url-bound?` routes in memory (see `tutorial.md` around line 239). So the live examples are in-memory:
- register routes;
- dispatch a navigation;
- render the matched route from the `:rf.route/*` subs (`:rf.route/id`, `:rf.route/params`, `:rf.route/transition`).

Most pages teach a url-bound app. Where the URL itself is the point, keep the code static. Add a cell where the matching, params, guards or transitions are the point.

Pages:
- `concepts.md`: route table and matching; params; a view switching on `:rf.route/id`.
- `tutorial.md`: steps that are about matching and navigation, as in-memory cells. Say in the prose that the cell routes in memory, and keep the url-bound boot static.
- `how-to/guard-unsaved-changes`, `require-sign-in-on-a-route`, `redirect-an-old-url`: guards and redirects run in memory.
- `how-to/load-page-data`: a route with `:resources` over the HTTP stub.
- Leave `how-to/configure-browser-urls` static; it is about the URL.
- `coming-from-react-router.md`: one comparison cell, if it helps.
- Leave `testing.md` static.

## Start after

PR #10791 (Playground: Fresco and every optional artefact in cljs-rf2 cells) must be merged first. Check with `gh pr view 10791 --json state`. Until it merges, the engine on `main` cannot run the cells this bead asks for.

## The new capability

The docs' live ` ```cljs-rf2 ` cells run on `docs/cljs/playground-rf2.js`, built from `docs/tools/playground/sci`. That engine now bundles:

- re-frame2 core and reagent2 (reagent-slim), as before;
- **Fresco**: `re-frame.fresco` and its `forms`, `overlay` and `motion` modules;
- **every optional artefact**:
  - machines, flows and schemas (as before);
  - **HTTP**: `re-frame.http.managed`, plus `re-frame.http.test-support` for stubs;
  - **resources**, **routing**, **epoch** and **SSR**.

Before PR #10791, a cell could use only core, reagent2, machines, flows and schemas. So pages teaching Fresco, HTTP, resources, routing, epoch history or SSR could only show static code. Now a reader can run those examples, edit them, and see the result.

## How to write a live cell

The fence is ` ```cljs-rf2 `; there is no separate Fresco fence. A cell runs when the page loads, and again on Mod-Enter after an edit. Its last form is rendered.

- **Which renderer.** The last form renders through **Fresco** when it contains:
  - a Fresco view (`h/defview`), or `h/frame-root` / `h/frame-provider`; or
  - a handler written as data, such as `:on-click [:inc]`.

  Otherwise it renders through **reagent2**. Plain hiccup looks the same either way. One page can mix reagent2 and Fresco cells, but one tree cannot. A plain fn or `reg-view` head inside a Fresco tree raises `:rf.error/fresco-bad-head`.
- **What a cell can require.**
  - `re-frame.core`, which includes `reg-view`, `reg-machine`, `reg-flow`, `reg-app-schema`, `reg-resource`, `reg-route`, `epoch-history` and `restore-epoch!`
  - `re-frame.fresco`, `.forms`, `.overlay` and `.motion`
  - `reagent2.*`
  - `re-frame.schemas`
  - `re-frame.http.managed` and `re-frame.http.test-support`
  - `re-frame.resources`, `re-frame.routing`, `re-frame.epoch` and `re-frame.ssr`
- **Not available:**
  - `h/defhost`, since a cell has no foreign React component to wrap
  - `re-frame.fresco.native`, `re-frame.fresco.server` and the Fresco test kit
  - Story, Xray, and the Ring/Node SSR hosts
- **Frames.** A cell that creates no frame uses `:rf/default`. A cell that wraps its tree in `frame-root` uses that frame, as a real app does.
- **Shared page state.** All cells on a page share the registrar and the frames, so a later cell can render a view an earlier cell registered. Leaving the page unmounts everything, destroys frames and removes the page's registrations.
- **HTTP without a network.** Stub `:rf.http/managed` and route the frame to the stub:

  ```clojure
  (require '[re-frame.core :as rf]
           '[re-frame.http.managed]
           '[re-frame.http.test-support :as http-test-support])

  (http-test-support/install-managed-request-stubs!
    {[:get "https://api.example.com/articles/intro"] {:reply {:ok {:title "Welcome"}}}})

  ;; ... events, subs and a view ...

  [rf/frame-root {:id :demo :fx-overrides {:rf.http/managed :rf.http/managed-test-stub}}
   [article-view]]
  ```

  - Key each stub on the exact `[method url]` the request sends. A miss reaches `:on-failure` with `no stub matched`.
  - Use `{:reply {:failure {...}}}` to demo errors.
  - Install stubs and never uninstall them: the stub stack is global.
  - Real requests also work, but only to `https` endpoints that allow CORS, and they depend on the network. Prefer stubs.
- **Never create a `:url-bound? true` frame.** It would take over the docs site's address bar. Routing works on in-memory frames.
- **Working examples to copy:**
  - The cells in `docs/tools/playground/test/smoke.test.mjs` cover a Fresco view, a data-handler cell, a stubbed HTTP request, a `reg-resource` load, `reg-route` and `render-to-string`; all of them pass in CI.
  - `docs/tools/playground/README.md` has the full rules and a troubleshooting table.

## What to do

1. Read `docs/AUTHORING.md` and follow it. Examples must be real, use the actual API, and be self-contained; keep the page's continuing example domain.
2. Go through each page in this section and find the examples where **running** the code would teach something reading it cannot. Good candidates are behaviour that changes on a click, a request moving through loading, success and failure, data flowing into a view, and a rendered result. Introduce running examples there: convert a static block to ` ```cljs-rf2 `, or add a cell next to it.
3. Do not convert every block. Keep code static when it is:
   - a fragment, an `ns` form or configuration;
   - server-side, or needs the unavailable pieces listed above;
   - or the live version would need setup that buries the point.

   A page with one well-chosen live example beats a page where every block runs. If a page gains nothing, leave it.
4. Within one page, give each cell's registrations distinct ids unless a later cell is meant to reuse an earlier one's. Cells share the registrar.
5. Fix stale prose you touch, but keep the diff to this section.

## How to verify

Nothing in CI runs the docs' cells, so clicking them yourself is the only check. Say what you clicked in the PR body.

- Build the engine: `cd docs/tools/playground && npm install && npm run build`. `npm run build:rf2` enters shadow-cljs, so it uses the machine-wide build lane; ask the coordinator for it first (`AGENTS.md`).
- Run `mkdocs serve` from the repo root. Open every page you changed and use every cell: it renders, its buttons and inputs work, and no cell shows `ERROR`. Then navigate to another page and back.
- Run `mkdocs build --strict` and `python scripts/check_doc_slugs.py`.

== VERDICT (livedocs-routing worker, PR #10802)
Converted 7 pages, 8 cells, all in-memory: every cell mounts rf/frame-root with an :initial-events navigation and no :url-bound?.
- concepts.md: 2 cells. "Try the matching rules" sends URLs through [:rf.route/handle-url-change url], views by :rf.route/id and prints params/query. A second cell does in-place :query-merge/:query on the same route table, in its own frame.
- tutorial.md: 1 cell, "Run it on this page": the complete app in memory, plus a demo address line (route-url) and typed-URL buttons. The url-bound boot and the steps stay static.
- how-to/guard-unsaved-changes.md: 1 cell (can-leave prompt, continue/cancel, save, save-and-close with :bypass-leave?).
- how-to/require-sign-in-on-a-route.md: 1 cell (can-enter, entry-denied handler, return trip with fragment, sign-out).

Left static: configure-browser-urls.md (about the URL), testing.md (JVM tests), index/examples/glossary (nothing to run).
Measured: a {:url "/articles?page=12abc"} navigate is refused silently, while the same URL through :rf.route/handle-url-change lands on :rf.route/not-found with :reason :validation. That is why the matching cell uses handle-url-change.

title: Test-suite pruning, second pass: every surface (one PR per artefact, largest suites first)
description:
MIKE'S INSTRUCTIONS (2026-10-02, verbatim):

for each distinct surface, carefully review the unit test suite and reduce unnecessary test cases. The main aim is a smaller, better design suited that preserves confidence in important behaviour, not simply fewer tests.  You can assume that existing coverage is excellent. 

Work one artefact at a time (propose an order, largest suites first), each in its own worktree and PR, babysat to green. Use background workers as needed. Within an artefact, work in these stages, in order:
1. UNDERSTAND THE SUITE. Map its structure, the behaviours and contracts it protects, and any tests failing today. Read the implementation wherever you need it to judge what a test actually proves. Record the baseline: tests, assertions, runtime.
2. REMOVE DUPLICATION. Find exact and near duplicates: tests exercising the same behaviour, under the same conditions, with the same failure mode. Keep the clearest one and delete or fold the rest. Similar-looking tests may protect different boundaries or regressions; keep those distinctions. A .cljc test that runs on both JVM and ClojureScript is not a duplicate, and neither is a pair covering genuinely platform-specific code.
3. REMOVE LOW-VALUE TESTS. For each candidate, ask: "What plausible bug would this catch that the retained tests would miss?" Candidates are tests that:
- repeat implementation details;
- verify trivial setup;
- assert little of consequence;
- test mock or library behaviour rather than ours.
Give a concrete reason for each removal, and name the retained test that covers its behaviour. Where it is unclear, plant a fault in the code under test and see what goes red: a test that is the only red for a plausible fault stays. Do not delete a test merely because it is small, awkward, flaky or currently failing.
4. IMPROVE ORGANISATION. Group what remains around behaviours or contracts, and fix unclear names. Fold repetitive cases into a table (`are` or a data table) where failures stay readable. Simplify fixtures and helpers where that makes the tests easier to understand. Do not add elaborate abstractions just to cut lines. Always keep:
- tests that pin documentation or spec wording (the *_guide_truth_* and terminology
tests). They guard prose, not code, so they look weak and aren't;
- self-tests of gates and ratchets;
- tests of documented error ids;
- regression tests for real past bugs, unless a retained test demonstrably catches the same failure.
VERIFY as you go:
- Change in small batches. Before each batch, predict the change in test and assertion counts. After it, run the artefact's suite and confirm the counts moved by exactly that much, with everything still green.
- Then run the repository checks CLAUDE.md requires.
- Treat coverage as supporting evidence, never as proof that a removal is safe.
- Before any shadow-cljs run, ask the mayor for the lane.
Proceed wherever the evidence is clear. Keep uncertain cases and say what makes them uncertain. Do not change production behaviour, weaken a retained assertion, or add replacement tests to hold the count up.

== HOW THIS PASS RUNS (worker session re-frame2-5a, 2026-10-02)

THIS IS THE SECOND PASS. The first pass ran under rf2-98kzs (implementation/), rf2-3h7v2 (tools/) and rf2-by74t (bench, skills, migration, scripts), all closed by 2026-10-02, about 46 children, roughly a 10% cut. Each first-pass child's close reason and PR body (removal ledger, kept-uncertain list, retained covers) is prior art for its artefact: read it in stage 1, and do not re-litigate a keep it recorded unless new evidence (a plant) settles it.

WHAT CHANGES FROM THE FIRST PASS. Mike's new line is "You can assume that existing coverage is excellent". So:
- no hunting for coverage gaps and no gap or defect beads. A defect noticed in passing gets ONE line in the PR body's "Noticed, not actioned" list, and that is all;
- the effort goes into design: cross-file duplication that the first pass's sub-area fences hid, low-value tests judged against an excellent retained suite, and organisation (grouping by contract, tables, clear names, simpler fixtures);
- the first pass's per-PR ceremony is trimmed to what the instructions ask for: predicted and measured deltas per batch, a removal ledger naming each retained cover, plants where a cover is unclear, and the kept-uncertain list.

RULES CARRIED FORWARD FROM THE FIRST PASS (each was ruled or measured there):
- a documented error id stays asserted somewhere, and a verbatim duplicate of its test may go (rf2-98kzs.3 ruling);
- stage 1 confirms that a runner actually EXECUTES each file in scope, and which lane (JVM, :node-test, :browser-test, prod gate, node --test, bb). A file no runner executes cannot be pruned on evidence: report it instead (rf2-by74t note);
- a test cited by name outside its file (spec, docs, another test, a workflow, a gate roster) stays unless the citation moves with it;
- a test a first-pass PR named as the retained cover for one of its removals may be removed only if another retained test covers both;
- production gates with a test-count floor (core, routing, ssr, epoch, ...): if a removal takes a gate below its floor, STOP and report; do not lower a floor in a pruning PR;
- hot zones: never edit implementation/deps.edn, implementation/shadow-cljs.edn or .github/workflows/* in a pruning PR; if test wiring must change, STOP and report;
- gate-shaped harnesses (e2e, acceptance, feature-matrix, live and integration harnesses) are out of scope.

MECHANICS:
- one child bead per artefact (or per sub-area of a very large artefact), created at dispatch, one worktree under re-frame2-worktrees named prune2-*, one PR babysat to green. Production code untouched; CI green on the same check count.
- ONE AT A TIME: the next child starts once the previous PR is green, not merged.
- THE SHADOW-CLJS LANE goes through the mayor's grant. Workers batch CLJS count verification into one end window per child (a scoped build holding every batch version, as rf2-3h7v2.9 did) and take head counts from the PR's CI. JVM lanes run freely.
- REPORT per child, in the PR body and as a summary on the child: baseline -> final (tests / assertions / runtime) per lane; per batch the predicted and measured deltas; each removal with its reason and retained cover; uncertain cases kept, with why.

CENSUS (2026-10-02, trunk 0221aef3e5; deftest forms plus JS test()/it() lines, a regex count and a CLAIM; each child's stage-1 runner baseline is the authority):

Total about 22,000.

ORDER (largest first; the three largest split by sub-area, as in the first pass):
1. tools/xray: panels/ (1550), top-level files (810), static/ + views/ (613), filters/theme/settings/diff/palette/chart (548). panels_e2e/, control_axes_e2e/, acceptance/ are gate-shaped and out of scope.
2. tools/story: ui/ (853), top-level story_* files (819), story/ top-level files (698), play/recorder/theme (358). panels_e2e/ out of scope.
3. implementation/core: the first pass's five sub-areas (frames/images/registration; trace/observability/errors/privacy; events/effects/interceptors; subscriptions/substrate/derivation; the remainder).
4. implementation/machines, 5. implementation/fresco, 6. implementation/scripts (the first pass gave 43 of its *.test.cjs files only automated scans), 7. tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp, 8. implementation/adapters, 9. implementation/resources, 10. tools/machines-viz, 11. bench/fresco, 12. implementation/ssr, 13. implementation/routing, 14. implementation/http, 15. implementation/epoch, 16. implementation/schemas, 17. tools/mcp-base, 18. tools/story-mcp, 19. implementation/ssr-ring, 20. implementation/flows, 21. implementation/ssr-node (NOT reviewed in the first pass), 22. skills/re-frame2-pair, then the small tail in census order (a suite whose review finds nothing to change closes with no PR), and tools/mcp-conformance last (a conformance contract, mostly keep-by-rule).
notes:
== ARRANGEMENT WITH THE MAYOR (2026-10-02 14:45:04 AUSEST)
- The mayor (session re-frame2-40) grants the shadow-cljs lane. I relay one request per child, at the end of that child's work, as "LANE REQUEST prune2-<x>: <what>, ~<minutes>", and release it as "LANE RELEASED prune2-<x>".
- The mayor merges green prune2 PRs on its tick. This session closes each child on merge, closes the epic, and reaps prune2-* worktrees on the worker's done report. Neither of us commits .beads from a prune2 branch.
- SKILLS FENCE: no prune2 child goes into a skills/<name>/ test directory while a skill review (rf2-jo4dg family) is open on that skill. Message the mayor before prune2 reaches skills/.
== RULING: production-gate test-count floors in this pass (mayor, 2026-10-03 03:0x AUSEST) ==
TRIGGER. rf2-zbnoc.9's worker measured scripts/test-core-prod-gate.sh at base 2a213d49e9: Ran 1814 tests / 8712 assertions against RF2_MIN_TESTS=1805, exit 0. That is slack 9, against the ~35 the script's own comment requires. As written, "do not lower a floor in a pruning PR" caps every core child at 9 net prod-lane removals, all children together.
RULING. The "do not lower a floor in a pruning PR" line above is this epic's mechanics, not Mike's verbatim instructions. It yields to two things. (1) The script's own maintenance rule (scripts/test-core-prod-gate.sh, the comment above RF2_MIN_TESTS): lowering is safe when the drop is accounted for by tests DELETED in the same diff (not unrostered, not tagged), the lane still reports 0 failures / 0 errors, and ~35 tests of slack survive. (2) The first-pass precedent: commit 1b4e1ac832 lowered RF2_MIN_TESTS 1860 -> 1805 inside the rf2-98kzs.9 pruning branch, under the coordinator's option-(a) ruling, set to the lane's new observed count minus 35.
SO, for every child of this epic and every production gate with a test-count floor (core, routing, ssr, epoch, ...): prune on evidence as usual. As the branch's LAST commit, set the floor to the lane's new observed count minus 35, in its own commit, named like 1b4e1ac832. The commit message gives before/after observed counts, says every test behind the drop is deleted in the branch (none tagged or unrostered), and gives the 0 failures / 0 errors run. Never set it lower than observed minus 35. Never move it without deletions beside it. If the floor file is shared with another in-flight worker, tell the mayor first.
== RULING (Mike, 2026-10-04): PRUNING CHILDREN RUN IN PARALLEL ==
Mike, verbatim: "The pruning tasks can be run in parallel" and "The touch seperate surfaces?" This replaces the MECHANICS line "ONE AT A TIME: the next child starts once the previous PR is green, not merged." Children now run concurrently, because each owns a separate surface: one artefact's test directory, plus at most the RF2_MIN_TESTS line of that artefact's own production-gate script. The shadow-cljs lane is still machine-wide exclusive and still goes through the mayor's grant. Concurrent children queue for it, and each batches its CLJS work into one end window. A child that would touch another artefact's tests, or a file another in-flight child owns, stops and tells the mayor. The mayor dispatched rf2-zbnoc.25 onward under this ruling, alongside the live rf2-zbnoc.24 (implementation/http).

title: Recordable coeffects: event- and processing-start-DB-derived demand on the original causal token (GH #10850)
description:
GitHub #10850. A state fold can need a variable number of fresh recorded identities whose COUNT comes from the current event payload and the DB at that event's processing start (example [:example/duplicate-list {:list-id id}]: one fresh id per current row, where earlier queued events may have edited the rows). The issue found no supported public recipe that derives this demand and generates the facts on the ORIGINAL causal token while keeping the event's FIFO position: a cofx [id arg] declaration stores its arg literally (cofx.cljc ~L416) and the supplier receives only that arg (~L829); registered interceptors run after satisfaction, and the initial causal map is captured before the chain (router.cljc ~L3040), so values minted in an interceptor are absent from the recorded token and strict re-presentation re-mints them. Rejected workarounds per the issue: precompute at enqueue (stale after earlier queued edits), capture rows at enqueue (changes the fold's data), a preparatory dispatch (loses FIFO position), a fixed oversized vector or all-entity fact map (records facts unrelated to the event's demand).

Ask (issue): confirm a supported preserving recipe if one exists; otherwise a public contract for pure demand derivation from the original event and processing-start DB followed by ordinary registered recordable generation on that same token. Acceptance: an earlier queued edit that grows and shrinks demand, a same-count row replacement, the original FIFO position and atomic fold, exact EDN fact recording and schema validation, supplied-value precedence, and strict replay with no additional host generation, all through public APIs.

Mayor triage 2026-10-04: valid, action it in two stages (cited lines re-checked at trunk a592708a84). STAGE 1, recipe check: test whether an existing supported recipe meets the acceptance list. The first candidate is a single recorded random SEED (one recordable coeffect, an EDN value) from which the handler derives the N ids deterministically, given the processing-start DB it already receives: one fact on the original token, FIFO and atomicity untouched, strict replay re-derives identical ids with no host generation, supplied-value precedence via the seed. Check it against EP-0017 (docs/EP/EP-0017-recordable-coeffects.md) and docs/core/coeffects.md, including whether derived ids honour the project's identity and schema rules. If it holds, document the recipe where readers meet recordable coeffects, and the GitHub issue closes with that PR. STAGE 2, only if no recipe holds: write a short design note proposing the minimal contract and STOP; a new public contract on the recordable-coeffect surface is Mike's ruling, so no implementation lands without it. The mayor closes this bead at merge (or records the held decision) and verifies the issue state.
notes:
== STAGE 1 RESULT 2026-10-04 20:57 AUSEST: a supported recipe exists, documented in PR #10853 (draft until marked ready; Fixes #10850)

THE RECIPE. One recordable coeffect supplies ONE fresh id (a uuid, `:schema :uuid`) for the whole operation. The handler counts the items in the processing-start `:db` it already receives, and derives each fresh item id from that one recorded value as plain data, `[copy-id i]`. The demand never has to reach the supplier, so the literal `[id arg]` argument (cofx.cljc L416 parse, L837 invocation) and the interceptor timing (router.cljc L3040, token captured before the chain) stop mattering.

DIFFERS FROM THE TRIAGE: not a seed. The triage's first candidate was "a random SEED". EP-0017 L313-314 rules seeds out ("suppliers record produced *values*, never seeds"), and so does its rationale at L837-839: a seed needs a bit-identical PRNG across hosts and versions. So the recorded fact is the fresh id itself, and the row ids are derived by data composition, never by a generator. The docs also say to avoid `hash` for UUID-typed derivations, because it differs between the JVM and JS. This fits spec/002 §Durable join keys: the derived ids are a pure function of a recordable fact plus prior frame-state. It also fits §The minting ladder: the doc keeps rung 1 (derive from state) first when ids only need app-db uniqueness.

EXECUTED CHECKS. JVM scratch namespace outside the tree, run against this worktree's implementation/core, epoch and schemas. It used public API only: init! with the plain-atom adapter, make-frame, reg-cofx, reg-event, dispatch-sync with :rf.cofx and :rf.cofx/mint-policy, app-db-value, epoch-history, restore-epoch! and replay-epoch!. The code under test is the doc's fence loaded verbatim; the only change is a supplier counter. `clojure -M -m cofxdemand.recipe`, exit 0, "SUMMARY checks=11 recipe-pass=11 control-red=11 => OK". Each item, with the recipe result and then its control, which went red:
- grow 3->4: PASS / precompute-at-enqueue copies 3 rows.
- shrink 3->2: PASS, 1 fact, 0 unused / precompute leaves 1 of 3 ids unused.
- same-count replace: PASS / capture-rows-at-enqueue copies stale "milk".
- FIFO + atomic (e1, dup, e3): PASS, whole copy in the duplicate's own epoch / preparatory dispatch lands after e3 and includes "salt".
- exact EDN recording at 7 rows: PASS, token keys exactly #{:rf/time-ms :list/copy-id}, EDN round-trip / handler-body mint records no fact.
- schema: supplied "not-a-uuid" gives :rf.error/cofx-value-invalid / the same supplier without :schema accepts it.
- EDN guard: a host-object generator gives cofx-value-invalid / an ambient supplier accepts it.
- supplied precedence: PASS, 0 supplier calls / unsupplied, 1 call.
- strict dispatch: PASS, absent gives :rf.error/missing-required-cofx with 0 calls / :live mints.
- strict replay (restore-epoch! then replay-epoch!): PASS, identical :lists and token, 0 host generations / handler-body mint and interceptor mint both re-mint on replay, db differs.

Sabotage of the committed doc fence ([copy-id i] to [(random-uuid) i]) gave exit 1: supplied and both replay checks FAIL. The skill-fence plant gave exit 1. Restores were blob-hash verified.

GATES (exit codes): check_doc_slugs 0, with a planted broken anchor giving 1. mkdocs build --strict 0, with 0 warnings. api-manifest doc-guide/doc-api tests 0, and a planted (rf/reg-cofxx gave 1. api-manifest skills-check 0. All 49 scripts/check_*.py and both scripts/check-*.sh 0.

FILES: docs/core/coeffects.md (new "### When the number of ids depends on state" under "Where a new id comes from") and skills/re-frame2/references/fundamentals/cofx.md (same recipe under the minting ladder). No implementation/spec/EP change. The issue closes on merge, so the bead stays open for the mayor.
close_reason: Merged as PR #10853 (rebase, trunk d7502f102a); GitHub #10850 verified CLOSED. Stage 1 resolved it: a supported recipe exists on today's public API, so no new contract is needed. One recordable coeffect supplies ONE fresh id (a uuid, :schema :uuid) for the whole duplication; the handler counts the rows in the processing-start :db it already receives and builds each row id from that single recorded value as plain data, [copy-id i], so the count never has to reach the supplier and neither the literal [id arg] nor the post-capture interceptor limit matters. MAYOR PREMISE CORRECTED: the triage proposed recording a random SEED; EP-0017 rules that out (L313-314 "record produced values, never seeds"; L837-839, a seed needs a bit-identical generator across hosts and versions), so the recipe records the produced id itself and derives with no generator. The docs also say to derive from state first when ids need only be unique within app-db, and warn against hash for UUID row ids (it differs between JVM and JavaScript). Executed in a scratch namespace against implementation/core, epoch and schemas, public API only, running the doc's own code block: clojure -M -m cofxdemand.recipe exit 0, checks=11 recipe-pass=11 control-red=11, covering demand growth (3 to 4) and shrink (3 to 2, no unused fact), same-count row replacement, FIFO position and atomic fold, exact EDN recording (keys exactly #{:rf/time-ms :list/copy-id}), schema refusal (:rf.error/cofx-value-invalid), non-EDN refusal, supplied-value precedence (0 supplier calls), strict policy (:rf.error/missing-required-cofx, 0 calls), and restore-epoch! then replay-epoch! with identical state and 0 generations; each control (precompute at enqueue, capture at enqueue, preparatory dispatch, handler-body or interceptor minting) went red. Docs: docs/core/coeffects.md "When the number of ids depends on state" and skills/re-frame2/references/fundamentals/cofx.md, 67 lines added. Only that scratch run covers the two code blocks; no committed gate does.

title: re-frame-migration: pin the M73 codemod example to a revision carrying its documented guarantees (GH #10858)
description:
GitHub #10858. skills/re-frame-migration/references/auto-call-site-rewrites.md M73 (~L562) pins its primary codemod git dependency to 8b17cc53d5 (L570), which predates the binding and discard fixes the surrounding paragraphs now document; the issue's replay of five public fixtures through scan-string/rewrite-string shows the pinned tool still emitting an unbound reg-event and rewriting #_ forms, while the current tool does not. The L579 fallback (subtract discarded findings by hand) corrects a count but cannot stop the older tool changing discarded bytes on a later --write.

Ask: the primary example selects an explicit, verified published revision with the documented guarantees (or states the minimum revision when the consumer supplies a pin); keep reproducible pinning, never 'latest'; restrict the discard fallback to read-only reporting or document a genuinely safe write.

Acceptance: the exact primary example's revision matches the M73 contract, historical warnings secondary; the documented invocation checked with bare, mixed accepted/held, discarded-only and active/discarded fixtures, including target-binding resolution and inactive-source preservation; no unspecified later revision needed; manual subtraction never presented as write protection; qualified-call behaviour, reproducible pinning and held-site semantics intact; works for any consumer repository.

Mayor triage 2026-10-04: valid, action it. Re-read at trunk 86462000da: the M73 recipe's copyable command pins :git/sha 8b17cc53d517de9359f5174a0d2fcfa4748091ab (a Fresco product-name sweep commit, shared with the reagent-to-fresco reporter's four pins in docs/core/fresco/20-migration-from-reagent.md x2, migration/reagent-to-fresco/codemod/README.md and skills/reagent-migration/SKILL.md), which predates the #10851/#10852 fixes merged in PR #10854 (trunk 0d4cf2e537). Three paragraphs after it carry 'at the sha above' caveats (CRLF churn, discarded forms, and the bare-binding note). No gate pins these shas equal: check_skill_migration_contract_drift.py and verify-version-lockstep.sh only mention :git/sha in templates. Fix: pin the M73 command to a verified trunk revision carrying the fixes, decouple it from the reporter's pin, drop the caveats the new pin discharges, and make the discard fallback read-only. Leave the reporter's four pins alone. The GitHub issue closes when the PR merges (`Fixes #10858` in the body); the mayor closes this bead at merge and verifies the issue reads CLOSED.

title: re-frame-migration: M-8 custom-effect census must be alias-, binding- and multiline-aware (GH #10864)
description:
GitHub #10864. skills/re-frame-migration/references/auto-call-site-rewrites.md, Effect-map consolidation (M-8), procedure step 1 (~L475) calls `rg "\(rf/reg-fx\s+:" src/` the step that collects the full custom effect-ID set. The issue's replay on five isolated files found only the one-line `rf/` case: it misses a multiline call (ripgrep does not span newlines without -U), another alias (`events/reg-fx`), a bare `:refer [reg-fx]` call and a fully qualified `re-frame.core/reg-fx` call; it also assumes `src/` is the only source root. Later steps treat keys outside the set as unknown, so missed registrations become misclassified, held work.

Ask: label the grep as CANDIDATE discovery and give a broader candidate search (any alias, bare and fully qualified heads, multiline, every configured source root), then the verification that turns candidates into accepted registrations: derive aliases and bare or fully-qualified bindings from each namespace's ns form, resolve keyword ids including `::` from the registering namespace, and keep comments, strings, #_ forms and unrelated same-named local functions out. Generic; no shipped collector required.

Acceptance: replaying the five fixtures recovers all five effect ids, keeping the one-line control; the recipe distinguishes candidate matches from verified active registrations and covers all source roots; alias and :: resolution follow namespace bindings; comments, discards and unrelated same-named functions are not accepted; a top-level return using a registered custom effect classifies correctly for M-8 whatever the registration's layout or import form.

Mayor triage 2026-10-04: valid, action it. Re-read at trunk 1ec6b38ada: M-8 step 1 still carries the literal-alias single-line rg command and calls it complete. title: re-frame-migration: M-8 fold into an existing :fx must preserve v1 effect order, not append unconditionally (GH #10869)
description:
GitHub #10869. M-8's fold of top-level custom effects into an existing :fx is written as unconditional existing-entries-first, in two places: skills/re-frame-migration/references/auto-call-site-rewrites.md, Effect-map consolidation (M-8), Procedure step 5; and migration/from-re-frame-v1/README.md, M-8 transformation step 4, `(into existing-fx new-fx)`. The issue shows that this can change source-observed execution order: v1 (re-frame 1.4.3 fx.cljc) runs :db first, then iterates the remaining map, and a small literal map is an array-map that keeps source order, so `{:db .. :demo/log .. :fx [..]}` ran log before the :fx rows in v1 but after them under the recipe (JVM witness: v1/preserving trace [:db :demo/log :demo/send :demo/send] vs existing-first [:db :demo/send :demo/send :demo/log]). v1 documents only :db-first, so the rest is source-observed behaviour, not a contract.

Ask: replace the blanket existing-first rule with an order-preserving fold - keep :db first and the existing rows' order and payloads, and place each folded entry where it ran in v1 when the order is source-provable (a small literal map); where the map is dynamic or the order is not provable, name the missing fact and hold only that site; distinguish v1's documented guarantee (:db first) from source-observed order. Update both passages together, generically.

Acceptance: bounded examples with a custom effect before and after an existing :fx keep the demonstrated delivery sequence with :db first and row order intact; a dynamic or unknown map example asks for the precise missing evidence or intent instead of appending unconditionally; the guide distinguishes v1's documented guarantee from source-observed behaviour.

Mayor triage 2026-10-05: valid, action it proportionately - Type A promises observably identical rewrites, and this fold can silently reorder effects. Checked at trunk 2380656fef. SEQUENCED: migration/from-re-frame-v1/README.md is a hot-zone file held by worker/migm70 (rf2-ys7gl, PR #10870); dispatch this bead only after #10870 merges. The GitHub issue closes when the PR merges (`Fixes #10869` in the body); the mayor closes this bead at merge and verifies the issue reads CLOSED.
notes:
== RESULT (worker/m8order, 2026-10-05 AUSEST) — PR #10871 (draft until marked ready), one commit

Both copies of the M-8 existing-:fx fold rule were replaced together: auto-call-site-rewrites.md §Effect-map consolidation (M-8) Procedure step 5, and migration/from-re-frame-v1/README.md M-8 transformation step 4. Nothing else in either file changed.

Verified at source:
- re-frame 1.4.3 `re_frame/fx.cljc` (from the jar; jar SHA-1 74e132cc59... matches its .sha1). Lines 51-58: a truthy :db runs first, then `doseq` over `(dissoc effects :db)`. Lines 112-121: the :fx handler walks its rows in order. Lines 43-44, the do-fx docstring: "You cannot rely on the ordering in which effects are executed, other than that `:db` is guaranteed to be executed first."
- Array-map threshold:
  - CLJS 1.12.145 compiler.cljc line 422 `(def ^:private array-map-threshold 8)`. emit-map `(<= (count keys) array-map-threshold)` emits PersistentArrayMap in order, else PersistentHashMap.fromArrays.
  - core.cljs line 7083 sets HASHMAP-THRESHOLD to 8, and -assoc past it converts to a hash map.
  - Clojure 1.12.4 PersistentArrayMap.HASHTABLE_THRESHOLD = 16 slots = 8 entries.
  - So source order holds for a literal of at most 8 entries. From 9 up, a literal iterates in hash order.

Acceptance lines, each with the passage or check that meets it:

1. Bounded examples with a custom effect before and after an existing :fx keep the delivery sequence, with :db first and row order intact.
   - Passage: step 5 / step 4, "put each folded entry before the existing rows when its key comes before :fx and after them when it comes after, keeping source order on each side; the existing rows keep their order and payloads", plus the worked example `{:db db :demo/log log :fx [...] :demo/ping p}` -> `{:db db :fx [[:demo/log log] ... [:demo/ping p]]}`.
   - Check: a JVM witness against the REAL v1 loop, `(:after re-frame.fx/do-fx)` loaded from the 1.4.3 jar, with recording handlers. Results under the documented fold, exit 0:
     - before = [:db :demo/log :demo/send :demo/send]
     - after = [:db :demo/send :demo/send :demo/log]
     - both = [:db :demo/log :demo/send :demo/send :demo/ping]
     - db-last-in-source still runs :db first
   - Every case matched v1, with :db first, payloads identical? and the rows in order.
   - The red: planting the old existing-first fold gave exit 1, and `before` came out [:db :demo/send :demo/send :demo/log]. Restored; the witness file's blob hash matched the pre-plant blob hash, and the rerun gave exit 0.
2. A dynamic or unknown map asks for the missing evidence instead of appending.
   - Passage: "Where the source can't prove the order — the map is built at run time (assoc, merge, cond->, a helper's return value) or the literal has more than 8 entries — hold that site alone (SKILL.md cardinal rule 2): name the missing fact, which side of the existing rows each folded effect must run on, and ask instead of appending." README: "flag that site alone for human review, naming the missing fact".
   - Check: the witness ran the same source `(fn [next-db base log] (assoc base :db next-db :demo/log log))` with two bases. It ran log AFTER the rows for one base and BEFORE them for the other, so the order is not in the source.
   - The 9-entry literal check gave PersistentHashMap, and v1 run order did not equal source order.
3. The guide distinguishes v1's documented guarantee from source-observed behaviour.
   - Passage, both files: "v1 guarantees only that a truthy :db runs first; every other key ran in the map's iteration order — observed behaviour, not contract".

Gates, each run by absolute path with its exit captured: all exit 0. They were check_doc_slugs, mkdocs build --strict, check_skill_migration_cites and its --self-test, contract drift, O-16/O-17 router drift, check_readme_links, the 42 other check_*.py, and the 4 check-*.sh. The O-16/O-17 router-drift gate cannot fail on these files. Planted faults in the edited lines went red, exit 1, for check_doc_slugs, cites, contract drift and mkdocs. title: fresco-migration MIG-26: a deferred callback rendered as a retained Reagent tree keeps a reactive read through a registered render boundary, not a hoisted snapshot (GH #10978)
description:
GH #10978 (Mike, 2026-10-06). A documentation clarification in the reagent-fresco-migration skill; no runtime defect is claimed.

AT TRUNK c491b138e3: skills/reagent-fresco-migration/references/catalog-judgment.md MIG-26 (L343-364), route 2: "It runs later -> hoist the read to render time and pass the value into the callback. rf/subscribe-once is the sanctioned snapshot ...". That is right for a NONRENDERING later callback (an event or a timer). It is wrong for a DEFERRED callback whose result is rendered as a retained Reagent component inside a real registered frame scope: hoisting, or a one-shot snapshot, changes read time and removes the retained tree's reactive updates. procedure.md (L151-204) already permits retained providers and renderer judgment, but no example connects those rules to this case.

Consumer evidence (from the issue). A retained chart's widget success callback reads live precision and returns a Reagent tree. A registered render extent of this shape keeps it reactive and frame-isolated:
  (rf/reg-view retained-result [{:keys [render props]}] (render props))
  ;; the provider calls this later; the returned component owns the read
  (fn [props] [retained-result {:render original-render :props props}])
In a mounted control with a custom frame and the default frame, each chart updated only from its own frame.

ASK. Qualify MIG-26 route 2. Classify each shared helper by its actual renderer and dynamic render extent, its invocation and read time, and whether it needs a snapshot or ongoing invalidation. Show three callers:
(a) a Fresco render helper (h/sub);
(b) a nonrendering later handler with a deliberate rf/subscribe-once snapshot;
(c) a deferred retained Reagent render whose returned component owns a reactive read through a registered render/frame boundary (the reg-view shape above).
Hoist only when snapshot semantics preserve the existing behaviour. Never call h/sub outside a Fresco render, and invent no bridge API. Keep the existing whole-view conversion / explicit-hold discipline and the captured queued-dispatch / FIFO guidance. Closes GH #10978.

Follow-ups found by the fourth-pass prune of the core subscription, reactive-substrate and derivation tests (rf2-txsk5.12, merged as PR #11014). Found by reading, not run; re-derive each at tip before acting. The PR body's "Dead code, stale text and gaps" section (gh pr view 11014 --json body --jq .body) is the source list.

ITEM 1, suspected defect, first. re-frame.core/unsubscribe's 2-arity is frame-first, [frame-id query-v], while subscribe's 2-arity is [query-v opts]. So (rf/unsubscribe q {:frame f}) resolves no cache entry and the ref leaks silently. Decide from spec/API.md, Spec 006 and the docs which shape is the contract. If the code disagrees with the spec, fix it with a test that is red on the current code. If the spec itself has the asymmetry, the ergonomic answer is the subscribe-symmetric [query-v opts] shape; make that change only if no caller depends on the frame-first form, and treat it as a public-API change (spec/API.md and spec/api-manifest-metadata.edn by hand, spec/api-manifest.edn regenerated with generate! in implementation/scripts/api-manifest). If that is not clear-cut, report a recommendation instead.

ITEM 2, dead code: delete each after confirming no caller in implementation/, tools/, examples/, skills/ and testbeds/.
- re-frame.interop/add-on-dispose!'s non-Reaction fallback branch.
- re-frame.subs.cache: the 2-arity forms of dispose-entry-now! and unsubscribe!, which only call their own 3-arity.
- re-frame.subs.cache/*disposal-cause*: bound at four sites, read nowhere.
- re-frame.subs/acquire-cache-reaction! with its *acquire-recovery* / record-acquire-recovery! channel (zero callers).
- re-frame.subs.tooling/sub-algebra-view's 1-arity.
- re-frame.derivation.graph/node-id (public, no caller).
- The JVM alias re-frame.subs/sub-cache-snapshot.
- re-frame.derivation.graph input-edges' (= :parametric inputs) guard, unreachable behind the sequential? check.
- The :source-db slot on :rf.observe/derived-tree records, which re-frame.projection never reads (check Spec 009 and the schemas before removing a documented slot).

ITEM 3, stale text.
- spec/006-ReactiveSubstrate.md section Subscription topology says a cyclic sub "will throw"; it emits :rf.error/sub-cycle and recovers to nil.
- spec/conformance/fixtures/data-classification-derived-tree-fails-closed-no-frame.edn cites re-frame.projection-cljs-test/derived-tree-nil-frame-fails-closed, which does not exist; the test is derived-tree-without-a-live-frame-fails-closed.
- scripts/test-core-prod-gate.sh says sub-dispose-trace-test pins "a resubscribe rebuilding a FRESH reaction"; no test there asserts that. Correct the comment, or add the assertion if it is a property worth pinning.
notes:
== WORKER PASS, 2026-10-09 AUSEST: PR #11018 (branch worker/core-subs-followups, head f1e1886d62 on trunk 1f94bb82dd) ==

ITEM 1: DECISION FOR MIKE. No code changed.
- The leak is real. A JVM probe on the plain-atom adapter:
  - After (rf/subscribe [:v] {:frame :probe/u}) the cache reads {[:v] 1}.
  - (rf/unsubscribe [:v] {:frame :probe/u}) returns nil and the cache still reads {[:v] 1}.
  - The frame-first (rf/unsubscribe :probe/u [:v]) empties it.
  - Mechanism: frame-target->id passes the vector through unchanged, (rf.frame/frame [:v]) is nil, and the when-let short-circuits.
- The frame-first shape is ruled, not drift:
  - Spec 006 says "No opts-map form (deliberate)".
  - Commit 87b3eec977 (rf2-bfadc6) records "Per Mike's ruling (Option A), unsubscribe deliberately stays frame-first".
  - Review finding rf2-pk4i6.4 #4 proposed a vector-first-arg refusal. It was dismissed: "can be noted on that ruling if it bites".
- It has bitten. 20 tools/xray test call sites, written 2026-09-09 to 09-11, call (rf/unsubscribe q {:frame f}). Each one releases nothing.
- Frame-first callers that would have to move:
  - Source: re-frame.substrate.spine, re-frame.fresco.impl.collector, re-frame.machines.timer (2 sites) and bench/fresco (12 sites).
  - Tests in core, adapters/reagent, epoch, derivation-conformance and fresco.
  - Prose in docs, skills and spec.
- Recommendation A: make unsubscribe [query-v opts] like subscribe, subscribe-once and dispatch. It is a public-API change, sequenced after the live fleet. The xray sites become correct with no edit.
- Minimum B, if the ruling stands: throw a typed error on a vector first argument, and rewrite the 20 xray sites frame-first.

ITEM 2: dead code.
- Done:
  - re-frame.subs.cache dispose-entry-now! and unsubscribe! are collapsed to [cache k frame-id]. No caller used the 2-arity. Control: a 2-argument call planted at the unsubscribe! site turned re-frame.sub-cache-test red with 4 ArityException errors.
  - re-frame.derivation.graph/node-id is deleted. Fixed-string census: 0 hits. The control needle derivation.graph/derivation-graph hit 25.
  - input-edges' unreachable (= :parametric inputs) clause is dropped. Replacing the guard with false left derivation-graph-test and conformance-test GREEN, so no JVM test pinned it. The new deftest parametric-sub-is-a-node-with-no-static-input-edge goes red under that plant.
- Not done, with reasons:
  - The interop/add-on-dispose! non-Reaction fallback. The premise does not hold. Under the JVM test-react adapter, whose derived value is a bare reify IDeref, core's sub build sends all 3 add-on-dispose! calls down the fallback. When I simulated the deletion, a layer-2 sub's inputs leaked ({[:a] 1, [:b] 1} left after the release, where the real code leaves {}). Making test-react's JVM derived value an rf.interop Reaction would make it deletable, but that is outside this item's fence.
  - acquire-cache-reaction!, *acquire-recovery* and record-acquire-recovery!, and subs.cache/*disposal-cause*. A standing retention ruling covers them: Ruling B on rf2-63t1i (2026-08-21; commit d964454ebf), "retained at zero callers", stated in code as "Do not delete it as residue". Deleting them is Mike's call.
  - The 1-arity of subs.tooling/sub-algebra-view. It HAS a caller, implementation/adapters/reagent/test/re_frame/runtime_cljs_test.cljs:585, which is in the live adapters/reagent worker's scope.
  - The JVM alias re-frame.subs/sub-cache-snapshot. It is documented public surface in spec/API.md and spec/002-Frames.md (002 is outside the fence), so removing it is a public-name change touching Spec 002.
  - :source-db on :rf.observe/derived-tree. Core never writes or reads it, and neither Spec 009 nor Spec-Schemas documents it. Its only producer is tools/story-mcp egress.cljc scrub-rendered. Prose in story-mcp and re-frame2-pair calls it the record's "default :source-db", a default core does not have. Follow-up outside core.

ITEM 3: all three done.
- Spec 006 Subscription topology now says a subscribe or compute-sub that reaches a cycle emits :rf.error/sub-cycle and recovers to nil without caching. Probe: subscribe returned a nil-deref reaction with an empty cache, and compute-sub returned nil, with emits at :where :subscribe and :compute-sub. Controls in re-frame.sub-cycle-cljs-test: removing the reactive recovery gave 3 errors; making compute-sub throw gave 1 failure.
- The conformance fixture now cites re-frame.projection-cljs-test/derived-tree-without-a-live-frame-fails-closed.
- The prod-gate comment now names what sub-dispose-trace-test's untagged deftests actually pin: substrate dispose keeps a held slot until its unsubscribe, and a throwing input release does not abort the walk. No FRESH-reaction assertion exists, and slot eviction implies the rebuild, so I corrected the comment rather than adding one.

GATES, exit codes captured from the runner:
- core clojure -M:test: exit 0, 1310 tests / 4931 assertions. Baseline 1309 / 4930, delta +1/+1 = the new deftest, as predicted.
- scripts/test-core-prod-gate.sh: exit 0, 1124 tests / 3272 assertions, 203 of 214 namespaces. RF2_MIN_TESTS is unchanged at 1085, because no test was removed.
- check_doc_slugs: exit 0. Sabotaged with a planted anchor: exit 1.
- mkdocs build --strict: exit 0.
- check_conformance_fixture_edn and 27 other ratchets and checks: all exit 0.
- clj-kondo on the changed files: 0 errors, 0 warnings.
- The CLJS lanes rely on the PR's CI. The shadow-cljs lane was not used.
close_reason: Merged as PR #11018 (rebase merge, tip fc82b9074e, 2026-10-08T19:44:55Z). ITEM 1: the leak is real (after (rf/subscribe [:v] {:frame f}), (rf/unsubscribe [:v] {:frame f}) returns nil and leaves {[:v] 1}), but frame-first is a ruled contract (87b3eec977, rf2-bfadc6, Option A), so unsubscribe is unchanged and the choice went to Mike as a decision bead. ITEM 2: deleted the subs cache's 2-arity dispose-entry-now! and unsubscribe!, derivation.graph/node-id, and input-edges' unreachable (= :parametric inputs) check (one new deftest pins the branch). Not done, with reasons: interop/add-on-dispose!'s fallback is reached under the JVM test-react adapter (removing it leaked a layer-2 sub's inputs); acquire-cache-reaction!, its recovery channel and *disposal-cause* stand under the retention Ruling B on rf2-63t1i; sub-algebra-view's 1-arity has a test caller; re-frame.subs/sub-cache-snapshot is documented public API; :source-db is set only by tools/story-mcp and not part of core (recorded, not filed). ITEM 3: Spec 006 cyclic-sub text, the conformance fixture citation and the prod-gate comment corrected. Core JVM 1309/4930 -> 1310/4931; prod gate 1124 tests; RF2_MIN_TESTS unchanged at 1085; rollup 88/88 green.

title: GH #10997: migration/setup - document Windows Gitlibs cache recovery for deeply nested worktrees
description:
GitHub issue #10997 (https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/issues/10997), filed 2026-10-08. Read the issue itself first; this bead summarises it and the issue governs where they differ.

PROBLEM (a claim from the issue, re-check at tip): skills/re-frame-migration/references/setup.md, and the setup skill it points to, explain fresh dependency resolution and the first compile but not the Windows case where a tools.deps build resolving Git dependencies from a deeply nested worktree fails before any application source compiles. Observed: a task-owned Gitlibs cache under the long path failed with "Filename too long"; with child-scoped core.longpaths=true it failed at checkout with "fatal: '$GIT_DIR' too big"; a short, separately owned GITLIBS root resolved and the build completed.

CHANGE (the issue's suggested improvement), as a conditional Windows note in the migration setup guidance:
- Identify cache-preparation failures as environment preparation, separate from the post-coordinate-swap application compile.
- Show a short, unique, task-owned GITLIBS root passed only to the owned build process, and the Git configuration actually used for long paths, saying plainly that it did not overcome the GIT_DIR length failure in that case.
- Require an explicit resource boundary if the short cache lives outside the worktree; preserve shared caches, other workers' repositories and global Git configuration.
- Prefer fresh resolution; if cache reuse is documented, warn that copied Git metadata may still point into another worktree, and verify ownership and references before changing anything.
- After recovery, keep the existing classpath/source-pin checks and compile evidence: cache repair never waives an acceptance gate.

Acceptance: a worker hitting these errors can classify them as environment preparation, recover using only its granted resources, and continue the same migration with no global configuration change and no interference with another worker.

NOT IN SCOPE: the instruction-packet reader issue (#10971, closed) and the stale Pair-server finding (#10787/#10793), both excluded by the issue itself.

GATES: scripts/check_doc_slugs.py covers skills/; nothing validates the prose itself, so say so in the PR body.

CLOSING: the PR body carries "Closes #10997" so the issue closes on merge. Cluster with the bead for #10998 (same skill, different file).

title: re-frame-migration: make the remaining search commands candidate searches under the Step 5 contract (causal-world-inputs src-anchored greps, floor-gate fixed-alias render scan)
description:
## Problem

Several re-frame-migration search commands are presented as if they find everything, but they miss shapes the rule covers. An agent who trusts the count misses sites.

The class was fixed this week one issue at a time:
- 5df8c1bfde (#10864): the M-8 `reg-fx` census found 1 of 5 shapes.
- e0a9745598: the same narrow search sat in three more places.
- 29a8e0d775 (#10872): the `:dispatch-later` search missed vector and bound arguments.
- 276c2f7484 (#10840): host reads behind helpers were missed.
- a527957b5d (#10893): 13 trigger cells were narrower than their rules.
- ef050b81af (#10831): the "closed" index was missing M-76, M-77 and O-14.

The contract is now written down once. `references/inventory-and-plan.md` Step 5 says:
- a trigger cell is where a search starts;
- the full rule is what the search must cover;
- a hit counts only when it resolves through the file's `ns` form.

Recipes now say "candidate search, then acceptance read".

## Remaining commands outside that contract (verified at trunk 9e84689562)

- **`references/causal-world-inputs.md` ~L40-47:** four `rg -n … src` commands (time, randomness, browser/storage facts, M-72 targets). They are anchored at `src`, so they miss test, dev and shared source roots. They are not labelled as candidate searches and do not point at the acceptance read.
- **`references/floor-gate.md` ~L55:** `rg -n 'ReactDOM\.(render|hydrate|unmountComponentAtNode)|reagent\.(dom|core)/render|\b(rdom|r|reagent)/render\b|unmount-component-at-node'`. It only finds the aliases `rdom`, `r` and `reagent`, so any other alias for `reagent.dom` (e.g. `rd/render`) is missed.
- The corpus M-51 search drift belongs to the sibling ownership bead, not this one.

## Direction

- Run each command from the project root, or across every source root the project declares.
- Label each as a candidate search, and link Step 5's acceptance read.
- For the floor-gate scan, match any alias resolved through the file's `ns` form (search for `reagent.dom` requires, then the alias's `/render` calls), or say plainly that the alias set is a starting point.

## Acceptance

- No search command in `skills/re-frame-migration/references/` is anchored at bare `src` or limited to fixed aliases without the candidate-search label and the Step 5 pointer.
- The PR lists every command it touched.
- The skill's structural tests and `check_doc_slugs.py` exit 0.

## Notes

Small; this can run in parallel with the ownership bead, since neither file is in that bead's rule set. No hot-zone files.

title: Qualified route enums don't round-trip: [:enum :sort/desc] emits desc, reads back :desc, app-emitted URL is not-found
description:
## Bug

A route slot declared as a keyword enum with qualified choices, such as `[:enum :sort/asc :sort/desc]`, does not round-trip:
- `route-url` writes `desc`;
- `match-url` reads `desc` back as the bare keyword `:desc`;
- with a validator loaded, the route's own schema rejects `:desc`.

So a URL that re-frame2 itself pushed lands on `:rf.route/not-found` on reload, Back/Forward or a shared link. Without a validator, the value silently changes identity. Two choices with the same bare name (`[:enum :a/x :b/x]`) collapse into one.

## Evidence

Code at 475bdcaacf:
- `implementation/routing/src/re_frame/routing/registry.cljc:716-726` (`normalize-type-form`): it compiles a keyword enum to `[:rf.route/enum-keyword #{"asc" "desc"}]`, the set of `name`s, which drops the namespace.
- `registry.cljc:916-921` (`coerce-by-type-form`): decode is `(keyword v)`, which yields an unqualified keyword.
- `registry.cljc:925-951` (`enum-keyword-token`): encode is `(name v)`.
- `reg-route` places no namespace restriction on enum items. Query *keys* already keep their namespace (`query-key->url-token`, `:953ff`: `:user/id` ↔ `"user/id"`). Enum *values* do not.

Repro (*probed* on the JVM at 9b20bf0093, whose routing sources are identical to 475bdcaacf; script `managed-routing-codec.clj`; validator loaded):

```clojure
(rf/reg-route :r/items {:query [:map [:sort {:optional true} [:enum :sort/asc :sort/desc]]]} "/items")
(rf/reg-route :r/tab   {:params [:map [:tab [:enum :tab/info :tab/edit]]]} "/t/:tab")

(rf.routing/route-url {:to :r/items :query {:sort :sort/desc}})  ;=> "/items?sort=desc"
(rf.routing/match-url "/items?sort=desc")   ;=> {:route-id :r/items :query {:sort :desc} :validation-failed? true}
(rf.routing/route-url {:to :r/tab :params {:tab :tab/edit}})     ;=> "/t/edit"
(rf.routing/match-url "/t/edit")            ;=> {:route-id :r/tab :params {:tab :edit} :validation-failed? true}

(rf/dispatch-sync [:rf.route/navigate {:to :r/items :query {:sort :sort/desc}}])
;; commits {:sort :sort/desc} and pushes /items?sort=desc
(rf/dispatch-sync [:rf.route/handle-url-change "/items?sort=desc" {:rf.route/cause :popstate}])
;; => current {:route-id :rf.route/not-found :params {:url "/items?sort=desc" :reason :validation}}
```

Contract:
- Spec 012:771 says keyword-enum values emit their declared token so that "`match-url(route-url(...))` recovers the canonical enum keyword".
- Spec 012:1335 says "`route-url ∘ match-url` is consequently the identity on every URL re-frame2 emits". `enum-keyword-token`'s docstring cites EP-0012 §Route Prism Laws for the same law.
- The cross-host enum tests use unqualified choices only (`routing_enum_prism_cljs_test.cljc:39, :52`).

## Expected

`[:enum :sort/asc :sort/desc]` round-trips through path and query: the URL re-frame2 emits decodes back to `:sort/desc`.

## Fix direction

Compile each keyword enum into a finite token→keyword map and its inverse, instead of a name set. Use these tokens:
- unqualified choices keep today's wire token (`asc`);
- qualified choices use the namespace-preserving token rule that query keys already use (`sort/desc`, percent-encoded per component).

That also separates same-bare-name choices. Decode looks the token up in the map, and encode looks the keyword up in the inverse.

A cheaper alternative is to reject qualified enum choices at `reg-route` with a loud error. Either closes the hole. The reversible map keeps the capability.

## Acceptance

- New JVM test that fails before the fix. Path and query round-trips preserve `:sort/desc` and `:tab/edit`, including `[:enum :a/x :b/x]`, where both choices survive distinctly.
- Unqualified wire tokens are byte-identical to today (`asc` / `desc`), so the existing `routing_enum_prism_cljs_test.cljc` cases are unchanged.
- The cross-host enum fixtures gain one qualified case, run on both hosts.
- A navigate to a qualified enum value followed by `handle-url-change` of the pushed URL lands on the route, not on `:rf.route/not-found`.

## Notes

- Origin: Sol review (Sol 12, insight 5), adopted by the Opus routing review (D2, action 5).
- Related: the `route-url` defaults bead in this batch also edits `route-url` in `registry.cljc`, so sequence the two. rf2-inhw8 (routing prune follow-ups) also touches `registry.cljc`.
- Hot zones: none.
- Supporting detail: `ai/findings/advisarial-review/opus/routing.md` §D2 Attack 2; `ai/findings/advisarial-review/sol/12-routing.md` §5.

title: An :accept that reshapes the body leaves :decode-marked secrets unredacted, with the trace stamped :classify for off-box
description:
## Bug

When a managed request's `:accept` reshapes the decoded body (`{:ok (:session decoded)}`), the success trace still applies the `:decode` schema's paths to the reshaped value and stamps it `:classify` for off-box export. The marked paths no longer line up, so a `:sensitive?` slot rides unredacted on the dev trace and into every off-box dev-session export: Xray captures, tool-pair / AI-pair egress, saved captures. Spec 014's own lead example and its machine example both reshape this way.

## Evidence

- `implementation/http/src/re_frame/http/transport.cljc:1641-1670` — `handle-response!` runs `:accept` on the decoded body (`:1655`) and hands `(:ok accepted)` to `finalise-success!` (`:1670`) → `dispatch-success!` (`:665-684`). The reply's `:value` is the accepted value; `ctx` still holds the pre-`:accept` body at `:decoded` (`:1641`).
- `transport.cljc:504-508` — `emit-reply-trace!` classifies that `:value` with the input schema: `(update reply :value classify-decoded (:decode ctx))`.
- `transport.cljc:561-566` — it stamps `:rf.http/off-box-body (off-box-body-disposition (:decode ctx))`, which is `:classify` for any vector `:decode` (`privacy_body.cljc:231-258`).
- `implementation/epoch/src/re_frame/epoch/tool_pair.cljc:1762-1795` — the off-box projector omits only `:omit`-stamped bodies; a `:classify` body passes through as it is.
- The `:rf.http/accept-failure` path is correct: it classifies the pre-`:accept` body (`transport.cljc:1653`).

Repro (*probed* at trunk on the JVM: a real `:rf.http/managed` request against an in-process server; the `:rf.http/replied` row is captured and passed through `omit-off-box-http-bodies`):

```clojure
;; response body: {"session":{"token":"SECRET"}}
{:request  {:url (str base "/x")}
 :decode   [:map [:session [:map [:token {:sensitive? true} :string]]]]
 :accept   (fn [v] {:ok (:session v)})
 :reply-to [:test/ok]}
```

| Case | On-box trace `:value` | Stamp | Off-box projected `:value` |
|---|---|---|---|
| Control: no `:accept` | `{:session {:token :rf/redacted}}` | `:classify` | `{:session {:token :rf/redacted}}` |
| Reshaping `:accept` | `{:token "SECRET"}` | `:classify` | `{:token "SECRET"}` |

The app receives `{:token "SECRET"}` in the reshaping case, which is correct: delivery stays raw.

Contract: Spec 014 §Response-body classification rule 1 (`spec/014-HTTPRequests.md:1415`) says a `:sensitive?` slot redacts "before the body rides a `:rf.http/*` trace event". Rule 3 (`:1417`) says a body whose shape is unknown fails closed off-box. The lead example (`:44-57`, `:115-117`) projects `(:article decoded)` out of `ArticleResponse`, and the machine example (`:1179-1180`) projects `(:session v)` out of `SessionResponse`, so the taught pattern is the one that leaks.

## Expected

A reshaped success value never ships a `:decode`-marked secret, either on the dev trace or off-box.

## Fix direction

- In `emit-reply-trace!`, treat a success `:value` that is not `identical?` to `(:decoded ctx)` as unschematized:
  - stamp `:rf.http/off-box-body :omit`;
  - on-box, redact `:value` wholesale when the `:decode` schema declares any `:sensitive?` mark.
- When `:value` is the decoded body itself, keep per-slot classification. That covers no `:accept` at all, and the domain-check form `(if ok? {:ok decoded} {:failure …})`.
- Never redact before `:accept`, because that would change application data.
- Add one sentence to 014 §Response-body classification rule 6: the success `:value` is classified per-slot only when it is the decoded body itself.

## Acceptance

- New JVM regression, in the style of `http_privacy_integration_test.clj`. For the reshaping `:accept` above:
  - the `:rf.http/replied` row is stamped `:omit`;
  - its on-box `:value` is `:rf/redacted`;
  - no `"SECRET"` appears in the `omit-off-box-http-bodies` output;
  - the app still receives `{:token "SECRET"}`.
  The test fails today, where the row is stamped `:classify` and carries the raw token.
- Controls stay green: no `:accept`, and an `:accept` returning `{:ok decoded}`, both keep `{:session {:token :rf/redacted}}` with `:classify`.
- Accept-failure rows are unchanged.

## Notes

- Origin: Sol review (14 §2), probed during the Opus cross-review; re-probed end to end at trunk.
- Related: the HTTP classifier draft for `[:ref]` decoders and vector-of-maps bodies (rf2-mn2ht.48) touches the same emit site and `privacy_body.cljc`. Do both in one worker, or sequence them.
- Hot-zone files: none (`spec/014-HTTPRequests.md` is not hot).
- Supporting detail: `ai/findings/advisarial-review/opus/http.md` D12.1 and Action 1a; `ai/findings/advisarial-review/sol/14-http.md` §2.

title: UIx use-sub keys on the frame keyword only: after a same-id destroy+recreate a mounted component reads the dead frame
description:
## Bug

A mounted UIx `use-sub` that survives a same-id frame destroy-and-recreate keeps reading the destroyed frame's state, and it never gets another notification. `use-frame` in the same component retargets to the new frame, so the component dispatches into the new frame while it displays the old one. Users notice this when a component reads a session frame that the app resets with `destroy-frame!` followed by `make-frame` under the same id, for example on logout or a tenant switch.

## Evidence

Trunk 475bdcaacf. All paths are under `implementation/core/src/re_frame/`.

- `substrate/spine.cljs:3095-3103`: the hook's `stable-key` is `#js [frame-kw query-v]`, reused whenever both are `=`. The frame keyword is equal across incarnations, so the key does not change when the frame is recreated.
- `substrate/spine.cljs:3193-3222`: the `render-snapshot` memo depends only on `#js [stable-key]`.
- `substrate/spine.cljs:3363-3557`: `subscribe-fn` is memoised on `#js [stable-key]`, so React never re-runs it for the same key.
- `substrate/spine.cljs:3318-3339`: `get-snap` derefs the reaction held in `committed-ref` whenever its tag is `identical?` to the current `stable-key`.
- `substrate/spine.cljs:3464-3482`: on disposal, the committed reaction's reacquisition callback deliberately lets go when `(rf.frame/frame stable-frame-kw)` is nil, which is the case during `destroy-frame!`. Nothing clears `committed-ref`, and nothing re-subscribes after the successor frame exists.
- `substrate/spine.cljs:974-1000`: `-dispose` clears the reaction's watchers (`:986`), so the hook's `on-change` watch is gone.
- `substrate/spine.cljs:939` and `:851-855`, with `:617-646`: `-deref` on the disposed reaction still runs its recompute closure, which derefs the source containers it was built over. Those are the destroyed frame's containers.
- `adapter/use_frame.cljs:139-157`: `use-frame` keys its memo on `frame-incarnation-token` as well as the keyword. Its docstring says the bundle "is pinned to the incarnation it was captured against, never to the address", so its next render yields the successor's ops.

Repro (*read*; traced in source, not run):
1. Install the UIx adapter, `(rf/make-frame {:id :f})`, seed `{:n 1}`, and `(rf/reg-sub :n (fn [db _] (:n db)))`.
2. Mount one component under `($ uix/frame-provider {:frame :f} …)` that calls both `(use-sub [:n])` and `(use-frame)`.
3. `(rf/destroy-frame! :f)`, then `(rf/make-frame {:id :f})` and seed it with `{:n 2}`.
4. Re-render the same mounted instance by changing an unrelated parent prop.

Expected: it shows 2, and later writes to the new `:f` re-render it. Traced result: `stable-key` is unchanged, so both memos hit and `get-snap` derefs the disposed reaction, which recomputes over the old frame's container. The component shows 1, and no later write to the new `:f` reaches it. A `dispatch` from its `use-frame` ops lands in the new `:f`.

Contract contrast: Spec 006 §Lifetime contract, guarantee 2 "No stale reads" (`spec/006-ReactiveSubstrate.md:1025`): "There is no path that returns a value from a destroyed frame's cache." The only witness across a reincarnation covers `use-frame` (`core/test/re_frame/adapter/react_shared_suite.cljs:3192`, `assert-use-frame-retargets-across-a-same-id-reincarnation`), not `use-sub`.

The ratom family (Reagent, reagent-slim) is not affected, because every Reagent render subscribes through the cache again.

## Expected

`use-sub` identifies its frame by incarnation, as `use-frame` does. After a same-id recreate, the next render of a mounted instance reads and listens to the successor.

## Fix direction

Add `(rf.frame/frame-incarnation-token frame-kw)` to `stable-key`. Compare it with `identical?` beside the existing `=` checks, as `use-frame` already does. The `committed-ref` and `provisional-ref` tags and the cleanup guards then follow the new key without further change. A nil token, when the id is not live at render, is a legitimate key value, as it is in `use-frame`.

## Acceptance

- Extend `assert-use-frame-retargets-across-a-same-id-reincarnation` (or add a sibling row in `react_shared_suite.cljs`) with a mounted `use-sub`, in both the ambient form and the explicit `{:frame :f}` form. After destroy, same-id create and a re-render of the same instance:
  - it renders the successor's value;
  - a later write to the successor re-renders it;
  - the successor's sub-cache ref-counts balance after unmount.
- The row fails on today's code.
- Control: with an unchanged incarnation, `stable-key` stays `identical?` across renders and `subscribe-fn` is not re-invoked. Existing ref-count churn tests stay green.

## Notes

- Origin: Sol review (report 18, insight 1), adopted by the Opus core-reactive-substrate and adapters cross-reviews.
- Related: rf2-1frc (closed) added the reacquisition seam for eviction by re-registration. Its frame-liveness guard is what makes the hook let go on destroy. The reincarnation case was not part of it. Sequence this with the bead on the 4 ms provisional escrow (rf2-mn2ht.38), because both edit `use-subscribe-2` in `spine.cljs`.
- Hot zones: none in code. If Spec 006 gains a sentence stating the hook key, that touches `spec/006-ReactiveSubstrate.md`.
- Supporting detail: `ai/findings/advisarial-review/opus/adapters.md` decision 12 and action 1; `ai/findings/advisarial-review/sol/18-adapter-uix.md` §1.
notes:
== DISPATCHED (mayor, 2026-10-10 18:54:12 AUSEST) == Clustered with rf2-mn2ht.4, .42, .41 and .36 (one defect pattern: state keyed on a frame keyword survives a same-id reincarnation) for one worker on worktree incarnation-leaks, branch worker/incarnation-leaks, one PR. Do not dispatch a second worker onto it until that worker reports.
== WORKER RESULT (incarnation-leaks, 2026-10-10 20:20 AUSEST) == FIXED in PR #11061 (commit 3754f24928), not closed; the mayor closes it on merge.

Where the fix lives:
- The fix site is implementation/core/src/re_frame/substrate/spine.cljs, not adapters/uix as the dispatch brief said. Only use-subscribe-2's stable-key derivation changed.
- The stable key now carries (rf.frame/frame-incarnation-token frame-kw), compared with identical? beside the = checks, as use-frame does. A nil token is a legitimate key value.
- The committed and provisional tags and the identity-guarded cleanup follow the new key. The 4 ms escrow (rf2-mn2ht.38) is untouched.

The test:
- The row lives in the UIx adapter's own test: uix_use_sub_dom_cljs_test/use-sub-follows-a-same-id-reincarnation. It was kept out of core's react_shared_suite so as not to touch core tests.
- It covers the ambient and the explicit {:frame} forms in one mounted instance. After destroy, a same-id create and a parent re-render, the instance reads the successor, re-renders on a later write, and holds 2 refs that drop to 0 on unmount. A same-incarnation re-render is the control.

Evidence:
- Red before and red again: scratch run 38037640576, :browser-test. The instance read [1 1] where [2 2] belongs, a later write never reached it ([1 1] where [3 3] belongs), and the successor's ref-count was 0 where 2 belongs.
- Green after: PR #11061 :browser-test, run 38039547560. The delta is +1 test / +6 assertions against main run 38038107033, as predicted.

The UIx use-sub hook's key now includes the frame's incarnation, so after a same-id destroy and recreate a mounted component reads and listens to the new frame. The hook lives in implementation/core/src/re_frame/substrate/spine.cljs (not adapters/uix as the bead said); only its key changed, and the new test sits in the UIx adapter's own tests. spec/006 not edited (it does not document the hook key).
