title: Resources: a generated-id mutation still pending across an epoch restore is settled as :error but never retired
description:
Found by the rf2-mn2ht.10 worker (PR #11064, merged at 56835a6f99). A CLAIM to reproduce at tip.

Since #11064, a generated-id :rf.mutation/execute row retires itself after an accepted reply: both settle handlers dispatch [:rf.mutation/clear {:instance id}] as their last effect. But a generated-id mutation that is still PENDING when an epoch restore runs is settled as :error by the restore path, and no reply ever arrives for it, so the retirement never fires and its instance row and ledger rows stay forever.

DIRECTION (smallest): the restore path's settle-as-:error for a generated-id instance also retires it, through the same clear machinery, so every settle of a generated-id instance ends in retirement. Caller-supplied ids keep their rows, as today.

ACCEPTANCE: a test with a pending generated-id mutation across an epoch restore leaves zero instance rows and zero [:rf.mutation ...] ledger rows; red at base, red again with the fix reverted.

Fence: implementation/resources (mutation_events, mutation_runtime) and, if the restore path lives there, implementation/epoch. Spec 016's §Retirement phase step may need one clause.
notes:
== WORKER RESULT (resources-2, 2026-10-10 21:15 AUSEST) == DEFECT HELD; FIXED on branch worker/resources-2, commit 786c368a6b (after rebase), PR #11076. Not closed; the mayor closes on merge.

Where the restore settle lives: implementation/resources, NOT implementation/epoch. Epoch's restore reaches it only through the :resources/reconcile-on-restore late-bind hook (epoch tool_pair.cljc reconcile-runtime-db-on-restore -> re-frame.resources.ssr/reconcile-on-restore -> dangle-pending-mutations!). No epoch file was touched.

Red before (src at the rf2-v2fw5 commit, new test added): resources_mutation_cljs_test/generated-instance-pending-across-a-restore-retires. Execute an anonymous :m/save (capturing transport, so it stays pending), then install the frame's own runtime-db back through ssr/reconcile-on-restore with a causal :restore-time-ms, as restoring an epoch captured mid-write does. Exit 1, 3 failures: 1 instance row and 1 [:rf.mutation ...] ledger row survived (expected 0 and 0), and the leftover generated row showed again in the supplied-instance block.

Fix: dangle-pending-mutations! (ssr.cljc) still dangles every pending instance to :error / :dangling-on-restore, and for a GENERATED id then retires it in the same pure pass: dissoc the instance row and work-ledger/drop-rows-for-key [:rf.mutation iid] -- the two primitives :rf.mutation/clear composes. A dispatch was not possible there (the reconcile is a pure install-time pass). A caller-supplied id keeps its dangled :error row and ledger row. The generated-id predicate moved from mutation_events (private) to mutation_runtime (public) so the settle handlers and the restore share one definition. The :rf.resource/restored trace still lists the retired id under :dangled-mutations.

Test updates: the new test above (generated: 0 rows / 0 ledger rows; supplied: :error :dangling-on-restore row and exactly its own ledger row). resources_restore_cljs_test/late-pre-restore-mutation-reply-is-suppressed-end-to-end used a generated id while asserting the dangled instance stays :error; its stated premise is the instance-level :current-work gate on a persisting dangled row, so it now uses a caller-supplied id (:article/edit-form) and is otherwise unchanged.

Spec 016: the §Mutations instance-id invariant gains one sentence (a generated-id instance still pending at an epoch restore is retired by that restore); §Restore and replay part 2 says the restore's settle is a generated-id instance's last, so the same pass retires it, and a supplied instance keeps its row. Phase-order step 7 is unchanged (it orders the reply path).

Evidence:

title: HTTP: a repeated non-Set-Cookie response header is a vector on the JVM but a folded string on CLJS; the JVM folds it (mayor's ruling, RFC 9110)
description:
Found by the rf2-vk20k worker (PR #11066, merged at 13498ca5f5), from reading the code, not from a probe. Probe first.

DEFECT: Spec 014's Successful-response metadata section (the :meta :headers paragraph) promises one cross-host shape for the response-header map: string -> string, or string -> vector of strings for a multi-valued header. The JVM (jvm-headers->map) returns a vector for a repeated non-Set-Cookie header. CLJS (fetch-headers->map) receives Fetch's comma-folded string, and Fetch offers no way to unfold it except getSetCookie, so CLJS cannot produce the vector. The two hosts disagree for a repeated non-Set-Cookie header.

MAYOR'S RULING (2026-10-10 21:35 AUSEST; Mike may reverse): option (a). The JVM comma-folds every repeated response header except Set-Cookie, as RFC 9110 §5.3 permits and as Fetch already delivers. Set-Cookie stays a vector on both hosts. Spec 014's :meta :headers paragraph is amended to say exactly that. Reason: the spec already promises ONE cross-host shape, CLJS cannot change, and folding is the RFC's own rule. The alternative, documenting the host difference, breaks that promise. The ruling exists only to choose which host moves.

ACCEPTANCE: a JVM test with a repeated non-Set-Cookie response header (for example two Vary values) asserts the folded string; red at base, red again with the fix reverted. A Set-Cookie test asserts the vector on the JVM, unchanged. Spec 014 is amended.

Fence: implementation/http (jvm-headers->map and its tests) and spec/014-HTTPRequests.md. Neither is a hot zone.
notes:
== WORKER: fixed in PR #11079 (http-3 worker, 2026-10-10 21:40 AUSEST, base 13498ca5f5, rebased onto 753addc602) ==

PROBE at base, one response with two Vary values and two Set-Cookie lines. The JVM jvm-headers->map gave vary ["Accept" "Origin"] and set-cookie as a 2-vector. Fetch Headers on Node v24.13.0 gave forEach vary "Accept, Origin" and getSetCookie as the 2 lines. So the hosts disagreed, as the bead says.

FIX per the mayor's ruling. jvm-headers->map now gives a single value as its string, and a repeated Set-Cookie as a vector of its verbatim lines. Any other repeated header is joined with ", " in wire order, which is RFC 9110 §5.3's combination and Fetch's own separator. Spec 014's Successful-response metadata :headers paragraph now says exactly that. The docstrings on jvm-headers->map, fetch-headers->map (docstring only in the :cljs branch, no CLJS code changed) and reply/success-reply were updated to match.

TEST: re-frame.http-set-cookie-parity-cljs-test/repeated-header-folds-except-set-cookie-cross-host. It is a .cljc test that runs on both hosts. One map must read vary as "Accept, Origin" and set-cookie as the 2-line vector. Scoped runs:
- red at base: exit 1, only the vary assertion failed;
- green with the fix: exit 0, 4 tests / 6 assertions;
- red again with transport_jvm.cljc reverted alone to its base blob: exit 1, same single failure.

After that the file was restored, and its blob hash matched the committed blob. The full http JVM lane went from 249 tests / 744 assertions to 250 / 746, exit 0.

Spec 014's :headers paragraph says exactly that. Cross-host .cljc test repeated-header-folds-except-set-cookie-cross-host: red at base (exit 1, only the vary assertion), green with the fix (exit 0), red again with transport_jvm.cljc reverted alone (exit 1), restored by blob hash. http JVM lane 249/744 -> 250/746, exit 0; CI 88/88 green.

title: api_md_check silently drops API.md var rows with an unknown kind marker, misspelt tier or missing backticks
description:
## Bug

The `spec/API.md` projection check (`api_md_check`) silently drops any var row it cannot classify. Three cases vanish:
- an unknown kind marker (`Macro` instead of `M`);
- a misspelt tier word (`frnt-porch`);
- a first cell that has lost its backticks.

A dropped row is never compared with the manifest, and the check still reports OK. The only backstop is a floor of 50 rows against about 150 live rows, which catches a collapse of the whole table but not one bad row.

## Evidence

All file:line references are at trunk 475bdcaacf (unchanged at b375cd0e42).

- `implementation/scripts/api-manifest/src/re_frame/api_manifest/api_md_check.clj`:
  - `parse-var-rows` (`:190-237`) keeps a row only when three things hold: the first cell is one backticked identifier, `var-kind-token` (`:108-115`) matches `^(Fn|M|Var)\b`, and `first-tier-token` (`:98-106`) finds a closed-vocabulary tier word.
  - Every other row takes `(recur remaining tier-column-index parsed-rows)` (`:235-236`), which drops it with no problem recorded.
  - The docstring (`:197-201`) says so: "That disappearance is silent by construction."
  - The floor `min-var-rows` is 50 (`:70-90`).
- `implementation/scripts/api-manifest/test/re_frame/api_manifest/api_md_check_test.clj:57-67` pins a `Macro` row vanishing.
- Repro (*probed*, JVM, from `implementation/scripts/api-manifest`):

  ```clojure
  (re-frame.api-manifest.api-md-check/parse-var-rows
    [[1 "| API | M/Fn | Signature | Status | Tier | Spec |"]
     [2 "|---|---|---|---|---|---|"]
     [3 "| `reg-event` | M | sig | v1 | front-porch | 001 |"]
     [4 "| `dispatch` | Macro | sig | v1 | front-porch | 002 |"]   ; unknown marker
     [5 "| `subscribe` | Fn | sig | v1 | frnt-porch | 006 |"]      ; misspelt tier
     [6 "| reg-sub | Fn | sig | v1 | front-porch | 006 |"]])      ; lost backticks
  ;; => one row, line 3. Lines 4-6 disappear, and check! would report OK.
  ```

- Census of the live `spec/API.md` (*probed*):
  - 150 var rows parse.
  - In Tier-column tables, exactly 3 backticked non-keyword first cells are dropped today, and all 3 are legitimately not var rows: two `(rf/configure! {…})` forms with a `—` marker (`:670`, `:695`) and `[:rf.interceptor/path <path-vector>]` (`:872`).
  - So a rule keyed on "the first cell is a single backticked *symbol-shaped* identifier" flags nothing on trunk.
- **Contract.** The ns docstring (`:1-11`) says every var row "must resolve to a manifest row, the Tier the row states must MATCH the manifest's `:tier`, and the kind … must MATCH". A dropped row is checked against neither.

## Expected

A Tier-table row whose first cell is a single backticked symbol identifier, but whose kind marker or tier cell the parser cannot recognise, fails the check and names its line.

## Fix direction

- In `parse-var-rows`, decide whether a row is var-shaped from its first cell alone: a backticked symbol-like identifier, not a keyword, list form or vector.
- Then grade the marker and the tier. Emit an `:unclassifiable-row` problem (line, cell values) instead of skipping.
- Keep the floor.
- Change the `Macro` test to expect a problem.

## Acceptance

- Unit tests, all on synthetic lines:
  - a row with marker `Macro` yields a problem naming its line;
  - a row with tier `frnt-porch` does the same;
  - a backticked symbol whose marker cell is prose does the same;
  - the three legitimate non-var shapes (a `(rf/configure! …)` form, a `[:vector …]`, a `:keyword`) are still skipped.
- The live `check!` stays green.
- `clojure -M:test` in `implementation/scripts/api-manifest` passes.

## Notes

- **Origin:** Sol review (surface 35, insight 3), adopted by the Opus tooling cross-review (D10, action 2e).
- **Related:** rf2-mn2ht.59 and rf2-mn2ht.60 are in the same artefact, with no file overlap; one worker could take all three.
- **Hot-zone files:** none. `spec/API.md` itself does not change.
- **Supporting detail:** `ai/findings/advisarial-review/opus/tooling.md` §D10; `ai/findings/advisarial-review/sol/35-api-manifest-spec-resource.md` §3.
notes:
== WORKER SUMMARY (2026-10-10, PR #11083, commit b1259a7e7a) ==
FIXED, as the Fix direction and Acceptance specify. The premise held at the branch base (753addc602): parse-var-rows dropped any row whose marker or tier word it could not read, with no problem recorded.

Fix (api_md_check.clj):
- In a Tier table, the first cell alone decides whether a row is a var-row. `var-ident-re` matches a single back-ticked symbol, bare or qualified. Its first character excludes `:`, `(`, `[`, `{`, a quote, `#` and a digit, so keyword, list and vector cells are still skipped.
- A var-row whose M/Fn marker (Fn / M / Var) or tier word cannot be read becomes `{:kind :unclassifiable-row :line :raw :kind-cell :tier-cell}`. check! prints it as `L<n> UNCLASSIFIABLE`.
- parse-var-rows and parse-api-md-var-rows now return `{:var-rows :problems}`. The 50-row floor is kept.
- `var-kind-marker?` was removed, since nothing uses it.
- The live parse is value-identical to the pre-change parse: 150 var-rows, 0 problems.

Acceptance tests: parse-var-rows-flags-a-var-row-it-cannot-classify, plus the Macro test changed to expect a problem. They cover a Macro marker, a frnt-porch tier and a prose marker cell, and check that the (rf/configure! …), [:rf.interceptor/path …] and :rf.http/managed shapes are still skipped. Results, scoped to api-md-check-test:
- red at base: exit 1, 6 failures;
- green: exit 0 (5 tests / 16 assertions);
- red-again with the src reverted alone: exit 1, 6 failures. The restore was verified by blob hash.
- Live plant: the dispatch row's marker set to `Macro` at spec/API.md L198 made api-md-check exit 1 with `L198 UNCLASSIFIABLE`. Before the fix that row was dropped silently.

GAP LEFT OPEN, as the bead's own Fix direction leaves it: a var-row whose first cell has LOST its backticks (the Bug's third case) is still skipped. A marker-keyed rule (any row whose M/Fn cell is Fn/M/Var is a var-row) would catch it. At tip it would also flag two grouped multi-var rows that api_md_check currently skips without grading them:
- `app-db-value` / `frame-state-value` (cross-ref, Tier `advanced/tooling`);
- `snapshot-registrar` / `restore-registrar!` / `make-reset-runtime-fixture` (Tier `testing`).
Splitting those rows into one row per var would let that rule land. Not done here: it is outside the Acceptance, and the posture is the smaller change.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #11083, merged at 1ad249eff4 (2026-10-10 AUSEST), for the two cases the Fix direction covers. In a Tier table, a single back-ticked symbol in the first cell makes a var row. A var row whose M/Fn marker or tier word cannot be read becomes an :unclassifiable-row problem, printed as L<n> UNCLASSIFIABLE, instead of being dropped. The live parse is unchanged (150 var rows, 0 problems). Acceptance: red at base (exit 1, 6 failures), green (exit 0, 5 tests / 16 assertions), red again with the src reverted alone. A live plant of Macro at spec/API.md L198 reds with L198 UNCLASSIFIABLE. The third case, a var row that has lost its backticks, is still skipped; it is filed as rf2-mn2ht.67, along with the two grouped rows that must be split first.

title: configure! with :epoch-history but no epoch artefact applies nothing and warns nothing, unlike a misspelt key
description:
## Bug

`(rf/configure! {:epoch-history {:depth 100}})` in a build without the `day8/re-frame2-epoch` artefact applies nothing and emits nothing, not even a trace warning. A misspelt key gets `:rf.warning/unknown-configure-key`, but a correctly spelled key whose producer is absent is swallowed. The programmer believes epoch history is configured when it is not.

## Evidence

**Where (trunk 475bdcaacf):**
- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/core.cljc:2854-2856`:

  ```clojure
  (when-let [opts (:epoch-history config-map)]
    (when-let [f (rf.late-bind/get-fn :epoch/configure!)]
      (f opts)))
  ```

  With the hook unbound, the key is dropped silently.
- `core.cljc:2881`: unknown bare keys, by contrast, emit `:rf.warning/unknown-configure-key`.
- The `configure!` docstring (`core.cljc:2720-2830`) documents the production `:trace-buffer` no-op, but says nothing about `:epoch-history` without its artefact.
- `implementation/core/test/re_frame/configure_test.clj:60-70` covers `current-config` omitting an absent producer on read. It does not cover feedback for a requested write.

**Repro (*probed*):** JVM, `clojure -M` from `implementation/core` (the core classpath has no epoch artefact), plain-atom adapter. Run at HEAD 9b20bf0093, whose `implementation/core` is byte-identical to 475bdcaacf.

```clojure
(rf/register-listener! :trace ::probe (fn [ev] …collect :rf.warning/* operations…))
(rf/configure! {:epoch-histroy {:depth 5}})   ; trace listener receives :rf.warning/unknown-configure-key
(rf/configure! {:epoch-history {:depth 5}})   ; returns nil; 0 warnings; nothing printed
```

**Contract:** `spec/Principles.md:83-87` and `spec/Conventions.md` §No silent swallow say that a recognised input the runtime cannot honour must signal. `spec/009-Instrumentation.md:2275` does let the epoch *read and listener* surfaces degrade silently, returning `[]`, `false` or `nil`. `configure!` is a write of explicit configuration, and that row does not list it.

## Expected

In a dev build, supplying `:epoch-history` without the epoch artefact emits one warning naming the key and the artefact to add. The other keys still apply, and production stays a silent no-op.

## Fix direction

- In `configure!`, when `:epoch-history` is present and `:epoch/configure!` is unbound, emit a dev-gated warning carrying the Maven coordinate from the core feature registry (`re-frame.features`). Then continue with the remaining keys.
- Either use a new id with its 009 catalogue row, or give the existing `:rf.warning/unknown-configure-key` a distinct `:reason`. A new id reads more truthfully, because the key is known.

## Acceptance

- New core JVM test (the epoch artefact is absent on that classpath): `configure!` with `:epoch-history` emits exactly one warning carrying the epoch coordinate, and still applies a sibling `:elision` key. It fails at trunk.
- With the epoch artefact present (an epoch-artefact test), no warning is emitted.
- The core production gate emits nothing.

## Notes

- Origin: Sol review (sol/01 §4, read); reproduced by JVM probe at trunk.

title: mcp-conformance tests give the old :isError cache-bypass reason (two sites)
description:
PR #11106 (rf2-g8oxc) deleted re-frame2-pair-mcp's precheck path, so its response cache is result-hash only. Under that cache, the reason "an unflagged failure can mask a later success" is false: a repeated error and a later success hash differently. The true reason the cache bypasses :isError results is that the cache-hit marker is a success result, so it must not stand in for a failure. PR #11106 changed every site inside its fence. Two sites outside it still give the old reason (CLAIMS; re-check at tip):
- tools/mcp-conformance/test/_runner.cjs near line 521, in a thrown error message;
- tools/mcp-conformance/test/live-re-frame2-pair-iserror.cjs near line 16, in a comment.
Reword both to the true reason. If a test asserts on the thrown message text, update the assertion in step. No behaviour change.
Gates: the mcp-conformance node tests that cover _runner.cjs, if they run without shadow-cljs; otherwise cite CI. Sequence after PR #11106 merges, so the wording matches what landed.
notes: == WORKER 2026-10-11 AUSEST: PR #11111 (draft until done, then ready). A census of "mask" over tools/mcp-conformance/test (line-wise, whitespace-flattened, and comment-stripped) found THREE true sites, not the two the description named: _runner.cjs assertIsErrorMatchesOk's thrown message, plus live-re-frame2-pair-iserror.cjs's header comment AND its assertReadFailureIsError failure message. All three now give the result-hash reason in PR #11106's wording: an unflagged failure is cache-eligible, so a repeat can come back as a success-shaped cache-hit marker rather than as the failure. The iserror failure message also drops "transient", which only mattered under the old reason. The other "mask" hits (_runner.cjs teardown, end-to-end-flag-gates, end-to-end-re-frame2-pair, end-to-end-story, live-re-frame2-pair-redaction, the classifications fixture) are unrelated senses and were left alone. is-error-matches-ok.test.cjs asserts only on the unchanged ":ok? false but isError is not true" prefix, so no assertion moved. Gates: node --check on both files exit 0; the unit test and the live variant were not run locally (no SDK install; build lane not granted), so the PR's CI is the gate. PR #11106 was still OPEN when this was written; the wording matched its diff at head 12b5f7e312, so re-check if that PR's wording changes before it merges.
close_reason: Merged as PR #11111 at 655a1cfc18. Three sites in tools/mcp-conformance/test (the message thrown by _runner.cjs assertIsErrorMatchesOk, and the header comment and assertReadFailureIsError message in live-re-frame2-pair-iserror.cjs) now give the result-hash reason for the :isError cache bypass: an unflagged failure is cache-eligible, so a repeat can come back as a success-shaped cache-hit marker instead of the failure. No behaviour change; no assertion matched the changed text. node --check exit 0 on both files.

title: Demote make-machine-handler to internal: drop the public var, its late-bind hook, the registration-home guard and its error id; Spec 005 teaches two test levels
description:
## Ruled work

Ruled under `rf2-mn2ht.26` (delegated by Mike, 2026-10-10 23:45 AUSEST, at HEAD `200a67df2d`); the full ruling, with its reasoning and the rejected options, is the `== RULING ==` note on that bead. This bead carries the work.

**Demote `re-frame.machines/make-machine-handler` to internal.** The fn stays in `re-frame.machines.lifecycle-fx.registration` for its two callers. The public var, its late-bind hook, the registration-home guard and its error id all go. Spec 005 teaches two test levels: pure `machine-transition`, and registered in a frame. No replacement testing API.

## Problem

`make-machine-handler` is public for one documented job, Spec 005 §Testing "Level 2" (call the unregistered handler with hand-built coeffects). That example threw `:rf.error/no-frame-context` for as long as it existed, until PR #11091 (merged `45960a05c8`, 2026-10-10) added `:rf.frame/id`. Its other stated job, at 005:1039, is "code-gen and loader pipelines minting handlers for computed ids". That is `reg-machine*`'s job, and it is what Story's loader actually calls (`tools/story/src/re_frame/story/loaders.cljc:194`, `rf.machines/reg-machine*`). Nothing outside the registration namespace calls the factory.

The seam is not a clean one:

- the caller hand-builds framework-internal coeffect keys (`:rf.frame/id`, `:rf.db/runtime`, `[:rf.runtime/machines :snapshots <id>]`);
- it refuses any machine carrying a `[:schemas :data]` schema (`:rf.error/machine-schema-requires-reg-machine`);
- the handler it returns is not pure. It reads the frame registry, emits traces, and on a machine's first boot writes `:sensitive` / `:large` elision claims into whichever live frame `:rf.frame/id` names (`registration.cljc:1161-1164`, `lower-at-spawn!`).

The project spends a guard, an error id, a drift-gate rule, four skill warnings and an evals line fencing this door off.

## Evidence (HEAD `200a67df2d`)

- **Production callers:** `register-machine-event!` (`registration.cljc:1440`, the body of `reg-machine*`) and `handler-meta-for` (`:1535`, spawned actors). Both are in the same namespace.
- **Public surface:**
  - the re-export at `implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines.cljc:80`;
  - the late-bind publication at `machines.cljc:425`, plus the directory row at `implementation/core/src/re_frame/late_bind/directory.cljc:364-366`. A repo-wide search for `:machines/make-machine-handler` finds only those two sites and migration rename rows, so nothing reads the hook.
- **Comment mentions outside the framework:** `examples/patterns/websocket/connection.cljs:85`, `examples/capabilities/machines/state_machine_walkthrough/core.cljc:215`, `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/epoch/view.cljs:3769`, `docs/tools/playground/test/smoke.test.mjs:103`, `testbeds/deep_machine/README.md:52`.
- **Guard:**
  - `*in-registration-home?*` at `registration.cljc:74-80`, with its comment block at `:54-66`;
  - the throw at `:986-1014`;
  - `binding` forms at `:1439` and `:1534`.
- **Two normative homes disagree about the factory's job:**
  - 005:1039: "public — the composition seam for callers that must build a handler *without* registering one, such as code-gen and loader pipelines minting handlers for computed ids";
  - `spec/API.md:1004`: "For Level-2 tests, not a registration door."
- **Level 1 gives the same answer for an ordinary transition** (JVM probe quoted in the ruling note on `rf2-mn2ht.26`). For an ordinary transition, Level 2 returns what `machine-transition` returns (same snapshot, same `:fx`), wrapped in the runtime-db envelope. Its one unique reach is the frame-free first-boot cascade, which a frame test covers in about four JVM lines.

## Fix direction

**One sequential worker, one PR.** Seven hot-zone holdings move together, and `spec/API.md` with its two manifests is one holding.

### Code

- `implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines.cljc`:
  - drop the re-export (`:80`) and the `set-fn!` (`:425`);
  - drop the mention in the ns docstring (`:27`).
- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/late_bind/directory.cljc:364-366`: drop the row. `late_bind_drift_test.clj` pins the directory against the publication sites, so both go in the same commit.
- `registration.cljc`:
  - delete `*in-registration-home?*` and its comment block;
  - delete the guard (`:986-1014`);
  - unwrap the two `binding` forms but keep their calls.
  - Respell `:where 'rf-machines/make-machine-handler` at `:1042`, per the `rf2-uewm` ruling (`:where` names a public var, a reserved event id or a full namespace). The handler runs for registered singletons and spawned actors alike, so the full namespace `re-frame.machines.lifecycle-fx.registration` is the safe spelling.
  - Then ratchet `scripts/where-sym-baseline.edn:24` (`"rf-machines/make-machine-handler" 1`) out, as `scripts/check_thrown_error_messages.py` directs.
- Docstrings and comments that present the factory as public or as "the bare path", reworded present-tense. Internal references to the fn by name are fine.
  - Framework: `core/src/re_frame/core.cljc:763`, `machines/deps.edn:4`, `cofx_attach.cljc:485`, `parallel.cljc:386`, `validation.cljc:5, 836, 2343`, `spawn.cljc:481, 1797`, `resolver.cljc:37`, `join.cljc:21`, `registration.cljc:4, 274, 292, 1366-1368, 1436, 1470, 1520, 1531`.
  - Outside the framework: the five comment sites listed above.

### Tests

- `implementation/core/test/re_frame/smoke_test.clj:143`: move the bare `(rf/reg-event :flow (rf.machines/make-machine-handler …))` to `rf/reg-machine` (or `rf.machines/reg-machine*`).
- Point the registration-refusal probes at the internal var `re-frame.machines.lifecycle-fx.registration/make-machine-handler`:
  - `machine_cofx_attach_test.clj:30`
  - `machine_cofx_sub_source_test.clj:41`
  - `parallel_root_on_test.clj:20`
  - `parallel_test.clj:9`
  - `region_on_done_test.clj:77`
  - `region_cross_region_target_test.clj:16, 34, 43`

  The two cofx tests need the factory's `index-ensure-sets` step, so `validate-machine!` cannot replace it there.
- `machine_schema_arity_test.clj`: delete the guard pin (`:144-153`) and its ns-doc mentions (`:12`, `:34`). Keep the rest.
- Delete `implementation/machines/test/re_frame/level2_handler_spec_example_test.clj`. It reads `### Level 2 — unregistered handler fn` out of Spec 005, and that section goes.
- **No new permanent test.** The existing gates are the failing-first pins:
  - the `api-manifest` job goes red when the var is gone but its API.md row or metadata row remains;
  - `late_bind_drift_test.clj` goes red when the directory row and the publication disagree.

  Quote one such red in the PR body.

### Spec (hot zones)

- **`spec/005-StateMachines.md`** (41 mentions):
  - Delete §`make-machine-handler` is a pure factory (`:1037-1047`). Keep its invariant as one sentence on the handler `reg-machine` registers and the spawn fx installs: it registers nothing, closes over no global state, and does not know its own id. That is what keeps singleton and spawned registration symmetric.
  - Delete §Testing Level 2 (`:4342-4361`), and the pyramid row for it.
  - Rewrite the §Testing lead at `:4306`. It currently reads "Three test levels fall out naturally from the pure-factory contract on `make-machine-handler`".
  - **Keep `### Level 1 — pure `machine-transition`` byte-identical.** Six inbound links target `#level-1--pure-machine-transition`: 002:2685, 005:1229, 005:4825, 008:23, API.md:1005 and Construction-Prompts:530.
  - Renumber `### Level 3 — registered in a test frame` freely: zero inbound links were measured to it or to the Level-2 anchor.
  - Reword `:1215` ("Level-1 and Level-2 tests can stub …").
  - Respell the examples at `:403`, `:491` and `:511` that call `(rf.machines/make-machine-handler …)` to show registration-time validation, and every "`make-machine-handler` rejects X", as `reg-machine` / "registration rejects X".
- **`spec/API.md` holding:**
  - remove the `:1004` row and the mentions at `:22` and `:32`;
  - remove `spec/api-manifest-metadata.edn:1538` and adjust its comment at `:1151`;

title: re-frame2-pair: report :built-from so a behaviour-stale server is detectable when its tool contract fingerprint is unchanged
description:
## Problem

The skill detects a stale MCP server by comparing the server's tool-contract fingerprint with the string `SKILL.md` states. 8748911a58 added this for #10787, where a long-running server built from old source offered 35 tools against the skill's 30. But `registry/contract-fingerprint` deliberately hashes **tool names and argument keys only**. A server that predates a **behaviour** fix therefore passes the check, and the agent then reads the old behaviour as an app finding. That is the failure the check exists to prevent.

## Evidence (verified at trunk 9e84689562)

- `skills/re-frame2-pair/SKILL.md` (~L101) still states contract `30-c1c787a3`.
- Since that contract string, three server changes altered what an agent sees without moving the fingerprint:
  - a773ff2241: orient's bounded result with `:truncated` (#10916);
  - 9671842e28: `:unknown-reason` and the new freshness hint (#10917);
  - 70362963f8: the EDN-tag decoder fix for dry-run envelopes (#10922).
- #10916, #10917, #10922 and #10923 were all observed against `30-c1c787a3`. A server built before 2026-10-05 passes today's check, then overflows on orient or hands back the old "run `npx shadow-cljs stop`" hint.

## Direction (minimal)

1. Bake the git commit of the server's source into the build at `npm run build`, as a closure-define defaulting to `"unknown"` when git is unavailable.
2. Return it as `:built-from` beside `:tool-contract` in the instructions/orient reply.
3. Add no new step on the happy path. Add one sentence to the skill: when a reply lacks something the skill describes, compare `:built-from` against `git log -1 --format=%H -- tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/src` (an ancestry check: `git merge-base --is-ancestor`) before calling it an app finding, and ask the user to restart the server if it is behind.
4. The fingerprint's meaning stays unchanged; it remains the cheap name/argument check.

## Acceptance

- The reply carries `:built-from`, and a server test asserts its presence and its default.
- The skill sentence is present.
- `tool_contract_test` and `scripts/check_skill_mcp_drift.py` stay green, and the fingerprint value is unchanged by this work.

## Notes

The server's own build config is `tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/shadow-cljs.edn`, which is **not** the hot-zone `implementation/shadow-cljs.edn`. Any local build of the server enters shadow-cljs, so it needs a build-lane grant (AGENTS.md).

Considered and rejected: hashing descriptor descriptions into the fingerprint. It would still not move for the freshness or decoder fixes, and it would force a re-copy into `SKILL.md` on every prose edit (24 commits to the descriptors file since 2026-09-01).

title: Fresco frame-root returned from a view bypasses hydration refusal and duplicates the page
description:
Audit of merged PR #11092. The Fresco adoption refusal only covers the eager tree walk; a normal root component returning h/frame-root still bypasses it and silently duplicates the server page.

Evidence: impl.mount/hydrate-root! binds roots/*adopting-walk?* only while tree builds the React element. The component body is executed later by React (collector/run-once and render-body), after that binding unwinds. impl.frame-boundary/lower checks only that dynamic flag before handing off to core frame-root-fc, whose first pass returns nil and whose layout effect mounts its children. Thus (h/render! root [app-view] container {:hydrate? true}), where app-view returns [h/frame-root {:id frame-id} [page]], retains precisely the unclaimed-root shape this PR fixes for an inline frame-root. The same guard remains on current main; no open owner was found by a live ledger export. The closed source's residual note acknowledges this gap but leaves it without a live task.

Validation: a fresh local Playwright/Chromium probe using installed React 19.3.0, reproducing frame-root-fc's actual two-pass useState/useLayoutEffect shape, produced: direct two-pass root = 2 copies, original server node retained, 0 recoverable errors; the SAME two-pass root returned from a view component = 2 copies, server node retained, 0 recoverable errors. Supported single-pass control = 1 original server copy, 0 errors. Host-nested control = 1 replaced copy, 1 recoverable error. Script: ai/pr-audit/11092-view-frame-root-probe.cjs in audit worker. This is a React shape probe plus source tracing, not execution of the Fresco CLJS runtime; no shadow-cljs lane was taken.

Proposed action: carry the existing root-local adoption signal through the frame-root component path so a frame-root returned by a view cannot duplicate the page silently. Reuse the named refusal and frame-provider guidance; do not add a general prewalk of user components or a new hydration framework. A late render-time refusal may recover by replacing the markup, but it must be explicit and leave one coherent page. Add one real Fresco DOM regression with [app-view] returning frame-root, alongside the existing inline test; the supported frame-provider adoption must retain the server nodes. Preserve hook ordering.
notes:

Dispatched to worktree fresco-view-root. It owns implementation/fresco src and tests, plus, only if needed, the adoption check in core's re-frame.views.frame-boundary/frame-root-fc. The Fresco DOM red/green runs in one build-lane window granted by the mayor on request. Do not dispatch it again.
== WORKER RESULT (fresco-view-root, PR #11137, 2026-10-11 16:2x AUSEST) ==
FIXED in "fix(fresco): a frame-root returned from a view is refused during hydration, not duplicated" (d824abc00e, test 0939667cc0). Awaiting merge; the mayor closes.

Mechanism: the Fresco frame-root head renders through an outer guard component (impl/frame_boundary.cljs frame-root-adoption-guard). It reads two hooks on every render, so hook order is fixed: roots/hydrating-here? (the root's adoption window is open AND was minted by the client door) and codec/adopted? (the existing useSyncExternalStore gate, false only on the server and on hydration's first client pass). Inside a client root's hydration pass, the guard throws the existing :rf.error/fresco-frame-root-adopting with its frame-provider recipe. React re-renders the root on the client over a cleared container. That pass reads the client snapshot and renders through, so the page appears once, live and freshly rendered, and the refusal reaches onRecoverableError as the cause of React's recovery error. hydrate-root! mints its window through the new roots/open-hydration-window!, which marks the window as a client root's. The server door's window is also open during its render, and without the mark every server-rendered frame-root would refuse. The inline (walk-time) refusal is unchanged. Core's frame-root-fc is untouched: reusing its adoption-context check would throw in both React's hydration attempt and its client retry, leaving an empty container.

PREMISE DELTA (accepted by the mayor): the literal repro (h/render! root [app-view] container {:hydrate? true}) does not duplicate. A public h/render! root carries no frame, so a defview at the top refuses first with :rf.error/no-frame-context (collector/resolve-frame!). The duplicate needs a frame in scope above the view. The regression therefore hydrates [h/frame-provider {:frame f} [ensuring-shell]], where the view returns [h/frame-root {:id f} [panel]], over the bytes of [h/frame-provider {:frame f} [panel]]. All other bead claims hold at tip.

Evidence: client_root_lifecycle_dom_cljs_test W4b, a-hydrating-first-render-refuses-a-frame-root-a-view-returns. Both runs were local, in one mayor-granted lane window, as a narrowed browser-test compile of that one namespace plus serve-and-run:

- GREEN (HEAD, blob hashes match): compile exit 0, run exit 0. 8 tests / 92 assertions, 0 failures. The counts match, so the row ran both times.
W5 in the same file (frame-provider adoption keeps the server's nodes) is the control, green in both runs.

FOR THE MAYOR (hot zones, not edited): spec/002-Frames.md's frame-root hydration paragraph says a frame-root reached through a view body "does not refuse it", and spec/009's :rf.error/fresco-frame-root-adopting row says the door "never sees" it. Both are stale once this merges. title: Fresco presence: use monotonic elapsed time for exit deadlines
description:
The private now function in implementation/fresco/src/re_frame/fresco/impl/presence_react.cljs uses Date.now for relative exit deadlines. If the calendar clock moves backward before the single expiry callback fires, presence/expire can return unchanged state because now is below the stored deadline. The effect depends on unchanged pending-signature and does not schedule a successor timeout, so a quiet tray can retain an exiting child indefinitely (for example deadline 1300, callback time 1100).

Use the host monotonic elapsed-time clock consistently for creating and comparing these private deadlines. Keep the pure numeric-time retention machine, single timeout owner, cleanup and public API. Align the existing fake-clock seam as necessary. Add no watchdog or second timer system; suspension still postpones callbacks until execution resumes.

Evidence: Sol report 25 section 4; impl/presence_react.cljs now/effect and impl/presence.cljs expire/pending-signature, baseline 7ddb51136714b00081b9b477cc93cb7c1f2da78e. Original report: ai/findings/advisarial-review/sol-history/2026-10-12-low-hanging-fruit/before/25-fresco-motion-overlays.md. This is a source-derived liveness path, not a newly reproduced runtime failure.
acceptance_criteria: A controlled driver witness rolls the calendar clock backward while elapsed time reaches expiry: the exiting node is removed without an unrelated render and its timer owner is cleaned up. Existing re-entry, deadline stability and unmount cleanup behavior remains. No new public configuration is introduced.
notes: == 2026-10-12 AUSEST: closed as a duplicate of rf2-ztt72 (item 2, presence clock), filed five minutes earlier from the Opus corpus and already dispatched. The extra detail here (monotonic for both creating and comparing deadlines, align the fake-clock seam, no watchdog) is copied into rf2-ztt72 notes.

title: Production schema boundary fails open without the schemas artefact, and a rejection computes diagnostics nobody receives
description:
Filed 2026-10-12 22:50:01 AUSEST at HEAD 5162360cf2, from the Opus adversarial review (schemas, actions 1-2) and cross-checked against Sol 10. Evidence below was read at HEAD.

## Problem

Two defects sit in the production schema boundary. Both are in `re-frame.spec/validate-at-boundary!` (`implementation/core/src/re_frame/spec.cljc:115-215`), and the first also affects recordable cofx.

**1. A declared production check fails OPEN when the schemas artefact is absent.** `:boundary? true` exists to gate untrusted payloads in release builds. When the `:schemas/validate-with-registered-fn` hook is nil, `validate-at-boundary!` returns `true`, and the handler runs unvalidated:

    (if (or (nil? validate-fn) ...) true ...)   ; spec.cljc ~:152

Recordable-cofx `:schema` validation does the same at `implementation/core/src/re_frame/cofx.cljc:698-703`, where `(nil? validate-fn)` returns the value unchecked. Nothing is reported in either case.

HTTP's schema `:decode` used to have the same gap and now refuses with `:rf.error/schemas-artefact-missing` (rf2-mn2ht.55, PR #11066), so the framework currently disagrees with itself. An earlier reviewer listed "fails open without the schemas artefact" as "documented behaviour" under rf2-3x7nj.5's "Considered and rejected". That was a triage note, not a ruling, and it predates the HTTP precedent.

Both docstrings lump together "schemas artefact absent" and "`set-schema-fns!` installed a nil `:validate`". Sol reports that a loaded artefact with a nil validator still publishes the seam, which returns pass (`implementation/schemas/src/re_frame/schemas/validate.cljc`). If so, a nil HOOK means only "artefact absent". Confirm this before relying on it.

**2. A production rejection computes diagnostics nobody receives.** After a failed check, `validate-at-boundary!` calls the application's explainer, runs the redaction hook, and builds the tags and an interpolated `:reason` string, all before `rf.trace/emit-error!`. The debug gate lives inside `emit-error!`, so none of that is skipped: arguments are evaluated first, and on the JVM and in non-advanced CLJS the explainer runs on every rejection.

## Sol cross-check

Sol 10 agrees independently, and its current-state audit (baseline 7ddb511367) still lists both. On item 1 it says: "make declared production checks fail clearly when infrastructure is missing… preserve the explicit nil-validator opt-out… a narrow missing-artefact failure for boundary/recordable-cofx checks is more useful than a general dev warning." On item 2 (its §6): "put rich explanation, redaction and tag construction under an explicit call-site debug gate… a release rejection should call the validator once, diagnostic explainer zero times, skip the handler and still report `:rejected`." Sol notes that the existing advanced-production tests pin refusal and reporting, but not zero explainer calls.

## Fix direction

1. When the hook is absent, `:boundary? true` and recordable-cofx `:schema` raise `:rf.error/schemas-artefact-missing`, matching HTTP's `:decode`. The handler doesn't run, and the cofx injection fails. A deliberately installed nil validator still passes, and no general dev warning is added. Spec: 010 §Production builds and §Non-Malli validators, plus 009's catalogue row for `:rf.error/schemas-artefact-missing` (spec/009 is a hot-zone file).
2. Wrap the explainer, redaction, tags and reason construction in `(when rf.interop/debug-enabled? ...)` at the call site. Validation, refusal and the always-on structural rejection record stay unchanged.

## Verification

- With the schemas artefact unloaded:
  - a `:boundary? true` handler with `:schema` doesn't run and reports `:rf.error/schemas-artefact-missing`;
  - the same holds for a recordable cofx with `:schema`;
  - `{:validate nil}` installed deliberately stays inert, and the handler runs.
  - Each of these is red before the fix and green after.
- In release posture (`debug-enabled?` false), a rejected boundary event calls the validator once and the explainer zero times (count calls with a stub explainer), skips the handler, and still emits the always-on rejection record.
- Lanes: the JVM core and schemas suites. The CLJS branch needs `npm run test:cljs`, and the advanced-production lane carries `schemas_boundary_prod_test.cljs`.
notes:
== DISPATCHED 2026-10-12 22:58:53 AUSEST by the mayor: worktree C:/Users/miket/code/re-frame2-worktrees/schema-boundary-open, branch worker/schema-boundary-open off 5162360cf2. FENCE: core spec.cljc + cofx.cljc boundary/recordable-cofx paths, schemas src only if needed, their tests, spec/010, spec/009 (HOT ZONE) the schemas-artefact-missing row only. JVM red/green; CI for CLJS.
== WORKER SUMMARY 2026-10-12 AUSEST (branch worker/schema-boundary-open, PR #11150, base 5162360cf2)

Premise check (verified at source, 5162360cf2): a nil :schemas/validate-with-registered-fn HOOK means only "schemas artefact absent". re-frame.schemas publishes the seam unconditionally at ns-load (implementation/schemas/src/re_frame/schemas.cljc:115), and the seam calls rf.schemas.validator/run-validator, which returns true when the installed validator is nil (validator.cljc:365-367). So an installed {:validate nil} reaches the boundary and cofx checks as a published seam that passes; it never looks like an unbound hook.

Fix:
1. re-frame.spec/validate-at-boundary!: absent :schema key -> true (unchanged); unbound validate hook -> throws :rf.error/schemas-artefact-missing (:where rf/reg-event, ex-data :failing-id + :frame, never the payload), so the handler does not run. Rejection diagnosis (explainer call, redaction, tags, interpolated :reason) now sits inside (when rf.interop/debug-enabled? ...), so a release rejection calls the validator once and the explainer never. Refusal and the router's always-on structural record are unchanged.
2. re-frame.cofx/validate-recordable-value!: declared :schema + unbound hook -> throws :rf.error/schemas-artefact-missing (:where rf/reg-cofx, ex-data :rf.cofx/id, :failing-id, :frame); injection fails, handler does not run. Every build.
3. Spec 010 Production builds (new paragraph "Without the schemas artefact the check refuses" + one clause on the gated diagnosis) and Boundary-validation seam (one paragraph); spec 009 :rf.error/schemas-artefact-missing row names both dispatch-time cases, the nil-validator distinction, and the :failing-id / :frame / :rf.cofx/id slots. Spec 010 has no "Non-Malli validators" heading; the matching section is "Default validator and the validator-fn extension point", subsection "Boundary-validation seam".

Red/green (re-frame.always-on-validation-production-test; tests committed first, run against unfixed source):
- dev lane (clojure -M:test -n ...): red 4 failures (boundary handler ran with 42; cofx folded 7), green 0. 11 tests / 21 assertions.
- prod-gate lane (-M:test:prod-gate -n ...): red 5 failures (adds explainer calls 1, expected 0), green 0. 13 tests / 25 assertions.

The developer would first meet the refusal in production. title: core-instrumentation: a path written and classified :sensitive in the SAME event ships raw in that event's :rf.event/db-pending trace (projection reads the pre-commit registry)
description:
## Defect

EP-0025's headline guarantee for the commit-plane classification effects is stated at `elision.cljc:383-386`: they "are applied WITH the `:db` write ... NOT as a later post-commit `:fx`, so a path classified in the SAME event is redacted from its first egress". The dev trace breaks it. The `:rf.event/db-pending` (t1) and `:rf.event/db-pending-post-flow` (t2) traces stamp the full pending app-db BEFORE the commit. `project-db-tags` projects that value against the LIVE registry (`rf.elision/registry-of` reads the frame's committed runtime-db). So when an event writes a secret AND returns `:sensitive [[path]]` for it — the canonical EP-0025 pattern — the event's own `:rf.event/db` slot ships the secret RAW to every trace listener, the per-frame ring and the epoch capture buffer. Only later events redact it.

## Where

- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/router.cljc:1827-1831` (t1) and `:1907-1911` (t2) — emit `:rf.event/db pending-db` before `commit-frame-effects!` folds the classification effects into runtime-db.
- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/classification.cljc:717-733` (`frame-has-declarations?`) and `:735-758` (`project-db-tags`) — both read the frame's committed registry, never the event's pending classification effects.
- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/elision.cljc:123-126` (`registry-of`) — reads `rf.frame/runtime-db-container`, the committed partition.
- The promise: `implementation/core/src/re_frame/elision.cljc:383-386`.
- Public entry: `rf/dispatch` / `rf/dispatch-sync` of an event returning `{:db … :sensitive [[…]]}`.

## Failure scenario

`(rf/reg-event :seed (fn [{:keys [db]} _] {:db (assoc db :auth {:token "SECRET-SAME-EVENT"}) :sensitive [[:auth :token]]}))`, then `(rf/dispatch-sync [:seed])`. A trace listener (Xray, or a Spec 009 §Composition-with-libraries forwarder) receives `:rf.event/db-pending` with `:rf.event/db {:auth {:token "SECRET-SAME-EVENT"}}`. `rf/trace-buffer` retains it, and so does the raw epoch record. A second event that writes a new value at the now-classified path is redacted — the gap is exactly the first-egress event the spec promises to cover.

## Evidence

EXECUTED — a bounded JVM probe from the reviewer scratch dir against the frozen tree at `034d0c8fc8` (nothing written to the tree), running the scenario above. Of the 8 trace events for `:seed`, exactly one carries the secret: `:rf.event/db-pending`, in its `:rf.event/db` tag. CONTROL: the follow-up `:rotate` event, which writes `"SECRET-SAME-EVENT-2"` at `[:auth :token]`, emits 0 trace events carrying either value.

Scope note (inspected): the off-box epoch projection re-roots `:rf.event/db` against the registry at PROJECTION time (`implementation/epoch/src/re_frame/epoch/tool_pair.cljc` `reroot-trace-event-db-slots`, reached from `elide-trace-events-slot` at `:2248`). A separate probe confirmed that the off-box-tool projection of the `:seed` epoch record carries the secret at 0 paths. The leak is therefore the on-box trace stream, ring and raw epoch record — which is still the surface EP-0025's "first egress" sentence is about — and not the MCP epoch door.

Tracker: no bead found for same-event / first-egress db-pending redaction (full-text search over a `bd export`).

## Smallest fix

Project the t1 / t2 `:rf.event/db` against the CANDIDATE registry: the committed registry with this event's classification effects applied. One option: the router computes `(rf.elision/apply-classification-effects <current-runtime-db> effects)` (pure, and the router already validates those effects pre-commit) and hands its `:rf.runtime/elision` to the projection through an internal tag. `project-db-tags` consumes and strips it, the same way `project-sub-tags` consumes `:rf.sub/classification`. Fence: `implementation/core/src/re_frame/router.cljc` (the two emit sites), `implementation/core/src/re_frame/classification.cljc` (`project-db-tags`), and possibly an `elision.cljc` helper that walks against an explicit registry. No hot-zone file.

## Gates

JVM core artefact: `clojure -M:test` from `implementation/core`. None of the touched forms sit in a `#?(:cljs …)` branch. `npm run test:cljs` covers the CLJS lane.

## Decision needed

No.
notes:
## Worker analysis (2026-09-23, branch worker/instr-privacy-3x7nj) — SEQUENCED behind the elision worker (mayor ruling: option B)

Status: NOT fixed in this worker's PR. The mayor ruled 4.3 is sequenced AFTER the elision.cljc worker's PR (rf2-3x7nj.4.1 offset-rooted egress / rf2-3x7nj.4.6 defrecord walk) lands, because the fix needs an additive helper in elision.cljc, which is that worker's fence, and 4.1 very likely reshapes the same `elide-against-frame` walk. Re-dispatch once that PR is on main; start from the design below.

### Reproduced at trunk 4b627ee9e2 (implementation byte-identical to review tree 034d0c8fc8)

JVM probe (core `:test` classpath, nothing written to the tree): `:seed` returns `{:db (assoc db :auth {:token "SECRET-SAME-EVENT"}) :sensitive [[:auth :token]]}`, dispatched with `dispatch-sync`. Of the 8 trace events for `:seed`, exactly one carries the secret: `:rf.event/db-pending`, at `[:tags :rf.event/db :auth :token]`. The raw epoch record carries it at `[:trace-events 2 :tags :rf.event/db :auth :token]` too. CONTROL: the follow-up `:rotate` event, which writes `"SECRET-SAME-EVENT-2"` at the now-classified path, emits 0 trace events carrying either value. The bead's premise holds exactly as written.

### Why a classification-side overlay is the WRONG fix

The tempting fix, inside classification.cljc alone: walk t1/t2 `:rf.event/db` against the committed registry (as today), then overlay this event's own `:sensitive` effect paths with classification's own walker (`redact-with-paths`). That walker does NOT have the committed registry's semantics. `re-frame.elision`'s wire walker has:
- the `:map-of` key skip (`fork-decl-paths`: after a declared segment is consumed, a map key can be a collection coordinate, so a declared `[:auth :token]` also matches runtime `[:auth "session-1" :token]`);
- index-free vector descent (`fork-index-paths`);
- owner-aware large markers (`marker-opts`).

classification's `walk-with-paths` has index-free only as an opt-in and NO map-of key skip. So a same-event path under a map-of slot would still ship raw in t1, and the next event (walked by elision) would redact it. Measured at 4b627ee9e2 with `[:user :token]` declared sensitive on a live frame, over `{:user {"s1" {:token "S"} :token "T"}}`:
- `elide-wire-value` gives `{:user {"s1" {:token :rf/redacted} :token :rf/redacted}}`;
- `redact-with-paths … {:index-free? true}` gives `{:user {"s1" {:token "S"} :token :rf/redacted}}`, with `"S"` RAW. That's a divergence, not a fix. Duplicating elision's walker in classification would be worse. So the fix needs elision's own walker, run against an explicit (candidate) registry, and that walker is private and reads the registry off the live container (`registry-of` → `rf.frame/runtime-db-container`).

### Proposed design (about 15 additive lines in elision.cljc, nothing existing changes behaviour)

1. elision.cljc: split `elide-against-frame [v opts frame-id]` so the walk body takes the registry VALUE:
   - `(defn- elide-against-registry [v opts frame-id reg] …)`: the current body, with `reg` passed in instead of `(registry-of frame-id)`.
   - `elide-against-frame` becomes `(elide-against-registry v opts frame-id (registry-of frame-id))`.
2. elision.cljc: one `^:no-doc` public fn, e.g. `elide-wire-value-against-registry [v frame-id reg]`. It keeps `elide-wire-value`'s fail-closed contract: `frame-id` must name a LIVE frame (`rf.frame/frame`), otherwise it returns `rf.privacy/redacted-sentinel`. Then it calls `elide-against-registry` with default opts (`{:frame frame-id}`).
   Rebase this onto whatever shape 4.1 leaves `elide-against-frame` in. The point is only "same walker, explicit registry".

### Router and classification half (the worker's own fence)

3. router.cljc, the `:rf/flows` interceptor's `:after` (t1 emit at `:rf.event/db-pending`, t2 at `:rf.event/db-pending-post-flow`; at 4b627ee9e2 lines ~1827 and ~1907). When `(rf.elision/classification-effect? effects)` is true, compute the candidate registry: `(get (rf.elision/apply-classification-effects <current runtime-db> effects) :rf.runtime/elision)`. It's pure, and the router already validates these effects pre-commit via `classification-effect-defect` (a malformed payload aborts before t1 anyway, but guard with the same defect check or a try so a projection helper can never throw on the emit path). `<current runtime-db>` is the pending runtime partition the flows pass already resolves (`pending-runtime-db`, or `(-> ctx :coeffects :rf.db/runtime)`). Carry it on the two emits under an internal tag, e.g. `:rf.event/candidate-elision`.
4. classification.cljc `project-db-tags`: consume and ALWAYS STRIP that tag, the way `project-sub-tags` consumes `:rf.sub/classification`. When present, walk `:rf.event/db` with `elide-wire-value-against-registry` against it, and gate on the candidate registry having declarations rather than `frame-has-declarations?`. Keep the nil-frame fail-closed arm first.
   Semantics this yields: this event's `:clear-sensitive` un-redacts in its own t1/t2 exactly as the committed registry will after commit (candidate = committed + this event's effects). That's the bead's specified behaviour. The alternative "committed ∪ additions" is more conservative but diverges from what the next egress shows.
5. Off-box is already right: `re-frame.epoch.tool-pair/reroot-trace-event-db-slots` re-walks `:rf.event/db` against the registry at PROJECTION time. A probe confirmed the off-box-tool projection of the `:seed` epoch record carries the secret at 0 paths. So no epoch change is needed.

### Regression test to write with the fix

A producer-derived test beside `re-frame.classification-effects-cljs-test` (`classify-then-egress-in-the-same-event-redacts` already pins the post-commit read; extend it to the t1 trace). Dispatch `{:db (assoc-in db [:user :token] S) :sensitive [[:user :token]]}`, find `:rf.event/db-pending`, and assert `[:tags :rf.event/db :user :token]` is `:rf/redacted`. Add one map-of case, e.g. a secret at `[:user "s1" :token]` with `[:user :token]` declared, which is exactly the case the rejected overlay would miss. Tag `^:requires-debug`, since the dev trace doesn't emit under the prod gate. Show it red with the router tag removed.
== SEQUENCED (mayor, 2026-09-23) ==

The instr-privacy worker (PR #10281, merged) stopped this item under ruling (B): the fix needs a small additive helper in elision.cljc, which the elision worker (rf2-3x7nj.4.1 / .4.6 / .4.7, PR #10279) is reshaping. Its reproduction and proposed design (the ~15-line split of elide-against-frame into a registry-taking walk plus a ^:no-doc fn, and the router / project-db-tags half) are in the note above this one. title: Incomplete epoch-history redaction: missing-rollup fallback retains sensitive record projections
description:
Audit of PR #9937, merge 98db4f19e4f850d7d88db45da654529554cdf568, source rf2-y8doi.13. tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/epoch.cljs:89-95 retains a record without :rf.epoch/sensitive? and removes sensitive events only from :trace-events. This is an explicitly documented and newly tested input shape (synthetic sync-epoch-history seeds / records without the rollup). A real build-record output with that rollup removed still has raw :frame-state-before/after, :db-before/after, :sub-runs, :renders, :effects and trigger fields. assembly.cljc:284-340 derives them before this gate; changing :trace-events does not scrub them. Reactive project-record reads :sub-runs/:renders directly (reactive_panel_subs.cljs:581-584), and app-db projection reads :db-after (app_db_diff_subs.cljs:242). Thus sensitive data/structure can still reach the surfaces the fallback claims to protect. The new regression only checks absence from :trace-events, so it pins the incomplete behavior. Normal current-producer records carrying a true rollup are dropped correctly; this finding is specifically the advertised missing-rollup fallback. Source-proven, not claimed browser-reproduced.

Required correction: apply the same whole-record grain used for rollup-sensitive records whenever an event is suppressed (the bundles-for-frame implementation in this PR already explains why editing one projection is unsafe). Alternatively stop accepting the missing-rollup shape explicitly rather than preserving a partial legacy scrub; do not add a compatibility framework or hand-maintain a list of payload slots. Keep trusted local-raw passthrough. Regression: assemble a real record with sensitive trigger/payload, remove its rollup, ingest through sync-epoch-history, and assert no record/payload survives anywhere, alongside ordinary non-sensitive and raw-profile controls.

Open Beads searched for epoch-history, redact-history and missing/no-rollup; no exact match. Source status must remain unchanged.

## What

Removed-machinery and truth residue left in spec text after PR #10392 (rf2-tv5ac.72 / rf2-aw34y), which could edit only certain sections. Worker ptspec006-tv5ac reported each item; re-verify each at your trunk. This is prose correction only.

## spec/004B-UI-Tree-and-Conversion.md (outside that PR's sections)
- t/text and t/attrs are still used. The shipped test-kit alias is ht (ht/text, ht/attrs, ht/find, ht/find-all).
- The Ripples section says there is no t/find, but ht/find and ht/find-all exist.
- Coverage Q12 contradicts how the kit records view boundaries. Read the kit and make Q12 true.
- The §Producers paragraph still refers to "compile error" rows; none remain.
- Compiled/interpreted mode wording remains in §Element fields and §Attr value normalization.
- v/html and v/custom-element still appear in rows that are not refusals. Make each row describe what the shipped code does, or remove it if it describes removed machinery.

## spec/004C-Roots-and-Mount.md
- §4 says root-ids are unique per page. That uniqueness rests on Layer 2, which §7 now marks "specified, not yet implemented". Say so, or qualify §4.

## spec/016-Resources.md (spec-authoring hygiene)
- A resolved item is listed under Open questions: move it or state it as resolved.
- A deferred item is marked tracked but names no bead: name the bead, or say it is untracked.
- "post-v1, untracked notes" is not a term the spec-authoring rules define: use the defined term.

## spec/009-Instrumentation.md (HOT; see the fence note)
- The catalogue marks :rf.error/duplicate-root-id retired, while 004C Layer 2 now reserves it as specified-not-implemented. Make the row agree with 004C.
- "R0 route-plan diagnostic projection" still uses the old slice naming. The spec/012 heading "(EP-0037 R0)" was deliberately kept, since headings are never renamed, so change only the 009 prose.

## Gates
python -m mkdocs build --strict; python scripts/check_doc_slugs.py (anchors); present_tense.py verify on each changed page; CLAUDE.md item (e)'s three numbers on each changed file. Say for each item whether it was fixed or the premise did not hold.

## Target

```clojure

(:kind (rf/current-adapter))  ; → :rf.adapter/reagent … ; nil for a kind-less custom map (no synthesised :custom)
```

description:

Line numbers measured at tip `13884f326f` (= origin/main, 2026-09-06 17:18 AUSEST) unless marked "dossier tip" (`6d513ba07f`, single-digit drift). Grep by NAME before editing — lines drift._

## Problem

`:on-spawn` is a spawn-spec callback `(fn [{:keys [data id]}] _)` that the runtime invokes PRE-COMMIT inside the transition fold (`apply-on-spawn`, `implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines/transition.cljc` ~:2320-2380), discards the return of, and then warns about when it is non-nil (`:rf.warning/on-spawn-return-ignored`, ~:2367; remedy vector ~:2374). The one plausible thing an author does with a spawned id — record it — is the thing the hook refuses; the transition reducer already binds it under `[:data :rf/spawned <invoke-id>]` (`transition.cljc:562`). Consumers: **0** — the two example hits (`examples/patterns/websocket/core.cljs:42`, `connection.cljs:69`) are prose saying "no `:on-spawn`". It drags along a root-level `:on-spawn-actions` registration slot, a `MachineElementEntry` schema row, source-coord stamping in the `reg-machine` macro, an action-ref id `:rf.machine.spawn/on-spawn` on the exception path, a conformance DSL arm, a four-mechanism 005 §Recording the spawned id section that exists only because the hook invites the wrong one, and a migration rule whose "after" block (M-35) shows the exact no-op as the correct migrated form.

**Ruling A (rf2-kuky.15): delete the family.** Not because the hook "can do nothing" — Codex is right that it runs application code pre-commit and a throw becomes machine-action failure with rollback (`spawn_on_spawn_throw_test.clj` pins that) — but because no consumer needs a pre-commit observer and its position complicates the otherwise data-oriented fold. The data path (`:rf/spawned` on the parent; `:rf/self-id` / `:rf/parent-id` on the child) becomes the one id-recording story. No shim, no deprecation, no "retired key" diagnostic.

## Target

- The spawn-spec vocabulary (`:spawn` and `:spawn-all` children, and `[:rf.machine/spawn]` args) loses `:on-spawn`; a spec that still carries it fails the EXISTING closed-vocabulary unknown-key diagnostic (`lifecycle_fx/validation.cljc` `known-spawn-spec-keys`).

title: api(trace): delete re-frame.trace's six alias defs; migrate 97 test files to re-frame.trace.tooling
description:
_Filed 2026-09-05 12:37:46 AUSEST by the API-review wave-3 coordinator from trace-epoch.md (ref trace-epoch.2); parent epic rf2-kuky. Local-only dossiers: ai/findings/API-review/{fable,codex}/ (gitignored; may be deleted)._

## Problem

`re-frame.trace` is a third door to six fns that already have a home (`re-frame.trace.tooling`) and a facade (`re-frame.core`). `implementation/core/src/re_frame/trace.cljc:944-957`:

```clojure
(def register-listener!     rf.trace.tooling/register-listener!)
(def unregister-listener!   rf.trace.tooling/unregister-listener!)
(def clear-listeners!       rf.trace.tooling/clear-listeners!)
(def trace-buffer           rf.trace.tooling/trace-buffer)
(def clear-trace-buffer!    rf.trace.tooling/clear-trace-buffer!)
(def configure-trace-buffer! rf.trace.tooling/configure-trace-buffer!)
```

The comment above them (`:945-949`) calls these "the canonical app-facing names" (rf2-ic1sv pick c, 2026-05-21). The stream-parameterized facade verb `(rf/register-listener! :trace id f)` superseded that on 2026-07-08 (rf2-9flalp, `89bb759305`); the door was never retired. Non-test code reaching any of the six through this namespace at tip: **core.cljc's own delegation only** (`core.cljc:2164` `:trace (rf.trace/register-listener! id f)`, `:2178`, `:2216`, `:2222`); every other hit is a comment. Tests, however, spell it everywhere: 97 test files (`register-listener!` 48, `unregister-listener!` 46, `clear-listeners!` 50, `trace-buffer` 1, the other two 0) — `git grep -l -E '(rf\.trace|re-frame\.trace)/(register-listener!|unregister-listener!|clear-listeners!|trace-buffer|clear-trace-buffer!|configure-trace-buffer!)' -- ':!ai/' | grep -E '_test\.|/test/|/tests/' | wc -l`.

The manifest rosters none of `re-frame.trace`, `re-frame.trace.tooling`, `re-frame.trace.projection` (`grep -c '"re-frame.trace' spec/api-manifest.edn` → 0), so the six are un-tiered public vars with no contract behind them.

## Target API

None added. `re-frame.trace` keeps the hot emit path (`emit!` `:860`, `emit-error!`, the bracket macros, `trace-event-frame`) and the `:trace/emit!` hook registration. The listener registry and ring are reached by the facade (`rf/register-listener! :trace …`, `rf/trace-buffer`, `rf/clear-trace-buffer!`, `(rf/configure! {:trace-buffer …})`) or, for fixtures and tools that already require it, `re-frame.trace.tooling/…`.

```clojure
;; core.cljc after: the facade delegates to the home directly
:trace  (rf.trace.tooling/register-listener! id f)      ; :2164
:trace  (rf.trace.tooling/unregister-listener! id)      ; :2178
trace-buffer        rf.trace.tooling/trace-buffer        ; :2216 (fence already lifted by @trace-epoch.1)
clear-trace-buffer! rf.trace.tooling/clear-trace-buffer! ; :2222
```

`core.cljc`'s ns form gains `[re-frame.trace.tooling :as rf.trace.tooling]` (it already requires `re-frame.trace.projection`, `:15`; tooling requires only `interop`, `late-bind`, `projection` — no cycle). The static require graph does not change (core → trace → tooling today); only the edge's spelling moves. `trace.cljc`'s own require of tooling STAYS: `trace.cljc:197` uses `rf.trace.tooling/call-with-deferred-fanout` on the JVM.

## Corroboration

One-reviewer area; codex concurs on this item verbatim: "retire the unused third-door aliases and align the spec, manifest, docs, and generated eval recipes" and "Retire the duplicate public read/clear spellings in `re-frame.trace`; keep implementation functions in their owning namespace." @observability.n's table lists `re-frame.trace/register-listener!` as unrowed with 0 consumers and may propose the same deletion — the coordinator de-duplicates; this bead carries the test migration either way.

## Deletion list

- `trace.cljc:944-957` (comment block + six defs).
- The rf2-ic1sv "pick c" rationale in `trace.cljc:41-48` (rewrite: the require stays for `:197`; production DCE is by `goog.DEBUG` gating of call sites, as `:44-48` already says).
- Stale prose naming the alias: `implementation/scripts/check-bundle-isolation.cjs:339-350` (also stale on its own terms — "thin late-bind shells" describes the pre-rf2-ic1sv `5b0eb9f9b8` world; after this bead `re-frame.trace` has no wrappers at all; the sentinel and `expectedAllowListHits` are NOT changed); `core.cljc:2103` comment; `implementation/epoch/src/re_frame/epoch/state.cljc:50` (`re-frame.trace/configure-trace-buffer!` → `re-frame.trace.tooling/…`); `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/drop_in.cljc:73`; `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/install.cljs:27`; `testbeds/spec-helpers.cjs:9`; `tools/story/spec/005-SOTA-Features.md:331`; `tools/xray/spec/011-Launch-Modes.md:502` (Xray spec rule: every `tools/xray/` dispatch updates `tools/xray/spec/*` in the same PR).

## Consumers to migrate

- 97 test files, mechanical: `rf.trace/<name>` (158 files alias `[re-frame.trace :as rf.trace]`, 44 as `trace`) → `rf.trace.tooling/<name>`, adding `[re-frame.trace.tooling :as rf.trace.tooling]` where absent (20 of the 97 already require it). Do NOT drop `[re-frame.trace :as rf.trace]` blindly — most of these files also use `rf.trace/emit!` / `trace-event-frame`; remove the require only where it becomes unused (the JVM linter / `npm run test:cljs-isolation` will say). ## Problem

EP-0029 A3 retired the machine-level `:data-schema` key by a clean pre-alpha break; the machine data-context schema lives at `[:schemas :data]` (`docs/EP/EP-0029-xstate-v6-machine-parity.md:225-226`; `spec/Spec-Schemas.md:2609-2611` says the `:schemas` block "REPLACES the retired root `:data-schema` slot"). Measured at tip 6445d0611b: `git grep -c -F ":data-schema" -- spec/005-StateMachines.md implementation/machines/src` → 0 in both. But several normative pages and code docstrings still teach the retired spelling as the live machine key, and one skill claims the RESOURCE `:data-schema` validates when `spec/016:760` says it does not. Every line here is true regardless of any @schema.2 ruling. No code bead in this area touches these lines.

Two `:data-schema` keys exist and only ONE is retired: the MACHINE key (retired → `[:schemas :data]`) and the RESOURCE key (live, reflection-only). Fix only lines that name the machine key; leave resource lines alone. This also means the spelling cannot be added to `scripts/check_retired_spellings.py` — a bare `:data-schema` is sanctioned on resources, so the gate's "where shapes allow" caveat applies; do not add it.

## Evidence — lines to fix (machine key named as live)

Spec (normative):
- `spec/010-Schemas.md:54` ("Machines … carry `:data-schema` at the top of the machine spec … named `:data-schema` rather than the bare `:schema`"), `:60` (the code sample `:data-schema DrawerData ;; validates :data`), `:170` (step 4a "from `reg-machine` `:data-schema`" ×2), `:186` (row 7 "its registered `:data-schema` (declared on the `reg-machine` spec…)"). `spec/010:306,438` name the RESOURCE key — leave.
- HOT-ZONE `spec/Conventions.md:323` ("a machine's data validator is `:data-schema`") and `:330` (the schema-family table row "machine `:data-schema` | `:data-schema` (the `reg-machine` key)" — rule 3's worked precedent now names a retired key; the qualify-where-a-sibling-makes-`:schema`-ambiguous rationale survives, because `[:schemas :data]` qualifies by nesting under the `:schemas` block instead of by name — say that). `Conventions.md:523` ("`:schema` / `:data-schema`" in the elision-classification paragraph) reads as resources — leave.
- HOT-ZONE `spec/009-Instrumentation.md:2476` (`:machine-data` row: "against its `:data-schema`").
- `spec/Privacy.md:107,111,112,164` ("machine `:data-schema`" — fix the machine half of each; the resource half stays).
- `spec/Security.md:93` ("machine `:data-schema`, resource `:data-schema` / `:params-schema`") — fix the machine half; `:120,248` list `:data-schema` / `:params-schema` / `:decode` without naming machines — leave.
- `spec/015-Data-Classification.md:495` (reference-list line "the machine `:data-schema` VALIDATES" — `:195,312` already say `[:schemas :data]`).
- `spec/001-Registration.md:219` ("`:schema` / `:data-schema` | Retained") — reads as resources; leave, but confirm.

Docs / skills / security note:
- `docs/api/re-frame.schemas.md:390` ("a machine's `:data-schema`").
- `implementation/SECURITY.md:34,248,265` ("machine / resource `:data-schema`" — fix the machine half).

Code docstrings / comments (no behaviour; machine key named as live):
- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/late_bind/directory.cljc:489` (`:machines/validate-machine-data!` description "against the registered machine's `:data-schema`"), `core.cljc:666`, `elision.cljc:20,538`, `classification.cljc:856,926`, `registrar.cljc:504` ("`:schema` / `:data-schema`" — confirm which key), `implementation/epoch/src/re_frame/epoch/tool_pair.cljc:177,184,187`, `implementation/schemas/src/re_frame/schemas/storage.cljc:224,260`, `schemas/walker.cljc:96,283`, `implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/payload_policy.cljc:476`, `implementation/core/test/re_frame/elision_probe.cljs:386,399` (comments), `implementation/core/test/re_frame/doc_metadata_prod_elision_test.clj:173` (a `:data-schema` in a load-bearing-keys list — confirm it is exercising the resource key; if it is the machine key the list is stale).

Leave as-is (already correct or historical): `docs/EP/**` (EP-0005 carries its own retirement banner at `:5`), `spec/Spec-Schemas.md:2609-2611`, `spec/015:195,312`, `tools/machines-viz/**` and `tools/xray/spec/003-Machine-Inspector.md:1186` (describe the key as retired), `tools/xray/spec/018-Event-Spine.md:1861` and every `resources/**` line (resource key).

## Target

Every normative sentence about the machine data schema names `[:schemas :data]`; every remaining `:data-schema` in `spec/`, `docs/api/`, `implementation/SECURITY.md` and `implementation/**/src` docstrings refers to the RESOURCE key; the resources skill no longer says the resource key validates.

## Corroboration

Drift found in passing by the fable review (`schema-configuration-and-validation.md` §What it would change; README §Doc drift found in passing) — true regardless of ruling; codex did not review it. Re-measure before editing: `git grep -n -F ":data-schema" -- spec docs/api implementation skills ':!docs/EP'`.

None — prose and docstrings only.

## Spec, docs, examples, skills, tests

Listed above. No manifest change, no migration README entry, no conformance change, no example change (the examples spell `[:schemas :data]` already — `examples/core/login/README.md:29`).

Touches `spec/Conventions.md` and `spec/009-Instrumentation.md` (one-toucher) — waits on @schema.1, which edits other lines of both. `spec/010` is also edited by rf2-xpd8 PR1 (row 4, ~:184 — this bead edits :186's `:data-schema` mention in the SAME row 7 table) — rebase after it merges if it lands first. Not worth blocking on.

## Risks

None beyond a careless sweep replacing a RESOURCE `:data-schema`. The acceptance grep below is written so the resource lines are expected survivors.

## Local dossier

ai/findings/API-review/fable/schema-configuration-and-validation.md (§What it would change, spec-pages bullet), ai/findings/API-review/fable/README.md (§Doc drift found in passing).
